items.title: ClinVar-GKM
items.text:
All of ClinVar, every week, as standardized records you can query with SQL or load in Python.

ClinVar-GKM turns each ClinVar release into records in the GA4GH GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) schemas — VRS, Cat-VRS and VA-Spec — and publishes them as JSON bundles and Parquet tables, free, with no sign-in. It is built and maintained by ClinGen.

Current version line: 1.2 (v1/1.2/, schema 1.2.0), with a new release within a day or two of each ClinVar weekly release. The newest files are on Downloads.

1.2.0 started a new version line. Change v1/1.1/ to v1/1.2/ in your scripts; see Version Lines.

items.title: Get started
items.text:
• Try it in your browser · 2 minutes

    Run SQL against all of ClinVar in a live console, with nothing to install. Then follow one variant end to end in the Quick Start.

    Open the query console

  • Get the data

    20 Parquet tables (5 KB to 1.7 GB each, 4.6 GB in all), full JSON bundles (4.9 GB compressed), or weekly deltas (usually under 30 MB).

    Choose your data

  • What can I do with it?

    Tasks the data makes possible, from finding conflicting classifications to harmonizing variants by VRS identifier.

    See what you can do

  • I know ClinVar's website

    Where each part of a ClinVar variation page lives in the data: the variant, its classifications, its submissions and their review status.

    Map the website to the data

New to SCV, VCV and RCV, propositions or bundles? Key Concepts explains them in five minutes, and the Glossary defines every term. How to Read These Docs maps the site to what you need.

items.title: What it covers
items.text:
Every release covers the whole of ClinVar's XML release: 100% of its variations and of its SCV (submitted), VCV (per-variant) and RCV (per-variant-and-condition) classifications.

ClinVar data type v1 status Variation aggregate classifications (VCVs) and variation-condition aggregate classifications (RCVs) Included Germline and somatic submissions (SCVs) Included Variations, with genes, HGVS, SPDI and VCF extensions Included Submitters Included Aggregate and case-level observations (example) Planned Functional data submissions (example) Planned

Planned items are not in v1 and will be added as the community asks for them. Functional data SCVs are left out of v1 even when they are linked to a classification SCV.

items.title: Data use and citation
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM re-represents ClinVar data from NCBI, and ClinVar's disclaimer and data use policy applies to it:

  • Not for direct clinical use without review by a genetics professional.
  • Cite ClinVar as the data source, and ClinVar-GKM (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18343663) if you used these files.
  • License: the code and the published files are CC0 1.0. CC0 covers ClinGen's contribution only; NCBI's and ClinVar's policies still apply. ClinVar-GKM is not an NCBI, NLM or NIH product.

Data Use and Citation has the citations and what to carry with the data when you redistribute it.

items.title: Help and news
items.text: Report data problems on GitHub Issues and ask questions in Discussions. Release announcements go to the clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org list (Stay Informed); changes are in the Changelog. How the data is made: Pipeline Overview. Other GKM data and tools: the GA4GH GKM Starter Kit.

items.title: Data Use and Citation
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM re-represents ClinVar data. ClinVar is produced by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), part of the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM). ClinVar-GKM is produced by ClinGen. ClinGen's CC0 dedication covers what ClinGen adds. The ClinVar content inside the files remains subject to NCBI's and ClinVar's own policies, which apply to everyone who uses or redistributes these files.

In short

  • Not for direct clinical use. The ClinVar disclaimer applies to this data unchanged: the information "is not intended for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional." See Clinical use.
  • Attribute ClinVar. ClinVar asks that anyone who distributes or copies its data provide attribution to ClinVar as a data source. Cite ClinVar, and cite ClinVar-GKM if you used these files. See How to cite.
  • CC0 covers ClinGen's contribution only. It adds no restriction, and it cannot grant rights that NCBI or ClinVar's submitters hold. See License.
  • Pass this on. If you redistribute these files or data derived from them, carry the attribution and the disclaimer with them. See Redistributing the data.

items.title: Data source
items.text:
The ClinVar content comes from the public XML releases of ClinVar, at NCBI, NLM, National Institutes of Health (NIH). The pipeline adds the GKM structure and the VRS identifiers it computes. Weekly and delta file names carry the ClinVar release date, and each version line's index.json and the Parquet manifest.json name the release each file was built from; see How Releases Work.

ClinVar is an archive of classifications made by its submitters. When submitters disagree, ClinVar's FAQ says that "ClinVar does not arbitrate and resolve these conflicts", and its disclaimer says that "NIH does not independently verify the submitted information." ClinVar-GKM changes the representation, not the classifications. It keeps each submission's submitter and dates: every SCV statement's contributions reference a record in the submitter section. ClinVar remains the authoritative source. Check a record on ClinVar before you rely on it, and see Known Issues for what the transformation does not yet carry.

items.title: Clinical use
items.text:
ClinVar's disclaimer and data use policy applies to ClinVar-GKM data as it does to ClinVar:

The information on this website is not intended for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional. Individuals should not change their health behavior solely on the basis of information contained on this website.

NLM's Medical Information and Advice Disclaimer urges users "to consult with a qualified physician for diagnosis and for answers to your personal questions." The same advice applies to this data.

items.title: ClinVar
items.text:
ClinVar asks for attribution in its data use policy: "If you distribute or copy data from ClinVar, we ask that you provide attribution to ClinVar as a data source in publications and websites." It asks you to cite one of the ClinVar publications. The newest is:

Landrum MJ, Chitipiralla S, Kaur K, et al. ClinVar: updates to support classifications of both germline and somatic variants. Nucleic Acids Res. 2025;53(D1):D1313–D1321. doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1090. PMID: 39578691.

The data use policy gives PMID 29165669 as an example (Landrum MJ et al., Nucleic Acids Res. 2018;46(D1):D1062–D1067).

To refer to a specific ClinVar record, follow ClinVar's FAQ: cite the SCV accession and version for a submission, and the VCV or RCV accession and version for an aggregate record. ClinVar-GKM keeps these accessions and versions in its statement ids and extensions.

items.title: ClinVar-GKM
items.text:
If you used these files, also cite ClinVar-GKM and name the release you used, for example the bundle file name or the Parquet manifest.json source_release:

Babb L, Ferriter K, O'Neill T. ClinVar-GKM. ClinGen. doi:10.5281/zenodo.18343663.

The repository's CITATION.cff has the machine-readable citation, and GitHub's Cite this repository button formats it.

items.title: License
items.text:
ClinGen dedicates the ClinVar-GKM code and the published files, the transformed bundles and Parquet sets, to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal. CC0 covers what ClinGen contributes: the transformation, the structure and the identifiers it computes. It adds no restriction of its own.

CC0 does not change the terms that apply to the ClinVar content inside the files:

  • NCBI's Molecular Data Usage policy says that "NCBI itself places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the data". It also says that some submitters "may claim patent, copyright, or other intellectual property rights in all or a portion of the data", and that NCBI "cannot provide comment or unrestricted permission concerning the use, copying, or distribution" of it. CC0 waives only rights that ClinGen holds, so it grants nothing in rights that a submitter may claim.
  • ClinVar's submission policy says that "Once the data are in ClinVar, they are available for unrestricted distribution."
  • CC0 itself (section 4) offers the work as-is, with no warranty, and disclaims responsibility for clearing other people's rights in it.

You are responsible for following NCBI's and ClinVar's policies, including their attribution request, when you use or redistribute this data.

items.title: Redistributing the data
items.text:
You may redistribute ClinVar-GKM files, or data derived from them, under CC0. When you do:

  • Keep the attribution. Name ClinVar as the data source, as ClinVar asks, and name ClinVar-GKM and the release.
  • Keep the disclaimer visible. Carry the clinical use disclaimer, or link to it, wherever people see the data. NCBI asks the same of services built on its servers: its Guidelines for Scripting Calls to NCBI Servers state that "NCBI's Disclaimer and Copyright notice must be evident to users of your service."
  • Keep the submitter attribution. ClinVar's introduction says that "Each submitter is explicitly acknowledged". Do not strip the submitter records or SCV contributions from data you pass on as ClinVar's classifications.
  • Don't imply endorsement. See No endorsement.

items.title: In the published files
items.text: The same source, attribution and disclaimer are carried with the data: in each version line's README.txt (for example v1/1.2/README.txt) and in the Parquet manifest.json (fields source, attribution, disclaimer, license). The frozen v1/1.0/ line is unchanged and predates them.

items.title: No endorsement
items.text: ClinVar-GKM is not an NCBI, NLM or NIH product and is not endorsed by them. NCBI's Website Disclaimer says that "NCBI does not endorse or recommend any commercial products, processes, or services", and NLM's logo policy restricts use of its logo. ClinVar-GKM uses no NCBI or NLM logo. Products built on this data should likewise name ClinVar as a source without suggesting that NCBI, NLM, NIH or ClinGen endorses them.

items.title: How to Read These Docs
items.text:
These docs serve three kinds of reader. Some want to understand the data, often starting from what they already know of ClinVar's website. Some want to know how ClinVar's XML becomes this format. Some are building a pipeline or an application on top of it. Find yours below, follow its path as far as you need, and use the tab map to jump around.

Whichever path you take, the Quick Start (ten minutes, nothing to install) and Key Concepts (five minutes) are the best first stops.

items.title: The sections at a glance
items.text:
The site has six tabs, one per reader goal:

Tab What it gives you Read it when Start Here What ClinVar-GKM is, a quick start, its key concepts, which data to choose, what you can do with it and the tools to set up, plus this guide, Data Use and Citation (the ClinVar disclaimer, how to cite, the license) and Stay Informed (the announcement list) You are new to the project, or about to use, publish or share the data Get the Data The files: monthly and weekly full bundles, weekly deltas, keeping a copy current, Parquet, and how releases work You need the data, or need to keep a copy current Build & Query Query with SQL (the 20 Parquet tables, a browser query console, joins and working at scale), Recipes, Build Your Own Dataset, tracking change over time, Working in Python (the GA4GH libraries on bundles and Parquet) and two end-to-end User Stories You want to work with the data in SQL or Python, or see it used for a real task Understand the Data What each part of the bundle means: variations, SCV, VCV and RCV statements, ID references and annotated examples, and Mapping & Vocabularies, which maps ClinVar's statement types, classifications and review status You want to understand the data How It's Built Each step from ClinVar's XML to the published bundle You want to know how a value was produced Reference The Data Model (every class and field, generated from the schemas), Versioning, Changelog, Release Validation, Known Issues, FAQ, Glossary and more You need exact field definitions, what changed, what is guaranteed, or a definition

The tabs build on each other:

  • Start Here orients you and gets you to a first result.
  • Get the Data delivers the files.
  • Build & Query turns them into tables you can query, and datasets of your own.
  • Understand the Data explains what is in them.
  • How It's Built explains how each value was derived from ClinVar.
  • Reference defines every field exactly, and records what changes between releases and what each release guarantees.

items.title: Path 1: I know ClinVar's website and want to understand the data
items.text:
Everything on a ClinVar variation page has a place in the bundle. This table maps the pieces of the page you know to where they live, and to the page that explains each one.

On ClinVar's website In ClinVar-GKM Explained in A variation (VCV000012582) and its details: HGVS names, location, genes A variation record (clinvar:12582), a Cat-VRS categorical variant, defined by GA4GH VRS allele and location records Variations The Germline classification and its review status A vcv statement in the germline group, with its aggregate classification VCV Statements The Somatic clinical impact and oncogenicity classifications vcv statements in the somatic clinical impact and oncogenicity groups VCV Statements, Statement Types Each row of Submitted classifications (an SCV) An scv statement, which points to its submitter, its proposition and its evidence SCV Statements A classification for one condition (an RCV) An rcv statement RCV Statements The condition (a MedGen-linked trait) A condition, or a conditionSet when there are several Output Format Review status stars The statement's review status, which also sets its rank when submissions are aggregated Review Status "Pathogenic", "Drug response", and the other classification terms A classification on a typed proposition (for example VariantPathogenicityProposition) Classifications, Proposition Types

Suggested order: 1. Key Concepts: variants, propositions, SCV, VCV and RCV statements, and how records point to each other. 2. Output Format, for how the bundle's sections fit together. 3. The statement pages, starting with SCV Statements. 4. The annotated Examples, to see one real variation end to end.

Keep the Glossary and the FAQ at hand. To explore without writing code, the query console runs SQL in your browser.

items.title: Path 2: I want to know how ClinVar's XML becomes this format
items.text:
The Pipeline Overview walks the whole release. ClinVar's XML is first loaded into relational BigQuery tables by the upstream clinvar-ingest pipeline and prepared by clinvar-ingest-bq-tools. ClinVar-GKM's stored procedures take over from there.

Suggested order: 1. Variation Identity and VRS Processing: how each variant gets its GA4GH VRS identity. 2. Cat-VRS: how a ClinVar variation becomes a categorical variant. 3. Conditions & Traits: how submitted conditions are matched to ClinVar's traits. 4. SCV Statements, then VCV Statements with their aggregation rules, then RCV Statements. 5. Export & Distribute: bundle assembly, weekly deltas, Parquet and publication.

When a value in the data surprises you, the matching pipeline step says where it came from. Mapping & Vocabularies records the mapping rules. Release Validation lists the checks every release passes before publication. Design decisions are recorded as ADRs, for example ADR 0007 on pipeline principles.

items.title: Path 3: I am building a pipeline or an application on this data
items.text:
Suggested order: 1. Choose Your Data, then How Releases Work: which files to use, the release schedule, the directory layout and when files move. Keep Your Data Current applies the weekly deltas to a local copy. 2. Versioning & Releases: what is guaranteed. ClinVar-GKM has been generally available since 1.1.0, and the current line is 1.2 (v1/1.2/); published files are immutable, and a breaking change opens a new major line. 3. Set Up Your Tools: the tools, versions, disk and memory the examples need. 4. The Build & Query tab, by interface: - SQL on Parquet: Query with SQL, from the 20 tables and joins to working at scale and other tools, then the Recipes. - Your own tables or subsets: Build Your Own Dataset builds Parquet from a bundle and cuts self-contained mini-bundles with gkm-bundle-parquet. Track Change Over Time compares releases. - Python: Working in Python loads bundle and Parquet records into the GA4GH libraries (vrs-python, cat-vrs-python and va-spec-python, collected in the GKM Starter Kit), with the library versions that read 1.2.0 (and 1.1.0), and validates a bundle with the GKM Toolkit. See also GA4GH Standards. - Worked problems: the two User Stories. 5. JSON bundles: the Output Format, ID References for resolving #/section/id pointers, and the Data Model for exact fields and schemas.

Before you depend on a release, check the Changelog for migration notes and Known Issues. The Release Validation page lists the checks behind each release.

items.title: Getting help and news
items.text:
• Questions and ideas: GitHub Discussions. The Roadmap is built from them.
  • Problems with the data: GitHub Issues.
  • Release announcements, version changes and events: the clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org email list. Stay Informed explains how to join.

items.title: Stay Informed
items.text: ClinVar-GKM announces releases, version changes, and events on an email list, the Google Group clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org. Anyone can join, and you don't need a Broad Institute or GitHub account.

items.title: What the list announces
items.text:
• Each monthly release. When a new monthly full bundle is published, an automatic message gives its link and checksum and a digest of the weekly deltas since the previous monthly: each one's date, the records it added, updated and deleted, and a direct link. The same post appears in the repository's Discussions → Announcements. Individual weekly releases aren't announced; follow the line's Atom feed, feed.xml (see Downloads), for those.
  • New versions. When a new version is ready (for example 1.1.0), with what changed and links to the Changelog and the downloads.
  • Version changes, in advance. Before any breaking change, the list carries the proposal (a Request for Comment) and its comment window. Before a republish into a new version line, it carries a notice with the switch-over date. See Versioning & Releases.
  • Corrections and known issues that affect published data. The current list is on Known Issues.
  • Events and presentations where ClinVar-GKM is featured, such as conference talks, workshops and webinars. Past decks are on Presentations.

items.title: Join the list
items.text:
With a Google account. A Google account can use any email address; it doesn't have to be Gmail.

  1. Open the group page: groups.google.com/a/broadinstitute.org/g/clinvar-gkm.
  2. Sign in, then select Join group.
  3. Choose how you receive messages: every email, a daily digest, or web only. Then confirm.

By email, without a Google account.

  1. Send an email, with any subject and body, to clinvar-gkm+subscribe@broadinstitute.org.
  2. Reply to, or follow the link in, the confirmation message that comes back.

To leave, select Leave group on the group page, or send an email to clinvar-gkm+unsubscribe@broadinstitute.org.

items.title: Other ways to follow along
items.text:
• Release feed: each version line publishes an Atom feed, for example https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/feed.xml, which any feed reader can follow. It lists every published release, including each weekly update.
  • GitHub: watch the repository. Choose Custom, then Releases and Discussions, to get tagged releases and change proposals.
  • Questions and feedback: GitHub Discussions for questions and ideas, and GitHub Issues for problems with the data.

items.title: User Story: Auditing a Submitter's ClinVar Footprint
items.text:
Why this matters

A lab that submits to ClinVar accumulates a large body of classifications over years — and it is easy to lose track of which ones have aged, slipped to a weak or flagged review status, or point at conditions and therapies that no longer look right. Because ClinVar-GKM republishes every ClinVar release as typed Parquet (and a self-contained bundle), a submitter can pull their own complete footprint and run a repeatable audit on every release — turning "is anything of ours stale or wrong?" into a query that produces a fresh report each time ClinVar updates.

At a glance

  • Implementer — a ClinVar submitting lab (worked example: the Institute for Genomic Medicine (IGM) Clinical Laboratory at Nationwide Children's Hospital, submitter 196472)
  • Products — VA-Spec, Cat-VRS, VRS, GKM-Core
  • Pattern — Submitter self-audit / QC across releases
  • Tools — DuckDB or pandas over the published Parquet; a mini-bundle cut with gkm-bundle-parquet select; optionally va-spec-python
  • Status — In production: generally available since 1.1.0; current line 1.2

New to GKM datasets?

The GA4GH GKM Starter Kit is the best place to get oriented — it collects the reference libraries, the GKM Toolkit for loading and exploring bundles, and other user stories showing how projects put GKM to work.

items.title: The challenge
items.text:
An active submitter can have hundreds to thousands of SCVs in ClinVar, submitted and re-evaluated over many years. Several quality questions are hard to answer from ClinVar's web UI or flat XML:

  • Which classifications are stale? Assertions last evaluated years ago may predate current criteria and warrant re-review.
  • Which sit at a weak or flagged review status? Submissions with no assertion criteria provided, no classification provided, or a flagged submission status stand out for cleanup.
  • Which point at odd conditions? Placeholder or non-specific traits ("not provided", "not specified") — or conditions that have since been remapped — are worth a look.
  • Which reference unusual therapies? For therapeutic-response submissions, a malformed or unexpected drug or drug combination is easy to miss one record at a time.

Answering these one variant at a time doesn't scale, and ClinVar offers no turnkey "export everything we submitted as a queryable table."

items.title: What GKM enables
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM makes the whole submission set queryable and self-describing:

  • Every SCV is a typed VA-Spec Statement with an explicit classification, a quality (the review status / star level), direction and strength, submitter contributions (each with a date and activity type), and a proposition linking the variant to a condition — or, for therapeutic response, to a therapy or therapy group.
  • The whole release is typed Parquet — one file per bundle section, keyed by id, with every property of a record in its own typed column — so filtering your SCVs and joining them to conditions, therapies, and variants is ordinary SQL.
  • Releases are dated and incremental. The Parquet dataset at v1/1.2/parquet/ is rebuilt from the newest release every week, so the same audit re-runs against each release and its results can be diffed over time.

items.title: The data
items.text:
To make this concrete, the repository ships nch-igm-bundle.json.gz — the complete GKM extract of one real submitter, the IGM Clinical Laboratory at Nationwide Children's Hospital (submitter 196472): all 2,443 of their SCVs plus every variation, condition, therapy, proposition, and submitter record those statements reference, in a single self-contained 1.6 MB file. It is exactly "everything one submitter has in ClinVar," and it is the shape an audit consumes. It was regenerated from the 2026-10-18 release with the maintainer sub-bundle tool — sub-bundle.py --submitter 196472 — so it carries the 1.1.0 proposition sections and schema_version 1.1.0, and it passes strict validation against the ClinVar-GKM schemas (6,432 records, 0 failing).

For the recurring, release-over-release audit, a submitter works from the published Parquet instead. A single DuckDB query flags the records that need a second look:

Prerequisites

The DuckDB CLI, tested with 1.5.4, run from a directory holding six files from v1/1.2/parquet/: scv.parquet, the four proposition*.parquet tables and condition.parquet, about 1.2 GB together (Downloads → Parquet Files). They must be local: read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') is a glob, and DuckDB can't expand a glob over HTTPS.

-- Everything submitter 196472 has in ClinVar, flagged for review.
-- Reads six downloaded files from v1/1.2/parquet/ (rebuilt from the newest release
-- every week): scv.parquet, the four proposition*.parquet tables and condition.parquet.
WITH mine AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.quality.name        AS review_status,
    cond.name             AS condition_name,
    (SELECT max(c.date)                        -- most recent evaluation
       FROM unnest(s.contributions) AS t(c)
      WHERE c.activityType = 'evaluated')      AS last_evaluated
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true) p ON s.proposition = p.id
  LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' cond          -- CASE keeps this an equi-join (fast); an AND in ON plans a nested loop
         ON cond.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition' THEN p.object END
  WHERE list_contains(
          [c.contributor FOR c IN s.contributions],
          'clinvar.submitter:196472')
)
SELECT
  id, classification, review_status, condition_name, last_evaluated,
  last_evaluated < '2022-01-01'                        AS stale,
  review_status IN ('no assertion criteria provided',
                    'no classification',
                    'flagged')                          AS weak_status,
  coalesce(lower(condition_name) IN ('not provided', 'not specified'), TRUE)
                                                        AS odd_condition
FROM mine
WHERE stale OR weak_status OR odd_condition
ORDER BY last_evaluated;

The columns are named after the bundle's properties; run DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM 'scv.parquet' to see them. Each proposition table has only the columns its propositions use, so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true) reads all four and covers every SCV. A contribution date is YYYY-MM-DD text, so max and the comparison with '2022-01-01' work on it directly. A condition-set object (object_section = conditionSet) has no condition.parquet row and is flagged for a look. The same idea extends to therapies: filter the propositions on object_section IN ('therapy', 'therapyGroup') and join object to the id of the therapy / therapyGroup tables (with propositionSomaticClinicalImpact.conditionQualifier for the tumor type) to spot a malformed or unexpected drug or drug combination.

Because the Parquet dataset is rebuilt from every weekly release, running the query each week and diffing against the previous run's output turns the audit into a standing report — new stale rows, newly flagged statuses, and newly odd conditions surface on their own.

items.title: The tools used
items.text:
• DuckDB / pandas — query the published Parquet locally and build the audit report; DuckDB reads the .parquet files directly with no load step.
  • The clinvar-gkm Parquet — one typed file per bundle section, refreshed every release.
  • gkm-bundle-parquet select — --driver submitter cuts one submitter's footprint out of a published bundle into a single portable mini-bundle, the shape of nch-igm-bundle.json.gz.
  • va-spec-python — optionally load the flagged statements as typed VA-Spec models for deeper, programmatic checks.

items.title: How to explore this
items.text:
• Get the data — Parquet Files (the one Parquet dataset, at v1/1.2/parquet/).
  • See one submitter's whole footprint — open nch-igm-bundle.json.gz (2,443 SCVs, self-contained).
  • Understand review status — Review Status (the star levels the audit flags on).
  • Extract your own — cut your submissions out of a published bundle with gkm-bundle-parquet select --driver submitter (One submitter's submissions), or filter the Parquet by your submitter id as shown above.
  • See more GKM use cases — the GKM Starter Kit's user stories.

items.title: User Story: Harmonizing ClinVar by VRS Identity
items.text:
Why this matters

ClinVar is the largest public collection of expert interpretations linking genetic variants to health conditions. But using it alongside other resources has meant reconciling how each one describes a variant — HGVS strings, genomic coordinates, assembly versions — even when they mean the exact same change. ClinVar-GKM republishes ClinVar in the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Model (GKM): every variant carries a computed VRS identifier — a content-based fingerprint that is identical wherever that same change appears — and every classification is a structured VA-Spec statement with its evidence and provenance attached. So you can look up a variant's ClinVar classifications by identity, and line ClinVar up against any other VRS-aware dataset, without translating coordinates.

At a glance

  • Implementer — ClinGen / ClinVar-GKM (a transformation of NCBI ClinVar)
  • Products — VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec, GKM-Core
  • Pattern — Cross-source variant harmonization
  • Tools — vrs-python and va-spec-python; the published clinvar-gkm bundle
  • Status — In production: generally available since 1.1.0; current line 1.2

New to GKM datasets?

The GA4GH GKM Starter Kit is the best place to get oriented — it collects the reference libraries, the GKM Toolkit for loading and exploring bundles, and other user stories showing how projects put GKM to work. clinvar-gkm is one such producer.

items.title: The challenge
items.text: A lab or knowledgebase that wants to annotate its variants with ClinVar's classifications has to answer "is my variant the same variant ClinVar classified?" — a surprisingly hard question when the two sides use different HGVS transcripts, 0- vs 1-based coordinates, or different genome builds. Teams end up maintaining brittle normalization code just to join two tables, and the join silently misses variants whose descriptions don't line up. And once a match is found, ClinVar's flat XML says what the classification is but not, in a machine-actionable way, who made it, how, or against which method.

items.title: What GKM enables
items.text:
clinvar-gkm removes both frictions:

  • Identity, not description. Each ClinVar variant is represented as a Cat-VRS CategoricalVariant over one or more VRS alleles. The VRS allele id (ga4gh:VA.…) is a digest of the normalized sequence change, so the same change computed from any other source produces the same id — the join is an equality check, no coordinate math.
  • Structured knowledge with provenance. Each classification is a VA-Spec Statement asserting a Proposition (variant → condition) with its strength, review status, submitter Contributions, and citations — the same shape whether it came from a single submitter (SCV), a variant-level aggregate (VCV), or a condition-level aggregate (RCV).
  • One self-describing file. Everything is delivered as a bundle of named sections that reference each other by #/section/id pointers, so a variant, its classifications, conditions, and submitters are all reachable from one download.

items.title: The data
items.text:
Take the ClinVar expert-panel call on BRCA1 c.68_69del (a pathogenic frameshift). In the bundle it is a small connected graph — the classification statement points at a proposition, which points at the variant, which resolves down to a VRS allele:

// scv/  — the expert-panel classification statement
{
  "id": "clinvar.submission:SCV004101425.2",
  "type": "Statement",
  "classification": { "name": "Pathogenic", "primaryCoding": { "code": "pathogenic", "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015" } },
  "quality": { "conceptType": "Quality", "name": "expert panel" },
  "proposition": "#/propositionPathogenicity/SCV004101425-PATH",
  "contributions": [ { "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:509268", "activityType": "evaluated", "date": "2024-06-11" } ]
}

// propositionPathogenicity/  — what it asserts
{ "type": "VariantPathogenicityProposition", "predicate": "isCausalFor",
  "subject": "#/variation/clinvar:17662", "object": "#/condition/clinvar.trait:76328" }

// variation/  → allele/  → the VRS identity you can join on
{ "id": "clinvar:17662", "type": "CategoricalVariant", "members": [ "#/allele/ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R" ] }

Any dataset that computes the same ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R allele — a VCF annotation pipeline, gnomAD, another knowledgebase — matches this ClinVar classification exactly, and can then read its strength, review status, submitter, and condition straight from the bundle.

items.title: The same join with the Parquet tables
items.text:
The published Parquet tables answer the same question with one query, with no bundle to parse. Given VRS allele ids for your variants (computed with vrs-python, or read from a VRS-annotated VCF), look them up in variation and read ClinVar's call from vcv.

Prerequisites

The DuckDB CLI (tested with 1.5.4) and curl, in bash or zsh. The query reads two published tables of the newest release, variation.parquet (1.7 GB) and vcv.parquet (148 MB); it finishes in about 2 seconds on a laptop. Tested on the 2026-11-15 release.

BASE="https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet"
curl -fO "${BASE}/variation.parquet"
curl -fO "${BASE}/vcv.parquet"

WITH mine AS (                     -- your VRS allele ids
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R')) AS t(vrs_id)
),
v AS (                             -- each ClinVar variant and its VRS allele
  SELECT id, name, unnest(members).id AS member_id FROM 'variation.parquet'
),
call AS (                          -- ClinVar's germline pathogenicity call per variant
  SELECT 'clinvar:' || CAST(substr(id, 4, 9) AS INTEGER) AS variation_id,
         classification.name AS clinvar_call, quality.name AS level
  FROM 'vcv.parquet'
  WHERE regexp_matches(id, '-G-PATH$')
)
SELECT m.vrs_id, v.id AS variation_id, v.name AS variation_name, c.clinvar_call, c.level
FROM mine m
JOIN v ON v.member_id = m.vrs_id
LEFT JOIN call c ON c.variation_id = v.id;

vrs_id                                     variation_id   variation_name                             clinvar_call  level
ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R  clinvar:17662  NM_007294.4(BRCA1):c.68_69del (p.Glu23fs)  Pathogenic    expert panel

Run it in duckdb started in the folder holding the two files. For many ids, replace mine with a file (read_csv('my-vrs-ids.txt', header = false, columns = {'vrs_id': 'VARCHAR'})). For every ClinVar variant at once, keyed by VRS id and by VCF position, see the VRS-keyed harmonization table recipe.

items.title: The tools used
items.text:
• vrs-python — compute the VRS allele id for your own variants to join against clinvar-gkm's allele section (GKM-Core + VRS).
  • va-spec-python — construct and validate the classification Statements / Propositions as typed Python models.
  • GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) — validates the bundle against the ClinVar-GKM schemas you supply. Its loader (load_bundle, resolve, export) needs upstream updates before it reads ClinVar-GKM bundles, so follow the #/… pointers with a dictionary lookup, as in Working in Python.
  • The clinvar-gkm bundle — the monthly full plus weekly deltas on Cloudflare R2.

items.title: How to explore this
items.text:
• Get the data — Downloads.
  • Understand the shape — Output Format and ID References (including a small resolve() helper for pointers).
  • Pull one variant's full graph — gkm-bundle-parquet select cuts a variant's propositions and statements out of a published bundle into a mini-bundle (a second pass adds what those statements point to); see One variant.
  • See more GKM use cases — the GKM Starter Kit's user stories.

items.title: Working in Python
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM records are GA4GH objects, so the GA4GH Python reference implementations read them directly: vrs-python (ga4gh.vrs), cat-vrs-python (ga4gh.cat_vrs) and va-spec-python (ga4gh.va_spec), collected with other tools in the GKM Starter Kit. This page loads records from a bundle and from Parquet, follows their #/section/id pointers, builds the libraries' pydantic models from them, and serializes the models back to JSON.

It assumes the bundle layout described in Output Format and ID References, and, for the Parquet section, the tables described in The 20 Tables.

Tested with

Every code block on this page was run on 2026-11-21 with:

  • Python 3.14.5 (an earlier run, on 1.1.0 data, used 3.12.8), ga4gh.vrs 2.4.0a6, ga4gh.cat_vrs 0.8.0a6, ga4gh.va_spec 0.5.0a7, ga4gh.gkm 0.4.1, pydantic 2.14.4, duckdb 1.5.4, pyarrow 26.0.1, ijson 3.6.0, requests 2.34.2, gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 (through uv 0.6.14), and the ClinVar-GKM schema tree at tag 1.2.0.
  • Bundle examples: 1.2.0 data, the 2026-11-15 weekly delta.
  • Parquet examples: the published 2.0 tables at v1/1.2/parquet/ (2026-11-15 release), and a mini-bundle cut from the 2026-11 full bundle.

The Parquet files are written with DuckDB 1.5.4: the duckdb_version in their manifest.json.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.11 or later (the model libraries need 3.10, ga4gh.gkm 3.11), with the packages in Install.
  • git, to get the schema tree for Validate a bundle.
  • uv, for uvx gkm-bundle-parquet in Statements, propositions and variants, or pip install gkm-bundle-parquet==2.0.0 instead.
  • Network access to data.clinvar-gkm.org (the delta, and the Parquet tables, which the examples read remotely) and w3id.org (schemas fetched on demand).
  • Data: the 5 MB weekly delta from Get the example files. Only the gkm-bundle-parquet select example reads a full bundle: 4.9 GB compressed (68.5 GB decompressed), streamed from disk, about 10 minutes.

Run the Python blocks in order, in one Python session: each block uses the names (bundle, resolve, scv, vrs, rows, …) defined by the blocks before it.

items.title: Install
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM 1.2.0, like 1.1.0, is written to VRS 2.1.1, Cat-VRS 1.1.1, VA-Spec 1.1.0 and GKM-Core 1.3.0, so the same library versions read both. The library releases that implement exactly those versions are, as of this writing, pre-releases:

Package Version Implements Provides ga4gh.vrs 2.4.0a6 VRS 2.1.1, GKM-Core 1.3.0 Allele, SequenceLocation, SequenceReference, CopyNumberCount, CopyNumberChange; ga4gh_identify ga4gh.cat_vrs 0.8.0a6 Cat-VRS 1.1.1 CategoricalVariant and its constraints ga4gh.va_spec 0.5.0a7 VA-Spec 1.1.0 Statement, EvidenceLine, the proposition classes, Agent, ConditionSet, TherapyGroup ga4gh.gkm 0.4.1 — the GKM Toolkit; validate_bundle_schema for validating a bundle

The latest stable releases (ga4gh.vrs 2.3.3, ga4gh.cat_vrs 0.7.2, ga4gh.va_spec 0.4.4) implement older schema versions (VRS 2.0.1, Cat-VRS 1.0.0, VA-Spec 1.0.1) and reject most ClinVar-GKM records, so pin the pre-releases. The libraries require Python 3.10 or later, and ga4gh.gkm 3.11 or later. ga4gh.gkm 0.4.1 pins the same three pre-releases.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -q "ga4gh.vrs==2.4.0a6" "ga4gh.cat_vrs==0.8.0a6" "ga4gh.va_spec==0.5.0a7" "ga4gh.gkm==0.4.1"
pip install -q "duckdb==1.5.4" pyarrow ijson requests    # Parquet, streaming and schema-fetching examples

Check what is installed and which schema versions the libraries implement:

from importlib.metadata import version

from ga4gh.cat_vrs import CATVRS_VERSION
from ga4gh.core import CORE_VERSION
from ga4gh.va_spec import VASPEC_VERSION
from ga4gh.vrs import VRS_VERSION

for package in ("ga4gh.vrs", "ga4gh.cat_vrs", "ga4gh.va_spec", "ga4gh.gkm"):
    print(f"{package:14} {version(package)}")
print(f"VRS {VRS_VERSION}, Cat-VRS {CATVRS_VERSION}, VA-Spec {VASPEC_VERSION}, GKM-Core {CORE_VERSION}")

ga4gh.vrs      2.4.0a6
ga4gh.cat_vrs  0.8.0a6
ga4gh.va_spec  0.5.0a7
ga4gh.gkm      0.4.1
VRS 2.1.1, Cat-VRS 1.1.1, VA-Spec 1.1.0, GKM-Core 1.3.0

items.title: Get the example files
items.text:
The bundle examples use one small file, clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz (5 MB): the published 2026-11-15 weekly delta, a 1.2.0 bundle of every record that changed that week.

Its path changes when its month ends (it moves to deltas/2026-11/), so the commands look it up in the line's index.json:

DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"] if d["release"] == "2026-11-15"))')
curl -fsO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"

The full bundles are about 4.9 GB compressed (68.5 GB decompressed). Don't json.load one; see Large bundles.

The repository also has nch-igm-bundle.json.gz (1.6 MB), a self-contained 1.1.0 sub-bundle of every SCV from one submitter, cut with Sub-Bundle Extraction, in which every pointer resolves inside the file (curl -fsLO https://github.com/clingen-data-model/clinvar-gkm/raw/ef9bea69b64e6c738533ec7f6d8be353e05c3a5d/nch-igm-bundle.json.gz). The same libraries read it; validate it against the schema tree at tag 1.1.0, not 1.2.0.

items.title: Load a bundle and follow pointers
items.text:
A bundle is one JSON object whose sections map an id to a record. json.load is enough to read one:

import gzip
import json

with gzip.open("clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz", "rt") as f:
    bundle = json.load(f)

print(bundle["schema_version"])
print({section: len(records) for section, records in bundle.items() if isinstance(records, dict)})


def resolve(pointer):
    """Return the record that a '#/section/id' pointer names."""
    section, key = pointer.removeprefix("#/").split("/", 1)
    return bundle[section][key]

1.2.0
{'location': 176, 'allele': 230, 'copyNumberChange': 3, 'gene': 5, 'variation': 5471, 'condition': 190, 'conditionSet': 138, 'submitter': 10, 'propositionPathogenicity': 3399, 'propositionClinvarCustom': 325, 'evidenceLine': 6064, 'scv': 17562, 'vcv': 2941, 'rcv': 2548}

Records point to each other with #/section/id strings. Continuing from the block above (bundle, resolve), follow one SCV down toward its reference sequence: statement → proposition → variation → defining allele → location → sequence reference.

scv = bundle["scv"]["clinvar.submission:SCV008145211.1"]
proposition = resolve(scv["proposition"])
variation = resolve(proposition["subject"])
allele = resolve(variation["constraints"][0]["allele"])
location = resolve(allele["location"])

print(scv["classification"]["name"], "|", resolve(scv["contributions"][0]["contributor"])["name"])
print(proposition["type"], proposition["predicate"], "->", resolve(proposition["object"])["name"])
print(variation["id"], variation["name"])
print(allele["id"], allele["name"])
print(location["id"], location["start"], location["end"])
print(location["sequenceReference"], "| sequenceReference section in the delta:", "sequenceReference" in bundle)

# The delta has no sequenceReference section. A sequenceReference key is the sequence's refget accession,
# and that, with the type, is all a VRS identifier uses of it (see the next section)
sequence = {"type": "SequenceReference", "refgetAccession": location["sequenceReference"].rsplit("/", 1)[1]}

Likely pathogenic | Department of Ophthalmology, Seoul National University Bundang Hospital
VariantPathogenicityProposition isCausalFor -> RP1-related dominant retinopathy
clinvar:5042631 NM_006269.2(RP1):c.2238_2239del (p.Lys746_Ser747insTer)
ga4gh:VA.1Oo5_TVyd33l8M9QsAac-ULaZR86hDCx NC_000008.11:g.54626120_54626121del
ga4gh:SL.sF-Pr6l0-_uRAtk8bv9UzOPYvr6TK9IC 54626117 54626121
#/sequenceReference/SQ.209Z7zJ-mFypBEWLk4rNC6S_OxY5p7bs | sequenceReference section in the delta: False

A delta is not self-contained

A weekly delta carries only the records that changed, so its pointers can name records that are only in the full bundle it applies to. The 2026-11-15 delta, for example, has no sequenceReference section, and 57 of its alleles and copy-number changes point to a location that is only in the full bundle. Resolve a delta's pointers against the full bundle after applying the delta.

items.title: Into the GA4GH models
items.text: Each section's records, except the ClinVar custom propositions, validate as one class from the libraries. A pointer string is accepted wherever a field allows a reference: the models type it as iriReference, and its .root holds the pointer.

items.title: VRS alleles and their identifiers
items.text:
Continuing from the pointer walk above (allele, location, sequence):

from ga4gh.core import ga4gh_identify
from ga4gh.vrs import models as vrs

vrs_allele = vrs.Allele(**allele)
print(type(vrs_allele.location).__name__, vrs_allele.location.root)


def content(record):
    """A record without its stored identifiers."""
    return {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k not in ("id", "digest")}


# Recompute the VRS identifier from content alone: inline the location and its sequence reference
fresh = vrs.Allele(**content(allele) | {"location": content(location) | {"sequenceReference": sequence}})
print(ga4gh_identify(fresh), ga4gh_identify(fresh) == allele["id"])

iriReference #/location/ga4gh:SL.sF-Pr6l0-_uRAtk8bv9UzOPYvr6TK9IC
ga4gh:VA.1Oo5_TVyd33l8M9QsAac-ULaZR86hDCx True

ga4gh_identify needs the location inline: the allele's digest is computed over its location's digest, and the location's over its sequence reference, of which it uses only type and refgetAccession. Recomputed this way, every allele and copyNumberChange id in the delta whose location is also in the delta (176 of 233) matches the published id.

items.title: Cat-VRS categorical variants
items.text:
A variation record is a Cat-VRS CategoricalVariant. Its defining constraint points to an allele (or, for copy-number variants, a location) record. Continuing with variation from the pointer walk:

from ga4gh.cat_vrs import models as catvrs

categorical = catvrs.CategoricalVariant(**variation)
constraint = categorical.constraints[0].root
print(type(constraint).__name__, constraint.allele.root)
print([relation.primaryCoding.code.root for relation in constraint.relations])
print({e.name: e.value for e in categorical.extensions if isinstance(e.value, str)})

DefiningAlleleConstraint #/allele/ga4gh:VA.1Oo5_TVyd33l8M9QsAac-ULaZR86hDCx
['liftover_to', 'transcribed_to']
{'categoricalVariationType': 'CanonicalAllele', 'definingVrsVariationType': 'Allele', 'clinvarVariationType': 'Deletion', 'clinvarSubclassType': 'SimpleAllele', 'clinvarCytogeneticLocation': '8q12.1'}

items.title: VA-Spec propositions and statements
items.text:
Continuing with proposition and scv from the pointer walk:

from ga4gh.va_spec import base as va

pathogenicity = va.VariantPathogenicityProposition(**proposition)
statement = va.Statement(**scv)
print(pathogenicity.predicate, pathogenicity.subject.root, pathogenicity.object.root)
print(statement.direction, statement.strength.name, statement.classification.primaryCoding.code.root)
print(statement.proposition.root)
print([e.name for e in statement.extensions])

isCausalFor #/variation/clinvar:5042631 #/condition/clinvar.trait:66395
supports Likely likely pathogenic
#/propositionPathogenicity/SCV008145211-PATH
['clinvarScvId', 'clinvarScvVersion', 'submittedCondition', 'clinvarScvReviewStatus', 'submittedScvLocalKey', 'submissionLevel']

Records in the scv, vcv and rcv sections load as Statement, and evidenceLine records as EvidenceLine. The ClinVar-GKM statement profiles (ClinvarScvStatement, ClinvarVcvStatement, ClinvarRcvStatement) add no top-level fields to VA-Spec's Statement; their ClinVar-specific content is in extensions.

items.title: Extensions and ClinVar-specific types
items.text:
• Extensions load as GKM-Core Extension objects. name is a string; value keeps whatever JSON the record holds, including the structured values such as submittedCondition and clinvarHgvsList. The libraries don't interpret them. Statement extensions and Variations document each one.
  • ClinVar custom propositions have no class in va-spec-python yet. The propositionClinvarCustom section holds ClinVar's own germline proposition types (ClinvarOtherProposition, ClinvarRiskFactorProposition, …). Work with them as plain JSON, as the bundle provides them. Every other section loads into a library class without loss; see Round trip.

items.title: The GKM Toolkit
items.text: The GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) validates a producer's bundle against that producer's schemas. That is its intended way to validate producer data: you supply the schemas, and it checks every record against them. Validation works on ClinVar-GKM 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 bundles today; the toolkit's loader does not yet read them (see Loading bundles).

items.title: Validate a bundle
items.text:
Call validate_bundle_schema with a validator= whose referencing registry holds the ClinVar-GKM 1.2.0 schemas and the GA4GH schemas they reference, taken from the schema/ tree of this repository at tag 1.2.0 (for a 1.1.0 bundle, use tag 1.1.0). The release checks use the same schemas; Release Validation lists the results, and its verification reports record, per published file, the schemas and tool versions used.

Get the schema tree. The GA4GH schemas come in through the va-spec submodule:

git -c advice.detachedHead=false clone -q --depth 1 --branch 1.2.0 --recurse-submodules --shallow-submodules \
    https://github.com/clingen-data-model/clinvar-gkm.git clinvar-gkm-1.2.0

Register every schema in the tree by its $id, then validate the delta (bundle, and scv from the pointer walk):

import os
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from referencing import Registry, Resource
from ga4gh.gkm.bundles import BundleValidationError
from ga4gh.gkm.bundles.schema_validation import validate_bundle_schema

# Every schema in the 1.2.0 tree, keyed by $id: ClinVar-GKM's own and the GA4GH schemas they reference
schemas = {}
for directory, _, files in os.walk("clinvar-gkm-1.2.0/schema", followlinks=True):
    for name in files:
        try:
            document = json.loads(Path(directory, name).read_text())
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
            continue  # Makefiles and YAML sources
        if isinstance(document, dict) and "$id" in document:
            schemas[document["$id"]] = Resource.from_contents(document)
print(sorted(Counter("/".join(uri.split("/")[5:7]) for uri in schemas).items()))

bundle_schema = json.loads(Path("clinvar-gkm-1.2.0/schema/clinvar-gkm/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json").read_text())
validator = Draft202012Validator(bundle_schema, registry=Registry().with_resources(schemas.items()))

# The first 100 records of each section: the whole delta takes about 17 minutes (see below)
part = {"schema_version": bundle["schema_version"]} | {
    section: dict(list(records.items())[:100]) for section, records in bundle.items() if isinstance(records, dict)
}
validate_bundle_schema(part, bundle_schema, validator=validator)  # raises BundleValidationError on a violation
print("valid:", sum(len(records) for records in part.values() if isinstance(records, dict)), "records")

broken = json.loads(json.dumps({"schema_version": "1.2.0", "scv": {scv["id"]: scv}}))
broken["scv"][scv["id"]]["direction"] = "sideways"  # not a VA-Spec direction
try:
    validate_bundle_schema(broken, bundle_schema, validator=validator)
except BundleValidationError as error:
    print(error)

[('cat-vrs/1.1.1', 16), ('clinvar-gkm/1.2.0', 76), ('gkm-core/1.3.0', 11), ('va-spec/1.1.0', 40), ('vrs/2.1.1', 26)]
valid: 1118 records
Bundle does not match its JSON Schema at scv/clinvar.submission:SCV008145211.1/direction: 'sideways' is not one of ['supports', 'neutral', 'disputes']

Records are validated as published, #/… pointers included, against the full ClinVar-GKM profiles. The 1,118-record slice takes about 30 seconds on one core; the whole delta, 39,062 records, validates in about 17 minutes (pass bundle instead of part).

The same schemas resolve by $id through w3id.org, so a registry can fetch them on demand instead of reading a local tree. The bundle schema itself can be fetched the same way, from https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json. Fetching makes one request per schema, so validate a slice, here the first 25 records of each section. This continues from the block above (bundle_schema, Resource, Draft202012Validator):

import functools

import requests


@functools.cache
def fetch(uri):
    return Resource.from_contents(requests.get(uri, timeout=30).json())


fetching = Draft202012Validator(bundle_schema, registry=Registry(retrieve=fetch))
part = {"schema_version": bundle["schema_version"]} | {
    section: dict(list(records.items())[:25]) for section, records in bundle.items() if isinstance(records, dict)
}
validate_bundle_schema(part, bundle_schema, validator=fetching)
print("valid:", sum(len(records) for records in part.values() if isinstance(records, dict)), "records;",
      fetch.cache_info().currsize, "schemas fetched")

valid: 293 records; 104 schemas fetched

validate_bundle_schema takes a whole bundle in memory. For multi-GB full bundles, the release used a streaming, multi-process wrapper around it; that wrapper is proposed for the toolkit, as gkm-validate-bundle, in ga4gh/gkm-starter-kit#128, which is not yet released. That wrapper takes hours on a full bundle (about 17 h on 64 cores for a 1.2.0 full), so the release validates every bundle with jsonschema-rs instead (src/scripts/validate-bundle.sh): the same bundle schema, registry and per-record document, in minutes. Its tests check that it fails the same records as the toolkit, and each version release also runs the toolkit on a sample of a full; see Release Validation.

items.title: Loading bundles
items.text:
The toolkit's loader needs upstream updates for ClinVar-GKM bundles

The toolkit's loader tools (load_bundle, Bundle.resolve, Bundle.export and its model conversion) do not yet read ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0 or 1.2.0 bundles. They need updating upstream in two ways:

  1. The most recent GKM spec versions, which 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 data use: GKM-Core 1.3.0, VRS 2.1.1, Cat-VRS 1.1.1 and VA-Spec 1.1.0. ga4gh.gkm 0.4.1 matches these only through the pre-release libraries above, and it accepts a schema version only when it equals the installed library's.
  2. A way to handle producer-specific classes outside VA-Spec. The loader resolves schema references only against the GA4GH schemas it ships, cannot be given a producer's schemas, and converts records only to GA4GH model classes. ClinVar-GKM extends them in schema/clinvar-gkm/: the ten custom propositions (ClinvarAffectsProposition … ClinvarUndefinedProposition), ClinvarGeneContextQualifier, the statement profiles ClinvarScvStatement, ClinvarVcvStatement and ClinvarRcvStatement, the variant profile ClinvarCategoricalVariant (with ClinvarCanonicalAllele, ClinvarCategoricalCnvChange, ClinvarCategoricalCnvCount and ClinvarNonConstrainedVariant) and ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine. load_bundle stops at the first of these references.

Until then, use the model libraries for the standard classes and plain JSON for the extended ones, as on this page. Related work: ga4gh/gkm-starter-kit#128.

items.title: From Parquet
items.text:
The Parquet tables have no data column: every property of a record is its own typed column, named after the bundle property, and a reference is the bare id of the record it names, not a #/… pointer (see No data column). How close a row is to its bundle record decides how to get a model from it:

  • The VRS tables (allele, location, sequenceReference): a row without its NULL columns is the bundle record, with bare-id references, apart from the few columns noted below. It builds the model directly.
  • Every other table keeps values in a table's shape: extension values in value_<kind> slots, list references as {id, section} STRUCTs, a _section column beside a reference, some nested values as JSON text. Query those tables for what you need, then take the records themselves from the bundle.

Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles covers gkm-bundle-parquet, the tool that builds the tables and cuts mini-bundles.

items.title: VRS records from rows
items.text:
Read rows as dictionaries through pyarrow, drop the NULLs, and build the models (vrs is imported in VRS alleles and their identifiers). Here, the alleles of three variants: variation.members gives each member's id and the table it is in.

import duckdb

P = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet"


def strip_nulls(value):
    """A row, or a STRUCT or list inside it, without its NULL fields."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: strip_nulls(v) for k, v in value.items() if v is not None}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [strip_nulls(v) for v in value]
    return value


def rows(query, params=()):
    """Run a query; return each row as a dict of column name to value, without NULLs."""
    table = duckdb.execute(query, list(params)).to_arrow_table()
    return [strip_nulls(row) for row in table.to_pylist()]


def by_id(table, ids, columns="*"):
    """Fetch the rows of one table whose id is in ids, keyed by id."""
    marks = ", ".join("?" * len(ids))
    query = f"SELECT {columns} FROM '{P}/{table}.parquet' WHERE id IN ({marks})"
    return {row["id"]: row for row in rows(query, ids)}


variants = by_id("variation", ["clinvar:10", "clinvar:12582", "clinvar:51592"], "id, members")
alleles = by_id("allele", [m["id"] for v in variants.values() for m in v["members"] if m["section"] == "allele"])
for allele_id, row in alleles.items():
    model = vrs.Allele(**row)
    print(allele_id, model.name, model.location.root)

ga4gh:VA.Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9 NC_000013.11:g.32338445A>C ga4gh:SL.Gga5J2ccypatzYD5tBIeQEU9K4sPXc6J
ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY NC_000006.12:g.26090951C>G ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ
ga4gh:VA.LDaqvF3c3y1IG8wF4mORiRfB--9Jjfzp NC_000012.12:g.25245350C>T ga4gh:SL.qaHcVvdl8j0lpLRt49hE-bFI81128Mk9

The allele's location is a bare id. Follow it, and the location's sequenceReference, and recompute the identifiers as above, with content and ga4gh_identify from there:

# The record's own properties: start_min, start_max, end_min and end_max are derived columns
locations = by_id("location", [row["location"] for row in alleles.values()],
                  'id, type, digest, sequenceReference, start, "end"')
# extensions keeps its values in value_<kind> slots; the identifier doesn't use it
sequences = by_id("sequenceReference", [row["sequenceReference"] for row in locations.values()],
                  "* EXCLUDE (extensions)")

for allele_id, row in alleles.items():
    location_row = locations[row["location"]]
    inline = content(location_row) | {"sequenceReference": sequences[location_row["sequenceReference"]]}
    recomputed = ga4gh_identify(vrs.Allele(**content(row) | {"location": inline}))
    print(allele_id, recomputed == allele_id)

ga4gh:VA.Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9 True
ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY True
ga4gh:VA.LDaqvF3c3y1IG8wF4mORiRfB--9Jjfzp True
  • Ranges. A location whose start or end is a VRS Range has NULL in that column. The bounds are in start_min and start_max (end_min, end_max), and the record's value is [start_min, start_max], with null for an open bound. Copy-number locations are the usual case.
  • Sequence references. id is the record's bundle key, which the record itself doesn't carry, and extensions keeps its values in value_<kind> slots.
  • Checked. In a build of the 2026-10-31 delta, every allele row (16,557) and location row (11,127), read this way, equals its bundle record with the record's #/… pointers cut to bare ids.

items.title: Statements, propositions and variants
items.text:
For the other tables, query the columns. The proposition → statement → variant walk from the bundle examples, from the tables (scv.proposition and variation.id are the join keys; Joining Tables covers every hop), with rows, by_id and P from the block above:

prop_row = rows(f"""
    SELECT id, subject, predicate, geneContextQualifier.name AS gene
    FROM '{P}/propositionClinvarCustom.parquet'
    WHERE subject = 'clinvar:10' AND type = 'ClinvarRiskFactorProposition'
      AND geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY id LIMIT 1""")[0]
scv_row = rows(f"SELECT id, classification.name AS classification FROM '{P}/scv.parquet' WHERE proposition = ?",
               [prop_row["id"]])[0]
variant_row = by_id("variation", [prop_row["subject"]], "id, name")[prop_row["subject"]]

print(prop_row["id"], prop_row["predicate"], prop_row["gene"])
print(scv_row["id"], scv_row["classification"])
print(variant_row["id"], variant_row["name"])

SCV001142520-RF isRiskFactorFor HFE
clinvar.submission:SCV001142520.1 risk factor
clinvar:10 NM_000410.4(HFE):c.187C>G (p.His63Asp)

To load these records into the library models, take them from the bundle the tables were built from: the weekly full of the manifest's source_release, which is weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz while the tables are current. gkm-bundle-parquet select cuts a mini-bundle from it: the SCV and every record it points to, directly or through other records, so every pointer in it resolves inside the file.

select reads the whole bundle, 4.9 GB compressed, so download it once and pass the local path; --full also takes a URL, but then streams the whole file on every run. uvx comes with uv; without it, pip install gkm-bundle-parquet==2.0.0 and run gkm-bundle-parquet in its place. --out must not exist yet: delete it to run again.

curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 select \
    --full clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz \
    --bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json \
    --driver scv --ids clinvar.submission:SCV001142520.1 --out SCV001142520.json.gz

One id costs about as much as many: pass every id you need in one run (--ids takes a comma-separated list, --ids-file a file of ids). On a local copy of the 2026-11 full bundle, this selection took about 9 minutes, including the first uvx install and hashing the file. The mini-bundle loads like the delta; this block continues from the Parquet blocks above (scv_row) and the model blocks (va, catvrs):

with gzip.open("SCV001142520.json.gz", "rt") as f:
    mini = json.load(f)


def lookup(pointer):
    """resolve(), for the mini-bundle."""
    section, key = pointer.removeprefix("#/").split("/", 1)
    return mini[section][key]


scv_record = mini["scv"][scv_row["id"]]
risk = lookup(scv_record["proposition"])  # a ClinVar custom proposition: plain JSON
print(va.Statement(**scv_record).classification.name, "|",
      lookup(scv_record["contributions"][0]["contributor"])["name"])
print(risk["type"], risk["predicate"], risk["geneContextQualifier"]["name"])
print(catvrs.CategoricalVariant(**lookup(risk["subject"])).name)
print({section: len(records) for section, records in mini.items() if isinstance(records, dict)})

risk factor | Center for Computational Genomics and Data Science, University of Alabama
ClinvarRiskFactorProposition isRiskFactorFor HFE
NM_000410.4(HFE):c.187C>G (p.His63Asp)
{'sequenceReference': 1, 'location': 1, 'allele': 1, 'gene': 2, 'variation': 1, 'condition': 1, 'submitter': 1, 'propositionClinvarCustom': 1, 'scv': 1}

Remote reads of big tables are slow

The tables are sorted by id, and each row group's id range is in the file footer, so a lookup by id reads only the row groups that can hold it. A filter on any other column (scv.proposition above) reads that column from every row group, one HTTP request each, and the CDN limits each client to about 55 requests per 10 seconds. For anything beyond a handful of lookups, download the tables you need and query them locally (Working at Scale).

items.title: Round trip
items.text:
model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) serializes a model back to JSON. Records carry no null fields (except the open bound of a VRS Range, which survives), so exclude_none=True loses nothing. Compare every record of the delta with its round trip (this uses vrs, catvrs and va from the blocks above):

from collections import Counter

from ga4gh.core.models import MappableConcept

MODELS = {
    "sequenceReference": vrs.SequenceReference, "location": vrs.SequenceLocation, "allele": vrs.Allele,
    "copyNumberCount": vrs.CopyNumberCount, "copyNumberChange": vrs.CopyNumberChange,
    "gene": MappableConcept, "condition": MappableConcept, "therapy": MappableConcept,
    "conditionSet": va.ConditionSet, "therapyGroup": va.TherapyGroup, "submitter": va.Agent,
    "variation": catvrs.CategoricalVariant, "evidenceLine": va.EvidenceLine,
    "scv": va.Statement, "vcv": va.Statement, "rcv": va.Statement,
}


def model_for(section, record):
    if section.startswith("proposition"):
        return getattr(va, record["type"])
    return MODELS[section]


tally = Counter()
for section, records in bundle.items():
    if isinstance(records, dict) and section != "propositionClinvarCustom":  # plain JSON, no library class
        for record in records.values():
            dumped = model_for(section, record)(**record).model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
            tally[section, "identical" if dumped == record else "differs"] += 1
for (section, result), n in tally.items():
    print(f"{section:33} {result:9} {n:5}")

location                          identical   176
allele                            identical   230
copyNumberChange                  identical     3
gene                              identical     5
variation                         identical  5471
condition                         identical   190
conditionSet                      identical   138
submitter                         identical    10
propositionPathogenicity          identical  3399
evidenceLine                      identical  6064
scv                               differs   17562
vcv                               identical  2941
rcv                               identical  2548

Every record comes back identical except for one field:

  • Contribution dates. VA-Spec 1.1.0 types Contribution.date as a date-time. The records carry a date ("2026-11-14"); the model parses it as midnight and writes it back with a time:

    dumped = statement.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
print(scv["contributions"][0]["date"], "->", dumped["contributions"][0]["date"])

    2026-11-14 -> 2026-11-14T00:00:00

    Every SCV has contribution dates, so every SCV differs in those fields only. Compare dates by their first ten characters, or restore them after dumping.

The same sweep over the 1.1.0 sample sub-bundle (nch-igm-bundle.json.gz) gives the same result: every SCV differs only in contribution dates, and every other record, apart from the plain-JSON custom propositions, is identical.

Key order is not preserved: the models write fields in class-definition order. Compare parsed objects, not strings.

items.title: Large bundles
items.text:
A full bundle is about 4.9 GB compressed and 68.5 GB decompressed, so a json.load of one does not fit in a laptop's memory. Three ways to work with it:

  • Stream it. ijson reads one record at a time; kvitems(f, "scv") yields each (id, record) of a section. Build a model per record, keep what you need, and memory stays flat. One pass reads the whole file.
  • Query the Parquet for the latest release to find the records you need, and cut just those out of the bundle with gkm-bundle-parquet select, as above.
  • Cut a mini-bundle without the Parquet. select also picks records by a condition on any section (--driver submitter --where "name = '…'"), follows their pointers, and writes a small bundle the libraries read like the delta; see Cut a mini-bundle.

Streaming the delta's scv section, for example, to count classifications (gzip, Counter and va are imported above):

import ijson

classifications = Counter()
with gzip.open("clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz", "rb") as f:
    for scv_id, record in ijson.kvitems(f, "scv", use_float=True):
        classifications[va.Statement(**record).classification.name] += 1
print(sum(classifications.values()), classifications.most_common(4))

17562 [('Uncertain significance', 7388), ('Likely benign', 3389), ('Pathogenic', 2242), ('Likely pathogenic', 1986)]

use_float=True makes ijson return floats instead of Decimal.

items.title: Validation
items.text: Validate a bundle shows the toolkit validating against the ClinVar-GKM schemas, as the release does; Release Validation lists the release results and links the published verification reports. The model libraries also validate each record against its GA4GH class as they load it, as in every example on this page.
