items.title: Vendored DuckDB-Wasm runtime
items.text:
These files power the in-browser live query console (docs/assets/duckdb-console.html). They are vendored (committed to the repo) rather than loaded from a CDN so the docs site is self-contained and offline-capable — there is no runtime dependency on jsdelivr.

Version: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.29.0 · Bundle: eh only (WebAssembly exception handling).

File Size What it is Source duckdb-eh.wasm ~34 MB DuckDB engine compiled to WASM (eh build; includes httpfs, parquet, json) dist/duckdb-eh.wasm from the npm package, verbatim duckdb-browser-eh.worker.js ~760 KB Web Worker that drives the engine (classic worker, self-contained) dist/duckdb-browser-eh.worker.js from the npm package, verbatim duckdb-browser.bundled.js ~220 KB The browser API (AsyncDuckDB, selectBundle, …) with its apache-arrow dependency inlined built locally with esbuild (see below)

items.title: Why only the eh bundle
items.text: DuckDB-Wasm ships three bundles: mvp, eh, and coi. coi needs cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP headers) that GitHub Pages cannot set, so it is unusable here. eh (exception handling) is supported by every modern browser, so the mvp fallback buys almost nothing for +38 MB. We vendor eh only.

items.title: Why duckdb-browser.bundled.js is a local build
items.text:
The package's own dist/duckdb-browser.mjs has a bare import — import * as … from "apache-arrow" — which a browser cannot resolve without an import map or a bundler. So we bundle it into one self-contained ESM. The build needs Node.js with npm (tested with Node 22.14 and npm 11.3, on macOS) and runs outside the repository. esbuild is pinned: with 0.28.2 these commands reproduce the committed bundle byte for byte.

mkdir ddw-build && cd ddw-build
npm init -y
npm i @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.29.0 esbuild@0.28.2
printf 'export * from "@duckdb/duckdb-wasm";\n' > entry.mjs
npx esbuild entry.mjs --bundle --format=esm --platform=browser --minify \
  --legal-comments=none --outfile=duckdb-browser.bundled.js
# then copy duckdb-browser.bundled.js here; copy the .wasm + .worker.js verbatim from node_modules/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/dist/

The bundle is named .js (not .mjs) on purpose: GitHub Pages has served .mjs with a non-JavaScript MIME type, which breaks the ESM import. A .js module imported with import … works and is served as text/javascript reliably.

The .wasm and .worker.js are copied verbatim from the same package version — do not re-minify them.

items.title: Upgrading
items.text: Bump the version in the commands above, rebuild all three files together (they must come from the same version), and smoke-test the console in a browser (counts, DESCRIBE, a remote query, an error) before committing. Git LFS is not an option — GitHub Pages serves the LFS pointer, not the file, so these stay as plain committed blobs.

items.title: Build Your Own Dataset
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM gives four ways to get the part of ClinVar you need. They read the same records, so the choice depends on the question, the release, the machine you have, and whether you need the records themselves or rows derived from them.

Path What you get Releases Machine Provenance and citation Query the published Parquet 20 typed tables you query with SQL; download only the tables a question reads The newest release only; the set is overwritten every release A laptop: the tables a question reads, from 2 MB (condition) to 1.7 GB (variation), 4.6 GB for all 20 Rows derived from the bundle; manifest.json names the release and the bundle's sha256 Build tables with gkm-bundle-parquet The same 20 tables, or only some of them, or only the rows of a selection Any release whose bundle you have: a monthly, a weekly full, a rebuilt past week, a delta Seconds for a delta or a selection; about 3.5 hours for a full bundle on a 16 GB machine, 40 minutes on a large one Every file records the tool, the schema set and the source bundle's sha256; verify checks them Cut a mini-bundle with select The records of one submitter, gene, variant or condition, and the records they point to, byte for byte as published Any release whose bundle you have Under 100 MB of memory; about 11 minutes to stream a full bundle, about 1 second for a delta The records themselves, as published; the mini-bundle validates against the schema and records its selection Read the JSON bundle Every record of a release, the format of record Every release: monthly fulls, weekly fulls of the current month, weekly deltas About 4.9 GB compressed for a full bundle; stream it, don't load it The published file and its sha256; what the GA4GH libraries read

Cite the release you used whichever path you take: Data Use and Citation.

items.title: Choose your path
items.text:
Start from the question.

You want to Take Start with Try a query without installing anything Published Parquet, in the browser Query with SQL (its live console) Answer a question across all of ClinVar today (counts, conflicts, a gene, a condition) Published Parquet Recipes Join ClinVar to a VCF, gnomAD or another VRS dataset Published Parquet VRS-keyed harmonization table A table per SCV for pandas, R or a spreadsheet Published Parquet Flat analysis table See what changed this week for your lab or your gene panel Build tables from the week's delta Your First Dataset Tables for a release other than the newest Build tables Parquet for one weekly release A slice as records to share, archive or load with the GA4GH libraries Mini-bundle Cut a mini-bundle Prove a set of tables matches its bundle Build tables, then verify Verify a set of tables Every record of a release, or to stay current week by week JSON bundle Get the Data, Keep Your Data Current Follow a variant's classifications across releases Bundles of each release Track Change Over Time

Three questions settle most choices:

  • Which release? The published Parquet is the newest release only. For any other release, build the tables from that release's bundle, or cut a mini-bundle from it. Previous Releases lists what each line keeps.
  • How big a machine? Querying a few published tables, building from a delta and cutting a mini-bundle all run on a laptop. Building all 20 tables from a full bundle needs about 10 GiB of memory and 30 GB of free disk, or a selection instead.
  • Rows or records? Parquet rows are for analysis: joins, counts, exports. When the result must carry the records as ClinVar-GKM published them, with every identifier and pointer intact, cut a mini-bundle.

items.title: The pages in this section
items.text:
• Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles: the full guide to gkm-bundle-parquet, with measured runs on a delta and on a full bundle.
  • Your First Dataset: one submitter's submissions from a weekly delta, as tables, a DuckDB query and a mini-bundle, in about five minutes.
  • CLI Reference: every command and option of gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0.
  • Recipes: tested queries over the published Parquet, including a gene-panel subset, a VRS-keyed harmonization table, a conflicting-classification watchlist, one submitter's dataset and a flat per-SCV table.

items.title: CLI Reference
items.text:
Every command and option of gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0, the tool that builds Parquet tables and mini-bundles from a ClinVar-GKM bundle, one line each, with a tested example for the main commands. The tool's own README at v2.0.0 is the authority; uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 <command> --help prints the same options. Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles explains when to use each command, with timings on a full bundle.

Prerequisites

  • uv (tested with 0.6.14), to run the tool as uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0, or the tool installed as in Install. Python 3.10 or later (tested with 3.14.5).
  • bash or zsh on macOS or Linux (tested in zsh 5.9 and bash 5.2).
  • Data: the examples read the 2026-11-15 weekly delta, clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz (5 MB), and its .sha256 sidecar, in the folder you run them from. Your First Dataset downloads both. Each example finishes in under 15 seconds.

  • The examples use the shell array P for the schema options; set it once:

    P=(--bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json --version-property schema_version)
Command Does build builds the Parquet tables of a bundle, or of a selection of it select writes a selection as a mini-bundle: the selected records, byte for byte rebuild turns a full set of tables back into a bundle with identical records verify checks a set of tables: the directory alone, the round trip, or every value against the bundle validate validates every record of a bundle against its JSON Schema generate writes a schema's default column set, or checks a column set against it compile-spec prints the compiled table spec of a schema and column set, with no build version prints the tool, spec, policy, DuckDB and validator versions

Exit codes. 0 success. 1 a check failed: verify found a problem, validate found a failing record (or the bundle lacks a root property the schema requires), generate --check found a difference. 2 anything else: a missing or unreadable input, an unknown option or section, a missing --bundle-schema, a refused column set, a selection with no driver keys.

items.title: The bundle
items.text: Option Commands Meaning --full <bundle> build, select (required); verify the bundle: a path or URL, .json or .json.gz; a URL is streamed --sha256 <hex> build, select, verify, validate the bundle's expected sha256; without it, a <file>.sha256 sidecar beside the bundle is checked when there is one

items.title: The schema
items.text:
Option Commands Meaning --bundle-schema <schema> required by build, select, validate, generate, compile-spec; optional for verify the bundle's JSON Schema: a URL, a file, or a schema-set directory for offline use --version-property <name> same the root property holding the bundle's version: schema_version for ClinVar-GKM --column-set <file> build, select, verify, generate --check, compile-spec a column set that is the schema's default written out, or a named projection; default: the generated default

The tables are generated from the schema, so the schema decides the columns: pass the schema of the bundle's own schema_version (Name the bundle's schema).

Projections are limited in 2.0.0. A column set of your own must declare projection: <name>, and can only rename a column (name as submitter_name) or give a type to a position the schema leaves as JSON text. It can't drop a column or a section: the build stops on a record holding a property no column covers. For fewer tables use --tables; for fewer columns, copy the columns you want into your own file with DuckDB (See the columns before you build).

items.title: The engine
items.text: Option Commands Meaning --threads <n> build, select, rebuild, verify DuckDB threads (default: DuckDB's, one per core) --memory-limit <size> build, select, rebuild, verify DuckDB's memory limit, e.g. 12GB (default: half the memory the process may use, or of a container's limit); a lower limit spills more, the files are the same --work-dir <dir> build, select, rebuild, verify where staged records and DuckDB spill files go (default: a directory beside --out); a full build needs about 30 GB free there --keep-work build keep the staging files, and a selection's mini-bundle, after the build

items.title: Selection
items.text:
build and select take these; select requires --driver. A selection starts from rows of the driver table and follows the bundle's #/… pointers.

Option Meaning --driver <table> the table the selection starts from, e.g. submitter, scv, variation, gene --where "<expr>" a DuckDB boolean expression over the driver table as the build makes it (no ;) --ids k1,k2 driver keys, added to the --where matches --ids-file <file> a file of driver keys, one per line, added to the --where matches --follow out\|in\|both follow pointers out of the selected records (the default), into them, or both --max-depth <n> stop after n pointer hops from the driver (default: no limit); 0 keeps only the driver rows --sections a,b only traverse and write these sections
  • Nested columns in --where. A STRUCT field is reached by its dotted path, classification.name = 'Pathogenic', and a list by a list comprehension: "[c.contributor FOR c IN contributions IF c.activityType = 'submitted'][1] = 'clinvar.submitter:500031'" selects one submitter's SCVs from the scv table.
  • Every --ids key must be in the bundle. One missing key stops the selection (driver key(s) not in …; nothing was written). To start from a list that may hold keys the bundle lacks, such as a delta, match them in --where instead: --where "subject IN (SELECT column0 FROM read_csv('ids.txt', header = false))", as in Gene-panel subset.
  • No driver rows, no selection. A --where that matches nothing stops with no driver keys (exit 2).
  • Hubs. --follow in or both from a widely shared record (a condition, a gene, a submitter) reaches a large part of the bundle. Keep --max-depth low.

On a delta, set --max-depth

A delta omits the sections in which nothing changed that week (the 2026-11-15 delta has no sequenceReference, copyNumberCount, therapy, therapyGroup or somatic proposition sections). In 2.0.0 a walk that reaches a pointer into an omitted section keeps reading the bundle and does not finish: for example --follow out from scv with no --max-depth reaches location and then sequenceReference. A full bundle has every section and is not affected. On a delta, stop the walk before it gets there: from scv, --follow out --max-depth 4 ends at location (tested on the 2026-11-15 delta).

items.title: build
items.text:
Reads one bundle and writes one Parquet file per section, plus manifest.json and table-spec.json. With --driver, builds the tables of a selection instead.

Option Meaning --full, --sha256 the bundle --bundle-schema, --version-property, --column-set the schema --out <dir> the output directory (required) --tables a,b build only these tables (default: all); such a set can't be rebuilt or round-tripped --threads, --memory-limit, --work-dir, --keep-work the engine --driver, --where, --ids, --ids-file, --follow, --max-depth, --sections selection 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" --out parquet/

built 20 table(s) of spec sections 2.0, 39062 rows
  sequenceReference                               0  e3e7d2b96baf
  …
  scv                                         17562  333222b90a40
  vcv                                          2941  ca684960ee57
  rcv                                          2548  b7796596ea52
manifest: parquet/manifest.json

Two tables only, with the engine options:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" --out two/ \
    --tables submitter,scv --threads 4 --memory-limit 2GB --work-dir work/ --keep-work

built 2 table(s) of spec sections 2.0, 17572 rows
  submitter                                      10  6451c8a350e0
  scv                                         17562  333222b90a40
manifest: two/manifest.json

The files are the same bytes as the full build's submitter and scv (same sha256): the engine options don't change the output. --keep-work left the staging directory under work/.

items.title: select
items.text:
Writes the mini-bundle of a selection: the selected records, verbatim, in the bundle's own layout (.json.gz; the file must not exist). The same inputs and options give the same bytes.

Option Meaning --full, --sha256 the bundle --bundle-schema, --version-property, --column-set the schema --out <file> the mini-bundle to write (required) --threads, --memory-limit, --work-dir the engine --driver (required), --where, --ids, --ids-file, --follow, --max-depth, --sections selection

Every SCV classified Pathogenic, with --max-depth 0 (no pointers followed) and a nested --where:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 select --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver scv --where "classification.name = 'Pathogenic'" --max-depth 0 \
    --out pathogenic-scvs.json.gz

selected 2242 record(s) in 1 section(s) from clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz: pathogenic-scvs.json.gz (491629 bytes, sha256 2253d30d…)
  scv                                          2242

One submitter and the SCVs that point to it, writing only those two sections:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 select --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver submitter --ids clinvar.submitter:510823 --follow in --max-depth 1 \
    --sections submitter,scv --out hema-scvs.json.gz

selected 288 record(s) in 2 section(s) from clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz: hema-scvs.json.gz (64432 bytes, sha256 bc89e6be…)
  submitter                                       1
  scv                                           287

A selection from a delta can point to records the delta doesn't carry; the tool counts them as dangling pointers and writes the mini-bundle anyway. A selection from a full bundle has none.

items.title: rebuild
items.text:
Writes a full set of tables back as a bundle whose records are identical to the source's (the same canonical JSON: key order, array order and spacing don't count), and checks it against the records sha256s the build recorded. Needs every table, manifest.json and table-spec.json, and no schema. Refuses a selection and a build with --tables.

Option Meaning dir the built directory (positional) -o, --out <file> the bundle to write, .json or .json.gz (required) --threads, --memory-limit, --work-dir the engine 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 rebuild parquet/ -o rebuilt.json.gz

rebuilt rebuilt.json.gz: bundle schema 1.2.0, 14 section(s), 39062 records, 68660443 bytes of text, records sha256 473016fd… (matches the manifest's records_sha256 and every section's section_records_sha256: record-identical to the source)

items.title: verify
items.text:
Checks a built directory against the spec the build wrote beside its manifest. Needs no schema; given --bundle-schema (and --column-set, if the build had one), it also checks that they compile to that spec.

Option Meaning dir the built directory (positional) (none) the directory check: every file matches the manifest's sha256 and row counts, and carries the expected metadata --roundtrip rebuild the records (hashed, not written) and compare their sha256s with the recorded ones and, with --full, the bundle's own; a full build only --bundle-recompute recompute every row and value from the bundle given with --full; for a selection, --full is its mini-bundle --full, --sha256 the bundle to compare with --bundle-schema, --version-property, --column-set also check they compile to the spec that wrote the files --report <file.md> write a Markdown report there, and a .json beside it --threads, --memory-limit, --work-dir the engine 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 verify parquet/ --report verify-report.md
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 verify parquet/ --roundtrip --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 verify parquet/ --bundle-recompute --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}"

report: verify-report.md and verify-report.json
verify pass: directory check: 0 problem(s)
verify pass: directory check: 0 problem(s); round trip: identical
verify pass: directory check: 0 problem(s); bundle recompute: 0 group(s) differ

items.title: validate
items.text:
Validates each record of a bundle on its own, as a one-section bundle with the bundle's version, so key patterns are checked too.

Option Meaning bundle the bundle: a path or URL (positional) --bundle-schema, --version-property the schema; validate against the schema of the bundle's own schema_version --sha256 the bundle's expected sha256 --engine rs\|python rs, jsonschema-rs (the default); python, the GA4GH GKM Toolkit's validator, the reference (much slower; needs gkm-bundle-parquet[reference] and Python 3.11 or later) --workers <n> worker processes (default: one per CPU) --failures <file> write every failing record's section, key and errors there, as JSON lines --json <file> write the counts and timings there, as JSON --max-print <n> how many failing records to print (default 20) 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 validate clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --workers 4 --failures bad.jsonl --json validate.json --max-print 5

…
records: 39,062  failing: 0  (8.3 s)
PASS

bad.jsonl is empty when nothing fails. validate.json holds bundle, bundle_sha256, engine, failing, records, schema_set_sha256, seconds, sections, version and workers. The python engine wasn't run for this page.

items.title: generate
items.text:
Writes the default column set of a bundle schema: every collection, every property its record schema allows. On stderr it lists every position kept as JSON text and every IRI with no declared target, with the reason.

Option Meaning --bundle-schema, --version-property the schema -o, --out <file> write the column set there (default: stdout) --check check --column-set against the default; exit 1 and list each difference if it differs --column-set <file> with --check: the column set to check 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 generate "${P[@]}" -o cols.yaml
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 generate --check \
    --bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json \
    --column-set cols.yaml

cols.yaml: complies: it compiles to the default (policy 2.0)

A column set names its own version property, so --check needs only --bundle-schema and --column-set.

items.title: compile-spec
items.text:
Prints the sections table spec a schema and column set compile to, as YAML, with no bundle and no build: every table, column and type, and the three sha256s each Parquet file records.

Option Meaning --bundle-schema, --version-property, --column-set the schema 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 compile-spec "${P[@]}" > spec.yaml
head -5 spec.yaml

# Table spec sections 2.0, compiled (ADR 0006): the default (policy 2.0).
# schema_set_sha256: 3b3920180d08f3343d7466ce55bbcb95f5cbc467c505a4e03797b8f3c48d6798
# column_set_sha256: e07436add989762e1ffaefe157565e660a5b5ee57178fcffdeb23b3826e7a6fd
# table_spec_sha256: 8f87c3bcc6cc4ee22da9c3c0f2b8a2cf666d848fbafee2d949ea17ab0a9a3b32 (of what affects the tables, compiler.table_spec_sha256)
name: sections

items.title: version
items.text:
Option Meaning --json print as JSON: tool_version, table_spec, table_spec_version, policy_version, schema_version_rule, kv_prefix, kv_prefixes_read, duckdb_version, validate_engines 
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 version --json

{
  "tool_version": "2.0.0",
  "table_spec": "sections",
  "table_spec_version": "2.0",
  "policy_version": "2.0",
  …
  "duckdb_version": "1.5.4",
  …
}

A script that records what built a set can keep this output beside the tables. An engine's version is null when it isn't installed (the python engine without the reference extra).

items.title: Your First Dataset
items.text:
This page builds one small dataset end to end: the submissions one laboratory added to ClinVar in one week, as Parquet tables, queried with DuckDB, and as a mini-bundle of the published records. It reads a 5 MB weekly delta and takes about five minutes, most of it reading.

Prerequisites

  • uv, to run gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 with uvx (tested with uv 0.6.14 and Python 3.14.5; the tool needs Python 3.10 or later). To install the tool instead, see Install.
  • DuckDB CLI, tested with 1.5.4, and curl and python3.
  • bash or zsh, on macOS or Linux. Tested in zsh 5.9, bash 5.2 and macOS's bash 3.2.
  • Data: the 2026-11-15 weekly delta (5 MB) and two small published Parquet tables, submitter.parquet (0.1 MB) and condition.parquet (2 MB), all downloaded below. Every command finishes in a few seconds with under 2 GB of memory.
  • Run the blocks in order, in one shell and one folder: later blocks use the files and the P array that earlier blocks make.

items.title: Get the input
items.text:
Make a folder and download the 2026-11-15 weekly delta with its checksum sidecar. A delta's path changes when its month ends, so the command looks the path up in the line's index.json:

mkdir -p first-dataset && cd first-dataset
DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"] if d["release"] == "2026-11-15"))')
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}.sha256"

A delta holds only the records that changed in that week's release. That makes it the right input for "what changed this week", and the wrong input for "everything about X" (see What the result covers).

items.title: Find the submitter
items.text:
Submitters are identified by id. Look the id up by name in the published submitter.parquet:

curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/submitter.parquet
duckdb -c "SELECT id, name FROM 'submitter.parquet' WHERE name ILIKE 'hema,%'"

┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            id            │                           name                           │
│         varchar          │                         varchar                          │
├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ clinvar.submitter:510823 │ Hema, HEMA – Genetic and Molecular Diagnostic Laboratory │
└──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

HEMA's first submissions to ClinVar are in the 2026-11-15 release.

items.title: Build the tables
items.text:
Every command that reads a bundle needs the bundle's schema. Put the two schema options in a shell array; an array works in both bash and zsh, where a plain string variable would reach the tool as one argument:

P=(--bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json --version-property schema_version)

Build the tables of a selection: start from the submitter (--driver submitter --ids …), follow pointers in both directions for two hops (--follow both --max-depth 2), and write a table per section:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver submitter --ids clinvar.submitter:510823 \
    --follow both --max-depth 2 \
    --out hema/

built 20 table(s) of spec sections 2.0, 1149 rows, a selection driven by submitter
  …
  submitter                                       1  80e5a1eaa6de
  propositionPathogenicity                      287  4556b6f69c83
  …
  evidenceLine                                  574  9df13aafdb32
  scv                                           287  ca7d38662aef
  …
manifest: hema/manifest.json

Progress lines go to stderr; tables with no rows are written too. The walk, hop by hop:

Hop Direction Records 0 the driver the submitter 1 in: records that point to the submitter its 287 SCVs 2 out of the SCVs, and in to them the 287 propositions they assert; the 574 VCV and RCV evidence lines that cite them

--max-depth keeps the walk small. Without it, --follow both keeps going through every shared record (a condition, a gene) and collects much of the bundle.

items.title: Query the tables
items.text:
Count the week's submissions by classification. The variant is the proposition's subject:

duckdb -c "
SELECT s.classification.name     AS classification,
       count(*)                  AS scvs,
       count(DISTINCT p.subject) AS variants
FROM 'hema/scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'hema/propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON p.id = s.proposition
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scvs DESC"

┌────────────────────────────┬───────┬──────────┐
│       classification       │ scvs  │ variants │
│          varchar           │ int64 │  int64   │
├────────────────────────────┼───────┼──────────┤
│ Uncertain significance     │   191 │      191 │
│ Pathogenic                 │    66 │       66 │
│ Likely pathogenic          │    26 │       26 │
│ Pathogenic, low penetrance │     2 │        2 │
│ Established risk allele    │     2 │        2 │
└────────────────────────────┴───────┴──────────┘

Name the conditions with the published condition.parquet (2 MB). The proposition's object is a condition id:

curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/condition.parquet
duckdb -c "
SELECT c.name AS condition, count(*) AS scvs
FROM 'hema/scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'hema/propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON p.id = s.proposition
JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = p.object
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scvs DESC, condition
LIMIT 5"

┌─────────────────────────────────────┬───────┐
│              condition              │ scvs  │
│               varchar               │ int64 │
├─────────────────────────────────────┼───────┤
│ Lynch syndrome                      │    67 │
│ ATM-related cancer predisposition   │    47 │
│ PALB2-related cancer predisposition │    24 │
│ CHEK2-related cancer predisposition │    22 │
│ BRCA2-related cancer predisposition │    21 │
└─────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘

A hereditary cancer laboratory. In general a proposition's object can also be a condition set (object_section = 'conditionSet'); Joining Tables shows that join. All 287 here name one condition.

items.title: Keep the records
items.text:
The tables are for querying. To keep the selection as records, byte for byte as published, write it as a mini-bundle with select and the same options, then validate it:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 select --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver submitter --ids clinvar.submitter:510823 \
    --follow both --max-depth 2 \
    --out hema.json.gz
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 validate hema.json.gz "${P[@]}"

selected 1149 record(s) in 4 section(s) from clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz: hema.json.gz (99427 bytes, sha256 28e17faa…)
  submitter                                       1
  propositionPathogenicity                      287
  evidenceLine                                  574
  scv                                           287
…
records: 1,149  failing: 0  (0.4 s)
PASS

The same inputs and options give the same bytes, so the sha256 identifies the selection. A mini-bundle is a real bundle: every tool that reads ClinVar-GKM bundles reads it, including build.

items.title: What the result covers
items.text:
The dataset holds what the 2026-11-15 delta holds, and nothing else:

  • It is the week's changes. Each of HEMA's 287 SCVs is version 1, new in this release, so here the week's changes are all of HEMA's submissions. For a submitter with older submissions, the same command returns only those that changed this week.
  • Unchanged records are missing. The variants and conditions the propositions point to didn't change this week, so the delta doesn't carry them. The condition names above come from the published Parquet instead.
  • The latest release can differ. The published submitter.parquet and condition.parquet are the newest release, overwritten weekly; the delta is fixed to 2026-11-15.

For everything about a submitter, run the same command on a full bundle (about 4.9 GB, from Monthly Full Bundles); select streams it in about 11 minutes with under 100 MB of memory. For the newest release, the published Parquet answers without the tool: One submitter's dataset.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
• CLI Reference: every option, including --where on nested columns, --ids-file and --sections.
  • Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles: full bundles, past weeks, verify and rebuild.
  • Recipes: questions over the whole release with the published Parquet.

items.title: Track Change Over Time
items.text:
A bundle is the state of ClinVar at one release. To follow how a variant's classification, or a submitter's submissions, changed from week to week, combine the releases into a history table: one row for each version of each statement, with the releases it was current for. This page builds that table from a monthly full and the weekly deltas, queries it, and shows the cheaper alternative when two points in time are enough: comparing two monthlies.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.9 or later (tested with 3.14.5) and the duckdb Python package (tested with 1.5.4):

    curl -fsSO https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/1.2/assets/scripts/track-history.py
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install duckdb==1.5.4

The later blocks run python3 in this virtual environment, from the same working directory. - Data. A history from deltas only downloads every delta since 2026-07-06 and its manifest: 20 deltas, 0.5 GB, and 0.26 GB of manifests. A complete history adds one monthly full, 4.5 GB, read once after its sha256 is checked. Comparing two monthlies reads two of them. See Scope for what each gives. - Disk and time. The deltas-only history is a DuckDB file of 0.12 GB, built in about 4 minutes after the download. A history from a monthly also holds a row for each of the monthly's statements (about 28 million), so expect a few GB.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
• History on the host starts at 2026-06-27. The first monthly is the frozen 1.1 line's 2026-07, built from the 2026-06-27 release, and the first delta is 2026-07-06. The same weeks are in the frozen 1.0 line, in schema 1.0.1; this page uses the newest line that holds each week.
  • It spans two schemas. Releases up to 2026-10-31 are in v1/1.1/ (schema 1.1.0); from 2026-10-31 on, in v1/1.2/ (schema 1.2.0). The 1.2 line starts from a checkpoint monthly at 2026-10-31, and its first delta, 2026-11-08, is computed against that checkpoint, so it carries ClinVar's changes only. A record that didn't change keeps, in the history, the form it had in the last 1.1 delta that carried it. The history keeps only values whose path and meaning are the same in both schemas (below): every row of the deltas-only history still current at 2026-11-15, 2,649,530 of them from 1.1 deltas, has the classification, review status and submitter of the same key in the 1.2.0 weekly full. For any other value, compare the two 2026-11 monthlies, v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz and v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz: both are the 2026-10-31 release, so every difference between them comes from the schema, not from ClinVar.
  • Release dates come from index.json. A bundle carries no release date. A row's valid_from is the release of the delta that added it, or the monthly's source_release for rows loaded from the monthly (current then, and possibly earlier). The dates inside records, such as an SCV's submitted contribution date, are ClinVar's dates, not release dates.
  • A history from deltas only sees every change from 2026-07-06 on, but not the state before a statement's first change: a statement that never changed has no row, and a statement's first row is its first new version. Start from a monthly to have both.

items.title: Build the history
items.text:
track-history.py builds the table in clinvar-gkm-history.duckdb:

Column Description section scv, vcv or rcv stable_id The key without ClinVar's version: the SCV accession (SCV000024262, the record's clinvarScvId), or the VCV or RCV accession with its group and type suffix (VCV000183114-G-PATH, RCV000041109-G-PATH-CP). The rows of one statement across versions share it key The bundle key, with the version (clinvar.submission:SCV000024262.158, VCV000183114.35-G-PATH) proposition The statement's proposition key. Proposition keys carry no version (SCV000024262-PATH, VCV000183114-G-PATH) classification classification.name review_status The clinvarScvReviewStatus (SCV) or clinvarReviewStatus (VCV, RCV) extension submitter An SCV's submitter: the contributor of its submitted contribution (clinvar.submitter:3) valid_from The release the row became current valid_to The release whose delta deleted or replaced it; NULL while it is current

It is a slowly changing dimension of type 2. For each delta, in release order, the script adds a row for every SCV, VCV and RCV record of the delta bundle, and closes the current row of every key the delta deletes (the manifest's deleted lists) or replaces. A new ClinVar version arrives as a delete of the old key and an add of the new one (Weekly Deltas), so it closes one row and opens the next under the same stable_id. It checks the chain (each delta's baseline_release is the release before it) and each download's sha256, and takes every path from the index.json files.

items.title: A complete history, from the first monthly
items.text:
MONTHLY=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(m["path"] for m in json.load(sys.stdin)["datasets"]["monthly"] if m["release"] == "2026-07"))')
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${MONTHLY}"
python3 track-history.py base clinvar-gkm_2026-07.json.gz --line v1/1.1
python3 track-history.py update

base finds the monthly in the line's index.json by its sha256 and loads its statements as current at its source_release (2026-06-27). This was not run for this page; reading a monthly's statements (about 28 million) is estimated at about 10 minutes, from the measured 12.5 s for the 0.9 million statements of the 2026-11-08 delta.

items.title: A history from deltas only
items.text:
python3 track-history.py base --from-release 2026-06-27
python3 track-history.py update

history starts at 2026-06-27 (deltas only, from 2026-06-27)
2026-07-06 (v1/1.1): 5535 statement rows added
2026-07-15 (v1/1.1): 11593 statement rows added
…
2026-10-31 (v1/1.1): 171431 statement rows added
2026-11-08 (v1/1.2): 924737 statement rows added
2026-11-15 (v1/1.2): 23051 statement rows added
history at 2026-11-15

Run update again after each weekly release to add the new deltas. update --to 2026-10-31 stops at a release.

items.title: Query the history
items.text: The queries run in DuckDB on clinvar-gkm-history.duckdb. Each block is a complete Python script; the output shown is from the deltas-only history at 2026-11-15.

items.title: One variant's classification timeline
items.text:
The germline pathogenicity classification ClinVar shows for a variant is its VCV aggregate statement, the -G-PATH key (VCV Statements). Its rows, oldest first:

python3 - <<'EOF'
import duckdb
con = duckdb.connect("clinvar-gkm-history.duckdb", read_only=True)
con.sql("""
  SELECT key, classification, review_status, valid_from, valid_to
  FROM history WHERE stable_id = 'VCV000487338-G-PATH'
  ORDER BY valid_from
""").show(max_width=200)
EOF

┌────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│          key           │        classification        │                    review_status                     │ valid_from │  valid_to  │
│        varchar         │           varchar            │                       varchar                        │  varchar   │  varchar   │
├────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────┼────────────┤
│ VCV000487338.20-G-PATH │ Pathogenic                   │ criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts │ 2026-09-05 │ 2026-09-13 │
│ VCV000487338.21-G-PATH │ Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic │ criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts │ 2026-09-13 │ 2026-09-23 │
│ VCV000487338.22-G-PATH │ Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic │ criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts │ 2026-09-23 │ 2026-09-28 │
│ VCV000487338.22-G-PATH │ Pathogenic                   │ criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts │ 2026-09-28 │ 2026-10-18 │
│ VCV000487338.23-G-PATH │ Likely pathogenic            │ reviewed by expert panel                             │ 2026-10-18 │ NULL       │
└────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────┴────────────┘

A new version is a new key; a change without a new version (2026-09-28) is a new row under the same key. The VCV accession's number is the variant's ClinVar variation ID: the proposition VCV000487338-G-PATH is about clinvar:487338. For the statements at other levels of the hierarchy (-G-PATH-CP, -G-PATH-EP, …), use their stable_id.

items.title: SCV reclassifications by submitter
items.text:
A reclassification is two consecutive rows of one SCV whose classifications differ: usually the delete of one version and the add of the next. Counted by submitter, with the submitters' names from the published submitter table (a 0.1 MB file):

curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/submitter.parquet
python3 - <<'EOF'
import duckdb
con = duckdb.connect("clinvar-gkm-history.duckdb", read_only=True)
con.sql("""
  CREATE TEMP VIEW scv_changes AS
  WITH s AS (
    SELECT *, lag(classification) OVER w AS before, lag(valid_to) OVER w AS before_to
    FROM history WHERE section = 'scv'
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY stable_id ORDER BY valid_from, key))
  SELECT stable_id, valid_from AS release, before, classification AS after, submitter
  FROM s WHERE before_to = valid_from AND after IS DISTINCT FROM before
""")
con.sql("""
  SELECT c.submitter, s.name, count(*) AS changes, count(DISTINCT stable_id) AS scvs
  FROM scv_changes c
  LEFT JOIN 'submitter.parquet' s ON s.id = c.submitter
  GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY changes DESC LIMIT 4
""").show(max_width=200)
EOF

┌──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────┬───────┐
│        submitter         │                   name                    │ changes │ scvs  │
│         varchar          │                  varchar                  │  int64  │ int64 │
├──────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────┼───────┤
│ clinvar.submitter:505870 │ CeGaT Center for Human Genetics Tuebingen │     628 │   628 │
│ clinvar.submitter:3      │ OMIM                                      │     319 │    42 │
│ clinvar.submitter:26957  │ GeneDx                                    │      38 │    38 │
│ clinvar.submitter:61756  │ Ambry Genetics                            │      37 │    37 │
└──────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────┴───────┘

Read the counts with the records in hand. 284 of OMIM's 319 changes are between Pathogenic and Affects on the same 42 SCVs, which take a new version almost every week: SCV000024286 alternates between the two in its versions 137 to 156. To see one SCV's versions, select its rows: WHERE stable_id = 'SCV000024286'.

items.title: Conflicts appearing and resolving
items.text:
A VCV aggregate whose classification becomes, or stops being, Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity, per release:

python3 - <<'EOF'
import duckdb
con = duckdb.connect("clinvar-gkm-history.duckdb", read_only=True)
con.sql("""
  WITH s AS (
    SELECT *, lag(classification) OVER w AS before, lag(valid_to) OVER w AS before_to
    FROM history WHERE section = 'vcv' AND stable_id LIKE '%-G-PATH'
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY stable_id ORDER BY valid_from, key))
  SELECT valid_from AS release,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE classification = 'Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity') AS appeared,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE before = 'Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity') AS resolved
  FROM s WHERE before_to = valid_from AND classification IS DISTINCT FROM before
  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 5
""").show()
EOF

┌────────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│  release   │ appeared │ resolved │
│  varchar   │  int64   │  int64   │
├────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤
│ 2026-11-15 │       18 │        6 │
│ 2026-11-08 │      124 │       36 │
│ 2026-10-31 │      184 │       47 │
│ 2026-10-24 │        9 │        1 │
│ 2026-10-18 │       64 │       66 │
└────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘

From deltas only, a conflict is counted when the VCV's earlier version is in the history too; a history from a monthly counts every one.

items.title: Compare two releases
items.text:
When two points in time are enough, skip the history: extract the statements of two monthlies and join them on stable_id. extract writes one release's statements, with the same columns as the history less the two dates, to a Parquet file. The 1.1 line's first and last monthlies, 2026-06-27 and 2026-10-31:

for MONTH in 2026-07 2026-11; do
  P=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/index.json | python3 -c "
import json, sys
print(next(m['path'] for m in json.load(sys.stdin)['datasets']['monthly'] if m['release'] == '${MONTH}'))")
  curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${P}"
  python3 track-history.py extract "clinvar-gkm_${MONTH}.json.gz" "statements-${MONTH}.parquet"
done

python3 - <<'EOF'
import duckdb
duckdb.sql("""
  SELECT stable_id, a.classification AS before, b.classification AS after
  FROM 'statements-2026-07.parquet' a JOIN 'statements-2026-11.parquet' b USING (section, stable_id)
  WHERE section = 'vcv' AND stable_id LIKE '%-G-PATH' AND a.classification IS DISTINCT FROM b.classification
  ORDER BY stable_id LIMIT 10
""").show()
EOF

A FULL JOIN adds the statements present in only one release (new variants, and withdrawn ones). Each monthly is a 4.5 GB download read once; the extraction is estimated at about 10 minutes per monthly (see A complete history). Two monthlies of the same line compare only ClinVar's changes; a monthly of v1/1.1 and one of v1/1.2 compare schemas too (Scope).

How these recipes were tested

  • The deltas-only history was built from the 20 published deltas from 2026-07-06 to 2026-11-15 (the 1.1 line then the 1.2 line), in 3.5 minutes on an Apple M2 Pro laptop with the delta bundles already downloaded, and every query above was run on it; the output shown is that run's.
  • Every row of it still current at 2026-11-15 (3,596,191 rows) was compared with the 2026-11-15 weekly full: each key is in the full, with the same classification, review status and submitter.
  • extract and the comparison query were run on two deltas in place of the two monthlies.

items.title: Downloads
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM is distributed as monthly and weekly full bundles plus weekly deltas (JSON), with one typed Parquet dataset of the latest release built from the bundle, free from Cloudflare R2 — no authentication, no egress fees. The layout follows NCBI's ClinVar FTP site. New here? See How Releases Work. Releases of older lines (1.1.x, 1.0.1) are under Previous Releases below.

1.2.0 starts a new version line, v1/1.2/

1.2.0 publishes into a new line folder, v1/1.2/, which starts with one checkpoint monthly and adds deltas from there. The 1.1.x releases stay, unchanged, in the frozen line v1/1.1/ (monthlies, deltas and archive; its weekly fulls and Parquet set are removed at the freeze). Change v1/1.1/ to v1/1.2/ in your scripts, or read the current line from the root index.json. See Version Lines and the changelog.

Before you use or share the data

These files carry ClinVar data from NCBI. ClinVar's disclaimer applies: the data is not for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional. Attribute ClinVar as the data source, cite ClinVar-GKM, and carry the attribution and disclaimer with any copy you redistribute. The CC0 dedication covers ClinGen's transformation only. See Data Use and Citation.

items.title: Latest Release
items.text:
Monthly full or weekly full?

The official monthly reflects the last release of the previous month; the newest weekly full is the current week. Choose Your Data compares every option, and How Releases Work gives the schedule.

The interactive release table needs JavaScript. Without it, fetch the release index directly: <code>curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -m json.tool</code> — or grab the newest monthly and weekly fulls: <code>curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz</code> <code>curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz</code>

Browse history and archives: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files. Earlier release lines: Previous Releases.

items.title: Previous Releases
items.text:
These docs describe the current line, v1/1.2/. The release lines frozen before it are listed here; each keeps its official monthlies and weekly deltas, unchanged, at the paths they had. Their files are listed on Previous Releases.

The list of earlier lines needs JavaScript. Without it, read the root version manifest, which lists every line, its status and the path of its own index: <code>curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/index.json | python3 -m json.tool</code>

items.title: Directory Structure
items.text:
Each release line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/; the current line is v1/1.2/, and the root index.json lists every line. The full directory tree, and the stable 00-latest names, are on How Releases Work.

Dated files move to another folder, or are deleted, when a month or year ends; Month and Year Rollover says which and when. Look up a dated file's current path in the line's index.json rather than writing it into a script.

items.title: How the layout mirrors NCBI
items.text:
The bundles are built from ClinVar's XML releases, so the layout follows NCBI's ClinVar XML folder:

NCBI ClinVar XML ClinVar-GKM v1/1.2/ xml/ — monthly releases and ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz top level — official monthlies and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz xml/weekly_release/ — the current month's weekly releases and 00-latest_weekly weekly/ — the current month's weekly fulls and clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz xml/archive/YYYY/ — monthly releases of prior years archive/YYYY/ — monthlies of prior years .md5 sidecars .sha256 sidecars — deltas/ — weekly deltas (ClinVar-GKM only) — parquet/ — one derived Parquet dataset (ClinVar-GKM only)

Each ClinVar-GKM monthly clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM lines up with ClinVar's ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM, and each weekly full or delta with the ClinVar weekly release of the same date.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• HTTP 403. The CDN serves only the root index.json and paths under /v1/; a path allowlist answers every other path with 403, not 404. A 403 usually means a URL from before the current layout, such as a bucket-root datasets/… path. Look up the file's current path in the line's index.json.
  • HTTP 404 under /v1/. The file is not there: a weekly full deleted at month end, a delta moved to deltas/YYYY-MM/, or a monthly moved to archive/YYYY/. See When files move.
  • HTTP 429. Requests are rate-limited. Download whole files and query them locally rather than issuing many small range requests.

items.title: File Format
items.text: Each file is a gzip-compressed JSON object: schema_version first, then the bundle sections in a fixed order, each a keyed collection of records of one class (see Output Format). Each record is written on its own line as compact JSON (raw UTF-8) with its object keys sorted at every depth, and the lists whose order carries no meaning and is not stable in ClinVar's source (a condition's aliases) are written sorted, so a record that has not changed has the same bytes in every release. The order of records within a section is not fixed and differs between releases.

items.title: Count records in a full bundle
items.text:
A full bundle is about 4.9 GB compressed and 68.5 GB decompressed, too large to load whole, but each record is on its own line, so a script can stream it. This counts the records of each section of the newest monthly, clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (from Monthly Full Bundles), in about a minute and 20 MB of memory on a laptop. It needs only Python 3 and gunzip, which macOS and Linux include:

gunzip -c clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz | python3 -c "
import sys
counts = {}
for line in sys.stdin:
    if line.startswith('  \"') and line.rstrip().endswith('{'):  # a section opens
        section = line.split('\"')[1]
        counts[section] = 0
    elif line.startswith('    \"'):                            # one record
        counts[section] += 1
for section, n in counts.items():
    print(f'{section}: {n:,}')
"

items.title: Feedback
items.text:
This project is in active development and we welcome community feedback. If you encounter data quality issues, have questions about the output format, or want to suggest improvements:

  • Open an issue on GitHub
  • Include the release date and specific records involved

items.title: Examples
items.text:
What this page answers

What real ClinVar-GKM records look like, from one variant to a whole VCV hierarchy. Start with the annotated walk-through of one submission, then open the example file closest to what you need from the tables below.

Example files are maintained in the examples/ directory of the repository. These serve as reference targets for the data structures produced by the pipeline and are useful for early adopters and for validating output against expected formats.

items.title: File Format
items.text:
Each file is a bundle fragment: a small JSON object with the same shape as a published bundle, {"schema_version": "1.2.0", "<section>": {"<key>": record}, ...}. It holds the record the file is named for (the top record) exactly as the bundle has it, so its references are #/<section>/<key> pointers, plus the records those pointers lead to.

Every pointer is followed, except pointers into the scv and variation sections, which stay pointers:

Pointer kept What it names Where to see one #/scv/… A submission aggregated by a VCV or RCV statement The SCV examples below #/variation/… A proposition's subject The Cat-VRS examples below

Pointers into vcv and rcv are followed, so a VCV or RCV file holds its whole aggregation hierarchy: the top statement and every nested layer statement below it (such as …-G-PATH-CP, or …-S-SCI-CP and …-S-SCI-CP-T1), each with its proposition, evidence lines and condition or condition set. The hierarchy ends at the #/scv/ pointers of the lowest layer. An SCV file holds the statement, its proposition, submitter, condition or condition set (with its member conditions), and any evidence line and therapy. A Cat-VRS file holds the variation with its alleles, locations, sequence references and genes, so every pointer in it resolves.

Fragments, not closed bundles

Every file validates against the bundle schema, but not every #/… pointer resolves inside the file. A kept pointer names a record in the full bundle of the same release. A published bundle resolves every pointer; for a closed extract of a few statements, see Sub-Bundle Extraction.

The files are regenerated from a published full bundle by src/scripts/extract-example.py; the examples readme has the command.

items.title: Annotated Walk-Through
items.text:
One submission, read field by field: clinvar.submission:SCV008145211.1, a likely pathogenic classification of an RP1 deletion for RP1-related dominant retinopathy, from the 2026-11-15 weekly delta of the 1.2 line. The record below is the delta's scv record with its keys reordered for reading; two contributions entries, the classification's description extension and most of the description text are left out (marked /* … */). The numbered comments are callouts, not part of the data.

{
  "id": "clinvar.submission:SCV008145211.1",               // (1)
  "type": "Statement",
  "proposition": "#/propositionPathogenicity/SCV008145211-PATH",   // (2)
  "classification": {                                       // (3)
    "type": "MappableConcept",
    "conceptType": "Classification",
    "name": "Likely pathogenic",
    "primaryCoding": { "code": "likely pathogenic", "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015" },
    "extensions": [ /* … */ ]
  },
  "strength": {
    "type": "MappableConcept",
    "conceptType": "Strength",
    "name": "Likely",
    "primaryCoding": { "code": "likely", "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015" }
  },
  "direction": "supports",
  "quality": { "type": "MappableConcept", "conceptType": "Quality", "name": "criteria provided" },   // (4)
  "description": "Deletion in exon 4, within the dominant cluster, creating a premature stop codon. …",
  "contributions": [                                        // (5)
    {
      "type": "Contribution",
      "activityType": "evaluated",
      "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:510572",
      "date": "2026-10-19"
    },
    /* … */
  ],
  "specifiedBy": {                                          // (6)
    "type": "Method",
    "name": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015",
    "methodType": "clinical testing",
    "reportedIn": { "type": "Document", "pmid": "25741868", "urls": [ "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25741868" ] }
  },
  "reportedIn": [
    { "type": "Document", "pmid": "34721897", "urls": [ "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34721897" ] },
    { "type": "Document", "pmid": "42847597", "urls": [ "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42847597" ] }
  ],
  "extensions": [                                           // (7)
    { "name": "clinvarScvId", "value": "SCV008145211" },
    { "name": "clinvarScvVersion", "value": "1" },
    { "name": "submittedCondition", "value": {
        "id": "SCV008145211.0",
        "type": "Disease",
        "medgen_id": "CN322606",
        "xrefs": [ { "code": "MONDO:0800400", "system": "MONDO" } ],
        "mapping": { "type": "XRef", "ref": "mondo", "value": "0800400" },
        "normalized_resolution": "tm reftype xref mondo",
        "normalized_match": "clinvar.trait:66395",
        "condition": "clinvar.trait:66395"
    } },
    { "name": "clinvarScvReviewStatus", "value": "criteria provided, single submitter" },
    { "name": "submittedScvLocalKey", "value": "RP1-012|MONDO:MONDO:0800400" },
    { "name": "submissionLevel", "value": "CP" }
  ]
}

The proposition the statement points to, from the propositionPathogenicity section (the gene and inheritance qualifiers trimmed to their names):

{
  "id": "SCV008145211-PATH",
  "type": "VariantPathogenicityProposition",
  "subject": "#/variation/clinvar:5042631",                 // (8)
  "predicate": "isCausalFor",
  "object": "#/condition/clinvar.trait:66395",              // (9)
  "geneContextQualifier": { "name": "RP1", "conceptType": "gene", /* … */ },                       // (10)
  "modeOfInheritanceQualifier": { "name": "Autosomal dominant inheritance", "conceptType": "modeOfInheritance", /* … */ }
}
# Field What it tells you 1 id The SCV accession and its version (.1). 2 proposition A pointer to what is claimed. The section name, propositionPathogenicity, already says it is a germline pathogenicity claim. 3 classification The submitter's classification, coded in the guideline's terms. strength and direction restate it on the VA-Spec scale: Likely, supports. See Classifications. 4 quality The submission level: this submitter gave assertion criteria. The ClinVar review status is in the extensions (7). 5 contributions Who did what, when: the submitter evaluated the variant on 2026-10-19, and submitted and created the record on 2026-11-14. Each contributor points into submitter. 6 specifiedBy, reportedIn The method (ACMG 2015, with its own citation) and the papers the submitter cited. 7 extensions ClinVar facts with no GA4GH field. submittedCondition records the condition as submitted (a MONDO code) and how it was matched to ClinVar trait clinvar.trait:66395: see submitted condition. 8 subject The variant: ClinVar variation 5042631, NM_006269.2(RP1):c.2238_2239del (p.Lys746_Ser747insTer). Follow its members to the VRS allele; ID References does this in code. 9 object The condition, RP1-related dominant retinopathy, a record in condition with a MedGen coding (CN322606). 10 qualifiers The gene (RP1, NCBI Gene 6101) and the mode of inheritance (HPO HP:0000006). The gene qualifier's geneContextSource extension says the submitter's symbol matched.

Every field is described on SCV Statements, and Where a Value Comes From traces each back to ClinVar's XML.

items.title: Read it yourself
items.text:
Prerequisites

Python 3.9 or later (standard library only; tested with 3.14.5) and the 5 MB 2026-11-15 weekly delta, a 1.2.0 bundle. Its path changes when its month ends, so look it up in the line's index.json:

DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"] if d["release"] == "2026-11-15"))')
curl -fsO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"

Run from the folder you downloaded the delta to. It loads the delta, follows the statement's pointers and prints what each one leads to:

import gzip
import json

with gzip.open("clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz", "rt") as f:
    bundle = json.load(f)

def resolve(ref):
    """Resolve a #/section/key pointer to the record it names."""
    section, key = ref.removeprefix("#/").split("/", 1)
    return bundle[section][key]

scv = bundle["scv"]["clinvar.submission:SCV008145211.1"]
proposition = resolve(scv["proposition"])

print(scv["classification"]["name"], "|", scv["quality"]["name"])
print(proposition["type"], proposition["predicate"])
print(resolve(proposition["subject"])["name"])
print(resolve(proposition["object"])["name"])
print(resolve(scv["contributions"][0]["contributor"])["name"])

Likely pathogenic | criteria provided
VariantPathogenicityProposition isCausalFor
NM_006269.2(RP1):c.2238_2239del (p.Lys746_Ser747insTer)
RP1-related dominant retinopathy
Department of Ophthalmology, Seoul National University Bundang Hospital

Print json.dumps(scv, indent=2) to see the whole record.

items.title: Practice Guideline and Expert Panel Submissions
items.text:
PG (practice guideline) and EP (reviewed by expert panel) submissions are aggregated as separate top-tier submission levels. PG outranks EP in the Aggregate Contribution Layer winner-takes-all selection, followed by CP, NOCP, NOCL, and FLAG. VCV000007105.214-G-PATH shows a PG winner with EP, CP and NOCP non-contributing; VCV000007105.214-G-DR shows an EP-only aggregate.

See VCV Statements output reference for field documentation.
