items.title: Keep Your Data Current
items.text:
Links: Weekly Deltas · Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

ClinVar-GKM publishes a release every week. This page keeps a local copy at the newest release by applying each weekly delta, instead of downloading a 4.9 GB full bundle or a 4.6 GB Parquet set every week. It covers:

  • a bundle copy: every record of a full bundle in a DuckDB table, updated in place;
  • Parquet tables: the published tables, with each delta's rows merged in;
  • a custom dataset cut from either, re-cut after each update;
  • missed weeks, rollovers and line changes, and how to check a copy.

If you need the newest release only now and then, downloading it is simpler: the newest weekly full is weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (Weekly Full Bundles), and the published Parquet is always the newest release (Parquet Files). To rebuild a past week, see Rebuild a past week.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.9 or later (tested with 3.14.5) and the duckdb Python package (tested with 1.5.4), installed in Get the script.
  • uv, for the Parquet recipe only: it runs gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 as uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0.
  • curl, for the downloads in the shell examples. macOS and Linux both have it.
  • Disk and time. A bundle copy starts from a full bundle: a 4.9 GB download, and a DuckDB database of about 40 GB that takes about 15 minutes to load (estimated from the measured load of a 1.8-million-record delta; the full load was not run for this page). A Parquet copy starts from the published set: a 4.6 GB download, and up to 5 GB more while a week is merged. A weekly delta is 5 to 60 MB.
  • Run every command from one working directory: later blocks use the script and files earlier blocks leave there.

items.title: How a delta updates a copy
items.text:
A copy is current when it holds the records of one release. Applying a delta moves it to the next release. Both recipes on this page follow the same rules:

  1. Record the release, line and schema version of the copy. A bundle carries its schema_version but no release date. The release comes from index.json: a monthly's source_release, or a weekly full's or a delta's release. The recipes find a bundle's entry in index.json by its sha256.
  2. Resolve the line from the root index.json. Its current names the current line (v1/1.2). If the copy is on another line, stop: a new line starts from its own checkpoint monthly, and its deltas don't apply to the old line's records (Line changes).
  3. Take every delta of that line whose release is later than the copy's, oldest first, with each one's path from the line's index.json (deltas, plus archives.<year>.deltas after a year rollover). Never compose a path: a delta moves to deltas/YYYY-MM/ when its month ends.
  4. Check the chain. The first delta's baseline_release equals the copy's release, and each later delta's baseline_release equals the previous delta's release. Check each delta's schema_version against the copy's, and each download's sha256 against index.json.
  5. Apply each delta in one transaction: delete every key its manifest lists under sections.<section>.deleted, delete every key the delta bundle holds, insert the delta bundle's records, and record the delta's release as the copy's. Deleting the delta's own keys before inserting them is the upsert: an updated record replaces the old one.

A new ClinVar version is a new key. SCV, VCV and RCV keys carry the accession's version, so a new version shows as a delete of the old key and an add of the new one (clinvar.submission:SCV000024262.157 deleted, clinvar.submission:SCV000024262.158 added, in the 2026-11-15 delta). The rules above handle it like any other delete and add. Proposition keys carry no version.

items.title: Keep a bundle copy current
items.text: The copy is a DuckDB database, clinvar-gkm.duckdb, with a table records(section, key, json) holding each record's JSON text as published, and a table state holding the copy's last_release, line and schema_version. keep-current.py loads it and applies the deltas, by the rules above.

items.title: Get the script
items.text:
curl -fsSO https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/1.2/assets/scripts/keep-current.py
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install duckdb==1.5.4

The later blocks run python3 in this virtual environment. In a new shell, run . .venv/bin/activate again.

items.title: Start from a full bundle
items.text:
Download the newest monthly of the line and load it. init looks the file up in the line's index.json by its sha256, so it knows the release without a date in the file (a monthly is at its source_release), and refuses a file that isn't listed:

curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz
python3 keep-current.py init clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

On the 1.2 line today this loads the 2026-11 monthly, so the copy is at 2026-10-31 and prints loaded clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz: at release 2026-10-31, line v1/1.2, schema 1.2.0 (the name of the dated monthly with the same sha256). The newest weekly full (v1/1.2/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz) works too, and leaves fewer deltas to apply. init reads the file twice, for its sha256 and then its records, and doesn't need it afterwards.

items.title: Apply the new deltas
items.text:
Run update after init, and again whenever you want the copy current; each run applies every delta published since the last:

python3 keep-current.py update
python3 keep-current.py status

From the 2026-11 monthly, update applies the 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15 deltas. The 2026-11-15 one prints:

applied 2026-11-15: {'A': 16335, 'U': 22738, 'D': 8296}
at release 2026-11-15

A, U and D are the manifest's added, updated and deleted counts; status prints the state and the number of records. The deltas are downloaded into gkm-cache/ and kept, so a rerun after an interruption doesn't download them again; delete the folder when you no longer need them. The line, chain and schema checks run on every manifest before the first delta is applied. Each delta is applied in one transaction, after its download's sha256 is checked, so the copy is always at one release.

items.title: Query the copy
items.text:
The JSON text is queried with DuckDB's JSON functions. A variant's current germline VCV classification (continues from Get the script):

python3 - <<'EOF'
import duckdb
con = duckdb.connect("clinvar-gkm.duckdb", read_only=True)
con.sql("""
  SELECT key, json->>'$.classification.name' AS classification
  FROM records WHERE section = 'vcv' AND key LIKE 'VCV000183114.%-G-PATH'
""").show()
EOF

┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐
│          key           │     classification     │
│        varchar         │        varchar         │
├────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
│ VCV000183114.35-G-PATH │ Uncertain significance │
└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘

That is the copy at 2026-11-15. The key carries the VCV's version, so match the accession with LIKE, not the key. To query typed columns instead of JSON text, keep the Parquet tables current (below).

How the bundle recipe was tested

  • Seeded copy. A copy was seeded with the records of the 2026-11-08 delta (1,779,702 records) and its state set to 2026-11-08: a test seed, not a full bundle, so the test ran in seconds. update applied the 2026-11-15 delta in 1.2 s. The copy then held 1,815,952 records, each equal, key and text, to an independent replay of the two deltas in Python dictionaries.
  • Refusals. update refused a copy on the frozen v1/1.1 line, a copy whose schema_version is 1.1.0, and a copy at a release no delta builds on (a broken chain); init refused a file not listed in index.json.
  • Records sha256. verify computed the seeded copy's records sha256 as gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 did for a build of the same records (f59fae5f…), and the same hashing over the 2026-11-15 weekly full gave the published value; see Check your copy.
  • The bundle layout. The reader init and update use was run over the whole 2026-11-15 weekly full (91,973,603 records, the longest 0.5 MB) without an unexpected line.
  • Not run on a full bundle. The 15-minute and 40 GB figures for init are estimates from the seeded load (17.5 s and 664 MB for 1.8 million records; a full bundle holds about 92 million). The cost of update on a full copy was measured on a synthetic table of 92 million rows: the deletes and inserts of a delta the size of 2026-11-08's (1.7 million of each) took about 1 s, so reading the delta (17 s for 2026-11-08) is most of it.

items.title: Keep Parquet current
items.text:
The published Parquet set is built for one release, the newest, and replaced every week (Parquet Files). To keep your own tables current without downloading the 4.6 GB set every week, start from the published set once, then merge each week's delta into it.

Each of the 20 tables holds one row per bundle record, and its id column is the record's bundle key (the same text). There are no child or join tables: lists and nested objects are LIST and STRUCT columns of the record's row. So a delta's change to a record is a change to exactly one row of one table, and the merge works table by table, by id:

  1. Build the delta's tables with gkm-bundle-parquet (9 s for the 2026-11-15 delta), with the same tool version and bundle schema as the published set, so the columns match.
  2. For each table, keep every row of your table whose id is neither in the manifest's deleted list for that section nor in the delta's table, and add every row of the delta's table.
  3. Write the new tables to a new folder, then swap it in, with the release they are at.

keep-current.py does this (Get the script):

python3 keep-current.py parquet-init clinvar-gkm-tables
python3 keep-current.py parquet-update clinvar-gkm-tables

downloaded 20 tables at release 2026-11-15
up to date at 2026-11-15

parquet-init downloads the published tables, checks each file's sha256 against the published parquet/manifest.json, and writes clinvar-gkm-tables/keep-current.json with the release, line, schema version and table spec they are at. parquet-update applies every newer delta, by the rules in How a delta updates a copy, and keeps each delta and its built tables in gkm-cache/. Run right after parquet-init, it has nothing to do; run it after each weekly release. --only scv,submitter on parquet-init keeps only those tables, and the updates then merge only them.

Query the tables as you query the published ones (see Query with SQL):

python3 -c "import duckdb; duckdb.sql(\"SELECT count(*) FROM 'clinvar-gkm-tables/scv.parquet'\").show()"

What it guarantees. Each merged table has the rows a build of the full bundle at the new release would have, as long as the tables you started from were exact and every delta in the chain was applied. Tested on real tables: tables built from the 2026-11-08 delta, with the 2026-11-15 delta merged in, held the same rows, in all 20 tables, as tables built from the 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15 records replayed together, with no id twice.

What it doesn't. Nothing checks the merged set's content. The files are not the bytes the tool would write: the row order, row groups and compression differ, so their sha256 never matches the published files. They carry no manifest.json of the tool's, so gkm-bundle-parquet verify and rebuild don't apply to them. At the newest release, parquet-check compares each table's row count with the published manifest and checks that no id appears twice. That catches a missed or doubled delta, not a changed value:

python3 keep-current.py parquet-check clinvar-gkm-tables

20 of 20 tables match the published row counts

To start again from exact tables, delete the folder and run parquet-init again.

Measured runs

On an Apple M2 Pro laptop (16 GB of memory, 10 cores): parquet-init downloaded the 2026-11-15 set (20 files, 4.6 GB) in 60 s. Merging a delta into the full published tables takes about 3 minutes (193 s, 6.2 GB peak memory, measured by merging the 2026-11-15 delta into the 2026-11-15 tables, which also showed that re-applying a delta changes nothing: every table kept the same rows). The merged files are smaller than the published ones (2.5 GB), because DuckDB's default Parquet settings differ from the tool's.

items.title: Keep a custom dataset current
items.text:
To keep a subset current, such as one submitter's SCVs or one gene's variants, update the merged tables (or the bundle copy) first, then cut the subset from them again after each update. For example, every SCV of one submitter and the pathogenicity propositions they make, from the tables kept by Keep Parquet current:

python3 - <<'EOF'
import duckdb
duckdb.sql("""
  COPY (SELECT * FROM 'clinvar-gkm-tables/scv.parquet'
        WHERE list_contains([c.contributor FOR c IN contributions], 'clinvar.submitter:505870'))
    TO 'submitter-scv.parquet';
  COPY (SELECT p.* FROM 'clinvar-gkm-tables/propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p
        JOIN 'submitter-scv.parquet' s
          ON s.proposition_section = 'propositionPathogenicity' AND s.proposition = p.id)
    TO 'submitter-propositions.parquet';
""")
EOF

Don't cut the subset from each delta and add it to last week's. A delta isn't a small bundle of your subset:

  • It holds only the records that changed. A selection follows references, and from a delta most of them lead to records that didn't change and aren't there, so the walk stops: the one-submitter selection on Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles, run on the 2026-11-15 delta, reports 72 references to propositions the delta doesn't carry. When the seeded test above cut this submitter's SCVs from tables holding only the 2026-11-08 delta's records, it found 159,886 SCVs but 9,319 of their propositions: the SCVs changed that week, most of their propositions didn't.
  • It carries no deletes. A deleted or re-versioned record is only in the manifest, so the old record would stay in your subset.
  • Records leave a subset. An SCV reclassified from Pathogenic to Uncertain significance no longer matches a classification.name = 'Pathogenic' filter, so its new version is not selected and its old one is never removed.

Cutting from complete, current tables has none of these problems, and takes seconds.

items.title: Missed weeks, rollovers and line changes
Missed weeks
items.text: Nothing to do: update and parquet-update apply every delta after the copy's release, in order, however many there are. Deltas are kept on the host for good (How Releases Work), so a copy can always catch up on its line. If the chain check fails, a delta is missing or the copy's release is wrong; start again from a full bundle or the published tables.

items.title: Month and year rollovers
items.text: At a month's first release its deltas move from deltas/ to deltas/YYYY-MM/, and at a year's first release the year's monthlies and deltas move to archive/YYYY/ (see Month and Year Rollover on How Releases Work). The file names and bytes don't change. Read every path from index.json (deltas and archives.<year>.deltas), as keep-current.py does, and a rollover changes nothing for a copy.

items.title: Line changes
items.text:
Deltas apply only to a copy of the same line. The 1.2 line's first delta (2026-11-08) has baseline_release 2026-10-31, the last release of the frozen 1.1 line, so a 1.1 copy at 2026-10-31 passes a chain check on dates alone; applying 1.2 deltas to it would mix 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 records. keep-current.py refuses:

refused: the copy is on v1/1.1 (frozen, superseded by v1/1.2); the current line is v1/1.2. Its deltas don't apply to this copy: start a new one on v1/1.2

Start a new copy on the new line: init from its checkpoint monthly (the line's first monthly; the checkpoint_full of its deltas' manifests), or parquet-init for tables. A copy also stops when a delta's schema_version differs from the copy's. See Version Lines on How Releases Work.

items.title: Check your copy
items.text:
The published Parquet's manifest.json gives records_sha256: a sha256 over every record of the bundle it was built from, in a canonical form (the definition is in gkm-bundle-parquet's round-trip.md). The published Parquet is the newest release, so when your bundle copy is at that release, its records sha256 must equal the published one:

python3 keep-current.py verify

It prints match or DIFFERENT, with both values, and exits 1 on a difference. It refuses a copy that isn't at the newest release; check it after the next update. A difference means the copy isn't the published state: start again from a full bundle.

verify hashes every record on every CPU. This hashing was tested at full size on the 2026-11-15 weekly full, streamed from the host instead of loaded into a copy: over its 91,973,603 records it gave d0d9dbf6abdad07582f88b4014eecd5f1350d9cbcd6b0dd47de5135e2eb0a859, the published Parquet's records_sha256, in 16 minutes including the download. On the seeded copy, which holds only two deltas' records, verify took 33 s and reported DIFFERENT, as it should.

items.title: Monthly Full Bundles
items.text:
Links: Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

Older release lines (1.1.x, 1.0.1) are on Previous Releases.

The official monthly full bundle is a gzip-compressed JSON file containing every variation, statement, proposition, condition, and supporting reference record for a release. It lines up with ClinVar's monthly ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM: clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM is built from the newest weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut, and the line's index.json names that release as the monthly's source_release. For example, the 2026-11 monthly has source_release 2026-10-31.

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz is a stable URL for the newest monthly. Monthlies are kept for good: at the end of each year they move to archive/YYYY/ (Directory Structure, Month and Year Rollover). Monthlies and deltas are the durable record: every past week can be rebuilt from them (Rebuild a past week).

The 1.2 line starts with one checkpoint monthly, the first 1.2.0 full (2026-11), and adds a monthly for every ClinVar monthly after it. The monthlies before it (2026-07 to 2026-10, schema 1.1.0) stay in the frozen line v1/1.1/, unchanged; see Version Lines.

Prerequisites

  • The curl recipe needs curl, and sha256sum (Linux, recent macOS) or shasum -a 256 (any macOS) to check the download.
  • The Python recipe uses Python 3 and only the standard library (tested with 3.14). New to Python? Install it from python.org/downloads or your OS package manager.
  • Disk. A monthly full is about 4.9 GB compressed and 68.5 GB decompressed; each recipe shows two downloads of the same bytes (the stable URL and the dated one), so run the one you need. Read it streamed (gunzip -c) rather than decompressing it to disk; see Count records in a full bundle.
Download a monthly full with curl 
# Newest official monthly full (stable URL)
curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

# Or a specific month of the current year, with its checksum
curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz
curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz.sha256
sha256sum -c clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz.sha256      # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c

# Decompress, only if you need the plain file: it is 68.5 GB, and gunzip -c streams it instead
gunzip clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz
Download a monthly full with Python 
import urllib.request

BASE = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2"

# Download the newest official monthly full bundle
urllib.request.urlretrieve(
    f"{BASE}/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz",
    "clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz"
)

# Download a specific monthly of the current year
urllib.request.urlretrieve(
    f"{BASE}/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz",
    "clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz"
)

# A prior year's monthly is under archive/YYYY/. 2026's monthlies move there when the first
# release of 2027 is published; from then on, 2026-11 is at
#     f"{BASE}/archive/2026/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz"

Validate a downloaded bundle

Every JSON bundle conforms to the ClinVar-GKM bundle schema (JSON Schema Draft 2020-12) — the same schema covers the monthly full, weekly deltas, and sub-bundle extracts. Every published bundle passes strict validation against it before release; see Release Validation. The GKM Toolkit validates a downloaded bundle the same way, given the ClinVar-GKM schemas; see Validate a bundle.

items.title: Parquet Files
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · How Releases Work

Older release lines (1.1.x, 1.0.1) are on Previous Releases.

Want to query the files, not just download them?

This page covers where the Parquet files live and how to keep a set current. Query the Data teaches querying them: a live in-browser console, every table's columns, how the tables join, and runnable recipes.

Parquet is derived from the bundle and overwritten every release

The JSON bundles are the release record. Parquet is a convenience: the tables hold the bundle's records, and the bundle can be rebuilt from them. One Parquet dataset is published per release line, rebuilt every release (weekly) from the newest weekly release and overwritten in place. There are no dated, per-delta or archived Parquet sets.

The 1.1 tables were removed when the 1.1 line was frozen

The 1.1 line's set, at v1/1.1/parquet/ (22 tables exported from BigQuery for the 2026-10-24 release), was deleted on 2026-11-23, when v1/1.1/ was frozen: a frozen line keeps its bundles and no Parquet. To get tables for a 1.1 release, build them from its bundle; see Parquet for Previous Releases. The 1.1 tables had different columns; see Moving from the 1.1 Tables.

This page describes the 1.2 line's set, at v1/1.2/parquet/: the 20 tables that gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0 builds from each 1.2 release's bundle. Parquet is built only from the bundle, never from BigQuery.

The dataset lives at one stable path, v1/1.2/parquet/, one file per section, with a manifest.json and a table-spec.json beside it:

v1/1.2/parquet/
  {section}.parquet      20 files, one per bundle section
  manifest.json          build date, source release and dataset, builder, schema version, each file's size, rows and sha256,
                         the records sha256 the tables rebuild to, and the ClinVar source, attribution, disclaimer and license scope
  table-spec.json        the table spec: every table's columns, how each maps to the bundle, and the foreign keys

The manifest also carries the data's provenance: source (ClinVar at NCBI, its data use policy and a citation), attribution, disclaimer and license (CC0 scope), matching Data Use and Citation. The manifest names the release the dataset was built from, so check it before comparing results with a bundle (the index's Parquet entry carries the same source_release). For an earlier state, see Earlier releases.

items.title: Available Parquet files
items.text:
Each Parquet file holds one bundle section, one row per record. Every table has an id column, and every field of the record has a typed column named after it, so filtering and aggregation need no JSON parsing. The tables are generated from the bundle's JSON Schema, with no hand-chosen columns. The column reference lists every column of every section.

Available Parquet files (20 sections):

File Description sequenceReference.parquet NCBI RefSeq sequence references location.parquet VRS SequenceLocation records allele.parquet VRS Allele records copyNumberCount.parquet VRS CopyNumberCount records copyNumberChange.parquet VRS CopyNumberChange records gene.parquet Gene records (MappableConcept with NCBI Gene / HGNC codings) variation.parquet CategoricalVariant records (Cat-VRS) condition.parquet Condition records (traits) conditionSet.parquet ConditionSet records (trait sets) therapy.parquet Therapy records (drug therapies, content-addressed) therapyGroup.parquet TherapyGroup records (combination therapies) submitter.parquet Submitter organization records propositionPathogenicity.parquet Pathogenicity propositions propositionOncogenicity.parquet Oncogenicity propositions propositionSomaticClinicalImpact.parquet Somatic clinical impact propositions (ClinicalSignificance, and the Diagnostic, Prognostic and TherapeuticResponse targets of SCI evidence lines) propositionClinvarCustom.parquet ClinVar custom propositions (the Clinvar* types) evidenceLine.parquet Evidence line records of SCV, VCV and RCV statements scv.parquet SCV statement records vcv.parquet VCV aggregate statement records rcv.parquet RCV aggregate statement records

items.title: Working with Parquet Files
items.text:
Download the Parquet files you need, then query them locally. The R2 hosting has rate limits and is designed for file downloads, not as a remote query endpoint for tools like DuckDB.

Prerequisites

  • DuckDB CLI for the shell and SQL examples (tested with 1.5.4): brew install duckdb on macOS, or see the install page.
  • Python 3 with pandas and pyarrow (pip install pandas pyarrow; tested with Python 3.14, pandas 3.1.1, pyarrow 26.0.1), plus the duckdb package for the DuckDB-from-Python example (pip install duckdb).
  • The Parquet files, from Download below: the full set is about 4.6 GB (scv.parquet alone is about 0.8 GB). Run every query from the folder that holds them: the queries read the files by name, such as 'scv.parquet'.

items.title: Download
items.text:
Download individual sections or all files at once:

Download sections with curl 
# The one published Parquet dataset, overwritten every release; manifest.json names its release.
BASE="https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet"
mkdir -p clinvar-gkm-parquet && cd clinvar-gkm-parquet
curl -fO "${BASE}/manifest.json"
curl -fO "${BASE}/table-spec.json"

# Download specific sections
curl -fO "${BASE}/scv.parquet"
curl -fO "${BASE}/propositionPathogenicity.parquet"
curl -fO "${BASE}/condition.parquet"

# Or download all 20 sections
for section in sequenceReference location allele copyNumberCount copyNumberChange \
               gene variation condition conditionSet therapy therapyGroup submitter \
               propositionPathogenicity propositionOncogenicity propositionSomaticClinicalImpact propositionClinvarCustom \
               evidenceLine scv vcv rcv; do
  curl -fO "${BASE}/${section}.parquet"
done

items.title: Query
items.text:
DuckDB is the fastest way to explore Parquet files — it queries them directly with no data loading step. pandas + pyarrow works well when you want DataFrames.

Query with DuckDB / pandas 
# Install DuckDB
brew install duckdb   # macOS
# or: pip install duckdb

# Query SCV statements
duckdb -c "
  SELECT id, classification.name AS classification, direction, strength.name AS strength, quality.name AS quality
  FROM 'scv.parquet'
  WHERE classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
  LIMIT 10;
"

# Count classifications across all SCVs
duckdb -c "
  SELECT classification.name AS classification, direction, COUNT(*) as n
  FROM 'scv.parquet'
  GROUP BY classification.name, direction
  ORDER BY n DESC;
"

# Join SCVs with propositions to find pathogenic variants for a specific condition
duckdb -c "
  SELECT s.id, s.classification.name AS classification, p.predicate, p.object
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition = p.id
  WHERE s.classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
    AND p.object = 'clinvar.trait:9580'
  LIMIT 10;
"

# Inspect the schema of any section
duckdb -c "DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM 'scv.parquet';"

DuckDB also works from Python:

import duckdb

df = duckdb.sql("""
    SELECT id, classification.name AS classification, direction, strength.name AS strength, quality.name AS quality
    FROM 'scv.parquet'
    WHERE classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
    LIMIT 100
""").df()

print(df)

With pandas / pyarrow:

import pandas as pd

# Load only the columns you need: a dotted path reads one field of a struct
scv = pd.read_parquet("scv.parquet", columns=["id", "classification.name", "proposition"])

# The struct field comes back named by its last segment
pathogenic = scv[scv["name"] == "Pathogenic"]
print(f"{len(pathogenic)} pathogenic SCVs")
print(pathogenic.iloc[0]["proposition"])

items.title: Column Reference
items.text:
The complete per-table reference — every column, type and description for all 20 sections — is in Query the Data → The 20 Tables. A summary:

Statement sections (scv, vcv, rcv) share a common set of typed columns:

Column Type Description id string Statement identifier type string Statement type proposition string The proposition's id proposition_section string The table that holds it: propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact or propositionClinvarCustom; read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true) covers all four classification struct (MappableConcept) Use classification.name (or classification.primaryCoding.code) — e.g., "Pathogenic" strength struct (MappableConcept) Use strength.name — e.g., "Definitive", "Likely" direction string Evidence direction ("supports", "disputes", "neutral") quality struct (MappableConcept) Use quality.name — submission or aggregate level, e.g., "criteria provided" hasEvidenceLines list\<string> Ids of the statement's evidence lines, all in evidenceLine extensions list\<struct> Named ClinVar attributes, each value in the value_<kind> field for its kind (e.g. value_string)

SCV statements include additional columns: description, contributions, reportedIn and specifiedBy. reportedIn is a list of citation Documents, one per ClinVar citation, and specifiedBy.reportedIn is the assertion method's Document; see scv.

The four proposition tables share id, type, subject, predicate, object, object_section and geneContextQualifier, and add the qualifiers their types allow (modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier, conditionQualifier), so read them together with union_by_name = true. See Gene context for what the gene context is (one representative gene per variant, not a submitter-asserted gene), and The columns for each column.

Run DESCRIBE in DuckDB to see the full schema for any section.

For how the sections join — including the columns that point at more than one table, where a single-table join silently drops rows — see Joining Tables; for task-oriented queries, see Recipes.

Example cross-section queries (SQL)

Run these in the duckdb shell (or as duckdb -c "…") from the folder that holds the files; they read scv.parquet, propositionPathogenicity.parquet, condition.parquet and submitter.parquet.

All SCVs for a gene — detailed view:

-- SCVs for BRCA1: classification, review status, condition
SELECT
    s.id AS scv_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.direction,
    s.strength.name AS strength,
    s.quality.name AS review_status,
    p.geneContextQualifier.name AS gene,
    c.name AS condition_name,
    c.primaryCoding.code AS condition_code
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition = p.id
LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c
       ON c.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition' THEN p.object END
WHERE p.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code = '672'    -- BRCA1 (NCBI Gene 672)
ORDER BY s.classification.name;

Classification summary for a gene:

-- Count SCVs by classification and review status for BRCA2
SELECT
    p.geneContextQualifier.name AS gene,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.quality.name AS review_status,
    s.direction,
    COUNT(*) AS scv_count
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition = p.id
WHERE p.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code = '675'    -- BRCA2
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scv_count DESC;

Restrict to submissions with criteria provided:

-- Only expert panel and criteria-provided SCVs for a gene
SELECT
    s.id AS scv_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.quality.name AS review_status,
    c.name AS condition_name
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition = p.id
LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c
       ON c.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition' THEN p.object END
WHERE p.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code = '7157'   -- TP53
  AND s.quality.name IN ('criteria provided', 'expert panel')
ORDER BY s.classification.name;

Cross-gene comparison — classification breakdown for multiple genes:

-- Compare pathogenicity classification distributions across genes
SELECT
    p.geneContextQualifier.name AS gene,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    COUNT(*) AS n
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition = p.id
WHERE p.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code IN ('672', '675', '7157', '4292')   -- BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, MLH1
  AND s.quality.name = 'criteria provided'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY gene, n DESC;

The gene filters use the NCBI Gene number in geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code, not the symbol in .name: a few SCVs carry a submitted symbol there with no normalized gene (see Gene context).

Submitter names and assertion methods are typed columns too: join submitter on the contributor id, and read specifiedBy.name:

-- SCVs with submitter name and assertion method
SELECT
    s.id AS scv_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    p.geneContextQualifier.name AS gene,
    sub.name AS submitter,
    s.specifiedBy.name AS method
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition = p.id
LEFT JOIN 'submitter.parquet' sub
       ON sub.id = [c.contributor FOR c IN s.contributions IF c.activityType = 'submitted'][1]
WHERE p.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code = '672'    -- BRCA1
  AND s.classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
  AND s.quality.name = 'expert panel'
LIMIT 20;

To get whole records back as JSON, use to_json() on a row, or rebuild the bundle from the tables with gkm-bundle-parquet rebuild; see The whole record.

items.title: Earlier releases
items.text:
Only the current Parquet dataset of each live line is published; it is overwritten every release, and weekly deltas, archives and frozen lines carry no Parquet. To work with an earlier state:

  • Build it from the bundles. Every official monthly stays published (in archive/YYYY/ after its year ends) with a .sha256 sidecar, and so does every delta. Rebuild the bundle for the week you need with the replay recipe, then build its tables with gkm-bundle-parquet (on PyPI), the tool that builds the published set. A full build needs a large machine; see Build Your Own. The columns come from the bundle's own schema version, so a bundle of schema 1.1.0 gives a wider set of tables than the 1.2.0 tables described here, unless you build it with ClinVar-GKM's 1.1.0 column set; see Parquet for Previous Releases.
  • Take only what you need. gkm-bundle-parquet select cuts a mini-bundle (one variant, gene or submitter and everything it refers to) from any published bundle, without a large machine.
  • The 1.0.1 generation is the frozen line v1/1.0/: its bundles and delta manifests, with no Parquet. Its bundles can't be built into tables; build from the v1/1.1/ bundle of the same release (why).

Parquet downloaded from an earlier release keeps its old tables and columns; see the changelog for what changed, and Moving from the 1.1 Tables for the 1.1 tables.

items.title: Previous Releases
items.text:
Links: Downloads · Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · How Releases Work

Each release line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/. When a new MINOR or MAJOR release starts a new line, the line it replaces is frozen: nothing in it changes again, and it is kept indefinitely. This page lists the frozen lines released before the line these docs describe, newest first, with their official monthly full bundles and their weekly deltas: in the latest docs, every frozen line. The other Get the Data pages describe this docs version's own line.

  • What a frozen line keeps: its official monthlies, the 00-latest copy of the newest one, its archive/YYYY/ folders and every weekly delta with its manifest, all at the paths they had when the line was current, with the same bytes and .sha256 sidecars. It gains a MANIFEST.json (every file's size and sha256) and a README.txt.
  • What a frozen line drops: its weekly full bundles and its Parquet set, deleted at the freeze. Any past week is rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas (Rebuild a past week), and Parquet is rebuilt from a monthly bundle with gkm-bundle-parquet.
  • Parquet for a frozen line: Parquet for Previous Releases gives the commands and the column set.
  • Which schema it uses: each line's bundles validate against that line's schema version, shown below. The changelog lists the changes between versions.

To keep reading one line, read releases only from its own index.json; see Finding and pinning a version. The docs that describe a line are in the version selector in the header: the 1.1 docs describe v1/1.1/, and their copy of this page lists the lines before 1.1.

Before you use or share the data

The data use terms and the ClinVar disclaimer apply to every line; see Data Use and Citation.

items.title: Frozen Lines
items.text:
The list is read from the root index.json, so a line appears here as soon as it is frozen. It shows only lines older than the one these docs describe.

The list of frozen lines needs JavaScript. Without it, read the root version manifest, which lists every line, its status and the path of its own index: <code>curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/index.json | python3 -m json.tool</code> — then a frozen line's index and plain-text guide, for example: <code>curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/index.json | python3 -m json.tool</code> <code>curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.0/README.txt</code>

items.title: How Releases Work
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files · Previous Releases

ClinVar-GKM releases are hosted on Cloudflare R2 object storage. All downloads are free with no authentication required and no egress fees. The layout follows NCBI's ClinVar XML folder, with monthlies at the top, weekly/ and archive/YYYY/; see Directory Structure below and How the layout mirrors NCBI.

This page is the reference for the release schedule, the directory layout and when files move. To decide which files to download, see Choose Your Data.

Distribution follows a full + delta model:

  • An official monthly full bundle — a gzip-compressed JSON file — is published once a month, lined up with ClinVar's monthly release. It contains every variation, statement, proposition, condition, and supporting reference record.
  • A weekly full bundle is published for every ClinVar weekly release, and kept for the current month only.
  • A weekly delta is published for every ClinVar weekly release. Each delta carries only the records that were added or updated since the prior release, in the same section structure as the full bundle, alongside a manifest that lists per-section adds, updates, and deletes.

The monthlies and the deltas are the durable record. A consumer that wants the state at any week takes a monthly full and replays the deltas after it; see Rebuild a past week and the manifest field reference.

The official monthly is a month-start baseline, not the current week

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz reflects the last release of the previous month — e.g. the 2026-10 monthly is built from the 2026-09-28 release, the last one before ClinVar's October monthly cut. For the current week, use the newest weekly full, or replay the deltas onto the monthly.

items.title: Release Cadence
items.text:
A weekly release is published for every ClinVar XML release, typically within 1-2 days of it. It writes the weekly full weekly/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, refreshes weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz, and writes the delta deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz with its manifest. All paths are under the line folder, v1/1.2/.

An official monthly full is published once a month, lined up with ClinVar's monthly VCV release. When ClinVar posts ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM.xml.gz at its XML index (early in month YYYY-MM), our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full is built from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut datetime — so e.g. the 2026-07 monthly comes from the 2026-06-27 release. That release is published as the monthly's source_release in index.json. The upload writes clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz and refreshes the clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz pointer. Each delta manifest's checkpoint_full names the official monthly that precedes the delta.

Every bundle has a .sha256 checksum sidecar. From 1.1.0, a monthly or delta file is never rewritten; see the exceptions below.

items.title: Directory Structure
items.text:
The root index.json is a thin version manifest that lists the release lines and points to each line's index. Each line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/; the current line is 1.2, served under v1/1.2/, with its release index at v1/1.2/index.json.

index.json                                    version manifest (each line -> its index)
v1/
  1.2/                                        current line
    index.json                                release index for the line
    feed.xml                                  Atom feed of the line's releases
    README.txt                                plain-text guide to the line
    clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz             newest official monthly full (stable URL)
    clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz               official monthly fulls, current year
    weekly/
      clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz    newest weekly full (stable URL)
      clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz           weekly fulls, CURRENT MONTH ONLY
    deltas/
      clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz     current month's weekly deltas
      clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json
      YYYY-MM/                                earlier months of the current year
    archive/
      YYYY/
        clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz           monthly fulls from prior years
        deltas/YYYY-MM/                       deltas from prior years
    parquet/
      {section}.parquet                       ONE Parquet dataset, the latest (built from the bundle; overwritten every release)
      manifest.json                           build date, source release, builder, per-file sha256
      table-spec.json                         every table's columns, types and derivations
  1.1/                                        frozen line: the 1.1.x releases (monthlies, deltas, MANIFEST.json; no weekly fulls, no Parquet)
  1.0/                                        frozen line: the 1.0.1 generation (bundles, delta manifests, MANIFEST.json; no Parquet)

Every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar (sha256sum -c format), like NCBI's .md5 files. The 00- prefix of the stable names sorts them before the dated files in a directory listing, as in NCBI's ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz. Scripts that need a dated file should look up its current path in the line's index.json, because dated files move at month and year ends (below).

items.title: Month and Year Rollover
items.text:
When What happens The first release of a new month is published The finished month's deltas move from deltas/ into deltas/YYYY-MM/. The finished month's weekly fulls are deleted, as NCBI deletes its weekly releases, except the newest: it is kept until the new month's official monthly is published (the monthly is normally a copy of it), then deleted. The first release of a new year is published The finished year's monthlies move into archive/YYYY/, and its delta folders into archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/.

A move changes a file's folder, never its bytes, name or checksum. Deleting the weekly fulls is the one deliberate exception to "published bundles are never removed": every deleted week can be rebuilt exactly from a monthly plus deltas (Rebuild a past week).

items.title: Parquet
items.text: Parquet is derived from the bundle. One Parquet dataset is published, at v1/1.2/parquet/, rebuilt from the newest weekly release and overwritten every release. Its manifest.json gives the build date, the release and dataset it was built from, the builder, the schema version, and every file's size and sha256. No Parquet is kept per month, per delta, in archive/ or in frozen lines. Past Parquet is rebuilt from the monthly bundles with gkm-bundle-parquet (PyPI), the separate tool that builds the published set; see Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles. See Parquet Files.

items.title: Version Lines
items.text:
Each version line has its own folder: v1/1.2/ for 1.2.x. A PATCH release (1.2.x) only adds new dated files to v1/1.2/. A new MINOR — including a content-only correction that must rewrite published bundles — starts v1/1.3/, and a new MAJOR starts v2/2.0/.

A new line starts with one checkpoint monthly: the first full built with the new schema, published as the official monthly of the ClinVar monthly it is the source of (ADR 0002). Its deltas run forward from it; the first delta's baseline_release is the checkpoint's source_release. Earlier releases are not republished into the new line. 1.2.0 started v1/1.2/ this way.

The line it replaces is frozen and kept indefinitely: its monthlies, 00-latest copy, deltas and archive stay unchanged at their paths, and it gains a MANIFEST.json (every file's size and sha256) and a README.txt. Its weekly fulls and its Parquet set are deleted at the freeze, because neither is a record: any week is rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas, and Parquet is rebuilt from a bundle. v1/1.1/ (schema 1.1.0, the 1.1.x releases) is frozen with superseded_by: "v1/1.2"; the 1.0.1 generation is the frozen line v1/1.0/, with bundles and delta manifests only. The root index.json lists every line and its status; Previous Releases lists the frozen lines and their files, and Versioning & Releases explains the version numbers.

items.title: Weekly Deltas
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

Older release lines (1.1.x, 1.0.1) are on Previous Releases.

The list groups deltas by year, newest first: the current year is open, and each earlier year is a collapsible list under Archived years.

A weekly delta is published for every ClinVar release. Each delta is a bundle, its .sha256 checksum and its manifest. The current month's deltas sit directly in v1/1.2/deltas/; earlier months of the year are in deltas/YYYY-MM/, and prior years in archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/:

v1/1.2/deltas/
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1108.json.gz             added + updated records (same section structure as the full bundle)
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1108.json.gz.sha256
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1108.manifest.json       per-section adds, updates, and deletes for this release
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz.sha256
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.manifest.json

That is the 1.2 line in November 2026. When December's first release is published, November's deltas move to v1/1.2/deltas/2026-11/. The frozen 1.1 line shows the finished-month layout, for example v1/1.1/deltas/2026-09/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-0928.json.gz.

A delta's folder changes when its month or year rolls over; its file name and bytes do not. The line's index.json lists every delta with its current bundle.path and manifest path, so look paths up there rather than composing them. Deltas carry no Parquet: Parquet is derived and published only for the latest release (Parquet Files).

Prerequisites

  • curl and sha256sum (Linux, recent macOS) or shasum -a 256 (any macOS), for the shell example.
  • Python 3, standard library only (tested with 3.14), for the Python examples.
  • A delta is a few MB to about 60 MB. Rebuilding a past week also downloads a monthly full (4.9 GB compressed, 68.5 GB decompressed), which replay-bundle.py streams.
Download a weekly delta with curl / Python 
# The newest delta, its checksum and its manifest. index.json lists every delta with its current path
# (a delta moves to its month's folder when the month ends); pick another by its "release" date.
HOST="https://data.clinvar-gkm.org"
read -r BUNDLE MANIFEST <<< "$(curl -fsS "${HOST}/v1/1.2/index.json" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
d = max(json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"], key=lambda d: d["release"])
print(d["bundle"]["path"], d["manifest"])')"
curl -fO "${HOST}/${BUNDLE}"
curl -fO "${HOST}/${BUNDLE}.sha256"
curl -fO "${HOST}/${MANIFEST}"
sha256sum -c "$(basename "${BUNDLE}").sha256"   # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c

import json
import urllib.request

BASE = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org"

# The newest delta, from the line's release index
index = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{BASE}/v1/1.2/index.json"))
newest = max(index["deltas"], key=lambda d: d["release"])
for path in (newest["bundle"]["path"], newest["manifest"]):
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{BASE}/{path}", path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])

items.title: Delta Bundle
items.text: The delta bundle has the same shape as the monthly full — a single JSON object with bundle sections at the root, each a keyed collection of objects. The difference is content: a delta contains only the records added or updated since its baseline release. Sections with no additions or updates are absent from the delta bundle. Deleted records are not present in the bundle — they are listed only in the manifest.

items.title: The delta manifest
items.text:
Each delta's manifest, clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json, describes exactly what changed and which monthly full the delta chain starts from:

{
  "release": "2026-11-15",
  "baseline_release": "2026-11-08",
  "compare_release": "2026-11-15",
  "pipeline_version": "1.2.0",
  "checkpoint_full": {
    "path": "v1/1.2/clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz",
    "release": "2026-10-31",
    "month": "2026-11",
    "sha256": "157ef338d1948cce…"
  },
  "sections": {
    "allele": { "added": 230,  "updated": 0,     "deleted": ["ga4gh:VA.zZ9dcuDMYuDkSzBwy7rLMI0R1zvZalla", "…"] },
    "scv":    { "added": 1023, "updated": 16539, "deleted": ["clinvar.submission:SCV007600890.1", "…"] },
    "vcv":    { "added": 2937, "updated": 4,     "deleted": ["VCV000183114.34-G-PATH", "…"] },
    "…": {}
  },
  "counts": { "A": 16335, "U": 22738, "D": 8296 },
  "schema_version": "1.2.0",
  "bundle": {
    "name": "clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz",
    "path": "v1/1.2/deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz",
    "size": 5355360,
    "sha256": "b370d3857ffd709b…"
  },
  "sha256": "b370d3857ffd709b…"
}

That is the 2026-11-15 manifest, cut to three of its 14 sections and the first key of each deleted list.

Field Description release The ClinVar release date this delta represents baseline_release The prior release this delta was diffed against — null only on the very first release compare_release The release the changes are computed to (equals release) pipeline_version The pipeline build stamp that produced the delta (git describe of the pipeline code) checkpoint_full The official monthly this delta's chain replays onto — the newest monthly whose source_release is on or before this delta's baseline_release — as {path, release, month, sha256}. release is that monthly's source_release (a YYYY-MM-DD release date, comparable with baseline_release), month is its YYYY-MM label, and sha256 is its checksum. path is where the monthly was when the delta was published; after a year rollover, find it in index.json by month. Every line starts with a monthly, so a delta always has one (the first delta of a line is refused unless its baseline_release is that monthly's source_release) sections Per-section change summary — added and updated counts plus a deleted list of primary keys counts Roll-up totals across all sections — A (added), U (updated), D (deleted) schema_version The delta bundle's own schema_version bundle The delta bundle as published: {name, path, size, sha256}. path is its folder at publish time; after a month rollover, find its current path in index.json sha256 The delta bundle's sha256 (the same value as bundle.sha256 and the .sha256 sidecar)

Deletes live only in the manifest. For each section, deleted is the list of keys that must be removed; the delta bundle itself carries only the added and updated records.

A new ClinVar version is a new key. SCV, VCV and RCV keys carry the ClinVar accession's version (clinvar.submission:SCV000024262.157, VCV000183114.34-G-PATH). When ClinVar bumps the version, the record's key changes, so the delta shows a delete of the old key and an add of the new one, not an update. In the 2026-11-15 delta, clinvar.submission:SCV000024262.157 is in the scv deleted list and clinvar.submission:SCV000024262.158 is a record of the bundle; 108 of the 128 deleted SCV keys, 2,394 of the 2,416 VCV keys and 1,224 of the 1,254 RCV keys come back under the same accession with a new version. A change that keeps the version is an update under the same key. To follow one accession across releases, match on the accession without its version, not on the key.

Don't check a replay by the manifest's counts. A section's added + updated can be larger than the number of records in the delta bundle. In the 2026-11-15 delta, conditionSet has added 149 and the bundle holds 138 records: condition sets with a single member are left out when the bundle is written. Every other section of that delta matches. Check a replay by comparing records, or against a published weekly full, not by counts.

items.title: Consumer Replay Model
items.text:
A monthly full plus the deltas after it rebuild the state at any weekly release. Every official monthly has a source_release in index.json: the weekly release it was built from (in the frozen v1/1.1/ line, the 2026-10 monthly has source_release 2026-09-28). Each delta records the release it was diffed against (baseline_release) and the release it brings you to (release).

For each delta, apply the manifest's deletes first, then upsert every record present in the delta bundle, section by section. To keep a local copy (a database of the records, or the Parquet tables) at the newest release this way, week after week, see Keep Your Data Current.

When the line changes, start again from the new line's monthly

Deltas apply only to a copy of the same line. A line's first delta builds on the end of the line before it: the 1.2 line's first delta (2026-11-08) has baseline_release 2026-10-31, the last release of the frozen 1.1 line, and both lines have a 2026-11 monthly with source_release 2026-10-31. So a copy built from 1.1 bundles passes a chain check on dates alone, and applying 1.2 deltas to it mixes 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 records.

Before applying a delta, check that its manifest's schema_version equals your copy's schema_version (the bundle's root property; in the frozen 1.0 line the manifests have none). When it differs, or the root index.json names a new current line, stop: download the new line's checkpoint monthly (the delta's checkpoint_full) and replay that line's deltas from it.

items.title: Rebuild a past week
items.text:
Weekly full bundles are kept only for the current month (Weekly Full Bundles). To rebuild the state at any weekly release W — a past week, or the newest one:

  1. Take the newest official monthly whose source_release ≤ W.
  2. Apply, in release order, every delta whose release is later than that source_release and ≤ W.
  3. Check the chain as you go: the first delta's baseline_release equals the monthly's source_release, and each later delta's baseline_release equals the previous delta's release. A mismatch means a release is missing; stop rather than apply a partial chain.
  4. Check the line: each delta's schema_version equals the monthly's. Take the monthly and the deltas from the same line's index.json; a date match alone doesn't prove it (see above).

The deltas to apply are chosen by release date, not by month. In v1/1.1/, the 2026-10 monthly is built from 2026-09-28, so rebuilding 2026-10-11 takes the 2026-10 monthly and applies the 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-11 deltas, both from the monthly's own month. (An earlier version of this page skipped deltas from the monthly's month; that missed them.)

A delta's checkpoint_full names the newest monthly whose source_release is on or before the delta's baseline_release, so it is the right base for that delta and every delta after it up to the next monthly. Its release is the monthly's source_release, the release the first delta of the chain must have as its baseline_release.

A line starts at its first monthly

Each version line holds only its own releases. v1/1.2/ starts with one checkpoint monthly, the first 1.2.0 full, and its deltas run forward from it: the first delta's baseline_release is that monthly's source_release. A week before the checkpoint is rebuilt from the frozen line that held it, v1/1.1/ (its index.json), with 1.1.0 records. replay-bundle.py below works on any line: pass --line.

Delta manifests in the frozen v1/1.0/ line

The 1.0.1 delta manifests in v1/1.0/ are kept byte-identical, so their paths still name the pre-1.1.0 v1/datasets/ and v1/deltas/ keys and every checkpoint_full says 2026-10. For that line, pick the monthly from v1/1.0/index.json (each monthly's source_release) as above, not from checkpoint_full.

To write a week's full bundle to disk, use replay-bundle.py. It follows the rules above (the monthly, the deltas by release date, the chain check), checks each download's sha256 against index.json, keeps only the deltas' records in memory, streams the monthly once, and writes the bundle in the published layout with a .sha256 sidecar. It needs only python3 (3.9 or later, standard library):

curl -fsSO --retry 5 https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/1.2/assets/scripts/replay-bundle.py
python3 replay-bundle.py --release 2026-11-15 --plan
python3 replay-bundle.py --release 2026-11-15

The first lists the monthly and deltas it would use; the second downloads them, replays the deltas and writes clinvar-gkm_2026-1115.replayed.json.gz.

For a week of the frozen 1.1 line, add --line v1/1.1. The Parquet for one weekly release section measures it and builds tables from the result.

items.title: Weekly Full Bundles
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

Older release lines (1.1.x, 1.0.1) are on Previous Releases.

A weekly full bundle is published for every ClinVar weekly release. It has the same content and structure as a monthly full, built from that week's release, so the newest one is the current state with no replay. The weekly fulls live in v1/1.2/weekly/, the counterpart of NCBI's xml/weekly_release/; weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz is a stable URL for the newest one (Directory Structure).

Weekly fulls are kept for the current month only

A month's weekly fulls are deleted after the month ends, as NCBI deletes its weekly releases (Month and Year Rollover gives the timing). Every past week can be rebuilt exactly from a monthly plus deltas (Rebuild a past week). Don't hard-code a dated weekly URL in a script that runs after the month ends.

Prerequisites

  • curl, and sha256sum (Linux, recent macOS) or shasum -a 256 (any macOS) to check the download.
  • Disk. A weekly full is about 4.9 GB compressed and 68.5 GB decompressed. Read it streamed (gunzip -c) rather than decompressing it to disk; see Count records in a full bundle.
Download a weekly full with curl 
# Newest weekly full (stable URL)
curl -fO https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz

# Or a dated weekly full, with its checksum. index.json lists the current month's weekly fulls
# (they are deleted when the month ends); this takes the newest, or pick one by its "release" date.
W=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
weekly = [w for w in json.load(sys.stdin)["datasets"]["weekly"] if not w["latest"]]
print(max(weekly, key=lambda w: w["release"])["path"])')
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${W}"
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${W}.sha256"
sha256sum -c "$(basename "${W}").sha256"      # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c

Monthly, weekly full, or monthly plus deltas?

Choose Your Data compares them. To keep a local copy current from a monthly plus the weekly deltas, use files from one line; when a new line starts, start again from its first monthly (Consumer Replay Model).

items.title: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
items.text: One short, dated file per significant decision — why we chose an approach, not just what the code does. ADRs are the shared, PR-reviewed record of the project's moving picture; CLAUDE.md points here rather than importing them so they don't bloat every session's context.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Filename: NNNN-kebab-title.md (zero-padded, monotonically increasing).
  • Copy 0000-template.md to start.
  • Keep it short. Link to the fuller design spec in superpowers/specs/ when there is one.
  • Status: Proposed → Accepted → (later) Superseded by NNNN. Don't rewrite history — supersede.
  • Land ADRs via PR review, like code.

items.title:
NNNN —
  • Status: Proposed | Accepted | Superseded by NNNN
  • Date: YYYY-MM-DD
  • Spec (if any): superpowers/specs/…
Context
items.text: What problem or force prompted this? What constraints matter?

items.title: Decision
items.text: What we decided, stated plainly.

items.title: Consequences

items.title: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-08-09
  • Spec: superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-incremental-gks-downstream-and-deltas-design.md
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: Context
items.text: Reprocessing every ClinVar release from scratch is expensive — the two costliest stages (variation identity and VRS resolution) recompute ~4.5M variants weekly even though ~0.3% change. Consumers also wanted just the changes, not a full re-download each week.
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Make the pipeline incremental by default: recompute only the records that changed since the prior release and carry the rest forward, gated by a gkm_pipeline_version stamp (full rebuild on version-invalidating changes). The delta is a byproduct of incremental compute — gkm_change_log + gkm_delta_build produce the A/U/D manifest and delta payloads, published to R2 as weekly delta bundles + Parquet alongside the monthly full.

  • Merge primitive for the dict/identity layers: UNION-CTAS (base WHERE NOT impacted UNION ALL recomputed).
  • gkm_vrs carry-forward uses a zero-copy CLONE of the prior release + DELETE/INSERT of the changed subset (with a deep-copy fallback when BigQuery's depth-3 clone chain fills).
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Large slot-time win on variation identity + vrsify; the dict aggregates are roughly break-even on cost — the delta product, not slot-time, justifies making them incremental too.
  • Correctness is enforced by oracles: full-vs-incremental (per table) and delta-reconstruction must be 0,0,0 before publish. This requires deterministic output (total-order ORDER BY, single-representative picks instead of ANY_VALUE).
  • Consumers reconstruct current state = latest monthly full + replay contiguous weekly deltas.
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-08-24
  • Spec: superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-clinvar-index-monthly-trigger-design.md
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: Context
items.text: The monthly full bundle was triggered by our own weekly cadence (a schema_on calendar-month boundary), publishing the prior release as "the month's full." That drifted from ClinVar's authoritative monthly cadence and mislabeled months, because ClinVar names a monthly _YYYY-MM for the month it is released in (early that month, reflecting ~prior-month data).
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: Decision
items.text: Anchor the monthly full to ClinVar's monthly VCV index (https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/xml/). Our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full = the most recent GKM-capable build with release date strictly before ClinVar's _YYYY-MM Released datetime, re-exported into the YYYY-MM slot. ClinVar's monthly XML is only a trigger signal — we never ingest it. A --month-label flag decouples the published slot from the source release date.
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Our monthly labels line up 1:1 with ClinVar's; e.g. the 2026-07 full is built from our 2026-06-27 release.
  • run-release.sh Stage 5 scrapes the index (bounded to months newer than the latest published full) instead of using schema_on; the full is a re-export of existing gkm_dict_* tables, not a rebuild.
  • A one-time re-align moved existing fulls to the new scheme. Prior-month/prior-year retention is still an open design (release browser + archiving spec).
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: 0003 — Roadmap generated from label-authorized discussions
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-08-26

items.title: Context
items.text: The docs Roadmap should reflect community priorities without hand-editing a page for every idea, and without a hand-maintained list that goes stale. GitHub Discussions already provide proposals, comments, and a built-in upvote signal.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
The Roadmap table (docs/reference/roadmap.md, between <!-- ROADMAP:START/END --> markers) is auto-generated from GitHub Discussions carrying the roadmap authorized label, ordered by upvote count (desc). src/scripts/generate-roadmap.py produces it; the deploy-docs workflow runs it on discussion events + a daily schedule + release/dispatch, then builds with zensical build and publishes to GitHub Pages.

  • Governance: a community member opens an Ideas discussion; a maintainer authorizes it by adding the label (removing the label drops it). Status comes from an optional status: <x> label.
  • Voting uses the built-in Upvote button (no emoji reactions, no downvote).

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Adding/removing/reordering roadmap items is done on the discussions, not in the repo — the site self-updates.
  • Build-time generation only: the live site is always current; the committed roadmap.md table is a snapshot that can lag (a commit-back step could close that gap if the repo file view must match exactly).
  • Upvote changes don't fire workflow events, so ordering refreshes on the daily schedule.

items.title: 0004 — Schema versioning & release change-management
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-08
  • Spec: superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-schema-versioning-and-release-management-design.md
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 by ADR 0008 and ADR 0009 (PR #168):
  • §1: a content-only correction that rewrites published bundles opens a new MINOR line folder (e.g. v1/1.2/); a PATCH only adds new dated files to the current line folder (ADR 0009 §5).
  • §3: a superseded line is frozen at the switch-over and kept indefinitely. There is no 6-month live window, no eol and no deprecated status; the root index.json statuses are current and frozen. "At most two lines" no longer applies (ADR 0008 (b)).
  • §5: the in-place exception closes with 1.1.0, which is GA (ADR 0008 (a)).

items.title: Context
items.text: The clinvar-gkm bundle schema is already 1.0.0 (in its $id URIs), but releases are dated, not schema-versioned, and nothing — not the index.json, the R2 path, nor the bundle — carries a machine-readable schema version. As the model evolves we need a contract that lets consumers pin a version, keeps prior releases flowing during a migration, and consults affected users before a breaking change — without forcing a full reprocessing on every change.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Adopt semantic versioning of the bundle schema and a release change-management policy (full detail in the spec):

  1. Semver on the bundle schema — MAJOR = breaking, MINOR = additive/backward-compatible, PATCH = no change to valid instances. A content-only change (e.g. a string value's format) is not a schema version change. (amended: see header)
  2. Upstream bumps are insulated — our level reflects the actual effect on the bundle we emit, not the upstream (va-spec/cat-vrs/vrs) bump level.
  3. Breaking change ⇒ new MAJOR line. The prior line stays fully live (monthly + weekly) for a 6-month window, then freezes (archived, immutable). The window end is a fixed calendar date (successor GA + 6 months) in the manifest. At most two lines run concurrently (N, N-1). (amended: see header)
  4. R2 layout: per-major dirs /v{major}/…, each with its own index.json; a thin root manifest lists active versions, their schema, status, and EOL (amended: see header). Existing 1.x is mirrored into /v1/ now (flat originals retained for backward compatibility).
  5. Initial-stabilization window: until a maintainer-declared GA, the 1.0.x line may take corrective breaking fixes in place (announced, not RFC'd). After GA, the full MAJOR/parallel-line/RFC machinery governs every breaking change. (amended: see header)
  6. Release notes per data release + a per-major CHANGELOG, co-located with each line's files.
  7. Subscribe/consult via GitHub Discussions Announcements (releases + RFCs), a Google Group (email, for non-GitHub consumers), and an RSS/Atom feed from index.json.
  8. Breaking-Change RFC: before any post-GA MAJOR — proposal + rationale + migration impact, notify the registry, 4-week minimum comment window.
  9. Schema in lockstep: schema/clinvar-gkm/ is the source of truth. Every output change moves the schema with it in the same PR — definitions for shape changes, field descriptions for content-only changes — regenerates json/ + the bundle schema (+ docs), bumps the $id version per (1) when the shape changes, and re-validates the examples. The $id version is the authoritative version string the manifest reports.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Consumers can pin a major line and keep receiving fresh data for 6 months after a breaking change; a machine-readable root manifest tells them what's current, deprecated, and when each line ends. (amended: see header)
  • The orchestrator and generate-r2-index.sh gain per-major output paths, a root manifest, a feed, and a stop-rule for frozen lines; release-notes/CHANGELOG generation is added. These are specced but not built here, and every live-R2 write stays a separately user-confirmed step.
  • Breaking changes cost ~2× pipeline/storage during a window and require a 4-week RFC post-GA — a deliberate trade for consumer stability.
  • The first breaking change under the §5 stabilization exception, the 1.1.0 proposition reorganization, is recorded in ADR 0006.
  • The prompting change (the submittedCondition CURIE de-pointer) is content-only, so it ships under the stabilization window without a version bump; this policy governs the first breaking change after GA.
  • Accepted additions: a bundle-level schema_version field (bundles self-identify) and a Home-page release indicator reading the root manifest. The email list (Google Group) was stood up on 2026-10-18 as clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org; it carries the same announcements as GitHub Discussions.

items.title: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-13
  • Spec (if any): —
  • Amended: 2026-10-20 by ADR 0009: the published paths changed; see Layout change (ADR 0009).
  • Amended: 2026-10-21: the Layout change (ADR 0009) notes now match the rules in src/scripts/cf-rules.sh on 1.0 (PR #182): weekly/ and README.txt bypass the cache, and weekly fulls are not cached as immutable.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Context
items.text:
Public distribution originally pointed consumers at the R2 development URL https://pub-f0ad0e0dac0345408dcc95bda20beb42.r2.dev. That endpoint is explicitly dev-only: Cloudflare rate-limits it (429s under load), throttles bandwidth, and supports no CDN caching, WAF, or rate-limiting rules. We needed a stable, production-grade hostname that consumers can hardcode long-term, with cache/abuse controls in front of the bucket.

Constraints that shaped the choice:

  • clinicalgenome.org is not usable as the host. Its authoritative DNS is on AWS Route 53, and ClinGen has no Cloudflare account. R2 custom domains must live in a Cloudflare zone. The supported ways to attach a Cloudflare-served hostname to an externally-hosted parent domain are all gated: full setup (move the whole org domain to Cloudflare — not our call), Partial/CNAME setup (Cloudflare Business plan), or Subdomain setup (Cloudflare Enterprise). None were viable.
  • A generic downloads.clinicalgenome.org / data.clinicalgenome.org would wrongly imply an org-wide ClinGen download hub; clinicalgenome.org hosts many independent data sources.
  • R2's defining property is $0 egress — so "download bandwidth" is never a cost. The only download-driven cost is Class B (read) operations, which are cheap and collapse to near-zero behind a CDN cache.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. Dedicated domain. Registered clinvar-gkm.org via Cloudflare Registrar (~$10/yr), which creates it as its own free Cloudflare zone — no dependency on ClinGen's Route 53 or any admin.
  2. Public host = data.clinvar-gkm.org, attached to the clinvar-gkm R2 bucket via R2 → Connect Domain (auto-creates a proxied record + TLS). data (not downloads) because consumers also range-read the Parquet in place (DuckDB/httpfs), which isn't a "download". The apex is left free for a future landing page.
  3. Scripts default to the custom host, env-overridable. All uploaders + the index generator set R2_PUBLIC_URL="${R2_PUBLIC_URL:-https://data.clinvar-gkm.org}". generate-r2-index.sh writes this as the base_url in index.json / the root manifest / feed.xml — the canonical consumer URL.
  4. Fee protection is CDN-side (Cache Rules + one rate-limit rule), plus an optional --purge path in the uploaders for the rare in-place overwrite.

The pub-…r2.dev dev URL still resolves (same bucket) and can be disabled in the dashboard once all consumers have migrated.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Easy: a stable branded URL, free egress, near-zero op costs behind caching, full WAF/cache control. Harder / must-know for future administrators — the runbook below.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Key identifiers
items.text: Thing Value Cloudflare account (R2) 09208aa33790838db213a21f630c33e7 R2 bucket clinvar-gkm S3 endpoint (writes) https://09208aa33790838db213a21f630c33e7.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (--profile r2) Public host (reads) https://data.clinvar-gkm.org (zone clinvar-gkm.org) Dev URL (legacy) https://pub-f0ad0e0dac0345408dcc95bda20beb42.r2.dev (still works; retire later)
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Reproducing the setup (if the domain/zone ever has to be rebuilt)
items.text:
1. Register / add the zone: clinvar-gkm.org via Cloudflare Registrar (or add any domain you own and point its nameservers at Cloudflare — full setup, free). Must be in the same Cloudflare account as the bucket.
  2. Connect the bucket: R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → Custom Domains → Connect Domain → data.clinvar-gkm.org. Cloudflare creates the proxied record + provisions TLS. Wait for Active.
  3. Verify it's proxied (Cache/WAF rules only act on proxied traffic): 
    dig +short data.clinvar-gkm.org      # → Cloudflare anycast IPs (104.x / 172.67.x), not an origin IP
curl -sI https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/index.json | grep -iE 'server|cf-cache-status'
#   → "server: cloudflare" + a "cf-cache-status:" header  ⇒ traffic is proxied, rules apply
    If a rule editor warns "may not be proxying traffic for (http.host …)", this is the check to run — R2 custom domains are proxied by design, so once Active the warning is a false positive.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Cache Rules (zone clinvar-gkm.org → Caching → Cache Rules)
items.text:
Object layout splits into write-once / immutable vs rewritten-every-release / mutable. Note "latest" appears both as a directory (/00-latest/) and inside a filename (clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz), and there are two index files plus a feed — the mutable matcher must catch all of them:

  • Immutable (dated, never overwritten): /v1/deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/…, /v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_<YYYY-MM>.json.gz, /v1/datasets/parquet/<YYYY-MM>/…, /v1/archives/….
  • Mutable (rewritten every release): root /index.json, /v1/index.json, /v1/feed.xml, /v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, and everything under any /00-latest/ tree (/v1/deltas/00-latest/…, /v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/…).

These are the paths before ADR 0009; the new paths are listed under Layout change (ADR 0009).

Two rules; last matching rule wins, so keep the pointer rule below the immutable rule:

Rule 1 "R2 immutable artifacts"   (FIRST)
  When:  (http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org")
  Then:  Eligible for cache; Edge TTL = Ignore cache-control, 1 month; Browser TTL = 1 day

Rule 2 "R2 mutable pointers"      (SECOND / last)
  When:  (http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org") and (
           http.request.uri.path contains "00-latest"
           or http.request.uri.path contains "index.json"
           or http.request.uri.path contains "feed.xml" )
  Then:  Bypass cache

This collapses Class B cost (immutable files serve from edge, never hitting R2) while mutable pointers are always fetched fresh. The long TTL is safe only because dated artifacts are write-once — see overwrite gotcha below. Two Free-plan constraints shaped this:

  • Max cacheable object = 512 MB (Free/Pro/Business; Enterprise 5 GB). The multi-GB JSON bundles therefore never cache — they always report cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC and stream straight from R2. That is fine: egress is $0 and it's one cheap Class B op per fetch. Caching's real win is the smaller/hot files (Parquet sections, manifests, index).
  • Minimum dashboard Edge TTL = 2 hours on Free. You can't set a short TTL for the pointers that way, so Rule 2 uses Bypass cache (always fresh) instead of a 1-minute TTL. If brief pointer caching is ever wanted, stamp Cache-Control: max-age=60 on those objects at upload and set Rule 2 Edge TTL to "use cache-control header if present" (origin TTLs aren't subject to the 2 h floor).

Verify with real GET requests (curl -I/HEAD reports DYNAMIC even when a GET caches): 

u=https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/deltas/<date>/manifest.json
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "$u" | grep -i cf-cache-status   # run twice → MISS then HIT (immutable)
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/index.json | grep -i cf-cache-status  # DYNAMIC/BYPASS
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Rate-limiting rule (Security → WAF → Rate limiting rules; 1 free IP-keyed rule)
items.text:
Live rule "R2 abuse backstop" (verified 2026-10-18):

When:  (http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org")
