Characteristics:  IP (ip.src)
Rate:  250 requests / 10 seconds
Then:  Block for 10 seconds
Order: first; Status: Active

The Free plan fixes the counting period and the block duration at 10 seconds; only the request count is adjustable. The original intent (300 requests / 1 minute, block 10 minutes) could not be expressed on Free and was first configured as 50 / 10 s. That blocked ordinary DuckDB queries after ~55 range requests, so on 2026-10-18 the threshold was raised to 250 / 10 s. A burst of 120 range requests in ~1 s now returns 206 throughout, and remote queries such as a GROUP BY over all of scv.parquet or a variant's PubMed ids (an scv × varcond-proposition join) complete in 10–35 s.

Keep it generous: DuckDB/httpfs issues many range GETs per query, cached hits still count toward the limiter, and a client that keeps retrying while blocked re-trips the rule. This is an anti-runaway backstop only — real exposure is pennies (free egress + $0.36 / million Class B, 10M/month free).
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Costs (order of magnitude)
items.text: Storage $0.015/GB-mo (a few $/mo at current size); Class B $0.36/million reads with 10M/mo free; egress $0. Caching + the write-once layout keep origin reads near-zero. There is no native hard spend cap. An account-wide budget alert at $10/month is configured (Manage Account → Billing → Billable Usage → budget alert; email only, it does not pause usage). R2-specific Usage Based Billing alerts (Alerts → Overview → Add) may need a paid plan.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Path allowlist rule (Security → WAF → Custom rules)
items.text:
Added 2026-10-18, active:

Name:  PATH ALLOWLIST - block requests outside published data paths
When:  http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org" and not (
         starts_with(path, "/v1/") or starts_with(path, "/archive/") or
         starts_with(path, "/.well-known/") or path in {"/" "/index.json"})
Then:  Block

Scanners probe hostnames for paths such as /wp-config.php, /.git/config and /actuator/health (about 1,600 such requests in the first four days). This rule blocks them at the edge with a 403, before they reach R2, so they cost no Class B operations. Unlike Browser Integrity Check, which is off for this zone because it rejected Python's default urllib user agent (HTTP 403, error 1010), it cannot be bypassed by faking a header. Tested on 2026-10-18: - index files, bundles, Parquet (including 206 range reads), the archive and CORS preflight are served; - scanner paths, stray documentation-site paths and the retired flat-root /datasets/… return 403.

When a new top-level path is published, add it to the rule.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Spend alert and kill switch
items.text:
R2 has no hard spend cap and the budget alert only emails, so pausing is manual. What can grow the bill: Class B reads that miss the cache (mostly range requests on files over 512 MB, which always go to R2), our own writes (Class A) and storage. Egress is $0.

If the alert fires:

  1. Stop our own writes: no run-release.sh, uploader or backfill runs.
  2. Find the cause: R2 → clinvar-gkm → Metrics (which operation type jumped); clinvar-gkm.org → Security → Events / Analytics (top IPs, ASNs, paths). If it is one client or network, block only that with a WAF custom rule on ip.src or ip.geoip.asnum.
  3. Pause all public reads with one command: 
    ./src/scripts/cdn-kill-switch.sh on       # block every request to data.clinvar-gkm.org at the edge
./src/scripts/cdn-kill-switch.sh status   # rule state + a probe of /v1/index.json (403 = blocked)
./src/scripts/cdn-kill-switch.sh off      # restore service
    It flips one WAF custom rule ("KILL SWITCH - block all public data"); cached hits are blocked too, so nothing reaches R2. Nothing in R2 changes. It needs CF_ZONE_ID and CF_WAF_TOKEN in ~/.config/clinvar-gkm/cloudflare.env; the token is scoped to zone clinvar-gkm.org with Zone → Zone WAF → Edit and Zone → Firewall Services → Edit. Run init once to pre-create the rule disabled. The dashboard equivalent is Security → WAF → Custom rules → toggle the rule.
  4. The r2.dev URL bypasses all of this. The public development URL serves the same bucket with no cache, WAF or rate limit. Disable it (R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → Public Development URL); nothing in the repo uses it any more.
  5. Harder stop, if needed: disconnect the custom domain (R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → Custom Domains). Reconnecting re-provisions TLS and takes a few minutes.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Overwrite gotcha + the --purge flag
items.text:
Within the 1-month immutable Edge TTL, Cloudflare serves cached bytes without revalidating against R2, and the cache is per-PoP. So overwriting an already-cached immutable file in place (e.g. re-publishing a release under the same date, or re-running a backfill over an existing month) serves stale, inconsistent content for up to a month. Routine releases are safe — they write new dated keys, and the only paths they overwrite (index.json, 00-latest/*) are on the 1-minute rule and self-heal.

For the rare in-place overwrite, the uploaders take --purge, which purges the CDN cache for the dated path(s) just written:

  • upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh … --purge → purges …/v1/deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/
  • upload-gkm-to-r2.sh … --purge → purges the dated monthly + dated Parquet set
  • backfill-monthly-to-r2.sh … --purge → purges ${DEST} (+ dated Parquet)

--purge requires a zone-scoped Cloudflare API token with Cache Purge permission (the object-scoped r2 token cannot purge), plus the zone id:

export CF_ZONE_ID=<clinvar-gkm.org zone id>
export CF_PURGE_TOKEN=<zone-scoped token with Cache Purge>
./upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh 2026-07-06 delta.json.gz manifest.json --purge

Without --purge nothing changes (routine behavior). With --purge but no token, the script warns and skips (non-fatal). Overridable host via CF_PUBLIC_HOST (default data.clinvar-gkm.org). All purge methods (URL, prefix, hostname, tag, everything) are available on all plans since 2025-04. Manual equivalent: 

curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/${CF_ZONE_ID}/purge_cache" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CF_PURGE_TOKEN}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"prefixes":["data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/datasets/"]}'   # or {"purge_everything":true}
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: CORS
items.text: Bucket CORS is applied out-of-band (apply-r2-cors.sh with an admin token, or the dashboard; policy in src/scripts/r2-cors.json) and is returned at the bucket level, so it passes through the custom domain. The docs download browser (docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js) now fetches from data.clinvar-gkm.org; ensure the docs-site origin is allowed in r2-cors.json.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Optional future: a clinicalgenome.org entry point
items.text: If a ClinGen-branded link is ever wanted, the Route 53 admin can host an S3 static-website redirect + Route 53 alias at e.g. clinvar-gkm-data.clinicalgenome.org → https://data.clinvar-gkm.org. Purely additive; not required for anything to work.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Bucket layout note
items.text: Only the v1/ tree is live. The bucket root holds just the thin index.json manifest (ADR 0004) alongside v1/; the pre-v1/ root datasets/ and deltas/ trees plus root README.txt were deleted on 2026-10-13. All uploaders (including backfill-monthly-to-r2.sh) and the docs now reference v1/… paths.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Layout change (ADR 0009)
items.text:
ADR 0009 replaces the /v1/ layout above with per-line folders modelled on NCBI's ClinVar FTP: v1/1.1/ holds the official monthlies and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, weekly/ (the current month's weekly fulls and clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz), deltas/ (current month at the top, earlier months in deltas/YYYY-MM/), archive/YYYY/ and one parquet/ dataset; the 1.0.1 generation becomes the frozen line v1/1.0/. What changes here (src/scripts/cf-rules.sh holds the exact rule expressions: show compares them with the live rules, apply is a user-confirmed step):

  • Immutable rule. Unchanged; it still matches every path, so in effect it covers everything the later rules do not catch: dated monthlies, deltas, delta manifests, .sha256 sidecars outside weekly/, archive/YYYY/, and frozen line folders' bundles and MANIFEST.json. The path list above no longer applies.
  • Mutable-pointer rule. Bypasses the cache for any path containing 00-latest (which also matches clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz), ending in /index.json, /feed.xml or /README.txt, or containing /weekly/. Weekly fulls and their sidecars are deleted at month rollover, so they are not cached as immutable.
  • Latest-Parquet rule. The "Latest Parquet: cache 1 day" rule (added 2026-10-18; edge 1 day, browser 1 h) matched /v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/, which no longer exists. It now matches any path under /v1/ containing /parquet/, which includes parquet/manifest.json. Without the change the overwritten Parquet would fall under the 1-month immutable rule.
  • Purges. Routine releases now overwrite (the Parquet dataset), move (deltas at month rollover, monthlies and deltas at year rollover) and delete (weekly fulls at month rollover; the finished month's newest once the new monthly is published) published paths. r2-rollover.sh purges every path it moved or deleted, and run-release.sh purges the parquet/ prefix after each rebuild; --purge above is no longer only for the rare in-place overwrite.
  • Path allowlist (WAF custom rule, documented on PR #173). Every published path stays under /v1/, so no new prefix is needed. /archive/ can be removed once archive/1.0.1/ has moved to v1/1.0/ and been deleted (cf-rules.sh apply --drop-archive).
  • Bucket layout note. The "Only the v1/ tree is live" note still holds; the old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/ and dated Parquet trees and archive/1.0.1/ are deleted in the ADR 0009 cleanup.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Spec (if any): superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-proposition-reorganization.md (plan PR #155)
  • Amended: 2026-10-20 by ADR 0009 (R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar, PR #168): Decision 2's "in place under /v1/" becomes the new line folder v1/1.1/, and the 1.0.1 generation becomes the frozen line v1/1.0/. Decisions 1, 3 and 4 stand.
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 by ADR 0008 and ADR 0009 (PR #168): the maintainer declared 1.1.0 GA. The initial-stabilization exception ends with 1.1.0; published files are immutable from 1.1.0, and a later breaking change opens v2/. A superseded line is frozen and kept indefinitely (no EOL date, no deprecation window), and a content-only correction that rewrites bundles opens a new MINOR line folder. 1.1.0 used a completion notice only (ADR 0008 (g)).
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Context
items.text:
The next release was being prepared as 1.0.2: a schema-conformance fix to ClinvarCategoricalVariant (#142) plus corrective data and Parquet fixes, delivered through a patch-style backfill of the published releases.

On 2026-10-18 the proposition reorganization was added to the same release. The four proposition sections and Parquet tables, grouped by object shape (varcond-, varcustom-, vartumor-, vartherapy-proposition), become four grouped by meaning (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom). The Parquet tables share one column schema, which renames some columns. Every statement and evidence-line pointer changes, so the patch backfill no longer fits. The release becomes one full rebuild of all 16 datasets, with every published bundle and Parquet set re-assembled and re-exported.

ADR 0004 gives three ways to label this:

  • §1: a PATCH must not change valid instances. Renaming sections and tables does, so 1.0.2 is wrong.
  • §3/§4: a breaking change after GA gets a new MAJOR line (/v2/) and the prior line stays live for 6 months, after a 4-week RFC (§8).
  • §5: until GA, the 1.x line may take breaking changes in place, announced rather than RFC'd. §5 names corrective fixes. The reorganization is a deliberate redesign, not a correction.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. Ship the proposition reorganization and the pending fixes as 1.1.0: the schema $ids (w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/…), the bundle schema_version const and the assembler's SCHEMA_VERSION.
  2. Publish it in place under /v1/, under the §5 stabilization exception. ADR 0004 §4 keys directories by MAJOR, so a MINOR stays in /v1/. All 4 monthly fulls, 00-latest, the 15 weekly deltas and every Parquet set are rewritten, and the old var*-proposition files are removed.
  3. No new MAJOR line, no parallel line, and no 1.0.2 tag. The release is one tag, 1.1.0, on the 1.0 release branch. The branch keeps its name, since it carries the 1.x line.
  4. This ADR extends §5 to cover a deliberate structural change made before GA, not only corrective fixes. After GA, the full MAJOR, parallel-line and RFC process governs every breaking change, as ADR 0004 says.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Rationale
items.text:
• Not a PATCH. Under §1 a PATCH changes no valid instance. This release renames sections, Parquet tables and columns, and rewrites every pointer, so 1.0.2 would mislabel it.
  • A MINOR is the most honest label that stays in /v1/. It is not strict semver, since a MINOR should be additive. But a consumer that pins a 1.0.x $id gets a clear signal that something changed, and the R2 layout stays put.
  • A new MAJOR costs more than it protects. /v2/ would double the pipeline and storage for 6 months and add a 4-week RFC. Before GA there are few consumers, so the parallel line would protect almost no one.
  • One rebuild. Labelling the fixes and the redesign together means one rebuild and one republish, not two.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Announcements (ADR 0004 §6, §7). These are required, in this order:
  • An advance notice with the cutover date, posted before any R2 overwrite.
  • A completion notice after the republish is verified.

Both go to GitHub Discussions Announcements, the v1/feed.xml Atom feed, the GitHub Release notes and the Changelog. The Google Group clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org went live on 2026-10-18 (#167). Today generate-r2-index.sh builds the feed from the R2 listing alone (one entry per file, no summary text), so the republish re-dates every entry but cannot carry the notice text. A notice entry in the feed is a generator follow-up. Both notices cover the old → new section and table mapping, the column renames, the 1.1.0 $ids and schema_version, the corrective fixes in the same release, and the fact that every published file is rewritten in place, so checksums change and earlier downloads should be refreshed. - Version strings. Every 1.0.2 string on the open 1.0 PRs (#142, #145, #153 and the rest) is relabelled 1.1.0 before they merge. Gate before tagging: grep -r 1.0.2 schema src returns nothing. - Tagging. Tagging 1.1.0 makes the new w3id $ids resolve through the existing dynamic rule (no .htaccess change). The 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 tags and their $ids stay resolvable. - Local copies. Copies downloaded before 1.1.0 keep the old sections and tables. The plan's migration notes show how to rebuild the new shape from their data column. - Precedent. The extension in Decision 4 ends at GA. Once GA is declared, a change like this needs a /v2/ line and an RFC.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: 0007 — Pipeline principles and simplification
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Plan: superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-pipeline-simplification.md

items.title: Context
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM exists to give the public community reliable, high-quality ClinVar data that significantly lowers the barrier to understanding, access, use and interoperability. The pipeline has to transform ClinVar into the GA4GH GKM schema set (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec) and stay maintainable by a small team, with as few points of failure as possible.

Size today (main @ 567272c; src/ is identical on 1.0 @ 6606d3d):

Part Count Lines BigQuery procedures and functions (src/procedures/*.sql) 22 files about 9,300 Release scripts (src/scripts/, top level) 31 files about 5,000 Parquet export SQL (src/scripts/parquet-schemas/*.sql) 21 files 193 Oracle and validation scripts (oracle-*.sh, validate-*) 10 files —

The 1.1.0 work found defects that fall into four classes. None of them is a one-off; each class comes from how the pipeline is built.

  1. Duplicated logic that drifted apart.
    • The Parquet SQL re-derives every table from the BigQuery gkm_dict_* tables, so it had to copy the bundle assembler's cleanup. The copy was incomplete: typed extensions in scv and evidenceLine Parquet carried all-null placeholder elements that the bundle does not have (#143).
    • Two null-strip implementations exist: the assembler's strip_empty and BigQuery's JSON_STRIP_NULLS. Applying JSON_STRIP_NULLS to the key/value tables would have broken the VRS Range nulls in 65,964 location rows (#143).
    • The proposition type → bundle section mapping is copied in 11 places: 8 procedure sites, the NDJSON export, the delta manifest and the conformance validator (#155 §2.3). The copies already differ in detail.
  2. Mixed reference forms. Bare CURIEs and #/section/key pointers were both used for references: 7,811,379 bare values in VCV proposition object and vcv- ConceptSet concepts on 2026-10-11 (#160). The published 1.0.1 Parquet held JSON-quoted pointers in vartherapy-proposition.object_therapy ("\"#/therapy/clinvar.therapy:…\""), fixed in #143. Consumers and our own Parquet SQL strip pointers with regexes in many places.
  3. Incremental and full builds disagreed.
    • Unordered aggregates made the procedures non-deterministic: two runs of unchanged SQL gave different fingerprints for gkm_dict_variation, the VCV/RCV aggregate tables, variation_hgvs and variation_identity (#161).
    • A duplicate allele key flipped between builds, so it showed up in weekly deltas (#157).
    • The VCV/RCV carry-forward parses the accession out of the proposition id (SPLIT(key, '-')), which ties the delta model to the id format (#155 §3.B).
  4. Upstream inputs trusted without checks.
    • clinvar_ingest.entrez_gene is missing 64,854 gene ids that gene_association uses.
    • rcv_mapping lists SCVs that are absent from the VCV data, 2–3 a week. It is a faithful parse of ClinVar's RCV XML, which runs out of sync with the VCV XML. One stale SCV left four RCV propositions with no object (#158).
    • ClinVar's VCV XML carries 16 malformed HGVS expressions with no sequence-type letter (#145).
    • single_gene_variation counts gene-association rows instead of distinct genes, so 55 haplotypes and genotypes whose alleles share one gene get no gene.

Each fix so far has been local. Without a shared standard, the same classes will recur.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
These five principles are normative. Every change to the pipeline or the published data is measured against them. A change that departs from one says so in its PR, with the reason; a lasting departure needs its own ADR.

  1. ClinVar fidelity. Never alter or drop source data silently. A repair keeps the original value in an extension, and an inferred value is marked as inferred. Examples: originalClinvarExpression / invalidClinvarExpression (#145), originalClinvarCitation (#156), geneContextSource (#159), and submittedCondition kept as the submitted CURIE.
  2. One source of truth. The JSON bundle is canonical. Every other published artifact (Parquet, lookup files) must be recomputable from the published bundle. Derived columns, join keys and lookup tables are allowed. A new fact goes into the bundle first and flows out from there.
  3. Conformance on real artifacts. Validate the actual published bundles, full and delta, with the GA4GH gkm-toolkit against the strict schemas. A hand-built sample or a sub-bundle does not count: it can mask export and assembler bugs.
  4. Determinism. The same input gives byte-identical output, and incremental output equals a full rebuild. Every aggregate, pick and array order that reaches an output uses a total order.
  5. Change published data only by rebuilding. One consolidated rebuild and backfill per release, with the docs updated in lockstep. Published files are never patched in place.

items.title: Rules these principles consolidate
items.text:
These rules already exist. The principles state the intent behind them; the detailed rules stay where they are.

Principle Existing rule Where it lives 1 ClinVar's submitted text is never altered or dropped #144 plan, decision A1; #145 2 The assembler (assemble-gkm-dicts.py + gkm_json_cleanup.py) is the single publish-layer cleanup point CLAUDE.md; scripts.md "Publish-layer cleanup & bundle conformance" 2 schema/clinvar-gkm/ is the source of truth for the schema ADR 0004 §9 3 Validate the real full and delta bundles with gkm-toolkit; sub-bundle.py output is not proof CLAUDE.md; scripts.md "Conformance validation" 3 Validate the data a procedure produces, not just that the SQL runs sql-procedures.md "Cat-VRS variant/constraint shapes" 4 Incremental procedures are byte-identical to a full rebuild; total-order ORDER BY; no ANY_VALUE for values the group key does not determine sql-procedures.md "Determinism / correctness"; ADR 0001 4 Full-vs-incremental and delta-reconstruction oracles report 0,0,0 before publishing sql-procedures.md 5 Settle every data decision, then run one consolidated rebuild and backfill; docs move with every PR maintainer rule, applied in #144 and #155 5 Never overwrite a published dated path without a CDN purge; every live R2 write is confirmed by a maintainer scripts.md "Cloudflare R2"; ADR 0005

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
The principles point the pipeline toward fewer moving parts. The simplification plan has the detail, the measurements and the decisions still needed. In summary:

  • Generate Parquet from the bundle output. Build the Parquet tables from the cleaned records the assembler writes, instead of re-deriving them from the dict tables in 21 SQL files. The copied cleanup and the placeholder class of bugs go away (principle 2).
  • One canonical definition per concept. Pointer formatting, pointer stripping, the type → section mapping and the list of tracked tables each get one shared definition (principles 2 and 4).
  • Re-evaluate the incremental machinery with cost data. Measure each procedure in full and incremental mode over several weeks before deciding where carry-forward pays for its complexity. The delta product does not depend on it: gkm_change_log already finds changes by diffing outputs (principle 4).
  • Input contract checks at the upstream boundary. Check the inputs before each run. A violation fails the run or is logged; it is never silently absorbed (principle 1).
  • One release gate command. The oracles, strict gkm-toolkit validation of the real bundles, the bundle-vs-Parquet recompute and the reference guard run as one command that blocks publish (principles 3 and 4).
  • Restraint on new published artifacts. Every new artifact needs a stated owner and gate, and derives from the bundle or the published Parquet (principles 2 and 5).

Other consequences:

  • The in-flight 1.1.0 release already applies parts of this: the canonical type → section function (#155), uniform #/ references with a bare-reference guard (#160), the determinism fixes (#161, #157) and the release gates in #155 §6.4. The simplification work starts after 1.1.0 ships.
  • Principle 5 retires the patch-style backfill used for the 1.0.0 conditionSet repair and prepared for 1.0.2 (#144). #155 had already moved 1.1.0 to a full rebuild.
  • Rebuilds cost more than patches. The #155 estimate for a full rebuild of all 16 datasets is about 3.4 TiB billed, about $21 at on-demand rates. That is small next to the cost of an unverifiable patch.
  • Reviewers gain a checklist: which principle does a change touch, and which gate proves it holds.
  • Once accepted, CLAUDE.md should point to this ADR from its project context section.

items.title: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Plan: superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-bundle-record-and-metrics.md
  • Amends: ADR 0004 §3 (no live window: a superseded line freezes at the switch-over and is kept indefinitely, with no EOL date) and §5 (the in-place exception ends with 1.1.0); ADR 0006 (on PR #146) consequences (advance notice, (g)).
  • Amended: 2026-10-20 by ADR 0009 (R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar): (a) weekly fulls are an exception to immutability; (c) archives are archive/YYYY/ inside a line, and the 1.0.1 generation becomes the frozen line v1/1.0/; (e) one overwritten Parquet dataset, none in archives.
  • Decided: 2026-10-21 (maintainer): 1.1.0 is GA (a); superseded lines are frozen and kept indefinitely, status frozen, with no eol, no deprecated status and no deletion window (b); a content-only correction that rewrites bundles opens a new MINOR line (c, ADR 0009 §5). Still open: N in (f).
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 to match the code merged on 1.0 (PR #182, r2_layout.py): the finished month's newest weekly full is kept until the new month's monthly is published (a); the switch-over notice uses status: "frozen" and superseded_by as the root and line index.json publish them (b); the Parquet manifest fields (e).
  • Amended: 2026-11-18 for 1.2.0 (maintainer decisions D1, D2, D6 of the 1.2.0 runbook): a new line may start from one checkpoint monthly plus deltas, without republishing history; a frozen line loses its weekly fulls and, once the next line has Parquet, its parquet/ (b), (c).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: Context
items.text:
Every corrective release so far has rewritten the published files under /v1/ in place: the 1.0.0 re-release, 1.0.1, and next the 1.1.0 republish (ADR 0006, on #146). Each rewrite replaced the bytes behind the same URLs. Anyone who downloaded an earlier generation now holds files that no longer exist anywhere, and nothing tells them which generation they have.

Before deciding how much machinery that problem deserves, we need to know whether anyone is downloading the data. What we know today:

  • Analytics exist only from 2026-10-14. Cloudflare GraphQL Analytics (httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups, per path, Free plan) covers data.clinvar-gkm.org from the day it started serving (ADR 0005). The zone rejects queries older than "4w3d", so it keeps about 31 days. Earlier traffic went to the r2.dev URL, which has no per-path analytics and is now disabled.

  • No complete full-bundle download so far. From 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-18, excluding our own IP:

    Path Requests Clients Served Reading v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz 18 8 IP/UA pairs 1.09 GB about 0.2 of one 4.8 GB full: at most a partial download dated monthly fulls (each) 2–4 — 0 bytes HEAD requests or link checks v1/deltas/00-latest/… delta 12 — 0.03 GB about 1–2 delta downloads old flat-root /datasets/… 7 — 0 bytes stale links

  • Parquet is not yet stable. The Parquet tables are re-derived from the BigQuery dict tables by separate SQL (ADR 0007, Workstream 1), and their layout changed in 1.0.1 and changes again in 1.1.0. The JSON bundles are the canonical output (ADR 0007, principle 2).

  • The 1.0.1 bundles are being archived to archive/1.0.1/ (the v1/ paths mirrored below it), with a MANIFEST.json (sha256 per file) and a README.txt, before the 1.1.0 republish rewrites /v1/. Under ADR 0009 this generation moves to the frozen line folder v1/1.0/.
  • No subscribers yet. The email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org has no members. When this ADR was proposed the schema had not been declared GA; the maintainer declared 1.1.0 GA on 2026-10-21 (a).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: Decision
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (a) The JSON bundles are the public record
items.text:
The monthly full and delta JSON bundles are the published record of ClinVar-GKM. From the 1.1.0 republish on, a published bundle file is immutable: the bytes behind a published bundle path are never replaced. A correction is published into a new line folder (c), and the folder it replaces is frozen with its bytes intact. The mutable pointers are not records: index.json, the root manifest, feed.xml and every 00-latest path keep moving to the newest release.

Two amendments from ADR 0009:

  • Weekly full bundles are not records. The current month's weekly fulls under weekly/ are a convenience copy and are deleted at month rollover, as NCBI deletes its weekly releases. The finished month's newest weekly full is kept until the new month's official monthly, a server-side copy of it, is published, and is deleted then. This is a deliberate exception to immutability. The records are the official monthlies and the deltas, from which any past week can be rebuilt exactly.
  • Moves change the path, not the bytes. At month and year rollover, deltas and monthlies move into deltas/YYYY-MM/ and archive/YYYY/. Their bytes, names and sha256 stay the same.

1.1.0 is GA (maintainer decision, 2026-10-21). The ADR 0004 §5 initial-stabilization period, which ADR 0006 extended to cover the 1.1.0 reorganization, ends with 1.1.0: the in-place exception is closed, published files are immutable from 1.1.0, and every later breaking change opens a new MAJOR line (v2/) under the ADR 0004 MAJOR-line and RFC process.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (b) A breaking change opens a new line
items.text:
A breaking schema change after 1.1.0 opens a new line, v2/2.0/ (ADR 0009 §1), built in full (every monthly full and every delta in the window being republished) alongside /v1/. The old line is then frozen at the switch-over: no new releases, and its files stay downloadable and unchanged. It carries a switch-over notice:

  • in its index.json and in its entry in the root manifest's versions: "status": "frozen" and "superseded_by" naming the line that replaced it (for example "v2/2.0"), as v1/1.0 already carries "superseded_by": "v1/1.1";
  • in its MANIFEST.json and README.txt (c);
  • on the email list and in GitHub Discussions Announcements.

Decided 2026-10-21 by the maintainer: a superseded line is frozen at the switch-over and kept indefinitely. Its status is frozen; there is no eol date, no deprecated status and no deletion window. This amends ADR 0004 §3: the prior line does not stay live for a 6-month window, and the root manifest carries no EOL date. Only one line is current at a time; frozen lines accumulate.

Amended 2026-11-18 (1.2.0). A new line may start from a checkpoint. It need not republish history: it may start with one checkpoint monthly, a full built with the new pipeline and published as the official monthly (ADR 0002) of the ClinVar month whose source release it is, plus deltas forward from it. The first delta's baseline_release is that monthly's source_release. v1/1.2/ starts this way, from clinvar-gkm_2026-11 ← 2026-10-31; the line it replaces keeps the releases before it. Before the freeze, the old line may receive its own final official monthly (a server-side copy of its newest weekly full): v1/1.1/ ends with clinvar-gkm_2026-11 ← 2026-10-31, the same ClinVar state as the 1.2 checkpoint.

At the freeze, a line keeps its records and loses its conveniences. Its official monthlies, 00-latest copy, archive/ and deltas stay forever, at their paths and with their bytes. Its weekly fulls (weekly/, including 00-latest_weekly) are deleted, as at a month rollover (a). Its parquet/ is deleted too, once the next line has published its own Parquet; until then it may be kept (r2-freeze-line.sh --keep-parquet) and the freeze is run again later without it. Neither is a record: any past week is a monthly plus deltas, and Parquet is derived (e).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (c) A replaced generation is kept as a frozen line folder
items.text:
Amended by ADR 0009. Each version line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/. A republish that replaces a line's bundles (a new MINOR or MAJOR) publishes into a new folder, and the folder it replaces is frozen in place and kept indefinitely (b): nothing is added, moved or deleted, apart from the freeze itself (its MANIFEST.json and README.txt are added, and its weekly fulls and Parquet removed, as amended in (b) on 2026-11-18), and it is listed from the root manifest with its status. A frozen folder carries:

  • a MANIFEST.json listing every file with its size and sha256;
  • a README.txt saying what the generation is, which release replaced it and why.

The 1.0.1 generation, first copied to archive/1.0.1/ on 2026-10-18, moves to v1/1.0/. There is no root archive/<version>/ folder any more: archive/YYYY/ now means the prior-year archive inside a line (v1/1.1/archive/YYYY/, monthlies plus deltas/YYYY-MM/). A content-only correction that must rewrite bundles is published the same way, as a new MINOR line folder; a PATCH only adds new dated files (ADR 0009 §5, decided 2026-10-21).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (d) Every manifest carries sha256 per file
items.text: Every manifest that lists a bundle (the per-line index.json, each delta manifest and each frozen line's MANIFEST.json) gives its size and sha256, and every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar. A user can then tell which generation a local copy belongs to by hashing it, without relying on dates or file names.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (e) Parquet is derived, not a record
items.text:
Parquet is a convenience view of a bundle, not a record:

  • The docs and the manifests label it "derived from the bundle; may be regenerated".
  • Amended by ADR 0009. One Parquet dataset is published per line, at v1/1.1/parquet/, rebuilt from the newest release and overwritten every release. parquet/manifest.json beside it gives derived: true, the build_date, the source_release and dataset, the builder and table_spec_version (the tool version), the schema_version, and each file's size and sha256. There is no Parquet in archive/YYYY/, in frozen line folders (v1/1.0/ has none) or per delta. This reverses the 2026-10-18 decision to keep one Parquet set per archived generation.
  • A versioned Parquet rebuild tool, clinvar-gkm-parquet (planned), builds the Parquet tables from a published bundle. It is versioned on its own cadence, declares which bundle schema_versions it accepts, and the pipeline pins a version of it (ADR 0007, Workstream 1), so a user can rebuild the Parquet of any monthly with the tool version that matches.
  • Caveat: the 1.0.x Parquet was produced by BigQuery SQL from the dict tables, not from the bundle, so it cannot be reproduced bit-for-bit. So is the 1.1.0 Parquet, since Workstream 1 starts after 1.1.0 ships. The tool can rebuild the content of those sets from their bundles, not their bytes.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (f) Download metrics decide how far to go
items.text:
A daily collector stores per-path request counts, bytes served and distinct-client counts for data.clinvar-gkm.org (no IP addresses). Estimated complete downloads of a bundle = bytes served ÷ its size.

Retention and the shape of a switch-over are no longer metrics questions: frozen lines and archive/YYYY/ are kept indefinitely, and a breaking change freezes the old line at the switch-over (b). The metrics decide how far to go beyond that:

  • Promote a frozen line or monthly if it shows N or more estimated complete downloads in a calendar month: consider a citable copy (for example a DOI) for it.

N is the maintainer's decision. The first review is 60 days after collection starts (plan, task 7).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (g) Announcements
items.text: An advance notice before a republish or a switch-over is required once the email list has subscribers or after GA, whichever comes first. With 1.1.0 GA, every later republish into a new line and every switch-over gets an advance notice. 1.1.0 itself used a completion notice only (changelog, GitHub Release notes, Discussions); this amends the advance-notice requirement in ADR 0006's consequences.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Storage. One frozen generation of bundles is about 24 GB (19 dated bundles, 19.3 GB, plus the 00-latest copies, 4.8 GB): about $0.36 a month at R2's $0.015/GB-month. Frozen lines are kept indefinitely, so this grows by one generation per new line. Only one Parquet dataset exists under (e), so dropping the dated Parquet sets saves about 65 GB. Weekly fulls add at most about 24 GB at the end of a month (ADR 0009). A v2/2.0/ line adds a full live line beside the frozen v1/ lines.
  • Operations. Each republish that replaces a line gains steps: freeze the old line folder, write and verify its MANIFEST.json, write its README.txt. Month and year rollovers move and delete files, and each move or delete is followed by a CDN purge of the old paths (ADR 0009). The uploaders and generate-r2-index.sh publish sha256, status / superseded_by, each monthly's source_release and the frozen lines in the root manifest (built in r2_layout.py, PR #182). A daily GitHub Actions job collects the download stats (secrets CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN, CF_ZONE_ID); a missed day can be collected again only within the 31-day retention.
  • For users. A monthly or delta file keeps the same bytes and name, though its folder changes at month and year rollover; a weekly full is gone shortly after its month, and is rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas; a superseded generation stays available indefinitely as a frozen line folder (v1/1.0/); a checksum tells them which generation they hold; a frozen line says what replaced it; and they can rebuild Parquet from any monthly with clinvar-gkm-parquet.
  • Metric limits. Cloudflare's adaptive sampling makes counts estimates. Distinct clients are counted per day by IP, so NAT undercounts and roaming clients overcount. Bytes ÷ size counts two half downloads as one. Traffic before 2026-10-14 is not measurable.
  • Harder: from 1.1.0 (GA), a mistake in a published bundle can no longer be fixed quietly. It needs a new MINOR line (content-only, ADR 0009 §5) or a new MAJOR line (breaking), with an advance notice (g).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: 0009 — R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-20
  • Amends: ADR 0004 §4 (directories per version line) and §1 (a content-only correction that rewrites bundles takes a MINOR line, §5 below), ADR 0005 (cache rules, path allowlist, layout note), ADR 0006 (on PR #146) Decision 2 (1.1.0 ships under v1/1.1/, not in place in /v1/), ADR 0008 (a), (c), (e)
  • Plan: superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-bundle-record-and-metrics.md
  • Decided: 2026-10-21 (maintainer): §5 is no longer open. A content-only correction that rewrites published bundles is released as a new MINOR line folder; a PATCH only adds new dated files.
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 to match the layout code merged on 1.0 (PR #182: r2_layout.py, r2-rollover.sh, cf-rules.sh, run-release.sh): the finished month's newest weekly full is kept until the new month's monthly is published (§2, §3, §4); weekly/ is not cached as immutable (Consequences); file names, the root and line index.json, checkpoint_full and the Parquet manifest fields (§1, §2).
  • Amended: 2026-11-18 for 1.2.0 (maintainer decisions D1, D2, D6 of the 1.2.0 runbook): a new line may start from one checkpoint monthly plus deltas; a frozen line's weekly fulls and, once the next line has Parquet, its parquet/ are deleted at the freeze (§1; ADR 0008 (b)).

items.title: Context
items.text:
The published bundles are built from NCBI's ClinVar XML releases. NCBI publishes them in a layout ClinVar users already know:

NCBI path What it holds pub/clinvar/xml/ the current year's monthly releases (ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM.xml.gz) and ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz xml/weekly_release/ the current month's weekly full releases and 00-latest_weekly; earlier weeks are removed xml/archive/YYYY/ the monthly releases of prior years

Every file has an .md5 sidecar, and every file name carries its date.

The ClinVar-GKM layout under /v1/ grew differently: datasets/ for monthly fulls, deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/ directories each holding a bundle and a manifest.json, dated Parquet sets under datasets/parquet/, a prior-year archives/ folder, and a superseded generation copied to a root archive/1.0.1/ (ADR 0008 (c)). Three problems came with it:

  • No weekly full. A user who wanted the current week had to download the monthly full and replay deltas.
  • No place for a new MINOR. ADR 0004 §4 keys directories by MAJOR only, so the 1.1.0 republish would have rewritten /v1/ in place (ADR 0006) and pushed the 1.0.1 generation out to archive/1.0.1/.
  • Two replay defects. Every delta manifest's checkpoint_full named the newest monthly (2026-10), not the monthly its chain starts from, and nothing published which release a monthly full was built from. The documented replay also compared months, so it skipped deltas from the checkpoint's own month.

items.title: 1. Version folders
items.text:
Each version line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/, starting with v1/1.1/:

  • A PATCH release (1.1.x) only adds new dated files to the current line folder. It never rewrites a published file (§5).
  • A new MINOR starts a new folder (v1/1.2/); a new MAJOR starts v2/2.0/.
  • A folder that a newer line replaces is frozen and kept indefinitely (ADR 0008 (b)): nothing is added to it, moved in it or deleted from it. Amended 2026-11-18 (1.2.0): except at the freeze itself, which adds MANIFEST.json and README.txt and deletes the line's weekly fulls (weekly/, including 00-latest_weekly) and, once the next line has published its own Parquet, its parquet/. Its official monthlies, 00-latest copy, archive/ and deltas stay forever, unchanged. Neither deleted kind is a record (§4; ADR 0008 (a), (e)).
  • Amended 2026-11-18 (1.2.0): a new line may start from one checkpoint monthly plus deltas instead of republishing history: the first full built with its pipeline, published as the official monthly (ADR 0002) of the ClinVar month whose source release it is. v1/1.2/ starts from clinvar-gkm_2026-11 ← 2026-10-31; v1/1.1/ gets the same month's monthly (a copy of its 2026-10-31 weekly full) before it is frozen.
  • The 1.0.1 generation, archived on 2026-10-18 to archive/1.0.1/, moves to the frozen line v1/1.0/.

The bucket-root index.json lists the lines: manifest_version: 2, current (the current line, "v1/1.1") and versions, keyed by line name ("1.1", "1.0"). Each entry gives line, major, minor, status ("current" or "frozen"), schema, superseded_by (the line that replaced it, such as "v1/1.1", or null), index and feed. There is no eol field. Consumers pick the entry whose status is "current".

Each line has its own index.json and feed.xml. A line's index.json carries the same line, status, superseded_by and schema_version, plus current_month, latest_release, datasets.monthly[], datasets.weekly[], deltas[], archives (keyed by year) and parquet (§2).

items.title: 2. The layout of a line
items.text:
v1/1.1/
  index.json, feed.xml, README.txt
  clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz              official monthly full (ADR 0002), current year
  clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz.sha256
  clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz            newest official monthly (same bytes), + .sha256
  weekly/
    clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz          weekly FULL bundle of the current month (§3), + .sha256
    clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz   newest weekly full (same bytes), + .sha256
  deltas/
    clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz    current month's deltas
    clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz.sha256
    clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json
    YYYY-MM/                               earlier months of the current year
  archive/YYYY/
    clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz            prior years' monthly fulls, + .sha256
    deltas/YYYY-MM/                        prior years' deltas
  parquet/                                 ONE Parquet dataset, overwritten every release
    {section}.parquet
    manifest.json

A frozen line keeps the shape it was frozen with. v1/1.0/ holds the monthlies 2026-07 to 2026-10 and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz at the top, every delta under deltas/YYYY-MM/, and MANIFEST.json, README.txt, index.json and feed.xml. It has no weekly/ and no parquet/.

  • Checksums. Every bundle (dated, 00-latest, weekly and delta) has a <file>.sha256 sidecar in sha256sum -c format (<sha256> <file name>), the counterpart of NCBI's .md5. The line's index.json repeats each bundle's sha256 and size.
  • Monthlies. The official monthly clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM is chosen as ADR 0002 says: the newest build before ClinVar's ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM datetime. run-release.sh publishes it as a server-side copy of that release's weekly full, or re-exports it from BigQuery if the weekly full is gone. Each monthly's source_release (the release it was built from) is published in the line's index.json, next to its release (the YYYY-MM label). The 00-latest copy is an entry with latest: true and the release it equals.
  • Weekly fulls are new. A full bundle is published for every weekly release. Only the current month's are kept, plus the finished month's newest one until the new month's official monthly is published (§3).
  • Deltas keep their manifests, now named clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json beside the bundle. Each manifest gains schema_version, bundle {name, path, size, sha256}, sha256 and checkpoint_full: the newest official monthly whose source_release is on or before the delta's baseline_release, so a replay can start from it. Its shape is {path, release, month, sha256}, where release is the monthly's source_release (comparable with baseline_release) and month is its YYYY-MM label.
  • Parquet is one dataset, rebuilt and overwritten every release from the newest release. parquet/manifest.json beside it gives derived: true, build_date, source_release, dataset, builder ("BigQuery export" until the tool ships), table_spec_version, schema_version, a note, and files[] with each file's name, size and sha256. The line's index.json summarizes it under parquet. No Parquet is kept anywhere else: not per month, not per delta, not in archive/ and not in frozen line folders. Past Parquet is rebuilt from the bundles with the clinvar-gkm-parquet tool (planned; until it ships, the 1.1.0 Parquet is exported by BigQuery).
  • Cleanup. Everything on R2 outside a published line and the root index.json is deleted: the old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/ and dated Parquet trees, and archive/1.0.1/ once it has moved to v1/1.0/.

items.title: 3. Rollover triggers
items.text:
run-release.sh runs r2-rollover.sh before a release's weekly uploads and again after its monthly step. The plan comes from r2_layout.py (plan_rollover) and is idempotent: when the line already matches the layout, nothing happens.

Trigger What moves or goes The first release dated in a new month The finished month's deltas (bundle, .sha256, manifest) move from deltas/ into deltas/YYYY-MM/. The finished month's weekly fulls and their sidecars are deleted from weekly/, except the newest, which is kept until the new month's official monthly is published: it is that monthly's ADR 0002 source candidate, and the monthly is a server-side copy of it. The rollover that runs after the monthly is published deletes it. The first release dated in a new year The finished year's monthlies and sidecars move from the line's top level into archive/YYYY/, and its deltas/YYYY-MM/ folders move into archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/. The month rollover runs too.

A move never changes a file's bytes, name or checksum, only its folder. The 00-latest pointers stay at their paths and are rewritten every release.

items.title: 4. Weekly fulls are deleted: an exception to immutability
items.text:
ADR 0008 (a) makes a published bundle immutable. Weekly fulls are a deliberate exception: they are a convenience copy of the current month, deleted at month rollover (the newest one once the next official monthly is published), as NCBI deletes its weekly releases. Nothing is lost: the official monthly is built from the newest release before ClinVar's monthly (ADR 0002), normally the finished month's last weekly, and any past week can be rebuilt exactly from a monthly plus deltas:

  1. Take the newest official monthly whose source_release ≤ the week W.
  2. Apply, in release order, every delta whose release is later than that source_release and ≤ W.
  3. Check the chain: the first delta's baseline_release equals the monthly's source_release, and each later delta's baseline_release equals the previous delta's release.

The monthlies and the deltas are the durable record.

items.title: 5. Content-only corrections open a new MINOR line
items.text: Decided 2026-10-21 by the maintainer. A correction that must rewrite published bundles without changing the schema shape (a content-only change, which ADR 0004 §1 does not count as a schema version change) is released as a new MINOR line folder: for example, 1.2.0 is published into v1/1.2/, and v1/1.1/ is frozen and kept (ADR 0008 (b), (c)). A PATCH (1.1.x) only ever adds new dated files to the current line folder and never rewrites one. This amends ADR 0004 §1 for that case: a release that rewrites published bundles takes a MINOR number even when the schema shape is unchanged. The new line's schema $id version and every bundle's schema_version move to that MINOR (for example 1.2.0) as well (decided 2026-10-22), so a bundle's schema_version always names the line folder it was published in.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Familiar for ClinVar users. The monthly, weekly/ and archive/YYYY/ folders and the 00-latest / 00-latest_weekly names match NCBI's. deltas/ has no NCBI counterpart and is our addition.
  • URLs move; bytes do not. A delta URL changes when its month rolls over, and a monthly URL changes when its year rolls over. File names and .sha256 stay the same, so a downloaded copy can still be identified. Scripts should resolve paths through the line's index.json, not hard-code them. A path written into an older delta manifest (checkpoint_full.path) can point at a monthly's pre-move location; resolve it by its release. The delta manifests in the frozen v1/1.0/ keep their 1.0.1 bytes, so their paths name the old v1/datasets/ and v1/deltas/ keys and their checkpoint_full always says 2026-10; use that line's index.json (each monthly's source_release) instead.
  • CDN purges. r2-rollover.sh purges every path it moved or deleted, or the edge would keep serving a moved small file for up to the 1-month immutable TTL (ADR 0005). run-release.sh purges the parquet/ prefix after every Parquet rebuild. The one-time 1.1.0 migration (republish-v1.sh) ends with a full purge; each of its steps is user-confirmed, with a dry run first. The rollover itself runs inside run-release.sh; --dry-run or --listing shows its plan first.
  • Cache rules. src/scripts/cf-rules.sh holds the expressions (show is read-only; apply is a user-confirmed step). Three cache rules, in this order; the last matching rule wins:
  • "R2 immutable artifacts" matches every path on data.clinvar-gkm.org: edge 1 month, browser 1 day. In effect it covers whatever rules 2 and 3 do not: dated monthlies, deltas, delta manifests and .sha256 sidecars outside weekly/, everything in archive/YYYY/, and frozen line folders' bundles and MANIFEST.json. These are write-once at their path; a rollover moves them to new keys and purges the old ones.
  • "R2 mutable pointers" bypasses the cache for any path containing 00-latest (which also matches clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz), ending in /index.json, /feed.xml or /README.txt, or containing /weekly/. Weekly fulls and their sidecars are not cached as immutable, because the rollover deletes them.
  • "Latest Parquet" matches any path under /v1/ containing /parquet/ (the dataset and its manifest.json): edge 1 day, browser 1 hour (ADR 0005), purged after every rebuild. It replaces the rule that matched /v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/, which no longer exists.

Bundles larger than 512 MB are never cached on the Free plan (ADR 0005), so these rules matter mostly for sidecars, manifests, indexes and Parquet. - Path allowlist. Every published path stays under /v1/, so the WAF path allowlist needs no new prefix. /archive/ can be dropped from it once archive/1.0.1/ has moved (cf-rules.sh apply --drop-archive). - Storage. Weekly fulls add up to five bundles of about 4.8 GB each at the end of a month, about $0.36 a month at most. Dropping the dated Parquet sets saves about 65 GB. - Tools that read the layout (the docs download browser, the DuckDB console, generate-r2-index.sh, the uploaders, clinvar-gkm-parquet) change with it. - ADR 0008 is amended: the immutability exception for weekly fulls, archives as archive/YYYY/ inside a line, the 1.0.1 generation as v1/1.0/, and one overwritten Parquet dataset with no Parquet in archives.

items.title: 0010 — Automated monthly release announcements
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-28
  • Amends: ADR 0004 §7 (the email list and Discussions carry the same announcements; this makes the monthly one automatic)

items.title: Context
items.text:
The email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org (a Google Group) and GitHub Discussions → Announcements are the two announcement channels (ADR 0004 §7), but nothing posted to them: the 2026-10-24 release went out without a notice. Weekly releases are too frequent to announce one by one. The official monthly full bundle (ADR 0002) is the natural checkpoint: it is the full a consumer starts from, and the weekly deltas since the previous monthly are what turned that one into this one.

Releases run by hand on a maintainer's machine (run-release.sh), so an announcement sent from there would depend on that machine being online and would put mail credentials on it.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. What is announced. Each new official monthly, once, with a digest of the weekly deltas after the previous monthly's source_release, up to and including this monthly's. Applied in order to the previous monthly they give this one, and every delta is listed in exactly one announcement. The digest gives each delta's release date, its added/updated/deleted record counts (the manifest's counts), its size and a direct link, and the email points to the Downloads pages, the line's index.json and feed.xml, and the Changelog.
  2. Where it runs. .github/workflows/announce-monthly.yml, every two hours and on demand. It reads only the published root index.json, the current line's index.json and the delta manifests (src/scripts/announce_monthly.py), so it announces exactly what consumers can download and needs nothing from the release machine. run-release.sh is unchanged; a new monthly is announced within about two hours.
  3. Which monthly is due. The newest official monthly of the current line, when its month is later than ANNOUNCE_AFTER (2026-10: monthlies published before this existed are never announced automatically) and later than every month already announced. A republish into a new version line therefore announces nothing.
  4. Both channels, each exactly once. The email goes over SMTP from releases@clinvar-gkm.org (not a person's account), and the same text is posted as a Discussion in Announcements with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN. Each channel is recorded in announced.json on the orphan branch ops/announcements as soon as it succeeds, so a re-run retries only what failed and never sends twice.
  5. Safe to try. A manual run is a dry run by default: the announcement goes to the job summary and an artifact. The repository variable ANNOUNCE_TO redirects the email (for a test send to yourself); unset, it is the list.

items.title: Setup (once)
items.text:
The sender is releases@clinvar-gkm.org, sent over SMTP through Resend's free plan (3,000 emails a month, 100 a day, SMTP included), so no person's mailbox or password is involved and nothing is paid for one email a month. Cloudflare's own Email Sending was considered and rejected: it needs the Workers Paid plan. Replies are forwarded by Cloudflare Email Routing (free) to a Broad Google Group of maintainers. Moving to another SMTP provider is a change of the secrets below only.

  1. Resend account. Sign up at resend.com with a maintainer's Broad address and invite the other maintainers, so the account doesn't depend on one person.
  2. Domain. Resend → Domains → Add Domain → clinvar-gkm.org. Add the DNS records it lists (DKIM TXT resend._domainkey, and the MX and SPF TXT on the send subdomain) in Cloudflare DNS as DNS only, then verify. Add _dmarc TXT v=DMARC1; p=none; in Cloudflare if no DMARC record exists.
  3. API key. Resend → API Keys → Create, with Sending access limited to clinvar-gkm.org.
  4. Replies. Cloudflare → clinvar-gkm.org → Email → Email Routing: enable it, add the maintainers' Broad group as a destination address (verified once, by a link mailed to it), and create the custom address releases forwarding to it.
  5. Let it post. In the clinvar-gkm Google Group, add releases@clinvar-gkm.org as a member with delivery No email (or allow it in Who can post) so its messages aren't held for moderation.
  6. GitHub. Settings → Environments → New environment announce; limit deployment branches to main. Secrets: SMTP_HOST = smtp.resend.com, SMTP_PORT = 465 (implicit TLS), SMTP_USERNAME = resend, SMTP_PASSWORD = the API key, ANNOUNCE_FROM = ClinVar-GKM Releases <releases@clinvar-gkm.org>.
  7. Test. Set the repository variable ANNOUNCE_TO to your own address. Run Monthly release announcement with month = 2026-10 and dry_run off: check the email, then delete the test Discussion and the 2026-10 entry on ops/announcements (or the branch). Delete ANNOUNCE_TO to send to the list.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Members hear about every monthly without anyone remembering to write it, and the digest is generated from the same index and manifests consumers use, so it can't drift from what is published.
  • Weekly releases are still not announced individually; a consumer who wants each one follows feed.xml.
  • Direct delta links in old announcements break when the deltas move (month rollover into deltas/YYYY-MM/, year rollover into archive/YYYY/, ADR 0009). The email says so and points to index.json, which always has the current paths.
  • Version releases, RFCs, corrections and events are still announced by hand.
  • A failed send shows as a failed workflow run; the next scheduled run retries it.

items.title: 0011 — Versioned documentation
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-19
  • Amends: ADR 0003 (which docs builds regenerate the Roadmap)
  • Amended: 2026-11-20 — dev removed; each version's data views read its own data line; a Previous Releases page (below)

items.title: Context
items.text:
The docs site was one build. Every docs merge to main overwrote the whole gh-pages branch, so the live site described main: the 1.2.0 profiles were documented before 1.2.0 was released, and a reader of the 1.1.0 data had no way to see the docs that matched it. A release deploy showed the tag's docs only until the next main run. Data lines already have folders (v1/1.1/, v1/1.2/, ADR 0009); the docs had nothing to match.

The maintainer set five requirements (2026-11-19), to be in place with the 1.1.0 docs before 1.2.0 ships: one docs version per minor line; the site root and the default are the latest release; main is still published, as dev, with its own colour and notice; existing unversioned links keep working; older releases are grey and say they aren't current.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. One docs version per release line, 1.1, 1.2, … — the same {major}.{minor} as the data line folder. A patch release (1.2.1) rebuilds its line's docs in place; patches never get their own version. The line's docs are built from its newest tag.
  2. dev is main, rebuilt on every docs merge, as today. It is never the default.
  3. Layout on gh-pages. One folder per version (1.1/, dev/), each a complete Zensical build with site_url set to …/clinvar-gkm/<version>/, so canonical links and sitemap.xml are per version. At the root, written by src/scripts/docs-versions.py:
    • versions.json (the format mike writes) lists the versions. The highest release line carries the alias latest, so a patch to an older line can't take latest from a newer one, and dev never has it.
    • index.html redirects to the latest release, keeping the query and #fragment.
    • 404.html is what GitHub Pages serves for any missing path. An unversioned link — every URL from before this change — goes to the same page in the latest release, or to its home when that page doesn't exist there. …/latest/<page> goes to that page in the latest release. A missing page inside a version goes to that version's home.
    • Anything else at the root is removed on every deploy (the first deploy removes the unversioned site); CNAME and .nojekyll are kept.
  4. The version selector is the theme's. [project.extra.version] provider = "mike" makes Zensical render the Material version selector from versions.json; switching versions keeps the reader on the same page when it exists in the other version. The mike tool itself isn't used: the workflow builds each version with zensical build and writes versions.json itself.
  5. Old / dev / latest is decided in the browser. docs/assets/js/versions.js reads versions.json on every page and compares the page's version to the latest alias. On dev it colours the header and tabs orange and shows a notice that the pages describe unreleased changes and aren't for production use; on an older release it colours them grey and shows a notice that this isn't the current version. Both notices link to the same page in the latest release, or its home. The latest release keeps the normal indigo. Nothing is baked into a build, so an older version turns grey on its own when a newer release ships, without being rebuilt. The result is cached for the browser tab so the next page doesn't flash indigo first.
  6. Older tags get the feature by overlay. src/scripts/build-versioned-docs.sh <ref> <version> <out> exports the ref's tree (the tag is never changed), copies in the files this feature owns (docs/overrides/main.html, partials/header.html, partials/source.html, 404.html, versions.js, versions.css) from the checkout running the build, sets site_url, adds the [project.extra.version] table if missing, regenerates the Roadmap, and runs zensical build --clean --strict and check-site-links.py. This is how 1.1, whose config predates versioning, gets the selector. A line whose tag lacks its docs is built from another ref. src/scripts/docs-line-sources.txt maps a release line to the ref its pages are built from and the release its header shows. The build script applies it on every trigger (release, schedule, dispatch), so the daily rebuild can't bring the tag's docs back. The 1.1.0 tag was cut on 1.0 without main's 1.1.0 docs: its pages give the pre-1.1 v1/datasets/… download URLs, which return 404, and its changelog has no 1.1.0 section. 1.1 is therefore built from 036bec2 (main right after the 1.1.0 forward-merge, #188) and shown as 1.1.0. Remove a line's entry when a newer tag of that line has correct docs; after changing the file, dispatch the line to rebuild it.
  7. Each version shows and links its own ref. The build sets [project.extra.source] to the ref it was built from: main (labelled with the build commit) for dev, the tag (or the line's label) for a release. The header's repository widget (partials/source.html) shows that ref and links …/tree/<ref>, instead of the latest GitHub release the theme fetches from the GitHub API; the stars and forks counts, which come from the same lookup, are dropped. edit_uri follows the ref the pages come from (edit/main/docs/ for dev, blob/<ref>/docs/ for a release, since a tag can't be edited); the edit and view buttons aren't enabled today. For a release, src/scripts/pin-repo-links.py rewrites the pages' links to this repository's files on main (/blob/main/…, /tree/main/…, /raw/main/…) in the exported tree to the ref the pages come from (the tag, or the line's source ref, so a 1.1 page links the 036bec2 files, where each linked path exists); a path the ref doesn't have stays on main and is listed in the build log. Links to issues, discussions, pull requests and releases stay as written: they are live, not versioned.

  8. When each version is deployed (.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml):

    Trigger Builds push to main touching the docs paths dev release: published for tag X.Y.Z (not a prerelease) X.Y from the tag; versions.json and latest updated daily schedule and discussion events dev, and the latest release from its newest tag workflow_dispatch, no inputs (on main) dev workflow_dispatch with ref and version that ref as that version, e.g. 1.1.0 as 1.1

    The latest release is rebuilt on the Roadmap triggers because the Roadmap is a live page (ADR 0003) and the latest release is the version most readers see. Older releases keep the Roadmap they had. 9. Publishing keeps the other versions. A run builds only its versions, then checks out gh-pages, replaces those folders, rewrites the root files and pushes; if another run pushed first, it starts again from the new tip. Runs are serialized per version (concurrency: deploy-docs-<version>), so a main merge can't cancel a release deploy.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Readers land on the docs for the data they can download today; unreleased changes are visible but marked. Every existing link and bookmark keeps working through the redirect.
  • A new release needs no docs step: publishing the GitHub release for X.Y.0 builds X.Y, makes it latest, and turns the previous line grey.
  • The release event runs the workflow file at the tag. A tag whose tree has the old whole-site deploy-docs.yml would overwrite every version with one unversioned build. Before publishing a release from a branch that predates this ADR — the 1.0 branch today — bring this workflow and its scripts (build-versioned-docs.sh, docs-versions.py, pin-repo-links.py) onto that branch, or remove its release trigger.
  • The overlay files must keep building against the oldest published docs version. A change to them is checked by building 1.1 from its tag (build-versioned-docs.sh 1.1.0 1.1 <out>).
  • Search is per version; results come from the version being read.
  • gh-pages gains one commit per deploy, as before.
  • One-time bootstrap after merge: the merge's own deploy publishes dev and removes the unversioned site (the root redirects to dev until a release exists); then dispatch the workflow with ref = 1.1.0, version = 1.1 to publish 1.1 as latest.

items.title: Amended 2026-11-20
items.text:
The sections above are kept as decided on 2026-11-19. The maintainer changed three things on 2026-11-20.

  1. No dev version (replaces §2 and the dev rows of §3, §5, §7 and §8). The dev docs weren't useful to readers, so main is no longer published. deploy-docs.yml has no push trigger; the daily schedule, the discussion events and a workflow_dispatch with no inputs rebuild only the latest release, from its newest tag; a release event and a dispatch with ref + version are unchanged. build-versioned-docs.sh and docs-versions.py accept only release lines X.Y. docs-versions.py drops any other entry from versions.json, so the next deploy removes the dev/ folder from gh-pages. Links to it already sent to readers (an announcement email links …/clinvar-gkm/dev/parquet/migrating-from-1.1/) keep working: the root 404.html sends …/dev/<page> to the same page in the latest release, or its home. versions.js and versions.css have only the latest and older states. A docs change reaches the site with a release, or by mapping the line to the fixed commit in docs-line-sources.txt (§6) and dispatching it.
  2. Each docs version shows its own data line. The download tables (r2-browser.js) and the live query console (duckdb-console.html) read the release line of the docs version in the page URL: the path segment after /clinvar-gkm/ (1.1) is looked up in the root index.json's versions. A URL without a version (a local build) or a version with no data line reads the current line. Before, every version showed the current line's files under prose about its own line. On a frozen line, the views whose files the freeze deleted (weekly fulls, Parquet) say so, with the freeze date from the line's MANIFEST.json, and link to the same page in the latest docs; the console no longer falls back to a hard-coded line. Both files join the overlay (§6), so rebuilding an older version ships them; they must keep the mount types older pages use.
  3. A Previous Releases page in Get the Data (docs/data-access/previous-releases.md) lists every line the root index.json marks frozen, newest first: its schema version, superseded_by, freeze date, links to its index.json, feed.xml, README.txt and MANIFEST.json, its monthlies and its deltas. The list is read at page load, so a line frozen later appears with no docs edit. It renders only on the docs of the current line; an older version's copy points to the latest docs.

The 1.2 docs gain the page by mapping 1.2 in docs-line-sources.txt to the 1.0 commit that adds it, shown as 1.2.0 (§6), and dispatching 1.2; dispatching 1.1 rebuilds it with the new data views.

items.title: Amended 2026-11-21
items.text:
The 2026-11-20 amendment is kept as written. The maintainer changed its item 3 on 2026-11-21, after reviewing the published 1.2 and 1.1 docs: the earlier lines were hard to find, and the 1.1 docs sent readers to the 1.2 docs for them.

  1. Each docs version lists the lines before its own (replaces "renders only on the docs of the current line"). On docs version X.Y, the Previous Releases list shows the lines the root index.json marks frozen whose number is lower than X.Y, newest first; never X.Y itself or a newer line. The latest (1.2) docs list 1.1 and 1.0; the 1.1 docs list only 1.0; a version with no earlier line says so. A page whose URL has no version (a local build) uses the current line. The download tables and the console still read X.Y's own line (item 2).
  2. The Get the Data landing page shows them inline. download.md has a Previous Releases section with a compact table of the same lines (data-r2-type="previous-summary": line, schema, status with superseded_by and freeze date, links to index.json, feed.xml, README.txt and MANIFEST.json), each linking to its monthlies and deltas on the Previous Releases page. The monthly, weekly full, delta and Parquet pages carry a one-line pointer to it.
  3. The 1.1 docs get the page too. Their content comes from 036bec2 (§6), which predates it, so docs-line-sources.txt maps 1.1 to the tip of the long-lived branch docs/line-1.1: 036bec2 plus the Previous Releases page, its nav entry, the landing-page section and the pointers, worded for the 1.1 line. Every other 1.1 page is unchanged. A later fix to the 1.1 docs is a commit on that branch, then a remap to its new tip and a dispatch of 1.1. Keep the branch: deploy-docs.yml checks out with fetch-depth: 0, which fetches every branch, and git archive needs the commit to be reachable.
  4. A frozen line's console shows no tables. A frozen line keeps no Parquet (ADR 0008), and the console's examples are written for the current tables, so on a frozen line's docs the console says at once that the line keeps no Parquet set and links the latest docs' console and Parquet Files page, even while the line's old set is still on R2 before its deletion.

items.title: 0012 — Documentation examples must run, and say what they need
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-21
  • Decided: 2026-11-22 (maintainer)
path: 0012 — Documentation examples must run, and say what they need

items.title: Context
items.text:
The docs carry about 120 runnable code blocks (shell, Python, SQL, R) across about 25 pages: downloading bundles and Parquet, querying with DuckDB, reading records with the GA4GH Python libraries, building Parquet with gkm-bundle-parquet, and running the release pipeline. Readers copy them as written. Nothing checked them: an example could break when a URL moved between data lines, a column was renamed, a package changed, or an earlier block it relied on was edited, and the page gave no sign. Some examples also assumed tools the page never named (a DuckDB extension, a Python package, a GNU-only command on macOS), so a new reader couldn't tell what to install.

Two pages already open with a !!! note "Prerequisites" admonition; most don't.
path: 0012 — Documentation examples must run, and say what they need

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. Every runnable example runs as written against the published data of the docs line it belongs to (the v1/{major}.{minor}/ folder the page describes), on macOS and Linux, in a clean environment set up the way the page says. A block that isn't meant to run as written (a fragment, pseudocode, a template with placeholders) is fenced as text, or says so in the sentence that introduces it. Examples use URLs that keep working: a stable name (…_00-latest…), a file that never moves, or a dated file looked up in the line's index.json. A path that moves (a current-month delta, which moves to its month's folder when the month ends; a weekly full, which is deleted at rollover; ADR 0009) is not written into a command. curl runs with -f, so a missing file fails instead of being saved as an error page.
  2. Every page with a runnable example states its prerequisites before the first example, in a !!! note "Prerequisites" admonition, or links to the page that does. It names:
    • each tool and package, with its install command or a link to its install page;
    • the language or tool version the examples were tested with (Python, DuckDB, R, gkm-bundle-parquet), and the minimum when one is known;
    • the data each example reads, with a link to where to download it;
    • access the reader must already have (a GCP project, bq auth, R2 credentials), on maintainer pages;
    • expected download size, disk, memory and run time when they exceed what a laptop handles in a minute or two (a full bundle is about 5 GB compressed and must be streamed, not loaded).
  3. Dependencies between blocks are stated. A block that uses a variable, view, macro, file or function made by an earlier block says which one ("continues from Load the bundle above").
  4. Platform differences are handled in the example. Use a portable command or show both forms (sha256sum / shasum -a 256); don't use GNU-only flags without a macOS note.
  5. Examples that cost money or write somewhere say so. Maintainer commands that run billable BigQuery jobs, write to GCS or R2, or execute Cloud Run jobs carry a warning and name the access they need. Reader-facing examples never need credentials.
  6. Shown output matches the current release. text output blocks and prose that describe results (column names, counts, shapes) are refreshed when the data line changes; counts may be marked as approximate.
  7. Verification. The examples on a page are run when the page changes, and every runnable example on the latest line is run before a minor release's docs are published. Frozen older lines (ADR 0008) are not retrofitted; their pages already say they aren't current.
path: 0012 — Documentation examples must run, and say what they need

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Writing an example now includes running it from a clean environment and filling in the page's Prerequisites note. Reviewers can ask for both.
  • Release prep gains a step: run the latest line's examples before its docs publish (ADR 0011). Until it is automated this is a manual pass; a follow-up should add a script that extracts the fenced blocks and runs them against a small fixture (a delta bundle, a Parquet sample) in CI, with the release-time pass covering the full-size data.
  • Pages pin the versions they were tested with, so a dependency release that breaks an example shows up as a version mismatch rather than a silent failure.
  • The 2026-11-21 audit that prompted this ADR, and the fixes it led to, are recorded in the pull request that adds it.
path: 0012 — Documentation examples must run, and say what they need

items.title: Variations
items.text:
What this page answers

How a ClinVar variation is represented: its name, its VRS allele or location, its HGVS and other expressions, its genes and its cross-references. Read it when you match ClinVar variants to your own data, or follow a statement's subject to the variant it is about.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The variation bundle section contains one record per ClinVar variation. Each record represents a ClinVar variation and its relationship to a resolved VRS genomic identity, along with expressions, cross-references, gene associations, and ClinVar metadata.

ClinVar variations are represented using the GA4GH Cat-VRS (Categorical Variation) specification (glossary). Their precise genomic forms are VRS alleles and locations, in the allele, location and copy number sections. Cat-VRS defines categorical variant types that group variants at a higher level than individual VRS alleles — bridging the gap between ClinVar's variation concept and VRS's precise genomic representations.

This section is produced by the Cat-VRS procedure.

items.title: Variation Types
items.text:
Every record has type CategoricalVariant and validates against one of four ClinVar profiles, in three groups:

  • CanonicalAllele (ClinvarCanonicalAllele) — The vast majority of ClinVar variations. ClinVar identifies each variation by mapping submitted variant attributes to a GRCh38 genomic allele (falling back to GRCh37 or NCBI36 for historical data).
