This defining allele becomes the DefiningAlleleConstraint, and the same genomic allele generates the VRS allele referenced via #/allele/. See the Cat-VRS CanonicalAllele specification.

  • Categorical CNV (ClinvarCategoricalCnvCount and ClinvarCategoricalCnvChange, two profiles) — Copy number variants use a DefiningLocationConstraint following the same identification approach, with an additional CopyCountConstraint when an absolute copy count is provided, or a CopyChangeConstraint when only gain/loss is indicated.

  • Non-constrained variant (ClinvarNonConstrainedVariant) — Haplotypes, genotypes, and other complex or ambiguously defined variants that cannot yet be mapped to a specific VRS allele or location. These rely solely on the ClinVar variation ID to distinguish them. Work continues within the GA4GH GKS workstream to expand VRS and Cat-VRS coverage for these types as community need arises.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a CategoricalVariant that validates against one of the four ClinVar profiles in ClinvarCategoricalVariant — ClinvarCanonicalAllele, ClinvarCategoricalCnvChange, ClinvarCategoricalCnvCount, or ClinvarNonConstrainedVariant. The profiles allow these top-level fields, and no description or aliases:

Field Type Description id string ClinVar-scoped identifier — clinvar:{variation_id} type string Always CategoricalVariant name string The ClinVar display name for the variation — e.g., NM_006269.2(RP1):c.2238_2239del (p.Lys746_Ser747insTer). See Where a Value Comes From constraints array Defining constraints linking to the resolved VRS variant. Absent on generalized variants. See Constraints mappings array Cross-references to external databases. See Mappings members array A pointer to the resolved VRS variant: #/allele/ for a CanonicalAllele, #/copyNumberChange/ or #/copyNumberCount/ for a copy number variant. Absent on generalized variants extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific metadata and supplementary data (0..*). See Extensions

items.title: Constraints
items.text:
The constraints array defines the relationship between the variation and its resolved VRS representation. The constraint type depends on the variant class:

Variation Type Constraint Type Key Fields CanonicalAllele DefiningAlleleConstraint allele — #/allele/{id} reference to a VRS Allele CategoricalCnvChange DefiningLocationConstraint + CopyChangeConstraint location — #/location/{id} reference; copyChange — loss or gain CategoricalCnvCount DefiningLocationConstraint + CopyCountConstraint location — #/location/{id} reference; copies — an integer Generalized None No VRS constraint — identified by ClinVar variation ID only

Each constraint is a ClinVar profile: ClinvarDefiningAlleleConstraint, ClinvarDefiningLocationConstraint, ClinvarCopyChangeConstraint, and ClinvarCopyCountConstraint. Their relations and match characteristic are fixed codings: liftover_to and transcribed_to (ClinvarLiftoverToRelation, ClinvarTranscribedToRelation) and is_within (ClinvarIsWithinMatch).

items.title: Allele Constraint Example
items.text:
The DefiningAlleleConstraint references a VRS Allele in the allele bundle section:

{
  "type": "DefiningAlleleConstraint",
  "allele": "#/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY",
  "relations": [
    {
      "type": "MappableConcept",
      "primaryCoding": { "code": "liftover_to", "system": "ga4gh-gks-term:allele-relation" }
    },
    {
      "type": "MappableConcept",
      "primaryCoding": {
        "code": "transcribed_to",
        "system": "http://www.sequenceontology.org/",
        "iris": ["http://www.sequenceontology.org/browser/current_release/term/transcribed_to"]
      }
    }
  ]
}

items.title: Location Constraint Example
items.text:
The DefiningLocationConstraint for copy number variants references a VRS Location:

{
  "type": "DefiningLocationConstraint",
  "location": "#/location/ga4gh:SL.5-SKfXZ941W7JbZW3UmQKtijyUfd6d7z",
  "matchCharacteristic": {
    "type": "MappableConcept",
    "primaryCoding": { "code": "is_within", "system": "ga4gh-gks-term:location-match" }
  },
  "relations": [
    {
      "type": "MappableConcept",
      "primaryCoding": { "code": "liftover_to", "system": "ga4gh-gks-term:allele-relation" }
    }
  ]
}

items.title: Mappings
items.text:
The mappings array contains cross-references to external databases. Each mapping is a ClinvarVariationMapping with a coding (database, identifier, IRIs) and one of three relation values:

Relation Meaning exactMatch The ClinVar self-reference — links back to the ClinVar variation page closeMatch ClinGen allele registry identifiers relatedMatch All other external databases (dbSNP, OMIM, UniProtKB, GTR, PharmGKB, etc.)

items.title: Example
items.text:
{
  "coding": {
    "system": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/",
    "code": "1799945",
    "iris": ["https://identifiers.org/dbsnp:rs1799945"]
  },
  "relation": "relatedMatch"
}

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Extensions carry ClinVar-specific metadata not part of the core Cat-VRS specification. Each extension follows the GA4GH Extension structure: { "name": "<name>", "value": <value> }, and each is a closed class with a fixed name and a typed value. Variation extensions appear on the CategoricalVariant record; the assembly extension appears on records of the sequenceReference section.

See Categorical Variant Extensions (Pipeline) for details on how these extensions are built during pipeline processing.

items.title: CategoricalVariant Extensions
items.text: Extension Name Value Type Description categoricalVariationType string The Cat-VRS category assigned to this variation: CanonicalAllele, CategoricalCnvChange, CategoricalCnvCount, or Undefined. Determines which constraint types are generated. definingVrsVariationType string The VRS class assigned during variation identity processing: Allele, CopyNumberChange, CopyNumberCount, Haplotype, Unknown, or Not Available. Reflects the upstream classification used to route the variant through VRS processing. clinvarVariationType string The variation type as reported by ClinVar (e.g., Deletion, single nucleotide variant, Duplication, Indel). Present when ClinVar provides a variation type. clinvarSubclassType string The variation subclass as reported by ClinVar: SimpleAllele, Haplotype, or Genotype. Present when ClinVar provides a subclass type. clinvarCytogeneticLocation string The cytogenetic band location of the variation (e.g., 1p36.22, 17q21.31). Present when ClinVar provides a cytogenetic location. vrsPreProcessingIssue string Issues detected during VRS pre-processing of the variation's input expressions. Present only when issues exist. May contain multiple issues separated by newlines. vrsProcessingException string Errors returned by the external VRS Python processing service. Present only when errors occurred during VRS resolution. clinvarHgvsList array of HgvsListItem Complete list of HGVS expressions from ClinVar for this variation, including nucleotide and protein expressions, molecular consequences (SO terms), and MANE transcript designations. clinvarGeneList array of GeneListItem Gene associations for this variation from ClinVar, with #/gene/ references to gene MappableConcepts, relationship types, and sources.

items.title: SequenceReference Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on ClinvarSequenceReference records in the sequenceReference section, which variations reach through #/allele/ → #/location/ → #/sequenceReference/ pointers.

Extension Name Value Type Description assembly string The genome assembly of this sequence reference: GRCh38, GRCh37, or NCBI36.

items.title: HgvsListItem
items.text:
Each item in the clinvarHgvsList extension array represents one HGVS expression entry from ClinVar's HGVSlist element for the variation.

Field Type Description nucleotideExpression object A ClinvarNucleotideExpression: the nucleotide HGVS expression with syntax (e.g., hgvs.c, hgvs.g) and value (the HGVS string). From 1.1.0, when ClinVar supplies an expression with no HGVS type letter, its submitted text is kept, unaltered, in this expression's extensions: invalidClinvarExpression (the submitted text) with expressionMerged: true when ClinVar also supplies a valid expression for the accession, which is the one listed; otherwise originalClinvarExpression (the submitted text) with expressionRepaired: true, on a listed expression with the type letter restored. nucleotideType string The type of nucleotide expression as reported by ClinVar: coding, non-coding, genomic, or genomic, top-level. maneSelect boolean true if this transcript is designated as MANE Select. Absent when not applicable. manePlus boolean true if this transcript is designated as MANE Plus Clinical. Absent when not applicable. proteinExpression object A ClinvarProteinExpression: the protein HGVS expression with syntax (typically hgvs.p) and value, and no extensions. Present only when a protein-level expression exists for the nucleotide expression. ClinVar protein text with no HGVS type letter is labelled hgvs.p. molecularConsequence array Sequence Ontology terms describing the predicted molecular consequence. Each entry is a ClinvarMolecularConsequenceCoding with code (ClinVar's SO identifier, passed through as is), system (http://www.sequenceontology.org/), iris (identifiers.org link) and name (SO term label). name is absent for an SO code outside the pipeline's 18-term lookup.

items.title: GeneListItem
items.text:
Each item in the clinvarGeneList extension array represents one gene association for the variation. Gene details (symbol, NCBI Gene ID, HGNC mapping) are on the referenced gene MappableConcept in the gene bundle section.

Field Type Description gene string #/gene/ncbigene:{id} reference to the gene MappableConcept in the gene bundle section. relationship_type string The relationship between the variation and the gene as reported by ClinVar (e.g., within single gene, genes overlapped by variant). source string The source of the gene association: submitted or calculated.

items.title: ID References
items.text:
What this page answers

What each identifier in a bundle means, and how to follow a #/section/key pointer to the record it names. Read it when you write code that joins records, or decode a VCV or RCV statement id.

items.title: Overview
items.text: The ClinVar-GKM bundle uses typed identifiers and #/ JSON pointer references to link objects across bundle sections. This page documents all identifier formats, reference patterns, and how to resolve them.

items.title: Identifier Namespaces
items.text:
All ClinVar-GKM identifiers use a prefix namespace to indicate the resource type:

Prefix Resource Type Format Example clinvar: Variation clinvar:{variation_id} clinvar:12582 clinvar.submission: SCV submission clinvar.submission:SCV{id}.{version} clinvar.submission:SCV001571657.2 clinvar.submitter: Submitter organization clinvar.submitter:{submitter_id} clinvar.submitter:508027 clinvar.trait: Condition / trait clinvar.trait:{trait_id} clinvar.trait:9580 clinvar.traitset: Condition set (conditionSet) clinvar.traitset:{trait_set_id} clinvar.traitset:1234 clinvar.conditionset: Condition set minted for a VCV aggregate clinvar.conditionset:vcv-{md5} clinvar.conditionset:vcv-c620785e2025efde81bdd15c814fa83d clinvar.therapy: Therapy (drug/procedure) clinvar.therapy:{sha256} clinvar.therapy:ab221549…d1c2b clinvar.therapygroup: Therapy group (combination) clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256} clinvar.therapygroup:df1d8467…9f05c ncbigene: Gene ncbigene:{gene_id} ncbigene:3077 ga4gh: VRS identity ga4gh:{type}.{digest} ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY SQ. Sequence reference SQ.{digest} SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV

VCV and RCV aggregate statement IDs use a hierarchical format without a namespace prefix — see VCV Statement IDs and RCV Statement IDs.

items.title: JSON Pointer References
items.text:
Objects reference each other using #/{section}/{key} strings. To resolve a reference:

  1. Split the string on / — the second segment is the bundle section name, the third is the key
  2. Look up the key in the named section of the bundle

items.title: Reference Patterns
items.text: Pattern Example Target Section #/sequenceReference/{key} #/sequenceReference/SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV sequenceReference #/location/{key} #/location/ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ location #/allele/{key} #/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY allele #/gene/{key} #/gene/ncbigene:3077 gene #/variation/{key} #/variation/clinvar:10 variation #/condition/{key} #/condition/clinvar.trait:9580 condition #/conditionSet/{key} #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:1234 conditionSet #/therapy/{key} #/therapy/clinvar.therapy:ab221549…d1c2b therapy #/therapyGroup/{key} #/therapyGroup/clinvar.therapygroup:df1d8467…9f05c therapyGroup #/submitter/{key} #/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500139 submitter #/propositionPathogenicity/{key} #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH propositionPathogenicity #/propositionOncogenicity/{key} #/propositionOncogenicity/SCV002345678-ONCO propositionOncogenicity #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/{key} #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/SCV003456789-TR propositionSomaticClinicalImpact #/propositionClinvarCustom/{key} #/propositionClinvarCustom/SCV004567890-RF propositionClinvarCustom #/scv/{key} #/scv/clinvar.submission:SCV001234567.1 scv #/vcv/{key} #/vcv/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP vcv #/evidenceLine/{key} #/evidenceLine/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP.contributing evidenceLine #/rcv/{key} #/rcv/RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP rcv

items.title: Where References Appear
items.text:
Object Type Field References Location sequenceReference #/sequenceReference/ Allele location #/location/ Variation members[] #/allele/ Variation constraints[].allele #/allele/ Variation constraints[].location #/location/ Variation extensions[].clinvarGeneList[].gene #/gene/ Proposition (all types) subject #/variation/ Pathogenicity / Oncogenicity / Custom / Diagnostic / Prognostic object #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ Therapeutic Response object #/therapy/ or #/therapyGroup/ Therapeutic Response conditionQualifier #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ ConditionSet concepts[] #/condition/, or #/conditionSet/ for a TraitSet nested in a minted vcv- set TherapyGroup concepts[] #/therapy/ SCV Statement proposition #/proposition{Pathogenicity,Oncogenicity,SomaticClinicalImpact,ClinvarCustom}/ SCV Statement contributions[].contributor #/submitter/ VCV Statement proposition #/proposition{Pathogenicity,Oncogenicity,SomaticClinicalImpact,ClinvarCustom}/ SCV Statement hasEvidenceLines[] #/evidenceLine/ VCV Statement hasEvidenceLines[] #/evidenceLine/ RCV Statement proposition #/proposition{Pathogenicity,Oncogenicity,SomaticClinicalImpact,ClinvarCustom}/ RCV Statement hasEvidenceLines[] #/evidenceLine/ EvidenceLine hasEvidenceItems[] #/scv/, #/vcv/, or #/rcv/

Releases before 1.1.0 had two bare-id references

From 1.1.0 every field above is a #/ pointer. Before, two condition references were bare ids: a VCV proposition's object when the VCV had a single condition (clinvar.trait:2478 rather than #/condition/clinvar.trait:2478; about 7.5 million propositions), and the concepts of the condition sets minted for VCV aggregates (clinvar.conditionset:vcv-…). A bare id names the same record: look up clinvar.trait: ids in condition and clinvar.traitset: ids in conditionSet. A bundle downloaded before the 1.1.0 republish still has the old form.

The condition, conditionSet, direct_match and normalized_match values in the submittedCondition and submittedConditionSet extensions are bare CURIEs by design. They record what was submitted and how it was matched; they are not references.

items.title: Resolution Example
items.text:
Prerequisites

Python 3.9 or later (standard library only; tested with 3.14.5) and the 5 MB 2026-11-15 weekly delta, a 1.2.0 bundle:

Its path changes when its month ends, so the commands look it up in the line's index.json:

DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"] if d["release"] == "2026-11-15"))')
curl -fsO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"

A full bundle is 4.9 GB compressed and 68.5 GB decompressed: too big to json.load. Stream it, or cut out the records you need; see Large bundles.

import gzip
import json

# Load the bundle
with gzip.open("clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz", "rt") as f:
    bundle = json.load(f)

def resolve(bundle, ref):
    """Resolve a #/section/key reference to the target object."""
    section, key = ref.removeprefix("#/").split("/", 1)
    return bundle[section][key]

# Look up a variation
variant = bundle["variation"]["clinvar:5042631"]

# Resolve its allele member
allele = resolve(bundle, variant["members"][0])

# Resolve the allele's location
location = resolve(bundle, allele["location"])

print(variant["name"])
print(allele["id"], allele["name"])
print(location["id"], location["sequenceReference"])

# A delta carries only the records that changed, and this one has no sequenceReference section.
# In a full bundle, the last hop resolves the same way:
#     seq_ref = resolve(bundle, location["sequenceReference"])

NM_006269.2(RP1):c.2238_2239del (p.Lys746_Ser747insTer)
ga4gh:VA.1Oo5_TVyd33l8M9QsAac-ULaZR86hDCx NC_000008.11:g.54626120_54626121del
ga4gh:SL.sF-Pr6l0-_uRAtk8bv9UzOPYvr6TK9IC #/sequenceReference/SQ.209Z7zJ-mFypBEWLk4rNC6S_OxY5p7bs

From pointers to GA4GH models

Working in Python follows these pointers from a statement to its sequence reference and loads each record into the GA4GH model libraries. The GKM Toolkit resolves and exports pointers for the bundles its loader reads; the loader needs upstream updates before it reads ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0 or 1.2.0 bundles.

items.title: SCV Proposition IDs
items.text:
SCV proposition IDs combine the SCV accession with an uppercase proposition type code:

{scv_id}-{PROP_CODE}
Component Description Examples scv_id SCV accession (without version) SCV001234567 PROP_CODE Uppercase proposition type code PATH, ONCO, SCI, ASSOC, RF, DR, NP, OTH, PROTECT, AFF, CS, CDFS, UNDEF

Examples: SCV001234567-PATH, SCV004565358-PROG, SCV004565358-TR

Target (somatic evidence line) propositions use the clinical impact assertion type codes: PROG, DIAG, TR.

items.title: VCV Statement IDs
items.text:
VCV aggregate statements use a hierarchical ID format reflecting the aggregation layer:

Layer Format Example Classification {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP Priority {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} VCV000012582.63-S-SCI-CP Aggregate {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} VCV000012582.63-G-PATH

Components:

  • group — statement group: G (Germline), S (Somatic), O (Oncogenicity)
  • PROP — proposition type code (uppercase): PATH, ONCO, SCI, ASSOC, etc.
  • level — submission level: PG, EP, CP, NOCP, NOCL, FLAG
  • TIER — classification tier (somatic only, uppercase): TIER 1, TIER 2, etc.

items.title: RCV Statement IDs
items.text:
RCV aggregate statements follow the same pattern as VCV but with an RCV accession:

Layer Format Example Classification {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] RCV000012345.10-G-PATH-CP Priority {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} RCV000012345.10-S-SCI-CP Aggregate {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} RCV000012345.10-G-PATH

The component abbreviations are the same as VCV.

items.title: VCV/RCV Proposition IDs
items.text:
VCV and RCV proposition IDs use the accession (without version) in the same layered format:

Layer Format Example Classification {accession}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] VCV000012582-G-PATH-CP Priority {accession}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} VCV000012582-S-SCI-CP Aggregate {accession}-{group}-{PROP} VCV000012582-G-PATH

items.title: External Cross-References
items.text:
Variation records contain mappings to external databases using standardized URL formats:

Database URL Pattern MedGen https://identifiers.org/medgen:{id} OMIM http://www.omim.org/entry/{id} HPO https://identifiers.org/{id} MONDO https://identifiers.org/mondo:{id} Orphanet http://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_{id} dbSNP https://identifiers.org/dbsnp:rs{id} ClinGen https://reg.clinicalgenome.org/.../by_caid?caid={id} UniProtKB https://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/{id} GTR https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/tests/{id} PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/{id}

Condition records contain mappings to disease/phenotype databases (OMIM, MONDO, HPO, Orphanet, MeSH) and a primaryCoding from MedGen.

items.title: Output "Bundle" Format Overview
items.text:
What this page answers

How a ClinVar-GKM bundle is laid out: its sections, how one record points to another, and the schema that validates it. Read it first, before the statement and variation pages, or whenever you open a bundle or a Parquet table and need to know where a record lives. For the ideas behind the data, start with Key Concepts.

The ClinVar-GKM release file uses a bundle format — a single JSON object with named sections at the root level. A bundle is a dictionary-style approach to organizing a large amount of data across heterogeneous classes in a single file, where each section is a keyed collection of objects of the same class. The key is the object's unique identifier, and the value is the complete object.

This design eliminates duplication (a sequence reference shared by thousands of locations appears once), keeps individual objects compact, and enables efficient lookups by ID.

items.title: Orientation
items.text:
The 20 sections hold four kinds of record. Each record names the others it depends on with a #/section/key pointer, so a reader follows pointers from a statement down to the sequence:

Kind Sections What it holds Points to Statements scv, vcv, rcv A classification: one submission (SCV), or ClinVar's aggregate for a variant (VCV) or a variant and condition (RCV) Its proposition; its submitters; its evidence lines Evidence lines evidenceLine The statements an aggregate counts (contributing) or sets aside (non-contributing), and an SCV's somatic evidence The scv, vcv or rcv statements it cites; an SCV's line, the proposition it targets Propositions propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom What a statement claims: a variant (subject) related to a condition or therapy (object) — see proposition variation; condition, conditionSet, therapy or therapyGroup Variants and concepts variation, allele, copyNumberCount, copyNumberChange, location, sequenceReference, gene, condition, conditionSet, therapy, therapyGroup, submitter The ClinVar variation as a Cat-VRS categorical variant and its VRS alleles and locations; conditions and condition sets; therapies; submitters variation → allele, copyNumberCount, copyNumberChange or location; those → location → sequenceReference; variation → gene; conditionSet → condition or conditionSet

A typical path: an scv statement → its proposition → the variation it is about → that variation's allele → location → sequenceReference. A vcv or rcv statement reaches its SCVs through evidenceLine records. Every published bundle resolves every pointer; a delta holds only the records that changed, so some of its pointers name records in the full bundle.

items.title: Structure
items.text:
The root object, one key per section (a bundle carries only the sections it has records for):

{
  "sequenceReference": { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "location":          { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "allele":            { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "copyNumberCount":   { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "copyNumberChange":  { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "gene":              { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "variation":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "condition":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "conditionSet":      { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "therapy":           { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "therapyGroup":      { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "submitter":            { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionPathogenicity":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionOncogenicity":          { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionSomaticClinicalImpact": { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionClinvarCustom":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "evidenceLine":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "scv":               { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "vcv":               { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "rcv":               { "<key>": { ... }, ... }
}

items.title: Variation Data Sections
items.text:
These sections contain the VRS and Cat-VRS variant data:

sequenceReference — Reference sequences (chromosomes, transcripts) with refget accessions, molecule type, and assembly information. Keyed by refget accession (e.g., SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV).

location — Sequence locations with start/end coordinates. Each location references its sequence via #/sequenceReference/{key}. Keyed by VRS location ID (e.g., ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ).

allele — VRS alleles with state and expressions (SPDI, HGVS, gnomAD). Each allele references its location via #/location/{key}. Keyed by VRS allele ID (e.g., ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY).

copyNumberCount — VRS CopyNumberCount records for copy number variants with absolute copy counts. Each references its location via #/location/{key}. Keyed by VRS ID.

copyNumberChange — VRS CopyNumberChange records for copy number variants with relative change types (gain, loss). Each references its location via #/location/{key}. Keyed by VRS ID.

gene — Gene MappableConcepts with NCBI Gene primaryCoding and HGNC mapping. Keyed by ncbigene:{gene_id} (e.g., ncbigene:3077).

variation — ClinVar variations with their defining constraints, cross-references, HGVS expressions, and gene associations. Most variations are represented as CanonicalAlleles with a defining VRS allele (via #/allele/); copy number variants use a defining location (via #/location/); complex variants use a generalized representation. Keyed by clinvar:{variation_id} (e.g., clinvar:10).

items.title: Supporting Data Sections
items.text:
These sections contain the condition, therapy, submitter, and proposition reference data:

condition — Trait and disease concepts from ClinVar, with MedGen primary coding and cross-references to OMIM, MONDO, HPO, Orphanet, and MeSH. Keyed by clinvar.trait:{trait_id} (e.g., clinvar.trait:9580).

conditionSet — Multi-condition groupings with member references (concepts → #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/) and a membership operator (AND or OR). Keyed by clinvar.traitset:{trait_set_id} for a ClinVar trait set (e.g., clinvar.traitset:1234), or clinvar.conditionset:vcv-{md5} for a set minted for a VCV aggregate.

therapy — Individual drug therapies (Therapy MappableConcepts) referenced by therapeutic-response propositions. Content-addressed and deduplicated (therapies have no native ClinVar id). Keyed by clinvar.therapy:{sha256}.

therapyGroup — Combination (multi-drug) therapies (TherapyGroup ConceptSets) whose concepts reference member therapies via #/therapy/, with a membership operator. Content-addressed and deduplicated. Keyed by clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256}.

submitter — Submitting organizations with name and identifier. Keyed by clinvar.submitter:{submitter_id} (e.g., clinvar.submitter:500139).

propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom — Classification propositions defining what a statement asserts (proposition type, predicate, subject, object, qualifiers). Propositions are delivered in four sections grouped by meaning (what kind of claim the proposition makes), so a section holds one kind of claim at every level (SCV, VCV, RCV):

  • propositionPathogenicity — VariantPathogenicityProposition (germline classifications); subject → object (a #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/), with typed qualifiers on SCVs (geneContextQualifier, modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier).
  • propositionOncogenicity — VariantOncogenicityProposition; subject → object (the tumor type, a #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/).
  • propositionSomaticClinicalImpact — VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition (SCV, VCV, RCV) and the VariantDiagnosticProposition, VariantPrognosticProposition and VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition that SCV evidence lines target. For Therapeutic Response, object references the therapy (#/therapy/ single, or #/therapyGroup/ combination) and the condition moves to conditionQualifier (#/condition/ or #/conditionSet/); the others point object at a condition.
  • propositionClinvarCustom — the 9 Clinvar* types (e.g. ClinvarRiskFactorProposition, ClinvarDrugResponseProposition) plus ClinvarUndefinedProposition — open subtypes of the VA-Spec SubjectVariantProposition base, each carrying its own real type name; subject → object with typed qualifiers (geneContextQualifier, modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier).

Each contains the SCV, VCV, and RCV propositions of its kind. Keyed by proposition ID (e.g., SCV001234567-PATH for SCVs, VCV000012582-G-PATH-CP for VCVs). A #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} pointer names the exact section a proposition lives in; the section is a function of the proposition type alone.

items.title: Statement Sections
items.text:
These sections contain the classification statements:

evidenceLine — Evidence line records referenced by statements via hasEvidenceLines arrays of #/evidenceLine/ pointers. Merges SCV, VCV, and RCV evidence lines into a single section: somatic clinical impact SCV evidence lines are keyed clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{version}, and VCV and RCV evidence lines are keyed by their statement id plus .contributing or .non-contributing.

scv — Submitted classification statements. Each SCV carries a classification, strength, direction, proposition reference, contributions (with submitter references), evidence line references, citations, assertion method, and extensions with submitted condition provenance. Keyed by clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{version}.

vcv — Variation-level aggregate classification statements. VCVs aggregate SCVs across a variation by classification, priority (somatic tiers), and submission level contribution. Evidence line references point to records in #/evidenceLine/. Keyed by the VCV layer ID.

rcv — Condition-level aggregate classification statements. RCVs follow the same aggregation structure as VCVs but are scoped to a specific RCV accession (variation + condition). Evidence line references point to records in #/evidenceLine/.

items.title: JSON Pointer References
items.text: Objects reference each other using #/{section}/{key} strings instead of embedding full objects inline. This keeps the file compact and enables consumers to resolve references by looking up the key in the named section.

items.title: Reference Patterns
items.text: Pattern Example Resolves To #/sequenceReference/{key} #/sequenceReference/SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV Sequence reference object #/location/{key} #/location/ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ Sequence location object #/allele/{key} #/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY VRS allele object #/gene/{key} #/gene/ncbigene:3077 Gene object #/variation/{key} #/variation/clinvar:10 Categorical variant object #/condition/{key} #/condition/clinvar.trait:9580 Condition object #/conditionSet/{key} #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:1234 Condition set object #/submitter/{key} #/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500139 Submitter object #/propositionPathogenicity/{key} #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH Proposition object (pathogenicity) #/propositionOncogenicity/{key} #/propositionOncogenicity/SCV002345678-ONCO Proposition object (oncogenicity) #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/{key} #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/SCV003456789-TR Proposition object (somatic clinical impact) #/propositionClinvarCustom/{key} #/propositionClinvarCustom/SCV004567890-RF Proposition object (ClinVar custom) #/scv/{key} #/scv/clinvar.submission:SCV001234567.1 SCV statement object #/vcv/{key} #/vcv/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP VCV statement object #/rcv/{key} #/rcv/RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP RCV statement object

items.title: Resolving References
items.text:
To resolve a reference string like #/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123:

  1. Split on / — the second segment is the section name (allele), the third is the key (ga4gh:VA.abc123)
  2. Look up the key in the named section of the root object
  3. The value at that key is the resolved object

items.title: Reference Depth
items.text: References are one level deep — a resolved object may itself contain references, but those are always to other root-level sections, never nested references within references. A consumer can fully resolve any object by following at most 2-3 hops (e.g., variation → allele → location → sequenceReference).

items.title: MappableConcept Pattern
items.text:
Several fields across statements use a MappableConcept structure — a typed object with a display name, optional primary coding, and optional extensions:

{
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Pathogenic",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "pathogenic",
    "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015"
  },
  "extensions": [ ... ]
}

Fields that use this pattern:

  • classification — the clinical significance label (conceptType: "Classification")
  • strength — the evidence strength (conceptType: "Strength")
  • quality — the quality of the assessment, from the review status or submission level (conceptType: "Quality")
  • evidenceOutcome — the evidence line outcome (conceptType: "Outcome")
  • strengthOfEvidenceProvided — the evidence line strength (conceptType: "Strength")

The conceptType identifies the kind of concept. The name is the human-readable display value. The primaryCoding provides a machine-readable code and system when available. SCV classifications and strengths may carry primaryCoding; aggregate VCV/RCV classifications and strengths, qualities, evidence outcomes, and evidence line strengths have only conceptType and name (plus extensions where their class defines them). Each field's ClinVar profile is listed on its Data Model class page.

items.title: Bundle Schema
items.text:
The bundle structure described above is formalized as a JSON Schema, authored to the GKM Starter Kit bundle-schema conventions:

JSON Schema: clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json

  • Draft 2020-12, root type: object — each root property is one of the bundle sections, and additionalProperties: false rejects unknown sections.
  • Each section is a keyed map whose keys must match the exact id format the pipeline builds (patternProperties — for example ^ga4gh:VA\.[0-9A-Za-z_-]{32}$ for allele and ^clinvar\.submission:SCV[0-9]{9}\.[0-9]+$ for scv), and whose values $ref a ClinVar profile by versioned W3ID URI — ClinvarAllele, ClinvarCondition, ClinvarScvStatement, the ClinvarVariant*Proposition profiles, and so on. Every section points at a ClinVar profile; the evidenceLine section picks ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine or ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine by key.
  • No section is individually required, so the same schema validates a monthly full bundle, a weekly delta, and a sub-bundle extract — each carries only the sections it touches.

Each ClinVar profile is its GA4GH class narrowed to exactly what the pipeline writes, so a record that validates is also a valid GA4GH record. An Implementation Schema explains the narrowing and its rules.

The schema constrains the bundle's shape (which sections may appear, how their keys are formed, and what each value validates against). The starter-kit's companion invariant — that every #/section/key pointer resolves within the bundle — is a producer-side guarantee, not expressible in JSON Schema alone.

items.title: Validating with the GKM Toolkit
items.text: The GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) validates a bundle against this schema when you supply the ClinVar-GKM schemas and the GA4GH schemas they reference, as a validator= for validate_bundle_schema. Every published bundle is validated this way before release (Release Validation); Working in Python shows the code. The toolkit's loader (load_bundle, resolve, export) needs upstream updates before it reads ClinVar-GKM bundles.

items.title: Parquet Output
items.text:
In addition to the JSON bundle, the latest release is published as typed Parquet files, one per bundle section (20 tables). They are built from the published bundle by gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0, not by the assembler. Every property of a record is a typed column, named after the bundle property, with references as bare ids, which makes them suitable for analytical workloads, DuckDB, pandas, or Apache Spark. The tables hold the records without loss: the tool rebuilds the bundle's records from them.

See Export & Distribute for how the Parquet files are produced (derived from the bundle, latest release only). To query them — every table's columns, how the tables join, and runnable recipes — see Query the Data.

items.title: Inlining References
items.text: A #/section/key reference resolves with one dictionary lookup in the bundle; ID References shows a small resolve() helper, and Working in Python follows a statement down to its sequence reference. The GKM Toolkit's Bundle.export() inlines references for the bundles it can load; its loader does not yet read ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0 bundles (see Loading bundles).

items.title: RCV Statements
items.text:
What this page answers

What ClinVar's aggregate says about one variant for one condition. Read it when you need a condition-specific classification (for example, a variant's pathogenicity for cystic fibrosis rather than across all its conditions). It builds on VCV Statements, which explains the layers.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The rcv bundle section contains one record per condition-level aggregate classification. Each record is a Statement that aggregates individual SCV submissions for the same variant and condition into a hierarchical summary — combining classifications across submission levels to produce a single condition-specific result. RCV is ClinVar's variant-and-condition record.

RCV statements differ from VCV statements in one important way: condition-scoped aggregation — each RCV is scoped to a specific condition (identified by trait_set_id), whereas VCV statements aggregate across all conditions for a variant. The condition is a #/condition/ record or a conditionSet.

RCV statements use #/ references for propositions, contributing SCVs, and lower-level RCV groupings. They are produced by the RCV Procedures.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a Statement with the following top-level fields:

Field Type Description id string RCV layer ID — e.g., RCV001781420.1-G-PATH-CP type string Always Statement proposition string #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} reference to the aggregate proposition (the section is set by the proposition type; see ID References) classification object MappableConcept — the aggregate classification label and its primaryCoding. See Classification strength object MappableConcept — the aggregate evidence strength direction string supports, disputes, or neutral — the direction the SCVs carry for the aggregate classification. See VCV Direction quality object Concept struct with conceptType: "Quality" and name (the submission level label, e.g., criteria provided, expert panel) extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific aggregate metadata (0..*). See Extensions hasEvidenceLines array #/evidenceLine/ references to contributing and non-contributing evidence. See Evidence Lines

The classification, strength, direction, and quality fields follow the same structure and rules as VCV Statements.

items.title: Classification
items.text:
RCV statements use the same MappableConcept classification as VCV:

{
  "type": "MappableConcept",
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "pathogenic/likely pathogenic",
    "system": "ClinVar"
  }
}

For somatic clinical impact (SCI) propositions, the classification label may include the tier, assertion type, and clinical significance.

primaryCoding (from schema 1.2.0) follows the same rules as VCV: see classification.primaryCoding. An SCI label is coded by its tier alone, without the assertion type, significance and count (Tier I (Strong) - diagnostic - supports diagnosis (1) → tier 1 / AMP/ASCO/CAP (AAC) Guidelines, 2017).

items.title: Proposition
items.text:
RCV propositions are delivered across the four proposition bundle sections (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) by meaning. Each RCV statement references its proposition via #/proposition<Meaning>/{id}.

A resolved RCV proposition contains:

Field Type Description type string Proposition type matching the underlying SCVs (e.g., VariantPathogenicityProposition) id string Proposition ID (e.g., RCV001781420-G-PATH-CP) subject string #/variation/clinvar:{id} reference predicate string Predicate matching the underlying SCVs (e.g., isCausalFor) object string #/condition/clinvar.trait:{id} or #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:{id} reference — the specific condition for this RCV

The key difference from VCV propositions: the object references the specific condition for this RCV accession, sourced from the representative SCV's condition mapping. A VCV proposition with several conditions references one OR condition set minted for the aggregate (see VCV Statements).

items.title: Evidence Lines
items.text:
Evidence lines work identically to VCV. The hasEvidenceLines field contains #/evidenceLine/ JSON pointer references to evidence line records in the evidenceLine bundle section:

{
  "hasEvidenceLines": [
    "#/evidenceLine/RCV001781420.1-G-PATH-CP.contributing",
    "#/evidenceLine/RCV001781420.1-G-PATH-CP.non-contributing"
  ]
}

At the Classification layer, evidence items within the referenced records point to SCVs via #/scv/. At the Priority and Aggregate Contribution layers, evidence items reference lower-level RCV groupings via #/rcv/.

See VCV Evidence Lines for the full field reference.

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Extensions carry aggregate metadata not part of the GA4GH VA-Spec statement model. Each extension follows the GA4GH Extension structure: { "name": "<name>", "value": <value> }. Extensions appear at two structural levels — on the top-level Statement and on the classification object.

RCV extensions follow the same patterns as VCV extensions. See RCV Extensions (Pipeline) for details on how these extensions are built during pipeline processing.

items.title: Statement Extensions
items.text: Extension Name Value Type Description clinvarReviewStatus string The aggregate review status derived from the submission level and aggregation outcome. Same value set as VCV Statement Extensions. Always present.

items.title: Classification Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on the classification MappableConcept within the Statement.

Extension Name Value Type Description conflictingExplanation string A formatted breakdown of conflicting classification counts (e.g., Pathogenic(3); Likely pathogenic(2)). Present only when the classification is conflicting.

items.title: SCI Classification Label Format
items.text:
For somatic clinical impact (SCI) propositions, the RCV aggregate classification label includes the tier, assertion type, and clinical significance:

<tier_label> - <assertion_type> - <clinical_significance> (<scv_count>)

Examples: Tier I - Strong - diagnostic - supports diagnosis (1), Tier II - Potential - prognostic - poor outcome (1)

items.title: Layer Hierarchy
items.text:
RCV statements use the same multi-layer aggregation hierarchy as VCV, with condition (trait_set_id) as an additional grouping dimension at every layer.

Layer ID Format Aggregates By Scope Classification {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] Classification label within submission level All Priority {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} Tier priority within submission level Somatic only Aggregate Contribution {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} Submission level (winner-takes-all) All

Submission level ranking is PG > EP > CP > NOCP > NOCL > FLAG.

See RCV Procedures for implementation details.

items.text:

  • RCV statement examples

items.title: SCV Statements
items.text:
What this page answers

What one submitter said about one variant: the classification, the condition as submitted, the method, citations and dates. Read it when you work with individual submissions, or need to see what lies under a VCV or RCV aggregate.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The scv bundle section contains one record per ClinVar submission (SCV). Each record is a VA-Spec Statement that captures a submitter's interpretation of a variant — including the classification, evidence, condition, variant, and method.

SCV statements use #/ references to link to propositions, submitters, and conditions in their respective bundle sections rather than embedding full objects inline.

This section is produced by the SCV Statements procedure.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a VA-Spec Statement with the following top-level fields:

Field Type Description id string SCV accession with version — clinvar.submission:SCV000123456.1 type string Always Statement proposition string #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} reference to the classification proposition (the section is set by the proposition type; see ID References) classification object MappableConcept — the submitter's classification. See Classification strength object MappableConcept — the evidence strength. See Strength direction string Whether the evidence supports, disputes, or is neutral toward the proposition quality object Concept struct with conceptType: "Quality" and name (the submission level label). See Quality description string Free-text interpretation summary (when provided by the submitter) contributions array Submitter and date information with #/submitter/ references. See Contributions specifiedBy object The classification method/guideline used. Its reportedIn is the method's citation Document, built like the statement's (including documentType). See Citations reportedIn array Supporting citations — one Document per ClinVar citation: a PubMed, DOI or Bookshelf reference, or a URL-only citation such as a CIViC evidence link. A Document carries documentType when ClinVar gives a citation type. See Citations extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific metadata (0..*). See Extensions hasEvidenceLines array Evidence lines for somatic clinical impact assertions. See Evidence Lines

items.title: Classification
items.text:
The classification field is a MappableConcept with the submitted classification:

{
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Pathogenic",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "pathogenic",
    "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015"
  },
  "extensions": [
    {
      "name": "description",
      "value": "for Hemochromatosis\nClassification is based on the criteria provided submission\nMay 2021 by Victorian Clinical Genetics Services"
    }
  ]
}

The primaryCoding provides the machine-readable classification code and system from the clinvar_clinsig_types lookup table. The extensions array contains a human-readable description summarizing the condition, submission level, evaluation date, and submitter.

items.title: Strength
items.text:
The strength field is a MappableConcept indicating the evidence strength:

{
  "conceptType": "Strength",
  "name": "Definitive",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "definitive",
    "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015"
  }
}

The primaryCoding is present when the strength can be mapped to a specific code in the classification system.

items.title: Quality
items.text:
The quality field is a Concept struct indicating the submission level:

{
  "conceptType": "Quality",
  "name": "criteria provided"
}
Field Type Description conceptType string Always "Quality" name string The submission level label (e.g., criteria provided, practice guideline, expert panel)

items.title: Contributions
items.text:
The contributions array records the submitter and key dates. Each contribution references the submitter via #/submitter/:

[
  {
    "type": "Contribution",
    "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500104",
    "date": "2022-12-24",
    "activityType": "submitted"
  },
  {
    "type": "Contribution",
    "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500104",
    "date": "2022-12-24",
    "activityType": "created"
  },
  {
    "type": "Contribution",
    "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500104",
    "date": "2021-05-06",
    "activityType": "evaluated"
  }
]

items.title: Citations
items.text:
reportedIn lists the submission's citations, and specifiedBy.reportedIn holds the citation for the assertion method. Each is a VA-Spec Document, one per ClinVar citation. A citation that ClinVar lists with several ids — ACMG 2015 has a PubMed id, a PMC id and a DOI — is a single Document:

{
  "type": "Document",
  "name": "ACMG, 2015",
  "documentType": "general",
  "pmid": "25741868",
  "doi": "10.1038/gim.2015.30",
  "urls": [
    "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25741868",
    "https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/4544753",
    "https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2015.30"
  ]
}
  • name is ClinVar's short label for the citation and documentType is ClinVar's citation type (general, practice guideline, review, Suggested Reading or file in FileTrack), both verbatim and present only when ClinVar gives them. The same holds for the method citation in specifiedBy.reportedIn
  • urls holds every resolvable URL, ClinVar's own URL first; a citation ClinVar gives only as a URL — a CIViC evidence link, for example — is {"type": "Document", "urls": ["https://civicdb.org/links/evidence/4846"]}
  • A citation that is only free text has no pmid, doi or urls. Its text is kept verbatim in the clinvarCitationText extension. Such text is often not a reference, e.g. a list of ACMG criteria.

The pipeline never changes ClinVar's citation data silently. When an invalid id is repaired, the Document's extensions keep the original:

{
  "type": "Document",
  "documentType": "general",
  "doi": "10.1155/2023/2564200",
  "urls": ["https://doi.org/10.1155/2023/2564200"],
  "extensions": [
    { "name": "originalClinvarCitation", "value": "doi:10.1155/2023/2564200" },
    { "name": "citationRepaired", "value": true }
  ]
}

An id that cannot be used, such as a DOI recorded as https, yields no doi or URL. It appears only as { "name": "invalidClinvarCitation", "value": "https" }. Method.reportedIn holds one Document. When ClinVar lists more than one citation for an assertion method, the first stays there and the rest are Documents in the Method's additionalClinvarMethodCitations extension. The full list of citation extensions and repair rules is on the Final Statements pipeline page.

items.title: Proposition
items.text:
SCV propositions are delivered across the four proposition bundle sections (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) by meaning, referenced by #/proposition<Meaning>/{id}. The proposition ID combines the SCV accession with an uppercase proposition type code:

SCV001234567-PATH

A resolved proposition contains:

Field Type Description id string Proposition ID (e.g., SCV001234567-PATH) type string Proposition type (e.g., VariantPathogenicityProposition) predicate string The relationship asserted (e.g., isCausalFor) subject string #/variation/clinvar:{id} reference object string The asserted object, as a reference. For most types: #/condition/clinvar.trait:{id} or #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:{id}. For VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition: #/therapy/clinvar.therapy:{sha256} (single) or #/therapyGroup/clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256} (combination) conditionQualifier string #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ reference — present on VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition (where object carries the therapy, so the condition moves to this qualifier) geneContextQualifier object Gene context: the variant's one representative gene, with NCBI Gene and HGNC identifiers. Its geneContextSource extension says where the gene came from. When the variant has no single gene, a placeholder named with the submitter's symbol and no coding modeOfInheritanceQualifier object Mode of inheritance with HPO coding (when submitted) penetranceQualifier object Penetrance qualifier (for low-penetrance/risk factor classifications)

items.title: Proposition Types
items.text:
Proposition Type Code Predicate Description VariantPathogenicityProposition PATH isCausalFor Germline pathogenicity/benignity VariantOncogenicityProposition ONCO isOncogenicFor Oncogenicity VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition SCI hasClinicalSignificanceFor Somatic clinical impact ClinvarAssociationProposition ASSOC isAssociatedWith Association ClinvarRiskFactorProposition RF isRiskFactorFor Risk factor ClinvarDrugResponseProposition DR hasDrugResponseFor Drug response ClinvarProtectiveProposition PROTECT isProtectiveFor Protective ClinvarAffectsProposition AFF hasAffectFor Affects ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition CS confersSensitivityFor Confers sensitivity ClinvarOtherProposition OTH isClinvarOtherAssociationFor Other ClinvarNotProvidedProposition NP hasNoProvidedClassificationFor Not provided ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition CDFS isConflictingDataFromSubmittersFor Conflicting data

For somatic clinical impact, target propositions (evidence line propositions) use these codes: PROG (Prognostic), DIAG (Diagnostic), TR (Therapeutic Response).

See Propositions for the full profile documentation.

items.title: Evidence Lines
items.text:
Evidence lines appear on somatic clinical impact (SCI) statements. Each evidence line carries a target proposition, direction, outcome, and condition extensions:

{
  "type": "EvidenceLine",
  "proposition": "#/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/SCV004565358-TR",
  "directionOfEvidenceProvided": "supports",
  "evidenceOutcome": {
    "conceptType": "Outcome",
    "name": "tier 1"
  },
  "extensions": [ ... ]
}

The evidenceOutcome is a MappableConcept with conceptType: "Outcome" indicating the tier classification for the target proposition.

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Extensions carry ClinVar-specific metadata not part of the GA4GH VA-Spec statement model. Each extension follows the GA4GH Extension structure: { "name": "<name>", "value": <value> }. Extensions appear at three structural levels — on the top-level Statement, on the classification object, and on proposition qualifier objects.

See SCV Extensions (Pipeline) for details on how these extensions are built during pipeline processing.

items.title: Statement Extensions
items.text:
Extension Name Value Type Description clinvarScvId string The ClinVar SCV accession without version (e.g., SCV001571657). Always present. clinvarScvVersion string The version number of the SCV submission (e.g., 2). Always present. submittedCondition SubmittedCondition Submitted condition provenance with normalization details, trait mapping, and the matched condition as a bare CURIE (clinvar.trait:{id}). Present when the SCV maps to a single condition. submittedConditionSet SubmittedConditionSet Submitted condition set provenance with multiple condition concepts. Present when the SCV maps to multiple conditions. clinvarScvReviewStatus string The ClinVar review status (e.g., criteria provided, single submitter). Present when the SCV has a review status. submittedScvClassification string The original classification text submitted by the submitter, preserved when it differs from the normalized classification name. Omitted when there is no submitted text. submittedScvLocalKey string The unique local key provided by the submitter for this submission. Present only when the submitter provided a local key. submissionLevel string The submission level code: PG, EP, CP, NOCP, NOCL, or FLAG. Present when the submission level can be determined.

Note

Only one of submittedCondition or submittedConditionSet is present per SCV — never both. The submittedScvClassification extension is omitted when the submitted classification matches the normalized label exactly, or when there is none.

items.title: Classification Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on the classification MappableConcept within the Statement.

Extension Name Value Type Description description string A formatted multi-line description summarizing the classification context: condition name, submission level, evaluation date, and submitter name. Always present.

The description template is: for <condition_name>\nClassification is based on the <submission_level_label> submission\n<evaluated_date> by <submitter_name>. When the submitter has no name, by <submitter_name> is left off, so the text is never empty.

items.title: Qualifier Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on proposition qualifier objects (geneContextQualifier, modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier), preserving the original submitter-provided values.

Extension Name Value Type Description submittedGeneSymbols array of string Gene symbols originally submitted by the submitter, verbatim, in submitted order. Present on geneContextQualifier when the submitter provided gene information. May differ from the normalized gene symbol. geneContextSource string Where the geneContextQualifier gene came from. Present on every geneContextQualifier. submittedSymbolMatches: the submitter's symbols include the qualifier's symbol. submittedSymbolDiffers: the submitter gave symbols, but none equals the qualifier's symbol; most are previous symbols of the same gene, so the genes are not necessarily different. inferredFromVariant: the submitter gave no symbols. submittedNotNormalized: the variant has no single representative gene, so the qualifier is a placeholder whose name is the submitter's symbol (several are joined with ,) and which has no primaryCoding. Symbols are compared after trimming spaces and ignoring case. The schema accepts only these four values (ClinvarGeneContextQualifier), on every proposition type. Added in 1.1.0; earlier placeholders are named submitted genes were not normalized. See the gene context FAQ. submittedModeOfInheritance string Mode of inheritance text as originally submitted. Present on all modeOfInheritanceQualifier objects, which are written only when the submitted text exists. Preserved alongside the normalized HPO coding. submittedClassification string Original submitted classification text that triggered the penetrance qualifier derivation. Present on all penetranceQualifier objects, which are written only when the submitted text exists.

items.title: SubmittedCondition
items.text:
The submittedCondition extension captures the provenance of how a single submitted condition was mapped to the normalized ClinVar trait. Present when the SCV maps to exactly one condition.

Field Type Description condition string CURIE of the resolved condition, clinvar.trait:{id}: the key of its record in the bundle's condition section, not a #/condition/… pointer. conditionSet string CURIE of a condition set, clinvar.traitset:{id} (a key in the conditionSet section). Usually absent; present when a single-trait submission maps to a multi-trait RCV. id string The submitted clinical assertion trait ID (e.g., SCV002769510.0). name string The submitted condition name. type string The submitted condition type (e.g., Disease, Finding). medgen_id string The submitted or resolved MedGen concept ID. original_medgen_match object The original MedGen match, with id and name, when the submitted MedGen ID was remapped to a different MedGen concept. Absent when no remapping occurred. direct_match string CURIE of the directly matched condition, clinvar.trait:{id}. Present only when it differs from normalized_match. normalized_match string CURIE of the final normalized condition, clinvar.trait:{id} (a key in the condition section). normalized_resolution string The resolution method used to match the submitted condition (e.g., tm reftype xref omim, random trait assignment). xrefs array Submitted cross-references with code and system. mapping object The trait mapping entry used for resolution: type, ref, value.

items.title: SubmittedConditionSet
items.text:
The submittedConditionSet extension captures provenance for multi-condition submissions. Present when the SCV maps to more than one condition.

Field Type Description conditionSet string CURIE of the resolved condition set, clinvar.traitset:{id} (a key in the conditionSet section). condition string CURIE of a condition, clinvar.trait:{id}. Usually absent; present when the RCV set resolves to a single trait. multiple_condition_explanation string ClinVar's explanation for the multi-condition grouping. concepts array One mapping per submitted condition, ordered by id, each with the fields of SubmittedCondition except condition and conditionSet.

items.text:

  • SCV statement examples — pathogenicity, oncogenicity, somatic clinical impact, therapeutic response, and other statement types

items.title: VCV Statements
items.text:
What this page answers

What ClinVar's variant-level aggregate says about one variant, and how it was reached from the submissions under it. Read it when you want ClinVar's overall classification of a variant, its review status, or which submissions counted towards it.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The vcv bundle section contains one record per variation-level aggregate classification. Each record is a Statement that aggregates individual SCV submissions into a hierarchical summary — combining classifications across submission levels to produce a single variation-level result. VCV is ClinVar's variant-level record; the aggregate review status is carried in the clinvarReviewStatus extension.

VCV statements use #/ references for propositions, contributing SCVs, and lower-level VCV groupings. They are produced by the VCV Procedures.

items.title: Layer Hierarchy
items.text:
VCV statements are built through a multi-layer aggregation hierarchy. The top-level output is the Aggregate Contribution layer; lower layers appear in the hasEvidenceItems of higher layers.

Layer ID Format Aggregates By Scope Classification {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] Classification label within submission level All Priority {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} Tier priority within submission level Somatic only Aggregate Contribution {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} Submission level (winner-takes-all) All

Submission level ranking at the Aggregate Contribution layer is PG > EP > CP > NOCP > NOCL > FLAG, with only matching submission levels aggregating together at the Classification layer.

The diagram below reads one statement id left to right and shows the layers for germline and somatic statements. It is drawn for the Parquet tables, whose ids, layers and levels are the bundle's.

See Aggregation Rules for detailed submission level logic and VCV Procedures for implementation details.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a Statement with the following top-level fields:

Field Type Description id string VCV layer ID — e.g., VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP type string Always Statement proposition string #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} reference to the aggregate proposition (the section is set by the proposition type; see ID References) classification object MappableConcept — the aggregate classification label and its primaryCoding. See Classification strength object MappableConcept — the aggregate evidence strength. See Strength direction string supports, disputes, or neutral — the direction the SCVs carry for the aggregate classification. See Direction quality object Concept struct with conceptType: "Quality" and name (the submission level label, e.g., criteria provided, expert panel) extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific aggregate metadata (0..*). See Extensions hasEvidenceLines array #/evidenceLine/ references to contributing and non-contributing evidence. See Evidence Lines

items.title: Classification
items.text:
The classification field is a MappableConcept with the aggregate classification label and its coding:

{
  "type": "MappableConcept",
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "conflicting classifications of pathogenicity",
    "system": "ClinVar"
  },
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "conflictingExplanation", "value": "Pathogenic(3); Uncertain significance(2)"}
  ]
}

The extensions array includes a conflictingExplanation when multiple contributing submissions have different clinical significance values. This extension is only present for CP-level aggregations with conflicts.

primaryCoding (from schema 1.2.0) codes the label. A label that is one classification term has the coding its SCVs carry, with the code in lower case (Pathogenic → pathogenic / ACMG Guidelines, 2015). A somatic clinical impact label is coded by its tier, without the tumor-type text (Tier I (Strong) for 2 tumor types → tier 1 / AMP/ASCO/CAP (AAC) Guidelines, 2017). Any other label, such as a combination, a conflicting classification or no classifications from unflagged records, is a ClinVar-defined term: the label in lower case as the code and ClinVar as the system. See classification.primaryCoding for the rules and the list of ClinVar-defined codes.

items.title: Strength
items.text:
The strength field is a MappableConcept: the strength the SCVs carry for the aggregate classification, from the same clinvar_clinsig_types row that gives the classification its primaryCoding:

{
  "conceptType": "Strength",
  "name": "Definitive"
}
Classification Strength Pathogenic; Benign; Oncogenic; Pathogenic, low penetrance; Established risk allele Definitive Likely pathogenic; Likely benign; Likely oncogenic; Likely pathogenic, low penetrance; Likely risk allele Likely Tier I (Strong) Strong Tier II (Potential) Potential Tier III; Tier IV; Uncertain significance; Conflicting; combinations such as Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic; any other label null (omitted)

A somatic clinical impact statement takes its tier's strength (at the priority and aggregate layers, the top tier's). A classification-layer statement with one SCV passes that SCV's strength through. See quality, direction, and strength.

items.title: Direction
items.text:
The direction field is a string: the direction the SCVs carry for the aggregate classification, from the same clinvar_clinsig_types row that gives the classification its primaryCoding. Every VCV statement has one.

Classification Direction Pathogenic; Likely pathogenic; Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic; Oncogenic; Likely oncogenic; the low-penetrance and risk-allele labels except Uncertain risk allele; Tier I; Tier II; association; and ClinVar's other proposition types supports Uncertain significance; VUS-high, VUS-mid, VUS-low; Uncertain risk allele; Tier III; conflicting data from submitters neutral Benign; Likely benign; Benign/Likely benign; Tier IV; association not found disputes Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity / oncogenicity (no lookup row) neutral The FLAG label no classifications from unflagged records (no lookup row) neutral Combinations not in the lookup, such as Uncertain significance/VUS-high (no lookup row) the direction every SCV in the group carries; supports if they differ

A somatic clinical impact statement takes its tier's direction (at the priority and aggregate layers, the top tier's). A classification-layer statement with one SCV passes that SCV's direction through. See quality, direction, and strength.

items.title: Proposition
items.text:
VCV propositions are delivered across the four proposition bundle sections (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) by meaning. Each VCV statement references its proposition via #/proposition<Meaning>/{id}.

A resolved VCV proposition contains:

Field Type Description type string Proposition type matching the underlying SCVs (e.g., VariantPathogenicityProposition) id string Proposition ID (e.g., VCV000012582-G-PATH-CP) subject string #/variation/clinvar:{id} reference predicate string Predicate matching the underlying SCVs (e.g., isCausalFor) object string One reference to the conditions of the contributing SCVs. A single condition is #/condition/clinvar.trait:{id}, or #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:{id} when it is a ClinVar trait set. Several conditions are #/conditionSet/clinvar.conditionset:vcv-{md5}: a ConceptSet minted for the aggregate, with membershipOperator: "OR" and one #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ reference per condition. Omitted when the contributing SCVs carry no condition

items.title: Evidence Lines
items.text:
Each VCV statement contains hasEvidenceLines — an array of #/evidenceLine/ JSON pointer references to evidence line records in the evidenceLine bundle section:

{
  "hasEvidenceLines": [
    "#/evidenceLine/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP.contributing",
    "#/evidenceLine/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP.non-contributing"
  ]
}

Each referenced evidence line record contains:

Field Type Description type string Always EvidenceLine directionOfEvidenceProvided string supports or neutral strengthOfEvidenceProvided object MappableConcept — Contributing or Non-contributing hasEvidenceItems array #/scv/ references (at classification layer) or #/vcv/ references (at priority/aggregate layers)

Contributing evidence lines use directionOfEvidenceProvided: "supports". Non-contributing evidence lines (lower-ranked submission levels) use directionOfEvidenceProvided: "neutral".

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Extensions carry aggregate metadata not part of the GA4GH VA-Spec statement model. Each extension follows the GA4GH Extension structure: { "name": "<name>", "value": <value> }. Extensions appear at two structural levels — on the top-level Statement and on the classification object.

See VCV Extensions (Pipeline) for details on how these extensions are built during pipeline processing.

items.title: Statement Extensions
items.text: Extension Name Value Type Description clinvarReviewStatus string The aggregate review status derived from the submission level and aggregation outcome. Always present. Values: practice guideline, reviewed by expert panel, criteria provided, single submitter, criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts, criteria provided, conflicting classifications, no assertion criteria provided, no classification provided, flagged submission.

items.title: Classification Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on the classification MappableConcept within the Statement.

Extension Name Value Type Description conflictingExplanation string A formatted breakdown of conflicting classification counts (e.g., Pathogenic(3); Likely pathogenic(2)). Present only when the classification is conflicting — multiple distinct significance values exist for a conflict-detectable proposition type.
