items.title: Data Model
items.text:
The ClinVar-GKM release file organizes data into bundle sections, each containing objects of a specific class. These classes form a directed graph of relationships — variants reference alleles, alleles reference locations, statements reference propositions, and so on.

This page explains how the ClinVar-GKM schemas relate to the GA4GH classes, gives a visual overview of how the classes relate to each other, and links to detailed documentation for each class.

items.title: An Implementation Schema
items.text: ClinVar-GKM publishes an implementation schema: ClinVar profiles of the GA4GH GKM classes (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec and GKM-Core), each narrowed to exactly what this project's pipeline produces. Every bundle section points at a ClinVar profile — allele at ClinvarAllele, condition at ClinvarCondition, scv at ClinvarScvStatement, and so on. The class pages in this section document those profiles: each page's Information Model lists only the properties the profile allows, with the narrowed types, values and pointer targets, and the base-class properties the profile forbids are listed below the table under Not used by ClinVar-GKM.

items.title: Why the profiles are narrowed
items.text:
• You know exactly what can appear. A profile lists the properties a record can carry and the values they can take. A property the profile forbids never appears in the bundle.
  • Validation catches pipeline regressions. Every published bundle, full and delta, is checked against these schemas before release, and every record a release publishes is strictly validated (Release Validation). A property, value or pointer the pipeline should not write fails validation instead of reaching consumers.
  • Tooling can be derived from the schema. Parquet column sets, documentation such as these class pages, and other tooling can be generated from a schema that describes the data precisely.
  • A ClinVar-GKM record is still a GA4GH record. The GA4GH base classes are unchanged. Every ClinVar profile is an allOf of its GA4GH base class plus the narrowing, and narrowing only ever restricts — it never widens. A record that is valid against a ClinVar profile is valid against the GA4GH class it narrows.

items.title: Narrowing rules
items.text:
• A property is forbidden only when the pipeline cannot write it. Forbidden properties are set to false. A property the pipeline can write stays allowed even when the current release happens to contain none — for example the isDiagnosticExclusionCriterionFor predicate, or ClinvarUndefinedProposition, the fallback for a classification that maps to no proposition type.
  • Enums are added only for values the pipeline fixes. A type, a predicate, a conceptType or an extension name is constrained to its exact values. Values that come from ClinVar or from upstream lookup tables are not restricted further: the type and group codes in statement and proposition ids, for example, match [A-Z]+ rather than a fixed list. Enumerations of ClinVar vocabularies that predate the narrowing, such as review status, are unchanged.
  • Every pointer is limited to the sections it may target. A #/<section>/<id> pointer carries a pattern naming its target section or sections: a proposition's subject matches ^#/variation/, an aggregate evidence line's hasEvidenceItems match ^#/(scv|vcv|rcv)/.
  • Extensions are closed classes. Each extension is its own class with a constant name, a typed value and no other properties, and each profile lists the extensions it accepts.
  • A profile is never more mature than its base. A profile of a draft GA4GH class is itself draft.
  • Section keys match the exact id format. Each bundle section's keys must match the full id the pipeline builds — a 32-character VRS digest, a 9-digit accession, a 64-character SHA-256 therapy key — not just a prefix. See ID References.
  • Validation runs on the real published bundles, not on hand-built samples, so export bugs cannot hide.

items.title: When the pipeline changes
items.text: A new property, or a new value for a field the pipeline fixes, is a schema change and is published under a new schema version — the version every bundle states in its schema_version. See Versioning & Releases.

items.title: Bundle Section Map
items.text:
The release bundle is a single JSON object of named sections — each section is a keyed collection mapping a typed id to one object. Objects link across sections with #/section/id JSON pointers. The map below shows every section, its object type, an example id, and its outgoing references. See ID References for the full pointer catalog.

The map renders at full size in a scrollable frame — scroll within it to follow the reference chain from statements down to VRS sequence references. Each drawer links to that section's class reference page.

Reading the map:

  • { } key is the section name — the JSON key under which that section's objects live
  • The pill is an example object id (the key within the section)
  • field → #/section/ lines are the outgoing cross-section references an object in that section carries
  • Solid arrows trace the primary reference flow between section clusters; dashed arrows are optional or back-references (e.g., evidence items pointing back at statements)
  • The four proposition* sections group the propositions by meaning (pathogenicity, oncogenicity, somatic clinical impact, ClinVar custom); a proposition's section is a function of its type

items.title: Variation Classes
items.text:
These classes represent the variant and its genomic context. Each section's records are a ClinVar profile of the VRS or Cat-VRS class; see Variations for the variant type hierarchy.

Class Bundle Section Key Pattern Description ClinvarSequenceReference sequenceReference SQ.{digest} Reference sequence with refget accession, molecule type, residue alphabet, and assembly ClinvarSequenceLocation location ga4gh:SL.{digest} Position or range on a sequence reference ClinvarAllele allele ga4gh:VA.{digest} Specific sequence change at a location ClinvarCopyNumberCount copyNumberCount ga4gh:CN.{digest} Absolute copy count at a location ClinvarCopyNumberChange copyNumberChange ga4gh:CX.{digest} Copy gain or loss at a location ClinvarGene gene ncbigene:{id} Gene concept with NCBI Gene primaryCoding and HGNC mapping ClinvarCategoricalVariant variation clinvar:{id} ClinVar variation with Cat-VRS representation and extensions

Every {digest} is the 32-character VRS digest.

items.title: Supporting Classes
items.text:
These classes represent the conditions, therapies, submitters, and propositions that support classification statements. Proposition content is delivered in four sections grouped by meaning; see Propositions for the type each section holds.

Class Bundle Section Key Pattern Description ClinvarCondition condition clinvar.trait:{id} Disease or phenotype with its primary coding and cross-references ClinvarConditionSet conditionSet clinvar.traitset:{id} or clinvar.conditionset:vcv-{md5} Grouping of conditions with an AND/OR membership operator ClinvarTherapy therapy clinvar.therapy:{sha256} Drug therapy (content-addressed); object of therapeutic propositions via #/therapy/ ClinvarTherapyGroup therapyGroup clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256} Combination therapy whose concepts reference #/therapy/ members ClinvarSubmitter submitter clinvar.submitter:{id} Submitting organization ClinvarVariantPathogenicityProposition propositionPathogenicity {scv_id}-PATH Pathogenicity propositions ClinvarVariantOncogenicityProposition propositionOncogenicity {scv_id}-ONCO Oncogenicity propositions ClinvarVariantClinicalSignificanceProposition, Diagnostic, Prognostic, TherapeuticResponse propositionSomaticClinicalImpact {scv_id}-{CODE} Somatic clinical impact propositions ClinvarGermlineCustomProposition subtypes propositionClinvarCustom {scv_id}-{CODE} ClinVar-specific proposition types (Risk Factor, Protective, Drug Response, …, Undefined)

Proposition keys show the SCV form; VCV and RCV propositions are keyed {accession}-{group}-{PROP}[-{level}], and somatic clinical impact propositions may add -{TIER}. See ID References for every key format.

items.title: Statement Classes
items.text:
These classes represent classification statements at different levels of aggregation and the evidence lines that connect them. All statements are profiles of the VA-Spec Statement type documented under Statements.

Class Bundle Section Key Pattern Description ClinvarScvStatement scv clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{ver} Submitted classification ClinvarVcvStatement vcv {vcv}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}[-{level}[-{TIER}]] Variant-level aggregate ClinvarRcvStatement rcv {rcv}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}[-{level}[-{TIER}]] Condition-level aggregate ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine evidenceLine clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{ver} Evidence line of a somatic clinical impact SCV statement ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine evidenceLine {vcv_or_rcv_id}.contributing / .non-contributing Evidence line of a VCV or RCV aggregate statement

See Statements for the aggregation structure and Evidence Lines for both kinds of evidence line.

items.title: ClinvarAffectsProposition
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A proposition describing a variant that affects a condition without implying causality. Used for ClinVar submissions classified as "affects". ClinVar has stopped accepting new submissions with this classification, but historical submissions remain.

JSON Schema: ClinvarAffectsProposition

Some ClinvarAffectsProposition attributes are inherited from ClinvarGermlineCustomProposition.

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description id string 1..1 The 'logical' identifier of the Entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID. This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference an object from another. type stringClinvarAffectsProposition 1..1 MUST be "ClinvarAffectsProposition". subject iriReferencepointer to #/variation/<id> 1..1 The variant, a '#/variation/' pointer into this bundle. predicate stringhasAffectFor 1..1 The relationship the Proposition describes between the subject variant and object condition. MUST be "hasAffectFor". object iriReferencepointer to #/condition/<id> or #/conditionSet/<id> 1..1 The condition the variant is associated with, a '#/condition/' or '#/conditionSet/' pointer into this bundle. geneContextQualifier ClinvarGeneContextQualifier 0..1 Reports a gene impacted by the variant, which may contribute to the association described in the Proposition (SCV propositions only). modeOfInheritanceQualifier ClinvarModeOfInheritanceQualifier 0..1 Reports a pattern of inheritance expected for the effect of the variant (SCV propositions only). penetranceQualifier ClinvarPenetranceQualifier 0..1 Reports the penetrance of the effect - the extent to which the variant impact is expressed by carriers (SCV propositions only).

Not used by ClinVar-GKM: name, description, aliases, extensions. The GA4GH base class defines these properties, but this profile forbids them (false), so they never appear in ClinVar-GKM bundles.

items.title: ClinvarAggregateClassification
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

The classification of a ClinVar VCV or RCV aggregate statement: a MappableConcept with its concept type, the aggregate classification label as its name, a ClinvarTermCoding for that label and, when the submissions conflict, an ExtensionConflictingExplanation. No id, description, aliases or mappings.

JSON Schema: ClinvarAggregateClassification

Some ClinvarAggregateClassification attributes are inherited from MappableConcept.

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description type stringMappableConcept 1..1 MUST be "MappableConcept". name string 0..1 A primary name for the concept. extensions ExtensionConflictingExplanation[] (unordered) 0..m The conflicting classifications, in an ExtensionConflictingExplanation. conceptType stringClassification 1..1 Must be 'Classification'. primaryCoding ClinvarTermCoding 0..1 The aggregate classification's code and its system. A label that ClinVar's classification terms define (for a somatic clinical impact statement, its highest tier, without the tumor-type text) has the coding its SCVs carry, with the code in lower case. Any other label (a combination of terms, a conflicting classification, or no classifications from unflagged records) is a ClinVar-defined term: the lower-cased label as the code and 'ClinVar' as the system.

Not used by ClinVar-GKM: id, description, aliases, mappings. The GA4GH base class defines these properties, but this profile forbids them (false), so they never appear in ClinVar-GKM bundles.

items.title: Extensions
items.text: These extensions are defined for ClinvarAggregateClassification.

items.title: ExtensionConflictingExplanation
items.text:
The classifications behind a conflicting aggregate classification, with the number of submissions for each (e.g., "Pathogenic(2); Uncertain significance(1)").

Field Type Limits Description name stringconflictingExplanation 1..1 Must be 'conflictingExplanation'. value string 1..1 The classifications and their submission counts, separated by '; '.

items.title: ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

An evidence line of a VCV or RCV aggregate statement. A 'Contributing' line (direction 'supports') lists the statements the aggregate statement is built from; a 'Non-contributing' line (direction 'neutral') lists those of a lower review-status priority that did not contribute. Its items are pointers to SCV statements (at the classification layer) or to VCV or RCV statements (at the priority and aggregate layers). No name, description, aliases, extensions, method, contributions, citations, target proposition, score or evidence outcome.

JSON Schema: ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine

Some ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine attributes are inherited from EvidenceLine.

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description id string 1..1 The 'logical' identifier of the Entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID. This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference an object from another. type stringEvidenceLine 1..1 MUST be "EvidenceLine". hasEvidenceItems iriReference[] (unordered)pointer to #/scv/<id> or #/vcv/<id> or #/rcv/<id> 1..m The statements the line groups, each a '#/scv/', '#/vcv/' or '#/rcv/' pointer into this bundle. directionOfEvidenceProvided stringone of supports, neutral 1..1 'supports' for a Contributing line, 'neutral' for a Non-contributing line. strengthOfEvidenceProvided ClinvarTerm 1..1 'Contributing' or 'Non-contributing', as a ClinvarTerm of concept type 'Strength'.

Not used by ClinVar-GKM: name, description, aliases, extensions, specifiedBy, contributions, reportedIn, targetProposition, scoreOfEvidenceProvided, evidenceOutcome. The GA4GH base class defines these properties, but this profile forbids them (false), so they never appear in ClinVar-GKM bundles.

items.title: ClinvarAggregateStatement
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A ClinVar aggregate statement — the shared base for VCV and RCV statements. Represents an aggregate classification across contributing submissions, grouping them into evidence lines by review status priority tier. Concrete aggregate statements are ClinvarVcvStatement (across all conditions for a variant) and ClinvarRcvStatement (scoped to a single condition or condition set). No name, description, aliases, method, contributions, citations, score or direct evidence.

JSON Schema: ClinvarAggregateStatement

Some ClinvarAggregateStatement attributes are inherited from Statement, ClinvarAggregateStatementProperties.

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description id string 1..1 The 'logical' identifier of the Entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID. This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference an object from another. type stringStatement 1..1 MUST be "Statement". extensions ExtensionClinvarReviewStatus[] (unordered) 0..m The aggregate review status, in an ExtensionClinvarReviewStatus. Absent on the somatic priority-layer statements. proposition iriReferencepointer to #/propositionPathogenicity/<id> or #/propositionOncogenicity/<id> or #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/<id> or #/propositionClinvarCustom/<id> 1..1 The aggregate proposition assessed by this VCV or RCV statement, a pointer into one of the bundle's proposition sections. Uses the same proposition types as SCV statements. The proposition at the aggregate level represents the consensus or highest-priority classification across contributing submissions. direction stringone of supports, neutral, disputes 0..1 A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates. strength ClinvarAggregateStrength 0..1 The strength of the aggregate classification (e.g. 'Likely'), when it has one. quality ClinvarQuality 1..1 The quality of the aggregate, from the submission level of its submissions. classification ClinvarAggregateClassification 1..1 The aggregate classification. hasEvidenceLines iriReference[] (unordered)pointer to #/evidenceLine/<id> 1..m The statement's evidence lines, each a '#/evidenceLine/' pointer into this bundle: always its contributing evidence line and, at the priority and aggregate layers, a non-contributing evidence line when there are non-contributing items. The evidence line's items point to the SCV statements (classification layer) or to the lower-layer aggregate statements (priority and aggregate layers).

Not used by ClinVar-GKM: name, description, aliases, specifiedBy, contributions, reportedIn, score, hasEvidence. The GA4GH base class defines these properties, but this profile forbids them (false), so they never appear in ClinVar-GKM bundles.

items.title: Extensions
items.text: These extensions are defined for ClinvarAggregateStatement.

items.title: ExtensionClinvarReviewStatus
items.text:
The aggregate review status for a VCV or RCV statement. Reflects the highest review status among contributing submissions (e.g., "practice guideline", "reviewed by expert panel", "criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts").

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A record of the allele section: a VRS Allele with its name and expressions, whose location is a pointer to a record of the location section. No description, aliases or extensions.

items.title: ClinvarCanonicalAllele
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A ClinVar canonical allele — the most common variant type. ClinVar identifies each variation by mapping submitted attributes to a GRCh38 genomic allele, which becomes the defining allele constraint. Carries ClinVar-specific extensions (HGVS list, gene list, cytogenetic location, variation type, etc.) alongside the Cat-VRS CanonicalAllele structure.

This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. items.title: ClinvarRcvStatement

Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A ClinVar RCV (reference clinical variant) statement. Represents an aggregate classification for a specific variant-condition pair across all submissions sharing the same proposition type and condition. RCV statements contain evidence lines that group contributing SCV submissions by review status priority tier, scoped to a single condition or condition set. RCV statements use the same proposition types as SCV statements. Unlike VCV statements which aggregate across all conditions for a variant, RCV statements are scoped to a single condition. Evidence lines at the RCV level follow the same priority tier structure as VCV statements.

Absent on the somatic priority-layer statements. proposition iriReferencepointer to #/propositionPathogenicity/<id> or #/propositionOncogenicity/<id> or #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/<id> or #/propositionClinvarCustom/<id> 1..1 The aggregate proposition assessed by this VCV or RCV statement, a pointer into one of the bundle's proposition sections. items.title: ClinvarScvStatement
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A ClinVar SCV (submitted clinical variant) statement. Represents a single submitter's assertion about a variant-condition relationship, including their classification, direction, strength, method, and contributions. Allowable proposition types at SCV level: Germline classification (9 types): VariantPathogenicityProposition, ClinvarRiskFactorProposition, ClinvarProtectiveProposition, ClinvarDrugResponseProposition, ClinvarAffectsProposition, ClinvarAssociationProposition, ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition, ClinvarOtherProposition, ClinvarNotProvidedProposition. Oncogenicity (1 type): VariantOncogenicityProposition. Somatic clinical impact (1 type): VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition with evidence lines carrying VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition, VariantDiagnosticProposition, or VariantPrognosticProposition. Conflicting data (1 type): ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition.

JSON Schema: ClinvarScvStatement

Some ClinvarScvStatement attributes are inherited from Statement, ClinvarScvStatementProperties.

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description id string 1..1 The 'logical' identifier of the Entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID. This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference an object from another. type stringStatement 1..1 MUST be "Statement". description string 0..1 A free-text description of the Entity. extensions ExtensionClinvarScvId | ExtensionClinvarScvVersion | ExtensionClinvarScvReviewStatus | ExtensionSubmittedScvLocalKey | ExtensionSubmissionLevel | ExtensionSubmittedScvClassification | ExtensionSubmittedCondition | ExtensionSubmittedConditionSet[] (unordered) 1..m SCV-level extensions including submission metadata, review status, and the submitter's original condition mapping. specifiedBy ClinvarMethod 0..1 The submission's assertion method. contributions ClinvarContribution[] (ordered) 1..m The submitter's submission, creation and evaluation of the record. reportedIn ClinvarDocument[] (unordered) 0..m The submission's citations. proposition iriReferencepointer to #/propositionPathogenicity/<id> or #/propositionOncogenicity/<id> or #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/<id> or #/propositionClinvarCustom/<id> 1..1 The proposition assessed by this SCV statement, a pointer into one of the bundle's proposition sections. It is one of the GA4GH standard proposition types (pathogenicity, oncogenicity, clinical significance) or a ClinVar-specific proposition type (risk factor, protective, drug response, affects, association, confers sensitivity, other, not provided, conflicting data). direction stringone of supports, neutral, disputes 0..1 A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates. strength ClinvarStrength 0..1 The strength of the classification (e.g. 'Likely'), when it has one. quality ClinvarQuality 1..1 The quality of the assessment, from the submission's review status. classification ClinvarScvClassification 1..1 The submitter's classification. hasEvidenceLines iriReference[] (unordered)pointer to #/evidenceLine/<id> 0..m Evidence lines for this SCV statement, each a '#/evidenceLine/' pointer into this bundle. For somatic clinical impact (SCI) statements, evidence lines carry target propositions (VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition, VariantDiagnosticProposition, or VariantPrognosticProposition) and an evidence outcome reflecting the AMP/ASCO/CAP tier. Germline and oncogenicity SCVs typically do not have evidence lines.

Not used by ClinVar-GKM: name, aliases, score, hasEvidence. The GA4GH base class defines these properties, but this profile forbids them (false), so they never appear in ClinVar-GKM bundles.

items.title: ExtensionClinvarScvReviewStatus

Field Type Limits Description name stringclinvarScvReviewStatus 1..1 Must be 'clinvarScvReviewStatus'. value stringone of criteria provided, single submitter, criteria provided, conflicting classifications, criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts, no assertion criteria provided, no classification provided, no assertion provided, practice guideline, reviewed by expert panel, flagged submission 1..1 The ClinVar review status for the submission.

Field Type Limits Description name stringclinvarScvVersion 1..1 Must be 'clinvarScvVersion'. value string 1..1 The version number as a string.

items.title: ExtensionSubmissionLevel
items.text:
The submission level category based on review status. Determines the aggregation tier when building VCV and RCV aggregate statements.

Field Type Limits Description name stringsubmissionLevel 1..1 Must be 'submissionLevel'. value stringone of PG, EP, CP, NOCP, NOCL, FLAG 1..1 Practice Guideline (PG), Expert Panel (EP), Criteria Provided (CP), No Criteria Provided (NOCP), No Classification Provided (NOCL), or Flagged Submission (FLAG). Ranked PG > EP > CP > NOCP > NOCL > FLAG.

items.title: ExtensionSubmittedCondition
items.text:
The submitter's original condition for single-condition submissions. Contains the submitted condition details and how they were mapped to the ClinVar canonical condition. Present on SCV statements and somatic evidence lines when the submission has exactly one condition.

Field Type Limits Description name stringsubmittedCondition 1..1 Must be 'submittedCondition'. value SubmittedCondition 1..1 The submitted condition mapping details. Includes a reference to the resolved condition and the full mapping provenance.

items.title: ExtensionSubmittedConditionSet
items.text:
The submitter's original conditions for multi-condition submissions. Contains the submitted condition set details, the multiple condition explanation (AND/OR), and an array of individual condition mappings. Present on SCV statements and somatic evidence lines when the submission has two or more conditions.

Field Type Limits Description name stringsubmittedConditionSet 1..1 Must be 'submittedConditionSet'. value SubmittedConditionSet 1..1 The submitted condition set with mapping details for each condition.

items.title: ExtensionSubmittedScvClassification
items.text:

Field Type Limits Description name stringsubmittedScvClassification 1..1 Must be 'submittedScvClassification'. value string 0..1 The original submitted classification string.

items.title: ExtensionSubmittedScvLocalKey
items.text:
The local key submitted by the submitter for this SCV, typically a combination of variant and condition identifiers used internally by the submitting lab.

Field Type Limits Description name stringsubmittedScvLocalKey 1..1 Must be 'submittedScvLocalKey'. value string 1..1 The submitter's local key string.

items.title: ClinvarSequenceLocation
items.text:

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description id string 1..1 The 'logical' identifier of the Entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID. It is used within a system to reference an object from another. type stringSequenceLocation 1..1 MUST be "SequenceLocation" digest stringpattern ^[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{32}$ 0..1 A sha512t24u digest created using the VRS Computed Identifier algorithm. sequenceReference iriReferencepointer to #/sequenceReference/<id> 1..1 The reference sequence for the location, a '#/sequenceReference/' pointer into this bundle. start integer | Range 0..1 The start coordinate or range of the SequenceLocation. items.title: ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine

items.title: ClinvarVcvStatement
items.text:
Trial Use

May change in future releases. See the GKM Maturity Model.

A ClinVar VCV (variant classification variant) statement. Represents an aggregate classification for a variant across all submissions sharing the same proposition type. VCV statements contain evidence lines that group contributing SCV submissions by review status priority tier (practice guideline, expert panel, criteria provided, no criteria provided). VCV statements use the same proposition types as SCV statements. Evidence lines at the VCV level point to the lower-layer VCV statements (in the vcv section), each carrying the same proposition type as the parent but scoped to a specific priority tier. The innermost (classification) layer's evidence lines point to the individual SCV statements as evidence items.

JSON Schema: ClinvarVcvStatement

Some ClinvarVcvStatement attributes are inherited from ClinvarAggregateStatement.

items.title: Information Model
items.text:
Field Type Limits Description id string 1..1 The 'logical' identifier of the Entity in the system of record, e.g. a UUID. This 'id' is unique within a given system, but may or may not be globally unique outside the system. It is used within a system to reference an object from another. type stringStatement 1..1 MUST be "Statement". extensions ExtensionClinvarReviewStatus[] (unordered) 0..m The aggregate review status, in an ExtensionClinvarReviewStatus. Absent on the somatic priority-layer statements. proposition iriReferencepointer to #/propositionPathogenicity/<id> or #/propositionOncogenicity/<id> or #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/<id> or #/propositionClinvarCustom/<id> 1..1 The aggregate proposition assessed by this VCV or RCV statement, a pointer into one of the bundle's proposition sections. Uses the same proposition types as SCV statements. The proposition at the aggregate level represents the consensus or highest-priority classification across contributing submissions. direction stringone of supports, neutral, disputes 0..1 A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates. strength ClinvarAggregateStrength 0..1 The strength of the aggregate classification (e.g. 'Likely'), when it has one. quality ClinvarQuality 1..1 The quality of the aggregate, from the submission level of its submissions. classification ClinvarAggregateClassification 1..1 The aggregate classification. hasEvidenceLines iriReference[] (unordered)pointer to #/evidenceLine/<id> 1..m The statement's evidence lines, each a '#/evidenceLine/' pointer into this bundle: always its contributing evidence line and, at the priority and aggregate layers, a non-contributing evidence line when there are non-contributing items. The evidence line's items point to the SCV statements (classification layer) or to the lower-layer aggregate statements (priority and aggregate layers).

items.title: Information Model

ClinVar's submitted text is never altered: when ClinVar supplies an expression with no HGVS type letter (e.g. NC_000017.10:9481617_9489649del), it is kept as an extension of the listed expression. If ClinVar also supplies a valid expression for the same accession, that one is listed with extensions invalidClinvarExpression (the submitted text) and expressionMerged (true). Absent or false when not applicable. proteinExpression ClinvarProteinExpression 0..1 The protein HGVS expression with syntax (typically hgvs.p) and value. Present only when a protein-level expression exists for the nucleotide expression. molecularConsequence ClinvarMolecularConsequenceCoding[] (unordered) 0..m Sequence Ontology terms describing the predicted molecular consequence. items.title: Concepts
items.text: Genes, conditions, and therapies are GKM-Core and VA-Spec concepts — a MappableConcept, or a ConceptSet for groups. ClinVar-GKM narrows each to a ClinVar profile, and narrows the codings and mappings they carry to the fields the pipeline writes.

items.title: Concept Sections
items.text:
ClinVar Profile Base Class Bundle Section Description ClinvarGene MappableConcept gene An NCBI Gene, with its primary coding and its HGNC mapping ClinvarCondition Condition condition A ClinVar trait, with its name, aliases, primary coding, and mappings ClinvarConditionSet ConditionSet conditionSet A set of conditions: its concepts are #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ pointers, joined by membershipOperator AND or OR ClinvarTherapy Therapy therapy A drug therapy named by its submitted text ClinvarTherapyGroup TherapyGroup therapyGroup A combination therapy: its concepts are #/therapy/ pointers

Two kinds of condition set share the conditionSet section: ClinVar trait sets (clinvar.traitset:{id}) and sets minted for VCV aggregates (clinvar.conditionset:vcv-{md5}).

items.title: Codings, Mappings, and Terms
items.text:
These classes appear inside concepts and statements rather than as section records.

Class Used For ClinvarCoding A code and its system, with an optional name and IRIs — the primary coding of a gene, condition, or qualifier ClinvarMappingCoding The coding of a concept mapping: a ClinvarCoding without a name ClinvarConceptMapping A mapping of a concept to a ClinvarMappingCoding, with its SKOS relation ClinvarTermCoding The coding of a ClinVar term: only a code and a system ClinvarCodedTerm A term of a ClinVar vocabulary (a strength, for example): a concept type, a name and, when it has one, a ClinvarTermCoding ClinvarTerm A term with no coding (a quality, for example): only a concept type and a name

The statement classes build on these: an SCV's strength is a ClinvarStrength (a ClinvarCodedTerm), and an aggregate's strength and every quality are ClinvarTerms. See Statements.

items.title: Evidence Lines
items.text:
Evidence lines in ClinVar-GKM are stored in the evidenceLine bundle section and referenced from statements via hasEvidenceLines arrays of #/evidenceLine/ JSON pointer strings. There are three underlying dict tables that are merged into the single bundle section: gkm_dict_evidence_line (SCV), gkm_dict_vcv_evidence_line (VCV), and gkm_dict_rcv_evidence_line (RCV).

SCV evidence lines appear only on somatic clinical impact (SCI) statements, linking the parent VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition to a specific clinical assertion type — therapeutic response, diagnostic, or prognostic. VCV and RCV evidence lines connect aggregate statements to their contributing and non-contributing evidence items at each aggregation layer.

Two ClinVar profiles narrow the VA-Spec EvidenceLine, and the bundle schema picks one by the record's key:

ClinVar Profile Key Pattern Used By ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{ver} Somatic clinical impact SCV statements ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine {vcv_or_rcv_id}.contributing or {vcv_or_rcv_id}.non-contributing VCV and RCV aggregate statements

items.title: When Evidence Lines Appear
items.text:
Statement Category Has Evidence Lines? Germline classification (PATH, RF, PROTECT, etc.) No Oncogenicity (ONCO) No Somatic clinical impact (SCI) — Tier I or II Yes Somatic clinical impact (SCI) — Tier III or IV No (no clinical assertion type)

Evidence lines are present only on Tier I and Tier II SCI statements, where ClinVar requires at least one clinical assertion type (therapeutic response, diagnostic, or prognostic) to support the tier classification.

items.title: Target Propositions
items.text:
Each somatic evidence line carries a targetProposition specifying the clinical assertion type, as a #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/ pointer. The target is one of these GA4GH VA-Spec standard types:

Code Type ClinVar Profile Predicates Description TR VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition ClinvarVariantTherapeuticResponseProposition predictsSensitivityTo, predictsResistanceTo Response to a specific therapy DIAG VariantDiagnosticProposition ClinvarVariantDiagnosticProposition isDiagnosticInclusionCriterionFor, isDiagnosticExclusionCriterionFor Diagnostic relevance PROG VariantPrognosticProposition ClinvarVariantPrognosticProposition associatedWithBetterOutcomeFor, associatedWithWorseOutcomeFor Prognostic significance

A somatic evidence line's directionOfEvidenceProvided is always supports. It carries no evidence items, strength, or score.

items.title: Evidence Outcome
items.text:
The evidenceOutcome field — a ClinvarTerm whose conceptType is Outcome — maps the AMP/ASCO/CAP tier to an evidence level:

Tier Evidence Outcome Tier I - Strong Level A/B Tier II - Potential Level C/D

items.title: Relationship to Parent Statement
items.text:
An SCI statement's structure connects the tiers to the clinical assertions:

SCV Statement
├── proposition: #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/{scv_id}-SCI
│   └── VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition (hasClinicalSignificanceFor)
├── classification: "Tier I - Strong"
└── hasEvidenceLines: #/evidenceLine/clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{ver}
    └── ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine
        ├── targetProposition: #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/{scv_id}-TR
        │   └── VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition (predictsSensitivityTo)
        ├── evidenceOutcome: "Level A/B"
        └── directionOfEvidenceProvided: "supports"

The parent statement asserts clinical significance (the tier), while the evidence line specifies what kind of clinical significance — which therapy, diagnostic criterion, or prognostic outcome the variant is relevant for.

items.title: Aggregate Evidence Lines
items.text:
A ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine groups the statements a VCV or RCV aggregate statement is built from:

Line directionOfEvidenceProvided strengthOfEvidenceProvided hasEvidenceItems {id}.contributing supports Contributing The statements the aggregate is built from {id}.non-contributing neutral Non-contributing Statements of a lower review-status priority that did not contribute

Each item is a #/scv/, #/vcv/, or #/rcv/ pointer. The strength is a ClinvarTerm whose conceptType is Strength. Aggregate evidence lines carry no target proposition, evidence outcome, or extensions.

items.title: Extensions
items.text: Somatic evidence lines also carry a submittedCondition or submittedConditionSet extension with the submitter's original condition details. Their values are a SubmittedCondition or a SubmittedConditionSet, the same structures the SCV statement's extensions carry.

items.title: Propositions
items.text:
A proposition defines what a statement asserts — the relationship between a variant and a condition. Each proposition follows the subject-predicate-object pattern from the GA4GH VA-Spec specification:

  • Subject (subject) — a reference to a ClinVar variation via #/variation/clinvar:{id}
  • Predicate — the relationship type (e.g., isCausalFor, isOncogenicFor)
  • Object (object) — a condition, disease, or phenotype, as a #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ reference (a therapy for therapeutic response)

Each proposition section points at its ClinVar profiles, which narrow the VA-Spec proposition classes to what the pipeline writes: subject, object, and conditionQualifier are pointers limited to the sections they may target, the qualifiers are ClinVar qualifier classes, and none carries name, description, aliases, extensions, or alleleOriginQualifier.

items.title: Proposition Types
items.text: ClinVar-GKM uses 13 proposition types: 3 from the GA4GH VA-Spec standard and 10 defined specifically for ClinVar submission categories. The 10 ClinVar-specific types are open subtypes of the VA-Spec SubjectVariantProposition base — each carries its own real type name (the former CustomProposition + customPropositionType model is retired).

items.title: GA4GH Standard Types
items.text:
These types are defined in the VA-Spec. Records keep the VA-Spec type name and validate against a ClinVar profile of it:

Code Type ClinVar Profile Predicate Description PATH VariantPathogenicityProposition ClinvarVariantPathogenicityProposition isCausalFor Germline pathogenicity/benignity ONCO VariantOncogenicityProposition ClinvarVariantOncogenicityProposition isOncogenicFor Oncogenicity classification SCI VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition ClinvarVariantClinicalSignificanceProposition hasClinicalSignificanceFor Somatic clinical impact

items.title: ClinVar-Specific Types
items.text:
These types handle ClinVar submission categories not covered by the GA4GH specifications. Several are no longer accepted as new submissions by ClinVar, but historical submissions remain in the dataset.

Code Type Predicate Description RF ClinvarRiskFactorProposition isRiskFactorFor Risk factor PROTECT ClinvarProtectiveProposition isProtectiveFor Protective DR ClinvarDrugResponseProposition hasDrugResponseFor Drug response AFF ClinvarAffectsProposition hasAffectFor Affects ASSOC ClinvarAssociationProposition isAssociatedWith Association CS ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition confersSensitivityFor Confers sensitivity OTH ClinvarOtherProposition isClinvarOtherAssociationFor Other NP ClinvarNotProvidedProposition hasNoProvidedClassificationFor Not provided CDFS ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition isConflictingDataFromSubmittersFor Conflicting data (germline only) UNDEF ClinvarUndefinedProposition isClinvarUndefinedAssociationFor Fallback for a classification that maps to no defined type

items.title: Somatic Evidence Line Propositions
items.text:
Somatic clinical impact (SCI) statements carry evidence lines with their own target propositions. These 3 types are targeted only by the targetProposition of a ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine, never by a statement's proposition:

Code Type ClinVar Profile Predicates TR VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition ClinvarVariantTherapeuticResponseProposition predictsSensitivityTo, predictsResistanceTo DIAG VariantDiagnosticProposition ClinvarVariantDiagnosticProposition isDiagnosticInclusionCriterionFor, isDiagnosticExclusionCriterionFor PROG VariantPrognosticProposition ClinvarVariantPrognosticProposition associatedWithBetterOutcomeFor, associatedWithWorseOutcomeFor

items.title: Bundle Sections
items.text:
Since 1.1.0, propositions are delivered in four bundle sections grouped by meaning. A proposition's section depends only on its type, at every level (SCV, VCV, RCV). The Parquet tables have the same names.

Section Types propositionPathogenicity PATH propositionOncogenicity ONCO propositionSomaticClinicalImpact SCI, DIAG, PROG, TR propositionClinvarCustom RF, PROTECT, DR, AFF, ASSOC, CS, OTH, NP, CDFS, UNDEF

Statements and evidence lines point at the section: #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH.

items.title: Common Attributes
items.text:
All ClinVar proposition types are subtypes of the VA-Spec SubjectVariantProposition (the ClinVar-specific types via the open ClinvarGermlineCustomProposition base; the standard types via VA-Spec's GeneticContextVariantProposition). Their ClinVar profiles allow these attributes:

  • subject — the variant being classified, a #/variation/ pointer
  • object — the asserted object, a pointer: a #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ for most types; a #/therapy/ or #/therapyGroup/ for VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition (drug therapies are content-addressed and deduplicated into the therapy / therapyGroup bundle sections)
  • conditionQualifier — for VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition only, the #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ the therapeutic response is asserted in (since object carries the therapy)
  • geneContextQualifier — the gene impacted by the variant, embedded as a ClinvarGeneContextQualifier. Its geneContextSource extension may only be submittedSymbolMatches, submittedSymbolDiffers, inferredFromVariant or submittedNotNormalized. Every ClinVar proposition profile types the qualifier this way, including the profiles of the VA-Spec types.
  • modeOfInheritanceQualifier — the submitted mode of inheritance, as a ClinvarModeOfInheritanceQualifier. Allowed on pathogenicity and the ClinVar-specific types only.
  • penetranceQualifier — low or risk, derived from a low-penetrance or risk-allele classification, as a ClinvarPenetranceQualifier. Allowed on pathogenicity and the ClinVar-specific types only.

The qualifiers appear on SCV propositions only; VCV and RCV propositions carry none. No ClinVar proposition carries alleleOriginQualifier.

See the individual class pages for the complete information model including all inherited fields.

items.title: Statements
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM statements are profiles of the GA4GH VA-Spec Statement type. They exist at three levels of aggregation. Each points, through its proposition, at the proposition that defines what is being asserted, in one of the four proposition sections (see Propositions).

The ClinvarStatement union type encompasses all three:

Level Profile Bundle Section Description Submission ClinvarScvStatement scv A single submitter's classification Variant aggregate ClinvarVcvStatement vcv Aggregate across all submissions for a variant + proposition type Condition aggregate ClinvarRcvStatement rcv Aggregate scoped to a specific variant + condition pair

VCV and RCV statements share the ClinvarAggregateStatement profile. None of the statement profiles carries name, aliases, hasEvidence, or score, and their proposition and hasEvidenceLines are #/ pointers limited to the proposition sections and the evidenceLine section.

items.title: SCV Statements
items.text:
Each SCV represents one submitter's assertion about a variant-condition relationship. SCV statements carry:

  • Classification — the submitter's classification (e.g., Pathogenic, Likely benign, Tier I - Strong), a ClinvarScvClassification with its code, its system, and ClinVar's description in an extension
  • Direction — whether the evidence supports, disputes, or is neutral toward the proposition
  • Strength — the strength of the assessment (e.g., definitive, likely), a ClinvarStrength, when the classification has one
  • Quality — the quality of the assessment, from the submission's review status, a ClinvarQuality
  • Contributions — the submitter's submitted, created, and evaluated activities with their dates, each a ClinvarContribution whose contributor is a #/submitter/ pointer to a ClinvarSubmitter
  • Method — the classification guideline used (e.g., ACMG Guidelines 2015, AMP/ASCO/CAP Guidelines 2017), a ClinvarMethod
  • Citations — reportedIn, each a ClinvarDocument with a PubMed id, DOI, or URLs

items.title: SCV Extensions
items.text:
Extension Description clinvarScvId SCV accession without version (e.g., SCV001571657) clinvarScvVersion Version number clinvarScvReviewStatus Review status (e.g., criteria provided, single submitter) submissionLevel Aggregation tier: PG, EP, CP, NOCP, NOCL, or FLAG submittedScvLocalKey Submitter's internal identifier submittedScvClassification Original classification before normalization (when different) submittedCondition Submitter's original condition for single-condition submissions submittedConditionSet Submitter's original conditions for multi-condition submissions

The submittedCondition extension's value is a SubmittedCondition, and the submittedConditionSet extension's value is a SubmittedConditionSet whose concepts are SubmittedConditionMappings. They trace how the submitter's original conditions were mapped to the ClinVar canonical conditions.

items.title: VCV and RCV Statements
items.text:
Aggregate statements group SCV submissions into a hierarchical evidence structure. Both VCV and RCV follow the same three-layer pattern:

  1. Classification layer — groups SCVs by classification label (e.g., all "Pathogenic" submissions)
  2. Priority layer — groups by review status tier (practice guideline > expert panel > criteria provided > no criteria provided)
  3. Aggregate contribution layer — references individual SCV submissions as evidence items

Each layer is connected via hasEvidenceLines — an array of #/evidenceLine/ JSON pointer references to ClinvarAggregateEvidenceLine records stored in the evidenceLine bundle section. Each statement has a contributing evidence line and, at the priority and aggregate layers, a non-contributing one when some items did not contribute; each line's hasEvidenceItems are #/scv/, #/vcv/, or #/rcv/ pointers. Sub-statements carry the same proposition type as the parent but are scoped to a specific tier or classification group.

An aggregate statement's classification is a ClinvarAggregateClassification — the aggregate label as its name, with no coding, and the conflicting classifications in a conflictingExplanation extension when the submissions conflict. Its strength is a ClinvarAggregateStrength and its quality a ClinvarQuality named from the submission level of its submissions.

items.title: Aggregate Extensions
items.text: Extension Description clinvarReviewStatus The aggregate review status (e.g., criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts). Absent on the somatic priority-layer statements

items.title: VCV vs RCV
items.text:
• VCV statements aggregate across all conditions for a variant — the object on the proposition may reference multiple conditions or a condition set
  • RCV statements are scoped to a single ClinVar RCV accession (one variant + one condition combination)

items.title: Variations
items.text:
ClinVar variations are represented using the GA4GH Cat-VRS (Categorical Variation) specification. Each variation maps to one of four ClinVar profiles of the Cat-VRS types, depending on how ClinVar resolves the variant's genomic identity.

The ClinvarCategoricalVariant union type encompasses all four. Its branches are mutually exclusive, so a variation record validates against exactly one of them:

Cat-VRS Type ClinVar Profile Members Constraints CanonicalAllele ClinvarCanonicalAllele #/allele/ ClinvarDefiningAlleleConstraint CategoricalCnv ClinvarCategoricalCnvChange #/copyNumberChange/ ClinvarDefiningLocationConstraint and ClinvarCopyChangeConstraint (loss or gain) CategoricalCnv ClinvarCategoricalCnvCount #/copyNumberCount/ ClinvarDefiningLocationConstraint and ClinvarCopyCountConstraint (an integer copy count) CategoricalVariant ClinvarNonConstrainedVariant none none
  • ClinvarCanonicalAllele — the vast majority of ClinVar variations, defined by a genomic allele mapped from the submitted variant attributes
  • ClinvarCategoricalCnvChange and ClinvarCategoricalCnvCount — copy number variants with a qualitative change or an absolute copy count
  • ClinvarNonConstrainedVariant — haplotypes, genotypes, and complex variants that cannot be mapped to a specific VRS allele or location; it carries no members or constraints

Variations carry mappings of type ClinvarVariationMapping: its ClinVar identifier (exactMatch), ClinGen allele identifiers (closeMatch), and other cross-references (relatedMatch).

items.title: ClinVar-Specific Extensions
items.text:
All ClinVar variant types share a set of extensions that provide ClinVar metadata not captured by the Cat-VRS base types. They are defined on ClinvarCategoricalVariant:

Extension Description clinvarHgvsList Complete list of HGVS expressions — nucleotide and protein forms, MANE select/plus designations, and molecular consequences (SO terms). Each entry is an HgvsListItem. clinvarGeneList Gene associations with #/gene/ references to ClinvarGene records, relationship types, and sources. Each entry is a GeneListItem. categoricalVariationType The Cat-VRS category assigned: CanonicalAllele, CategoricalCnvChange, CategoricalCnvCount, or Undefined. definingVrsVariationType The VRS class from upstream processing: Allele, CopyNumberChange, CopyNumberCount, Haplotype, Unknown, or Not Available. clinvarVariationType The variation type as reported by ClinVar (e.g., Deletion, single nucleotide variant, Duplication). clinvarSubclassType The ClinVar subclass: SimpleAllele, Haplotype, or Genotype. clinvarCytogeneticLocation Cytogenetic band location (e.g., 17q21.31). vrsPreProcessingIssue Issues detected during VRS pre-processing. Present only when issues exist. vrsProcessingException Errors from the VRS processing service. Present only when errors occurred.

items.title: VRS Composition Chain
items.text:
Variants reference their resolved VRS representations through bundle-internal #/ pointers:

Variation → #/allele/{id} → #/location/{id} → #/sequenceReference/{id}

Copy number variants follow the same chain through #/copyNumberChange/ or #/copyNumberCount/ records, each of which points to a #/location/.

  • Alleles (ClinvarAllele) carry the state, SPDI/HGVS/gnomAD expressions (ClinvarAlleleExpression), and a location pointer
  • Copy number records (ClinvarCopyNumberChange, ClinvarCopyNumberCount) carry the copy change or count and a location pointer
  • Locations (ClinvarSequenceLocation) carry start/end coordinates and a sequence reference pointer
  • Sequence references (ClinvarSequenceReference) carry the refget accession, molecule type, residue alphabet, and an assembly extension (e.g., GRCh38)

Each of these is a ClinVar profile of its VRS class: the VRS fields the pipeline does not write (such as description and aliases) are forbidden, and the nested object references are #/ pointers into the bundle.

items.title: Start Here
items.text:
Release

Counts on this page are from the 2026-11-15 release (the Parquet set published 2026-11-20). The Parquet tables are built from the JSON bundle and rebuilt each release, and one set is published per release line, overwritten every release, so the console's numbers are today's and may be higher than this page's.

New tables from release 1.2.0

From release 1.2.0 the tables are built by gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0 and published at v1/1.2/parquet/: 20 tables with different columns from the 22 BigQuery-exported tables the 1.1 line published at v1/1.1/parquet/ (since removed). This track describes the new tables. If you have queries for the old ones, see Moving from the 1.1 Tables.

ClinVar-GKM publishes all of ClinVar as Parquet — 20 typed tables you query with SQL, with no database server and no data-loading step. This page gets a real answer from real ClinVar data in about five minutes: no joins, no genomics background, and — to begin — nothing to install.

items.title: Run a query now
items.text:
The console below runs SQL in your browser, directly against the published data at data.clinvar-gkm.org. It reads the Parquet set of the current release line, v1/1.2/parquet/, overwritten every release; the Release label shows the release it was built from. When a new line starts, its Parquet set is published shortly after its first release, and the console has no tables to read until then (see the timeline). Pick an example from the dropdown and press Run. The first query loads the engine (a few seconds, once); everything after is immediate. A query still running after 15 seconds is stopped, and the console shows the commands to download the tables it reads and run the same query on your machine.

The first example counts every condition in ClinVar: 23,450. condition.parquet is the right table to start with — about 2 MB, one row per condition, and a plain-English name column, with none of the variant identifiers or nested structures the larger tables carry.

items.title: Three queries
items.text:
Each of these is in the console's Example dropdown. Read them top to bottom — they go from "how much is here" to "find the one I care about".

Prerequisites

  • In the console: nothing to install.
  • On your machine: the DuckDB CLI (tested with 1.5.4) and curl, and condition.parquet (about 2 MB) downloaded into the directory you run DuckDB from, as in Put the file on your machine.
  • Querying a URL instead of a file (FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/…'): DuckDB installs and loads its httpfs extension the first time a query reads a URL, which needs internet access to DuckDB's extension repository. Where that is blocked, install it by hand (installing extensions), or download the file first.
-- 1. How many conditions are there?
SELECT count(*) FROM 'condition.parquet';

-- 2. What do they look like?
SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet' LIMIT 10;

-- 3. Find one you care about
SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet' WHERE name ILIKE '%marfan%';

The third returns 13 rows — every ClinVar condition whose name mentions Marfan, from Marfan syndrome to Neonatal Marfan syndrome. ILIKE is a case-insensitive match and % means "any text here".

These queries name the file as 'condition.parquet' — how you run them once the file is on your machine. The console above points the same queries at the published URL for you.

items.title: Put the file on your machine
items.text:
To go past the browser console — larger queries, your own scripts, repeated work — download the file and query it with DuckDB, a single self-contained binary.

BASE="https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet"
curl -fO "${BASE}/condition.parquet"

duckdb -c "SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet' WHERE name ILIKE '%marfan%'"

The Downloads → Parquet Files page lists every file and the stable URL. The tables are built from the bundle and rebuilt each release: the published set is always the latest release. For an earlier release, or for just the records you need, build the tables yourself from a published bundle.

items.title: No terminal at all
items.text:
Two ways to query without installing anything:

  • The console on this page (above) — already running against the published data.
  • The DuckDB Web Shell at shell.duckdb.org — drag a downloaded condition.parquet onto the page (or use Import), then run SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet'; (quote the file name: the shell registers a file, not a table).

items.title: Get the answer into a spreadsheet
items.text:
Excel and Google Sheets cannot open Parquet, but one line turns a result into a CSV they can:

duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet') TO 'conditions.csv' (HEADER)"

items.title: Where to go next
items.text:
condition.parquet is 1 of 20 tables. The rest hold the variants, the clinical assertions (SCVs), and the ClinVar aggregates (VCVs and RCVs) — and they reference each other. The table map shows all 20 at a glance; from there, pick by the question you have:

  • What columns does a table have? — Anatomy of a Table
  • How do the tables join? — Joining Tables
  • Give me a working query for a real task — Recipes
  • The big tables are slow or run out of memory — Working at Scale
  • I work in Python, R, or Spark — Beyond DuckDB
  • I want the tables for another release, or a small slice as JSON — Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles
  • A dataset of my own: a gene panel, one submitter, a week's changes — Build Your Own Dataset, starting with Your First Dataset
  • I have queries for the 1.1 tables — Moving from the 1.1 Tables
  • I want tables for a frozen line (v1/1.1/, v1/1.0/) — Parquet for Previous Releases

items.title: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles
items.text:
The published Parquet is built by one open tool, gkm-bundle-parquet, from the published JSON bundle. You can run the same tool yourself to:

  • build the tables for any release, including releases whose Parquet is no longer published (for one week, see Parquet for one weekly release; for the frozen lines, see Parquet for Previous Releases);
  • cut a mini-bundle: the records of one submitter, one variant or one gene and everything they point to, as a small JSON bundle or a small set of tables;
  • rebuild the bundle from a set of tables and prove the records are identical;
  • validate a bundle against its JSON Schema.
Source, issues, docs github.com/clingen-data-model/gkm-bundle-parquet: the README, generate.md (how the tables follow from the schema), column-set-format.md, round-trip.md, validate.md Package pypi.org/project/gkm-bundle-parquet, version 2.0.0 Writes table spec sections 2.0, default policy 2.0, with DuckDB 1.5.4 (pinned) Needs Python 3.10 or later

Shorter routes

This is the full guide. Your First Dataset walks one selection, from download to a DuckDB query, in about five minutes; the CLI Reference lists every command and option; and Build Your Own Dataset helps choose between building and the published Parquet.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.10 or later (tested with 3.14.5), and one way to run the tool: uv (uvx, as the examples are written; tested with 0.6.14), pipx, or pip in a virtual environment of your own. See Install.
  • bash or zsh. The commands work in both, on macOS and Linux.
  • A bundle. The examples read the 2026-11-15 weekly delta, clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz (5 MB, 39,062 records), downloaded in Build the tables. The full-bundle examples read the newest monthly, clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (4.9 GB compressed), from Monthly Full Bundles.
  • Resources. Every command on the delta finishes in under 15 s with under 2 GB of memory. A full-bundle build takes about 3.5 hours on a 16 GB machine (10 GiB of memory, about 30 GB of free disk), or 40 minutes on a large one (A full bundle); a full-bundle select streams, taking about 11 minutes and under 100 MB of memory.
  • Run every command from one working directory: later blocks read the files earlier blocks write.

Measured runs

Every command on this page was run with gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 from PyPI, on an Apple M2 Pro laptop (16 GB of memory, 10 cores), against the published 2026-11-15 weekly delta (v1/1.2/deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz, 5 MB, 39,062 records). The output quoted is the real output. Figures for a full bundle come from a 16 GB cloud machine and the tool's own release measurements (A full bundle), except the full-bundle select and the weekly replay, which were run on this laptop.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Install
items.text:
The quickest way to run the tool is uvx, from uv: it fetches the pinned release and runs it, with nothing to install. Every command on this page is written that way, as uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 …, so you can paste it as it is:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 version

gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0: table spec sections 2.0, policy 2.0; duckdb 1.5.4
…

version --json prints the same as JSON (the tool, table spec, policy, DuckDB and validator versions), for a script that records what built a set.

To have a gkm-bundle-parquet command instead, install it with one of these (uv, pipx, or pip into a virtual environment of your own), then write gkm-bundle-parquet wherever this page writes uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0:

uv tool install gkm-bundle-parquet==2.0.0

pipx install gkm-bundle-parquet==2.0.0

pip install gkm-bundle-parquet==2.0.0

command not found: gkm-bundle-parquet

The shell finds no installed command. Run the uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 form, or install the tool with one of the lines above (after uv tool install or pipx install, open a new shell if the command is still not found: uv tool update-shell or pipx ensurepath puts their folder on your PATH).

DuckDB is pinned exactly (1.5.4), because the bytes of the files depend on it, so uvx, uv tool and pipx keep it apart from a DuckDB you use for queries.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Name the bundle's schema
items.text:
Every command that reads a bundle takes the bundle's JSON Schema, --bundle-schema. The tables are generated from that schema, so the schema decides the columns. For a ClinVar-GKM bundle, pass the schema $id of the bundle's own schema_version, and --version-property schema_version:

Bundle schema_version --bundle-schema 1.2.0 (line v1/1.2/) https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json 1.1.0 (line v1/1.1/) https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json

The tool fetches the schema and every schema it references once, and caches them (~/.cache/gkm-bundle-parquet/). A schema-set directory works too, for offline use.

  • A 1.2.0 bundle gives exactly the tables this guide documents. Its schema narrows ClinVar-GKM's classes and declares the target table of most references, so nearly every value gets a typed column: 146 top-level columns over the 20 tables. generate lists the 51 positions it keeps as JSON text, mostly extensions nested inside extensions.
  • A 1.1.0 bundle gives wider tables. Its schema leaves many classes open, so the 1.1.0 2026-10-31 delta (495,547 records) built with the 1.1.0 schema has 339 top-level columns, and generate lists 181 JSON-text positions. The records are the same; only the columns differ. ClinVar-GKM publishes a column set that narrows them to what 1.1.0 bundles hold; see Parquet for Previous Releases.

The commands below use a shell array for the two options, written "${P[@]}"; an array works in both bash and zsh, where a plain string variable would reach the tool as one argument. Set it once in the shell you run the other blocks in:

P=(--bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json --version-property schema_version)
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Work offline with a schema set
items.text:
To build where there is no network, or to pin the exact schema files a build used, write the schema and every schema it references into a directory once, with vendor-schemas.py from the tool's source (it isn't in the PyPI package; uvx --from runs it with the tool's own libraries):

curl -fsSO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clingen-data-model/gkm-bundle-parquet/v2.0.0/scripts/vendor-schemas.py
uvx --from gkm-bundle-parquet==2.0.0 python vendor-schemas.py \
    https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json clinvar-gkm-1.2.0-schemas/

clinvar-gkm-1.2.0-schemas: 143 files, schema set sha256 3b3920180d08f3343d7466ce55bbcb95f5cbc467c505a4e03797b8f3c48d6798

Then pass the directory as --bundle-schema; the tool reads it with no network:

P_OFFLINE=(--bundle-schema clinvar-gkm-1.2.0-schemas/ --version-property schema_version)

Use "${P_OFFLINE[@]}" wherever this page writes "${P[@]}". The schema set sha256 is the same as the URL's, so the tables are the same: built from the 2026-11-15 delta with the network blocked and an empty schema cache, all 20 files had the same sha256 as the build from the URL. On a machine without a network, the tool must already be installed there too.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Build the tables
items.text:
Download the 2026-11-15 weekly delta and its checksum sidecar into the working directory. Every delta example on this page reads it. Its path changes when its month ends (it moves to deltas/2026-11/), so the commands look it up in the line's index.json:

DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"] if d["release"] == "2026-11-15"))')
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}.sha256"

build reads one bundle and writes one Parquet file per section, plus manifest.json and table-spec.json (uses P from Name the bundle's schema):

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" --out parquet/

built 20 table(s) of spec sections 2.0, 39062 rows
  sequenceReference                               0  e3e7d2b96baf
  location                                      176  8b17d4d0e861
  allele                                        230  dbc7056a155d
  …
  propositionPathogenicity                     3399  4f59dd9944fe
  …
  evidenceLine                                 6064  038fd5c573b3
  scv                                         17562  333222b90a40
  vcv                                          2941  ca684960ee57
  rcv                                          2548  b7796596ea52
manifest: parquet/manifest.json

The last column is the start of each file's sha256. Progress lines go to stderr. A delta holds only the records that changed that week, so some tables are empty.

On the delta: 9 s, 1.9 GB peak memory, 5 MB of output (20 tables, manifest.json, table-spec.json).

  • The bundle's checksum. Pass --sha256 <hex>, or keep the published <file>.sha256 sidecar beside the bundle and the tool checks it. A bundle URL works as --full too; it is streamed.
  • Every row is checked. Before a file is written, each row is turned back into JSON and compared with its source record. A difference stops the build; nothing is dropped silently.
  • What you get is the published layout. The same bundle and schema give the same tables and the same table_spec_sha256 as the published set.
  • Only some tables. --tables submitter,scv builds only those tables (on the delta: 4 s, 1.0 GB peak memory). Such a set is for querying: verify reports the other tables missing, and rebuild and verify --roundtrip need every table.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: A full bundle
items.text:
To build the tables of a whole release, pass a monthly or weekly full bundle (about 4.9 GB compressed; 91,973,603 records in the 2026-11-15 weekly full), such as clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz from Monthly Full Bundles. It builds on a 16 GB machine; more memory makes it faster.

Command 16 GB machine 128 GiB machine build 3 h 19 min, 10.0 GiB peak 38 min, 65 GiB peak verify --bundle-recompute 9 min verify --roundtrip over 2 h (not run to the end) 30 min rebuild 20 min validate (rs engine) 11 min

The 16 GB machine is a Google Cloud e2-standard-4 (4 vCPUs, 16 GB of memory, SSD, Debian 12), building the 2026-11-15 weekly full on 2026-11-22 with the defaults and a --work-dir. The same command for the newest monthly (replace /big/disk/tmp with a directory on a disk with about 30 GB free):

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz "${P[@]}" --out parquet-full/ \
    --work-dir /big/disk/tmp

All 20 tables were written, with no --threads 1 needed. The machine as a whole peaked at 11.3 GiB used, with no swap. The round trip was stopped after 2 hours, still running, when the measurement ended. The 128 GiB machine figures are the tool maintainers' own, on a 16-core cloud machine, for the 2026-10-31 full relabelled as 1.2.0.

The output is 4.6 GB. Disk: the staged records and DuckDB's spill files go to --work-dir (default: beside --out); on the 16 GB machine they peaked at 24 GiB beside the bundle, so plan for about 30 GB free there plus the bundle and the output. validate was also run on the laptop, on a full bundle: 24 minutes, with 0 failing records (see Parquet for one weekly release).

Memory. Without --memory-limit, the tool gives DuckDB half the memory the process may use (the machine's, or a container's limit when lower), and DuckDB spills to --work-dir past that. The limit is DuckDB's, not the whole process's: on the 16 GB machine the default gave DuckDB about 7.8 GiB and the process peaked at 10.0 GiB. So the default suits a machine the build has to itself. Set --memory-limit lower only when other work needs the memory, and leave about 3 GB above it for the rest of the process; a lower limit means more spilling and a slower build, and wasn't measured. The limit doesn't change the files: a build that spills writes the same bytes. When you need only part of a release, cut a mini-bundle instead.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Parquet for one weekly release
items.text:
build reads one bundle (--full), so a full set of tables for one week is built from that week's full bundle:

The week How The newest release Already published at v1/1.2/parquet/; see Parquet Files A week in the current month Download its weekly full from v1/1.2/weekly/ (Weekly Full Bundles) and build --full it Any earlier week Rebuild that week's full bundle from a monthly plus deltas (below), then build --full it

Building any full bundle takes about 3.5 hours on a 16 GB machine, or 40 minutes on a large one (A full bundle). To get only some of the week's records, use its full bundle for selections instead: select streams it.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Rebuild a week's full bundle
items.text:
Weekly fulls are kept only for the current month. For an earlier week, download replay-bundle.py, a script ClinVar-GKM publishes. It needs only python3 (3.9 or later, standard library), in bash or zsh:

curl -fsSO --retry 5 https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/1.2/assets/scripts/replay-bundle.py
python3 replay-bundle.py --release 2026-11-15 --plan

line v1/1.2, release 2026-11-15
  monthly clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz (source_release 2026-10-31, 4,881,641,096 bytes)
  delta   clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1108.json.gz (60,824,851 bytes)
  delta   clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz (5,355,360 bytes)

--plan lists what it would use and stops. Without it, the script downloads them and writes the week's bundle:

python3 replay-bundle.py --release 2026-11-15

What it does:

  • It picks the bundles from index.json as Rebuild a past week says: the newest official monthly whose source_release is on or before the week (never the 00-latest copy), and every delta after that source_release, up to and including the week, in release order. It checks the chain (each delta's baseline_release is the release before it) and stops on a gap.
  • It checks every download. Each bundle's sha256 must match index.json. Downloads are retried, and a partial download resumes. A bundle already in the folder (--dir, default the current one) is used when its sha256 matches, so a monthly you downloaded before isn't downloaded again.
  • It needs little memory. It reads the deltas into memory as text, section by section: each delta's deletes (from its manifest) and then its records. It then streams the monthly once: a record a delta replaced is written from the delta, a deleted one is dropped, any other is copied as it is, and each section ends with the deltas' new records.
  • It writes the published layout. The result, clinvar-gkm_2026-1115.replayed.json.gz, has the same one-record-per-line layout and schema_version as the published bundles, and a .sha256 sidecar beside it.

Measured on the laptop, rebuilding 2026-11-15 from the 2026-11 monthly and the 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15 deltas (1,818,764 records and 1,669,779 deletes): 7.6 minutes in an empty folder, downloads included (6.4 minutes with the monthly already there), 2.2 GB peak memory, a 4.9 GB bundle of 91,973,603 records. Both runs wrote the same bytes (sha256 876b41ec…): the output doesn't depend on the run.

It matches the published weekly full. Compared with v1/1.2/weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1115.json.gz section by section, by the record count and the sum of the sha256 of every record line (its key and its text, so the order of records doesn't matter), all 20 sections are equal: every record of the rebuilt bundle has the published record's exact text. Only the order of the records within a section differs. And the tool reads it:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 validate clinvar-gkm_2026-1115.replayed.json.gz "${P[@]}"

bundle: clinvar-gkm_2026-1115.replayed.json.gz (sha256 876b41ecb379019726fa1f80124400a6770bde359b33b2f1a787fb14c35436aa, sidecar)
version: 1.2.0; schema set sha256 3b3920180d08f3343d7466ce55bbcb95f5cbc467c505a4e03797b8f3c48d6798
engine: rs; 10 workers
  section                                records  failing cpu ms/rec  compile s
  …
records: 91,973,603  failing: 0  (1,438.0 s)
PASS

Then build it, as for any full bundle (A full bundle; not run on the replayed file for this page, which holds the same records as the weekly full measured there):

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm_2026-1115.replayed.json.gz "${P[@]}" --out parquet-2026-1115/

For a week of the frozen 1.1 line, add --line v1/1.1 to the script, and build with the 1.1.0 schema and column set (Parquet for Previous Releases). Tested on 1.1's 2026-10-24 (the 2026-10 monthly and four deltas, 91,502,593 records, 7.3 minutes with the downloads), every record matches the published weekly full of that week, but not every one byte for byte: 1,461 condition records list their aliases in another order. The 1.1 pipeline wrote that array in the order its source gave, which changed between releases (1.2.0 sorts it), so a 1.1 replay keeps the order of the monthly and deltas. As sets of values, the tool's round-trip comparison, they are identical.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: Cut a mini-bundle
items.text:
A selection starts from rows of one table, the driver, and follows the bundle's #/… references to collect related records. The result is a mini-bundle: those records, byte for byte as published, in the bundle's own layout. It is a real bundle: every tool that reads ClinVar-GKM bundles reads it.

Option Meaning --driver <table> the table the selection starts from --where "<SQL>" a DuckDB condition over that table's columns, e.g. name = 'OMIM'; a field inside a STRUCT column by its dotted path, e.g. classification.name = 'Pathogenic' --ids a,b / --ids-file f starting keys (added to --where) --follow out add every record a selected record points to (the default) --follow in add every record that points to a selected record --follow both both, from every record reached --max-depth N stop after N reference hops from the driver; 0 keeps only the driver rows --where matched --sections a,b only traverse and write these sections

Two rules from the CLI Reference: every --ids key must be in the bundle (to start from a list that may hold keys a delta lacks, match it in --where with a subquery that reads the file), and on a delta, set --max-depth, because in 2.0.0 a walk into a section the delta omits doesn't finish.

Choose --follow and --max-depth with the bundle's hubs in mind. Following references out of a record always ends: a statement points to its proposition, which points to its variant and condition. Following them in to a widely shared record does not: --follow in from the condition not provided collects millions of propositions. Keep --max-depth low whenever the walk can reach a condition, gene or submitter from the inside.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: One submitter's submissions
items.text:
Every SCV of one submitter, their propositions and evidence lines, the variants and conditions they are about, and the VCV and RCV statements that cite them:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 select --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver submitter --where "name = 'ClinGen Leukodystrophy and Leukoencephalopathy Variant Curation Expert Panel, ClinGen'" \
    --follow both --max-depth 3 \
    --out leukodystrophy-ep.json.gz

selected 219 record(s) in 5 section(s) from clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz: leukodystrophy-ep.json.gz (17718 bytes, sha256 989c64af…)
  submitter                                       1
  evidenceLine                                   73
  scv                                            72
  vcv                                             1
  rcv                                            72

1 s on the delta. From the submitter, depth 1 reaches its SCVs; depth 2 their propositions and the VCV and RCV evidence lines that cite them; depth 3 the variants, the conditions and the citing VCV and RCV statements. A delta holds only the records that changed that week: here the SCVs changed but their propositions didn't, so the walk stops at them, and the run also reported 72 references to records the delta doesn't carry (the unchanged propositions). A selection from a full bundle has none.
path: Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles

items.title: One variant
items.text:
