items.text:
File clinvar-gkm-1.1.0.columns.yaml URL https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/1.2/assets/column-sets/clinvar-gkm-1.1.0.columns.yaml For bundles of schema_version 1.1.0: every bundle in v1/1.1/ Schema it pairs with --bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json Tool gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0

--column-set takes the file or the URL. The set is the tool's own 1.1.0 test fixture, with one change: it names the schema $id that the 1.1.0 URL actually serves (…/1.1.0/json/ClinvarGkmBundle, from the 1.1.0 tag), so it pairs with that URL. The tool's fixture names the $id corrected after the tag, which the URL doesn't serve, and is refused with it.

items.title: Build the tables
items.text:
The commands run the tool with uvx, which runs a pinned release without installing it; with the tool installed (Install), write gkm-bundle-parquet in place of uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0. They work in bash and zsh.

Prerequisites

  • uv for uvx (tested with 0.6.14), or gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 installed with pipx or pip (Install); it needs Python 3.10 or later (tested with 3.14).
  • curl, python3 (step 1) and shasum (macOS) or sha256sum (Linux).
  • Data: a v1/1.1/ bundle, found in step 1 and downloaded in step 2. A delta is 2 to 150 MB; the 24 MB delta in the examples built in 37 seconds with a 3.1 GB memory peak and verified in 29 seconds on a 16 GB Apple M2 Pro. For a monthly, see Time and memory first.
  • Each step continues from the one before: step 2 downloads a path that step 1 prints, and steps 3 and 4 read the file step 2 downloaded and the parquet/ folder step 3 writes.

items.title: 1. Find the bundle
items.text:
Read the paths from the line's own index.json. A frozen line keeps every path, but the folders differ by month (the line's last month of deltas is in deltas/, earlier months in deltas/YYYY-MM/), so copy the path rather than guess it.

curl -sSf --retry 5 -o index.json https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/index.json && python3 -c '
import json
d = json.load(open("index.json"))
for m in d["datasets"]["monthly"]:
    print("monthly", m["release"], m["source_release"], m["size"], m["path"])
for x in d["deltas"]:
    print("delta  ", x["release"], x["bundle"]["size"], x["bundle"]["path"])'

-f makes curl stop with the HTTP error when a request fails, instead of saving the server's error page, and && runs Python only when the download succeeded; --retry 5 rides out a brief server error (HTTP 5xx).

A monthly is a full bundle (4.5 to 4.8 GB compressed, about 90 million records); its source_release is the weekly release it holds. The newest monthly is listed twice: under its own name and as clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, a copy of it. A delta holds only what changed in one weekly release (2 to 150 MB). To get a full bundle for a week between monthlies, replay the deltas onto the monthly first with replay-bundle.py --line v1/1.1; see Parquet for one weekly release and Rebuild a past week.

items.title: 2. Download it and check its sha256
items.text:
B=v1/1.1/deltas/2026-09/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-0928.json.gz
curl -f --retry 5 -O "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/$B" -O "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/$B.sha256"
shasum -a 256 -c "$(basename "$B").sha256"

B is a path from step 1. On Linux, sha256sum -c does the same as shasum -a 256 -c. The commands on this page hold no # comments: zsh, unlike bash, reads # in a pasted command as text unless setopt interactivecomments is on.

items.title: 3. Build
items.text:
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-0928.json.gz \
    --bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json \
    --column-set https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/1.2/assets/column-sets/clinvar-gkm-1.1.0.columns.yaml \
    --out parquet/

--column-set also takes the downloaded file. For a monthly, give the monthly's file name, and see Time and memory first.

The tool reads the .sha256 sidecar beside the bundle and records it in manifest.json. A build that completes lists the 20 tables and their rows; a build that stops names the section, the record key and the property no column covers:

error: table submitter: … record: key clinvar.submitter:509943: top-level field(s) no column covers: [name]

No published 1.1 bundle stops the build (see What is verified). If one does, build that bundle with no --column-set (the wide default) and open an issue.

If the build stops with a DuckDB Parallel CSV Reader error

On one of the 18 deltas (2026-08-16), gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 stops with NotImplementedException: Not implemented Error: The Parallel CSV Reader currently does not support a full read on this file, with or without a column set. It comes from DuckDB reading the tool's own staging files, not from the bundle. Run the same command again with --threads 1, and pass --threads 1 to verify too: both then complete, and the round trip is identical.

items.title: 4. Prove that nothing was lost
items.text:
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 verify parquet/ --roundtrip --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-0928.json.gz

verify pass: directory check: 0 problem(s); round trip: identical

--roundtrip --full rebuilds the records from the tables and compares them with the bundle's own records, by their canonical form (round trip). To keep the rebuilt bundle, run rebuild parquet/ -o rebuilt.json.gz instead: it ends with record-identical to the source when every record matches.

items.title: Time and memory
items.text:
Bundle build (time, peak memory) verify --roundtrip Where 2026-10-31 delta, 495,547 records 22 s, 2.4 GB 16 s, 0.9 GB a 16 GB laptop 2026-09-23 delta, 4,530,457 records (the largest) 82 s, 3.3 GB 66 s, 1.7 GB a 16 GB laptop a full bundle, about 92 million records 3 h 19 min, 10.0 GiB over 2 h a 16 GB cloud machine a full bundle, about 92 million records 38 min, 65 GiB 30 min a 128 GiB machine

Every delta builds on a laptop. The full-bundle figures are for the 1.2 line's 2026-11-15 weekly full (A full bundle); a 1.1.0 monthly with this column set is the same size of job. On a 16 GB machine it needs about 30 GB free in --work-dir and a few hours; a monthly was not built on a laptop for this page. If you need only part of a release, cut a mini-bundle instead: select takes the same --bundle-schema and --column-set.

items.title: What is verified
items.text:
Run on 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21 with gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0, the published 1.1.0 column set and the 1.1.0 schema URL. No monthly was built whole (a job of hours, as above); the two monthlies at the ends of the line were scanned instead, and every other v1/1.1/ bundle is made of their records and the deltas':

  • Every published v1/1.1/ delta (18 deltas, 2026-07-06 to 2026-10-31, 10,267,303 records): each built, rebuild reported it record-identical to the source, verify --roundtrip --full passed, and a separate record-by-record comparison of the rebuilt bundle with the source, keeping array order, found no difference. The 2026-08-16 delta needed --threads 1 (see the note under Build).
  • The newest monthly, clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz (source release 2026-10-31, 91,854,927 records), was streamed once, and every property each record holds was listed with the JSON kind of its value and the section each #/… pointer names, then compared with what the verified deltas hold. 528 records hold something no delta holds: the 38 therapy and 10 therapyGroup records, 463 somatic clinical impact propositions that point to a therapy, a therapy group or a condition set or carry a condition qualifier, and 17 statements and evidence lines with a method or condition extension no delta has. Built on their own with the column set, those 528 round-trip identically. Every other record holds only what the verified deltas hold. The scan took 26 minutes on the laptop.
  • The oldest monthly, clinvar-gkm_2026-07.json.gz (source release 2026-06-27, 86,810,319 records), was streamed the same way on 2026-11-21: no key appears twice, and its sha256 matches its sidecar. Compared with what the verified deltas and the 2026-11 monthly hold, 14 variation records hold something new: extensions nested inside a nucleotideExpression (for example invalidClinvarExpression with a string value, and expressionMerged with a boolean). Built on their own with the column set, those 14 round-trip identically (verify --roundtrip --full identical; rebuild record-identical).
  • The monthlies between (2026-08, 2026-09 and 2026-10) were not scanned on their own. Each equals the 2026-07 monthly plus the deltas after it, as the delta-reconstruction check proved for each release when it was published, so each of their records is a record of the 2026-07 monthly or of a verified delta.

So every record any published v1/1.1/ bundle holds is covered by the 2026-07 and 2026-11 monthlies and the 18 deltas, and no published 1.1 bundle stops the build. A full bundle you rebuild for one week is made of the same records.

items.title: The 1.0 line
items.text:
The 1.0 line (v1/1.0/, schema 1.0.1) can't be built with gkm-bundle-parquet, with or without a column set, for two reasons:

  • Its schema closes each part of a class. In the 1.0.1 schema each class combines a GA4GH class with a ClinVar-GKM part (allOf), and the ClinVar-GKM part says additionalProperties: false. Read strictly, as the tool reads it, a variation may then hold only extensions, and a statement only extensions, proposition and hasEvidenceLines. The generated default has no column for id, type or constraints, and a column set can't add a property the schema doesn't allow, so the build stops on the first variation. The 1.1.0 schema fixed this.
  • Some bundles hold a key twice. In 10 of the 15 published v1/1.0/ deltas, one to seven allele keys appear twice, with different expressions. The tool refuses a bundle with a repeated key (section allele, key ga4gh:VA.…: appears 2 times).

Use the 1.1 line instead. v1/1.1/ holds a bundle for every release v1/1.0/ holds: the same monthlies (2026-07 to 2026-10) and the same weekly deltas (2026-07-06 to 2026-10-11), built from the same ClinVar releases with schema 1.1.0. Build the tables from the v1/1.1/ bundle of the release you need, as above. The 1.0 bundles themselves stay published unchanged; see Previous Releases.

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Release

Outputs on this page are from the published Parquet of the 2026-11-15 release (built 2026-11-20 with gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0), queried with DuckDB 1.5.4 on an Apple M2 Pro laptop (16 GB of memory). The gene-panel recipe's tool step reads the 2026-11-15 weekly delta. The published set is overwritten every release: re-run a recipe to get today's numbers.

Each recipe answers one question: the question in plain language, a query you can run, and what to expect. They run against downloaded files; most touch one of the larger tables, which is too much for the live console. See Start Here to download.

Change the line marked -- <- to ask about your own variant, condition, gene or submitter. Joining Tables explains each join used here.

Prerequisites

  • DuckDB CLI, tested with 1.5.4. No extension is needed.
  • All 20 tables in one folder, about 4.6 GB: download them with the loop on Parquet Files → Download, then start duckdb in that folder. The queries name each table by its file name ('scv.parquet') and read the four proposition tables with the glob proposition*.parquet.
  • Each recipe stands alone and names the tables it reads, so you can download only those. Most finish in a few seconds; the ones that read every variant's gene or HGVS list take 10 to 15 seconds on the test laptop, longer when the files aren't in the operating system's cache. The release-wide exports need up to 5 GB of memory.
  • The gene-panel recipe also runs gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 with uv (tested with 0.6.14), in bash or zsh, and reads a weekly delta (5 MB) it downloads.
Recipe Tables it reads Everything ClinVar says about one variant variation or allele, the propositions, vcv, rcv, scv, submitter, condition, conditionSet PubMed ids cited for a variant variation, the propositions, scv Variants submitted for a condition condition, conditionSet, the propositions, scv, variation One submitter's footprint submitter, scv Why a variant is "conflicting" vcv, evidenceLine, scv, submitter Variants in a genomic window sequenceReference, location, allele, copyNumberCount, copyNumberChange, variation Gene rollup of ClinVar's calls variation, gene, vcv PubMed ids cited for every variant in a gene variation, gene, the propositions, scv Gene-panel subset gene, variation; then a bundle, with gkm-bundle-parquet VRS-keyed harmonization table sequenceReference, location, allele, variation, vcv Conflicting-classification watchlist vcv, evidenceLine, scv, submitter One submitter's dataset submitter, scv, the propositions, variation, condition, vcv Flat analysis table, one row per SCV scv, the propositions, variation, submitter, condition, conditionSet Export a slice to CSV or Parquet the propositions, scv

items.title: Everything ClinVar says about one variant
Find the variant
items.text:
If you know the ClinVar variation id, you already have it: clinvar:<id>. Otherwise look it up by any HGVS expression ClinVar lists for it (coding c., genomic g., non-coding n., on any transcript or assembly):

SELECT id, name
FROM 'variation.parquet'
WHERE list_contains(
        flatten([[h.nucleotideExpression.value FOR h IN e.value_object_array]
                 FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'clinvarHgvsList']),
        'NM_000059.4:c.4090A>C');                                            -- <- your HGVS

id             name
clinvar:51592  NM_000059.4(BRCA2):c.4090A>C (p.Ile1364Leu)

This scans every variant's HGVS list, the largest part of the 1.66 GB variation.parquet: about 7 seconds on the test laptop. For a GRCh38 genomic expression the allele table is much faster, because it is a short string column:

SELECT v.id, v.name
FROM 'allele.parquet' a
JOIN (SELECT id, name, unnest(members) AS member FROM 'variation.parquet') v
     ON v.member.id = a.id                -- an equality join; list_contains() in ON plans a nested loop
WHERE a.name = 'NC_000013.11:g.32338445A>C';

allele.expressions also holds the SPDI and gnomAD forms (13-32338445-A-C); see the VRS chain.

items.title: ClinVar's aggregate calls
items.text:
One row for each VCV root statement (one per classification type) and each RCV (one per condition), with the condition names resolved:

WITH prop AS (                    -- all four proposition tables, one glob
  SELECT id, type, subject, object, object_section
  FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
),
set_names AS (
  SELECT cs.id, string_agg(c.name, '; ' ORDER BY c.name) AS member_names
  FROM 'conditionSet.parquet' cs, unnest(cs.concepts) AS t(m)
  JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = m.id
  GROUP BY cs.id
),
agg AS (
  SELECT 'VCV' AS tier, id, proposition, quality.name AS level, classification.name AS classification FROM 'vcv.parquet'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'RCV', id, proposition, quality.name, classification.name FROM 'rcv.parquet'
)
SELECT a.tier, a.id AS statement, p.type AS proposition_type, a.level, a.classification,
       coalesce(c.name, sn.member_names) AS condition
FROM agg a
JOIN prop p ON p.id = a.proposition
LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition'    THEN p.object END
LEFT JOIN set_names sn          ON sn.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'conditionSet' THEN p.object END
WHERE p.subject = 'clinvar:51592'                                            -- <- your variant
  AND NOT regexp_matches(a.id, '-(PG|EP|CP|NOCP|NOCL|FLAG)(-T[0-9])?$')     -- root statements only
ORDER BY a.tier DESC, a.id;

tier  statement                proposition_type                 level              classification        condition
VCV   VCV000051592.122-G-NP    ClinvarNotProvidedProposition    no classification  not provided          not specified
VCV   VCV000051592.122-G-PATH  VariantPathogenicityProposition  expert panel       Benign                Breast-ovarian cancer, familial, susceptibility to, 2
RCV   RCV000044344.34-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Benign                Hereditary breast ovarian cancer syndrome
RCV   RCV000113272.28-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  expert panel       Benign                Breast-ovarian cancer, familial, susceptibility to, 2
RCV   RCV000120319.33-G-NP     ClinvarNotProvidedProposition    no classification  not provided          not specified
RCV   RCV000120319.33-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Benign/Likely benign  not specified
RCV   RCV000131014.17-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Benign/Likely benign  Hereditary cancer-predisposing syndrome
RCV   RCV000389513.13-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Likely benign         Fanconi anemia complementation group D1
RCV   RCV000469910.10-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Benign                Familial cancer of breast
RCV   RCV000656601.24-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Benign                not provided
RCV   RCV000770724.10-G-PATH   VariantPathogenicityProposition  criteria provided  Benign                Breast and/or ovarian cancer

Drop the root-statement filter to see each level statement as well (-EP, -CP, -NOCP, …); Reading a variant's statements explains them.

items.title: Every submission
items.text:
Who submitted, what they said, at what level, for which condition, and when they last evaluated it:

WITH prop AS (
  SELECT id, type, subject, object, object_section
  FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
),
set_names AS (
  SELECT cs.id, string_agg(c.name, '; ' ORDER BY c.name) AS member_names
  FROM 'conditionSet.parquet' cs, unnest(cs.concepts) AS t(m)
  JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = m.id
  GROUP BY cs.id
)
SELECT replace(s.id, 'clinvar.submission:', '') AS scv,
       sub.name                AS submitter,
       s.classification.name   AS classification,
       s.quality.name          AS level,
       coalesce(c.name, sn.member_names) AS condition,
       [x.date FOR x IN s.contributions IF x.activityType = 'evaluated'][1] AS last_evaluated
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN prop p ON p.id = s.proposition
LEFT JOIN 'submitter.parquet' sub
       ON sub.id = [x.contributor FOR x IN s.contributions IF x.activityType = 'submitted'][1]
LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition'    THEN p.object END
LEFT JOIN set_names sn          ON sn.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'conditionSet' THEN p.object END
WHERE p.subject = 'clinvar:51592'                                            -- <- your variant
ORDER BY last_evaluated DESC, scv
LIMIT 3;

scv              submitter                                                                    classification  level              condition                                  last_evaluated
SCV000072357.18  Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae), Labcorp                                 Benign          criteria provided  Hereditary breast ovarian cancer syndrome  2026-02-03
SCV000602753.7   ARUP Laboratories, Molecular Genetics and Genomics, ARUP Laboratories        Benign          criteria provided  not provided                               2025-05-19
SCV004243027.2   Center for Genomic Medicine, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen University Hospital  Benign          criteria provided  not specified                              2025-03-04

36 submissions for this variant; drop the LIMIT to see them all. date is ISO text, so it sorts correctly as text; CAST(date AS DATE) gives a DATE.

items.title: PubMed ids cited for a variant
items.text:
PubMed ids appear only on SCVs (individual submissions), in scv.reportedIn[].pmid. The variant, VCV and RCV records carry none. So the query goes from the variant to its propositions, and from the propositions to the SCVs that cite them.

WITH v AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM 'variation.parquet' WHERE id = 'clinvar:10'         -- <- your variant
),
prop AS (                                     -- all four proposition tables, one glob
  SELECT id, subject FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
),
cites AS (                                    -- one row per (SCV, cited PubMed id)
  SELECT p.subject AS variant_id, s.id AS scv_id, unnest(s.reportedIn).pmid AS pmid
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN prop p ON p.id = s.proposition
  WHERE p.subject IN (SELECT id FROM v)
)
SELECT v.id AS variant_id, v.name AS variant_name, c.pmid,
       'https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/' || c.pmid AS pubmed_url,
       count(DISTINCT c.scv_id) AS n_scvs,
       string_agg(DISTINCT replace(c.scv_id, 'clinvar.submission:', ''), ', '
                  ORDER BY replace(c.scv_id, 'clinvar.submission:', '')) AS scvs
FROM cites c JOIN v ON v.id = c.variant_id
WHERE c.pmid IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY n_scvs DESC, c.pmid;

For clinvar:10, NM_000410.4(HFE):c.187C>G (p.His63Asp), the most-cited PubMed ids, each with the SCVs that cite it. Selected columns:

pmid      n_scvs  scvs
19159930       5  SCV000198337.5, SCV001194094.2, SCV001251532.1, SCV001519563.1, SCV002568070.8
8696333        5  SCV000461883.3, SCV001519563.1, SCV002502480.1, SCV002506442.3, SCV006582525.2
19554541       4  SCV000198337.5, SCV000461883.3, SCV001194094.2, SCV002769510.1
9356458        4  SCV000219176.11, SCV001519563.1, SCV002568070.8, SCV006582525.2
…

The query leaves out one kind of citation on purpose: scv.specifiedBy.reportedIn.pmid is the paper describing the submitter's classification method, such as the ACMG/AMP guidelines (PMID 25741868). It appears on most submissions, so it says nothing about the variant. Add it only if you want it.

Asking this often?

If you look up many variants, materialize the statement–proposition join once. Each lookup then reads one small table, and the PubMed ids are already gathered into a list per SCV.

items.title: Variants submitted for a condition
items.text:
Every variant with a submission for one condition, with how submitters classified it. A submission can name the condition directly or as a member of a condition set, so the query collects both (see Seam B):

WITH target AS (
  SELECT id FROM 'condition.parquet' WHERE name = 'Marfan syndrome'          -- <- your condition
),
members AS (                      -- one row per (condition set, member id)
  SELECT cs.id AS set_id, m.id AS member_id
  FROM 'conditionSet.parquet' cs, unnest(cs.concepts) AS t(m)
),
sets AS (                         -- the sets that list the condition directly
  SELECT m.set_id AS id FROM members m JOIN target ON target.id = m.member_id
),
objects AS (                      -- the condition itself, plus every set that contains it (one level of nesting)
  SELECT id FROM target
  UNION
  SELECT id FROM sets
  UNION
  SELECT m.set_id FROM members m JOIN sets ON sets.id = m.member_id
),
prop AS (
  SELECT id, subject, object FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
)
SELECT p.subject AS variant_id, v.name AS variant_name,
       count(*) AS scvs,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.classification.primaryCoding.code IN ('pathogenic', 'likely pathogenic'))  AS p_lp,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.classification.primaryCoding.code = 'uncertain significance')           AS vus,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.classification.primaryCoding.code IN ('benign', 'likely benign'))       AS b_lb
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN prop p ON p.id = s.proposition
JOIN 'variation.parquet' v ON v.id = p.subject
WHERE p.object IN (SELECT id FROM objects)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scvs DESC, p.subject
LIMIT 10;

variant_id      variant_name                                scvs  p_lp  vus  b_lb
clinvar:163462  NM_000138.5(FBN1):c.7754T>C (p.Ile2585Thr)    13    13    0     0
clinvar:16451   NM_000138.5(FBN1):c.3509G>A (p.Arg1170His)    13     1    4     7
clinvar:42394   NM_000138.5(FBN1):c.5788+5G>A                 13    13    0     0
clinvar:16445   NM_000138.5(FBN1):c.8176C>T (p.Arg2726Trp)    11     0    4     7
…

The counts use the normalized classification.primaryCoding.code, not the submitted text; Anatomy of a Table explains why.

items.title: One submitter's footprint
items.text:
What one organization has submitted, by classification and submission level. The Auditing a Submitter's Footprint story walks through this kind of audit in depth.

WITH sub AS (
  SELECT id FROM 'submitter.parquet' WHERE name = 'Mayo Clinic Laboratories, Mayo Clinic'   -- <- your submitter
)
SELECT s.classification.primaryCoding.code AS classification,
       s.quality.name                      AS level,
       count(*)                            AS scvs
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
WHERE [c.contributor FOR c IN s.contributions IF c.activityType = 'submitted'][1] IN (SELECT id FROM sub)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scvs DESC;

classification          level                           scvs
uncertain significance  criteria provided               18,830
benign                  criteria provided               18,791
likely benign           criteria provided               10,983
pathogenic              criteria provided                2,543
likely pathogenic       criteria provided                2,047
…

Find a submitter's exact name with SELECT id, name FROM 'submitter.parquet' WHERE name ILIKE '%mayo%'.

items.title: Why a variant is "conflicting"
items.text:
ClinVar calls 184,296 variants Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity in 2026-11-15. This finds them:

SELECT classification.name AS classification, count(*) AS variants
FROM 'vcv.parquet'
WHERE regexp_matches(id, '-G-PATH$')                -- the germline pathogenicity root statement
  AND classification.name ILIKE 'conflicting%'
GROUP BY ALL;

To see why one variant is conflicting, list the submissions behind each level of its pathogenicity call, grouped by what they said. This walks the VCV evidence lines down to the SCVs (Seam E):

WITH scv_vcv AS (
  SELECT regexp_replace(el.id, '\.(non-)?contributing$', '') AS vcv_statement_id,
         item.id AS scv_id
  FROM 'evidenceLine.parquet' el, unnest(el.hasEvidenceItems) AS t(item)
  WHERE el.id LIKE 'VCV000000010.%-G-PATH-%'                                -- <- your variant's VCV accession
    AND item.section = 'scv'
)
SELECT x.vcv_statement_id,
       s.classification.primaryCoding.code AS classification,
       count(*) AS scvs,
       string_agg(DISTINCT sub.name, '; ' ORDER BY sub.name) AS submitters
FROM scv_vcv x
JOIN 'scv.parquet' s ON s.id = x.scv_id
LEFT JOIN 'submitter.parquet' sub
       ON sub.id = [c.contributor FOR c IN s.contributions IF c.activityType = 'submitted'][1]
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY x.vcv_statement_id, scvs DESC, classification;

vcv_statement_id              classification              scvs  submitters
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-CP    pathogenic                    41  3billion; AiLife Diagnostics, …
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-CP    likely pathogenic              2  Genomic Medicine Center of Excellence, …
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-CP    uncertain significance         2  Cambridge Genomics Laboratory, …
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-CP    pathogenic, low penetrance     1  Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae), Labcorp
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-FLAG  benign                         1  Pathology and Clinical Laboratory Medicine, …
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-FLAG  uncertain significance         1  Laboratory for Molecular Medicine, …
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-NOCP  pathogenic                     8  Clinical Genetics DNA and cytogenetics Diagnostics Lab, …

The call comes from the -CP level, the highest present. Among those 46 submissions, two say uncertain significance against 43 pathogenic or likely pathogenic; that disagreement is the conflict. The -NOCP and -FLAG submissions are listed but don't count toward the call. The VCV accession number is the variation id zero-padded to nine digits (clinvar:10 → VCV000000010).

items.title: Variants in a genomic window
items.text:
Every variant (alleles and copy-number variants) whose location overlaps a window on GRCh38 chromosome 13. Coordinates are interbase (0-based, end-exclusive), so the window [32338400, 32338500) covers 1-based positions 32,338,401–32,338,500.

WITH seq AS (
  SELECT id FROM 'sequenceReference.parquet' WHERE name = 'NC_000013.11'    -- <- chromosome (RefSeq accession)
),
loc AS (
  SELECT id, start_min, start_max, end_min, end_max FROM 'location.parquet'
  WHERE sequenceReference = (SELECT id FROM seq)
    AND start_max < 32338500 AND end_min > 32338400                         -- <- window
),
vrs AS (
  SELECT id, location FROM 'allele.parquet'
  UNION ALL SELECT id, location FROM 'copyNumberCount.parquet'
  UNION ALL SELECT id, location FROM 'copyNumberChange.parquet'
)
SELECT v.id, v.name, l.start_min, l.start_max, l.end_min, l.end_max
FROM vrs
JOIN loc l ON l.id = vrs.location
JOIN (SELECT id, name, unnest(members) AS member FROM 'variation.parquet') v ON v.member.id = vrs.id
ORDER BY l.start_max, v.id;

id              name                                              start_min  start_max  end_min    end_max
clinvar:146305  GRCh38/hg38 13q11-34(chr13:18445862-114327173)x1  NULL       18445861   114327173  NULL
clinvar:151282  GRCh38/hg38 13q11-34(chr13:18456040-114340285)x3  NULL       18456039   114340285  NULL
clinvar:59851   GRCh38/hg38 13q11-34(chr13:18565048-114327173)x3  NULL       18565047   114327173  NULL
…

244 variants in this 100-base window in 2026-11-15. 35 of them are copy-number variants whose start or end is an uncertain range, like the three above: ClinVar knows the deleted or duplicated span covers at least [start_max, end_min), but not how far beyond it. For a definite coordinate the min and max columns are equal.

The query matches on the span each variant certainly covers. To include every variant that may reach the window, match on the outer bounds instead, treating NULL as unbounded: coalesce(start_min, 0) < 32338500 AND coalesce(end_max, 9e9) > 32338400 (641 variants here).

items.title: Gene rollup of ClinVar's calls
items.text:
ClinVar's germline pathogenicity call for every variant in a gene. Genes come from the variant's ClinVar gene list (ncbigene: ids), not the gene-context symbol, which isn't a reliable gene join.

WITH v AS (                       -- variants whose ClinVar gene list names the gene
  SELECT x.id
  FROM (SELECT id,
               unnest(flatten([[g.gene FOR g IN e.value_object_array
                                IF g.relationship_type IN ('within single gene', 'within multiple genes by overlap',
                                                           'asserted, but not computed')]
                               FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'clinvarGeneList'])) AS gene_id
        FROM 'variation.parquet') x
  JOIN 'gene.parquet' gene ON gene.id = x.gene_id      -- an equality join, so DuckDB plans a fast hash join
  WHERE gene.name = 'MYH7'                                                    -- <- your gene symbol
)
SELECT classification.name AS clinvar_call, count(*) AS variants
FROM 'vcv.parquet'
WHERE regexp_matches(id, '-G-PATH$')                                          -- germline pathogenicity root
  AND 'clinvar:' || CAST(substr(id, 4, 9) AS INTEGER) IN (SELECT id FROM v)   -- VCV accession number = variation id
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY variants DESC;

clinvar_call                                  variants
Uncertain significance                           3,034
Likely benign                                    1,697
Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity       560
Likely pathogenic                                  257
Benign                                             146
Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic                        95
…

Nearly all the work, about 8 seconds on the test laptop, is reading the gene lists in variation.parquet. The relationship_type filter drops large copy-number variants that merely overlap the gene and variants near it; remove it to include them.

Reach into nested lists with [… FOR … IN …], not unnest

The gene filter above uses a list comprehension. Written instead with unnest(extensions) and unnest(value_object_array), the same filter returns the same variants, but unnest first expands every variant's whole extension list into rows, which is many times slower and uses more memory.

items.title: PubMed ids cited for every variant in a gene
items.text:
The gene filter from the rollup, joined to the PubMed query:

WITH v AS (                                  -- variants whose ClinVar gene list names the gene
  SELECT x.id, x.name
  FROM (SELECT id, name,
               unnest(flatten([[g.gene FOR g IN e.value_object_array
                                -- drop large CNVs that merely overlap the gene, and near-gene variants:
                                IF g.relationship_type IN ('within single gene', 'within multiple genes by overlap',
                                                           'asserted, but not computed')]
                               FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'clinvarGeneList'])) AS gene_id
        FROM 'variation.parquet') x
  JOIN 'gene.parquet' gene ON gene.id = x.gene_id      -- an equality join, so DuckDB plans a fast hash join
  WHERE gene.name = 'MYH7'                                                     -- <- your gene symbol
),
prop AS (
  SELECT id, subject FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
),
cites AS (
  SELECT p.subject AS variant_id, s.id AS scv_id, unnest(s.reportedIn).pmid AS pmid
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN prop p ON p.id = s.proposition
  WHERE p.subject IN (SELECT id FROM v)
)
SELECT v.id AS variant_id, v.name AS variant_name, c.pmid,
       count(DISTINCT c.scv_id) AS n_scvs
FROM cites c JOIN v ON v.id = c.variant_id
WHERE c.pmid IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY v.id, c.pmid;

One row per (variant, PubMed id). For MYH7 that is 6,981 rows in 2026-11-15, covering 1,696 variants and 1,095 distinct PubMed ids. For a list of distinct PubMed ids instead, wrap the final SELECT and group by pmid. Like the rollup, nearly all of its 13 seconds on the test laptop is reading the gene lists.

items.title: Gene-panel subset
items.text:
The question. Which records concern the genes on my panel, and what changed on them this week?

For a laboratory or curation group that works on a fixed gene list and wants its part of ClinVar as tables or as records.

Reads gene.parquet (3 MB) and variation.parquet (1.7 GB) to turn gene symbols into variant ids; then a bundle, with gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0.

Write the panel, one gene symbol per line, into the folder you run DuckDB from:

printf 'MYH7\nMYBPC3\nTNNT2\nTNNI3\nTPM1\nACTC1\nMYL2\nMYL3\n' > panel.txt

Then, in DuckDB, write the ids of every variant whose ClinVar gene list names a panel gene (the same gene filter as the gene rollup):

COPY (
  WITH panel AS (
    SELECT g.id FROM read_csv('panel.txt', header = false, columns = {'symbol': 'VARCHAR'}) p
    JOIN 'gene.parquet' g ON g.name = p.symbol
  )
  SELECT DISTINCT x.id
  FROM (SELECT id,
               unnest(flatten([[g.gene FOR g IN e.value_object_array
                                IF g.relationship_type IN ('within single gene', 'within multiple genes by overlap',
                                                           'asserted, but not computed')]
                               FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'clinvarGeneList'])) AS gene_id
        FROM 'variation.parquet') x
  WHERE x.gene_id IN (SELECT id FROM panel)
  ORDER BY x.id
) TO 'panel-variants.txt' (HEADER false);

panel-variants.txt holds 16,059 variant ids for these eight genes in 2026-11-15 (19 seconds). That list is the panel's key into every release.

The week's changes, as tables. Download the 2026-11-15 weekly delta into the same folder, then build the tables of a selection: every germline pathogenicity proposition about a panel variant, and the statements that point to it. The --where reads the ids file, so ids the delta doesn't carry are simply not matched:

DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in json.load(sys.stdin)["deltas"] if d["release"] == "2026-11-15"))')
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}.sha256"
P=(--bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.2.0/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json --version-property schema_version)
uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1115.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver propositionPathogenicity \
    --where "subject IN (SELECT column0 FROM read_csv('panel-variants.txt', header = false))" \
    --follow in --max-depth 1 \
    --out panel/

built 20 table(s) of spec sections 2.0, 34 rows, a selection driven by propositionPathogenicity
  …
  propositionPathogenicity                       17  4500826d4d63
  …
  scv                                             5  c95cc8a9571f
  vcv                                             6  28b71479ea6d
  rcv                                             6  9be4add670a3
manifest: panel/manifest.json

Then, in DuckDB, every changed statement about a panel variant:

SELECT p.subject AS variant, s.id AS statement, s.classification.name AS classification
FROM read_parquet(['panel/scv.parquet', 'panel/vcv.parquet', 'panel/rcv.parquet'], union_by_name = true) s
JOIN 'panel/propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON p.id = s.proposition
ORDER BY variant, statement;

variant          statement                          classification
clinvar:1060806  RCV007130300.1-G-PATH              Likely pathogenic
clinvar:1060806  RCV007130300.1-G-PATH-CP           Likely pathogenic
clinvar:1060806  VCV001060806.11-G-PATH             Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity
clinvar:1060806  VCV001060806.11-G-PATH-CP          Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity
clinvar:1060806  clinvar.submission:SCV008145506.1  Likely pathogenic
clinvar:235031   clinvar.submission:SCV008131696.1  Pathogenic
…

17 rows: 5 new SCVs on five panel variants, and the 12 VCV and RCV statements that changed with them. That is the week's changes only: a delta holds only the records that changed that week. The same command on a full bundle (clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, about 4.9 GB, from Monthly Full Bundles) gives the panel's whole record. To keep the records rather than tables, run select with the same options and --out panel.json.gz (Cut a mini-bundle).

Why this is hard with ClinVar's XML. The genes of a variant sit inside each variant's XML record, so a panel subset means parsing the whole release to find the variants, and then again to collect the submissions about them. Here the variant ids come from one query, and the tool follows the bundle's references to collect the records that mention them.

items.title: VRS-keyed harmonization table
items.text:
The question. For every ClinVar variant on GRCh38: its VRS allele id, its VCF-style coordinates, and ClinVar's call, in one file sorted by position for joining to a VCF, gnomAD or another VRS-aware dataset.

For bioinformaticians annotating variant calls, and knowledgebases that match their variants to ClinVar's.

Reads sequenceReference, location (428 MB), allele (701 MB), variation (1.7 GB) and vcv (148 MB).

COPY (
  WITH grch38 AS (                  -- GRCh38 chromosome sequences
    SELECT id FROM 'sequenceReference.parquet'
    WHERE list_contains([e.value_string FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'assembly'], 'GRCh38')
  ),
  a AS (                            -- GRCh38 alleles, with their gnomAD-style key
    SELECT a.id AS vrs_id, a.digest AS vrs_digest, a.name AS hgvs_g,
           [x.value FOR x IN a.expressions IF x.syntax = 'gnomad'][1] AS gnomad
    FROM 'allele.parquet' a
    JOIN 'location.parquet' l ON l.id = a.location
    WHERE l.sequenceReference IN (SELECT id FROM grch38)
  ),
  v AS (                            -- each variant and its allele
    SELECT id AS variation_id, name AS variation_name, unnest(members).id AS member_id
    FROM 'variation.parquet'
  ),
  call AS (                         -- ClinVar's germline pathogenicity call, one per variant
    SELECT 'clinvar:' || CAST(substr(id, 4, 9) AS INTEGER) AS variation_id,
           split_part(id, '-', 1) AS vcv,
           classification.name AS clinvar_call, quality.name AS review_level
    FROM 'vcv.parquet'
    WHERE regexp_matches(id, '-G-PATH$')
  )
  SELECT split_part(a.gnomad, '-', 1) AS chrom,
         CAST(split_part(a.gnomad, '-', 2) AS BIGINT) AS pos,
         split_part(a.gnomad, '-', 3) AS ref,
         split_part(a.gnomad, '-', 4) AS alt,
         a.vrs_id, a.vrs_digest, a.hgvs_g,
         v.variation_id, v.variation_name, c.vcv, c.clinvar_call, c.review_level
  FROM a
  JOIN v ON v.member_id = a.vrs_id
  LEFT JOIN call c ON c.variation_id = v.variation_id
  WHERE a.gnomad IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY CASE chrom WHEN 'X' THEN 23 WHEN 'Y' THEN 24 WHEN 'MT' THEN 25 ELSE TRY_CAST(chrom AS INTEGER) END,
           pos, ref, alt, v.variation_id
) TO 'clinvar-vrs-grch38.parquet' (FORMAT parquet);

14 seconds and 2.7 GB of memory on the test laptop; a 500 MB file of 4,618,658 rows, one per GRCh38 allele, in chromosome order (1–22, X, Y, MT) and then by position. Selected columns:

chrom  pos    ref  alt  vrs_id                                     variation_id     vcv             clinvar_call            review_level
1      66926  AG   A    ga4gh:VA.-mXR2-dm4-wqnOb5QgVsIga0a6Qfq0I_  clinvar:3385321  VCV003385321.2  Uncertain significance  criteria provided
1      69134  A    G    ga4gh:VA.43Poe4YtM_kc0qf1FtG8ooVY2tSmCnMt  clinvar:2205837  VCV002205837.2  Likely benign           criteria provided
1      69241  C    T    ga4gh:VA.ripmOgVei3TsCVW7AZnpSlZjTRN1USSg  clinvar:4562067  VCV004562067.1  Uncertain significance  criteria provided
  • chrom, pos, ref and alt come from the allele's gnomAD-style expression (13-32338445-A-C): 1-based, with VCF's anchor base for insertions and deletions, and chromosomes named without chr.
  • vrs_id is the key for VRS-aware data: compute the same id for your variants with vrs-python and join on it, with no coordinates involved.
  • 254,276 rows have no clinvar_call: variants with no germline pathogenicity classification (somatic-only submissions, or none). 1,440 alleles are left out: 1,031 neither on GRCh38 nor with a gnomAD-style expression, 305 on another assembly, and 104 on GRCh38 with no gnomAD-style expression.

To annotate a VCF, join on the four VCF fields. A small one to try (a real VCF works the same way; its ## header lines are skipped):

printf '##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\nchr6\t26090951\t.\tC\tG\t.\t.\t.\nchr13\t32338445\t.\tA\tC\t.\t.\t.\nchr17\t43124027\t.\tACT\tA\t.\t.\t.\nchr1\t10000\t.\tA\tG\t.\t.\t.\n' > my.vcf

SELECT x.chrom, x.pos, x.ref, x.alt, h.vrs_id, h.variation_id, h.clinvar_call, h.review_level
FROM read_csv('my.vcf', delim = '\t', comment = '#', header = false, auto_detect = false,
              columns = {'chrom': 'VARCHAR', 'pos': 'BIGINT', 'id': 'VARCHAR', 'ref': 'VARCHAR', 'alt': 'VARCHAR',
                         'qual': 'VARCHAR', 'filter': 'VARCHAR', 'info': 'VARCHAR'}) x
LEFT JOIN 'clinvar-vrs-grch38.parquet' h
       ON h.chrom = replace(x.chrom, 'chr', '') AND h.pos = x.pos AND h.ref = x.ref AND h.alt = x.alt
ORDER BY x.chrom, x.pos;

chrom  pos       ref  alt  vrs_id                                     variation_id   clinvar_call                                  review_level
chr1   10000     A    G    NULL                                       NULL           NULL                                          NULL
chr13  32338445  A    C    ga4gh:VA.Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9  clinvar:51592  Benign                                        expert panel
chr17  43124027  ACT  A    ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R  clinvar:17662  Pathogenic                                    expert panel
chr6   26090951  C    G    ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY  clinvar:10     Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity  criteria provided

auto_detect = false is needed: DuckDB's CSV sniffer rejects a VCF's header lines. For a tool that wants text, such as bcftools annotate, write the table as tab-separated text instead: COPY (SELECT * FROM 'clinvar-vrs-grch38.parquet') TO 'clinvar-vrs-grch38.tsv' (HEADER, DELIMITER '\t').

Why this is hard with ClinVar's XML. The XML describes a variant by coordinates and HGVS expressions per assembly, with no identifier computed from the change itself. Matching another dataset means normalizing both sides the same way (shifting insertions and deletions, choosing a representation) and hoping they agree. Here each allele carries its VRS id, which any VRS implementation computes the same way from the same normalized change.

items.title: Conflicting-classification watchlist
items.text:
The question. Every variant ClinVar calls Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity, one row each, with how many submissions sit on each side and who submitted them.

For curators, expert panels and laboratories deciding which conflicts to resolve, and anyone tracking whether a lab's submissions disagree with others'.

Reads vcv (148 MB), evidenceLine (265 MB), scv (785 MB) and submitter.

The call comes from one level of submissions (expert panel, criteria provided, …). The root statement's .contributing evidence line names that level's statement, and the level's own .contributing evidence line names its SCVs, so the query counts exactly the submissions behind the call (Why a variant is "conflicting" walks one variant).

COPY (
  WITH conflicting AS (             -- the germline pathogenicity root statement of each conflicting variant
    SELECT id AS vcv_statement, split_part(id, '-', 1) AS vcv
    FROM 'vcv.parquet'
    WHERE regexp_matches(id, '-G-PATH$')
      AND classification.name = 'Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity'
  ),
  level AS (                        -- the level statement the call comes from (-CP, -EP, ...)
    SELECT c.vcv, c.vcv_statement, item.id AS level_statement
    FROM conflicting c
    JOIN 'evidenceLine.parquet' el ON el.id = c.vcv_statement || '.contributing',
         unnest(el.hasEvidenceItems) AS t(item)
  ),
  scvs AS (                         -- the submissions that level counts
    SELECT l.vcv, l.vcv_statement, item.id AS scv_id
    FROM level l
    JOIN 'evidenceLine.parquet' el ON el.id = l.level_statement || '.contributing',
         unnest(el.hasEvidenceItems) AS t(item)
    WHERE item.section = 'scv'
  ),
  said AS (
    SELECT x.vcv, x.vcv_statement, x.scv_id,
           CASE WHEN s.classification.primaryCoding.code IN ('pathogenic', 'likely pathogenic') THEN 'P/LP'
                WHEN s.classification.primaryCoding.code IN ('benign', 'likely benign')         THEN 'B/LB'
                WHEN s.classification.primaryCoding.code = 'uncertain significance'            THEN 'VUS'
                ELSE coalesce(s.classification.primaryCoding.code, s.classification.name) END AS side,
           sub.name AS submitter
    FROM scvs x
    JOIN 'scv.parquet' s ON s.id = x.scv_id
    LEFT JOIN 'submitter.parquet' sub
           ON sub.id = [c.contributor FOR c IN s.contributions IF c.activityType = 'submitted'][1]
  )
  SELECT vcv,
         'clinvar:' || CAST(substr(vcv, 4, 9) AS INTEGER) AS variation_id,
         count(*) AS scvs,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'P/LP') AS p_lp,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'VUS')  AS vus,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'B/LB') AS b_lb,
         list(DISTINCT submitter ORDER BY submitter) FILTER (WHERE side = 'P/LP') AS p_lp_submitters,
         list(DISTINCT submitter ORDER BY submitter) FILTER (WHERE side = 'VUS')  AS vus_submitters,
         list(DISTINCT submitter ORDER BY submitter) FILTER (WHERE side = 'B/LB') AS b_lb_submitters
  FROM said
  GROUP BY vcv
  ORDER BY vcv
) TO 'conflicts-watchlist.parquet' (FORMAT parquet);

4 seconds; 184,296 rows, one per conflicting variant, matching the count in Why a variant is "conflicting". The submitter lists are NULL where a side has no submissions. The widest disagreements, pathogenic against benign:

SELECT vcv, scvs, p_lp, vus, b_lb, len(p_lp_submitters) AS p_lp_labs, len(b_lb_submitters) AS b_lb_labs
FROM 'conflicts-watchlist.parquet'
WHERE p_lp > 0 AND b_lb > 0
ORDER BY scvs DESC, vcv
LIMIT 3;

vcv               scvs  p_lp  vus  b_lb  p_lp_labs  b_lb_labs
VCV000002547.121    34    11   21     2         10          2
VCV000002542.117    33     1   17    15          1         15
VCV000163878.87     33     3   29     1          3          1

1,297 conflicts have submissions on both the pathogenic and the benign side; 152,879 are uncertain against benign, and 30,004 pathogenic against uncertain. A few dozen count other classifications (risk factor, low penetrance) on one side, which the three columns leave out. Filter on a submitter's name in the lists to watch one laboratory's conflicts, or join variation_id to the gene-panel ids.

Why this is hard with ClinVar's XML. The XML gives the conflicting call and a text description of the counts, but to name the disagreeing submitters you have to collect the variant's submissions and work out which review level ClinVar counted. Here the evidence lines record which submissions the call was made from.

items.title: One submitter's dataset
items.text:
The question. Everything one submitter has in ClinVar: each SCV with its variant, condition, classification and date, next to ClinVar's own call for the variant.

For a laboratory auditing its submissions, a consortium collecting its members' work, or anyone comparing one submitter with the aggregate. Auditing a Submitter's Footprint tells this story in depth.

Reads submitter, scv (785 MB), the four proposition tables (405 MB), variation (1.7 GB), condition and vcv (148 MB).

COPY (
  WITH sub AS (
    SELECT id FROM 'submitter.parquet' WHERE name = 'Mayo Clinic Laboratories, Mayo Clinic'   -- <- your submitter
  ),
  mine AS (                         -- the submitter's SCVs
    SELECT s.id, s.proposition, s.classification.name AS classification, s.quality.name AS level,
           [x.date FOR x IN s.contributions IF x.activityType = 'evaluated'][1] AS last_evaluated
    FROM 'scv.parquet' s
    WHERE [x.contributor FOR x IN s.contributions IF x.activityType = 'submitted'][1] IN (SELECT id FROM sub)
  ),
  prop AS (
    SELECT id, subject, object, object_section
    FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
  ),
  call AS (                         -- ClinVar's germline pathogenicity call per variant
    SELECT 'clinvar:' || CAST(substr(id, 4, 9) AS INTEGER) AS variation_id, classification.name AS clinvar_call
    FROM 'vcv.parquet'
    WHERE regexp_matches(id, '-G-PATH$')
  )
  SELECT replace(m.id, 'clinvar.submission:', '') AS scv,
         p.subject AS variation_id, v.name AS variation_name,
         c.name    AS condition,                  -- NULL when the object is a condition set
         m.classification, m.level, m.last_evaluated,
         k.clinvar_call
  FROM mine m
  JOIN prop p ON p.id = m.proposition
  LEFT JOIN 'variation.parquet' v ON v.id = p.subject
  LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition' THEN p.object END
  LEFT JOIN call k ON k.variation_id = p.subject
  ORDER BY scv
) TO 'mayo-scvs.parquet' (FORMAT parquet);

Under a second; 56,132 rows. Selected columns:

scv             variation_name                            condition      classification     clinvar_call
SCV000256908.1  NM_000038.6(APC):c.1045C>T (p.Gln349Ter)  not provided   Likely pathogenic  Pathogenic
SCV000256909.1  NM_000038.6(APC):c.120G>A (p.Glu40=)      not specified  Likely benign      Benign/Likely benign
SCV000256910.3  NM_000038.6(APC):c.1213C>T (p.Arg405Ter)  not provided   Pathogenic         Pathogenic

How the submitter's calls line up with ClinVar's:

SELECT classification, clinvar_call, count(*) AS scvs
FROM 'mayo-scvs.parquet'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scvs DESC
LIMIT 4;

classification          clinvar_call                                  scvs
Uncertain significance  Uncertain significance                        12963
Benign                  Benign                                        10046
Benign                  Benign/Likely benign                           8805
Uncertain significance  Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity   6112

As records. To keep the submitter's records as published, for sharing or for the GA4GH libraries, cut a mini-bundle from a full bundle (about 4.9 GB) with gkm-bundle-parquet. It streams the bundle once per hop, with little memory; this full-bundle command wasn't run for this page:

uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 select --full clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz "${P[@]}" \
    --driver scv --where "[c.contributor FOR c IN contributions IF c.activityType = 'submitted'][1] = 'clinvar.submitter:500068'" \
    --follow out \
    --out mayo.json.gz

P is the schema array from Gene-panel subset; look up the submitter id with SELECT id, name FROM 'submitter.parquet' WHERE name ILIKE '%mayo%'. --follow out from the SCVs adds their propositions, variants, alleles, locations, conditions and the submitter. The same command on a weekly delta returns only the week's changed SCVs, and needs --max-depth 4 (On a delta, set --max-depth); Your First Dataset walks one.

Why this is hard with ClinVar's XML. A submitter's assertions are spread across the variant records they are about, so collecting one submitter's work means reading every variant record in the release. Here it is one filter on the scv table, and the joins bring the variant, the condition and ClinVar's call alongside.

items.title: Flat analysis table, one row per SCV
items.text:
The question. One wide table, one row per submission: the variant, the proposition, the condition, the submitter, the classification, the date and the cited PubMed ids, for pandas, R or a statistics package.

For analysts who want ClinVar as a single data frame.

Reads scv (785 MB), the four proposition tables (405 MB), variation (1.7 GB), submitter, condition and conditionSet.

COPY (
  WITH prop AS (                    -- all four proposition tables, one glob
    SELECT id, type, subject, object, object_section
    FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
  ),
  set_names AS (                    -- a condition set's member names, in one string
    SELECT cs.id, string_agg(c.name, '; ' ORDER BY c.name) AS member_names
    FROM 'conditionSet.parquet' cs, unnest(cs.concepts) AS t(m)
    JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = m.id
    GROUP BY cs.id
  )
  SELECT replace(s.id, 'clinvar.submission:', '')                      AS scv,
         p.subject                                                     AS variation_id,
         v.name                                                        AS variation_name,
         p.type                                                        AS proposition_type,
         p.object                                                      AS condition_id,
         coalesce(c.name, sn.member_names)                             AS condition_name,
         sub.name                                                      AS submitter,
         s.classification.name                                         AS classification,
         s.classification.primaryCoding.code                           AS classification_code,
         s.quality.name                                                AS level,
         [x.date FOR x IN s.contributions IF x.activityType = 'evaluated'][1] AS last_evaluated,
         [r.pmid FOR r IN s.reportedIn IF r.pmid IS NOT NULL]          AS pmids
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN prop p ON p.id = s.proposition
  LEFT JOIN 'variation.parquet' v  ON v.id = p.subject
  LEFT JOIN 'submitter.parquet' sub
         ON sub.id = [x.contributor FOR x IN s.contributions IF x.activityType = 'submitted'][1]
  LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON c.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'condition'    THEN p.object END
  LEFT JOIN set_names sn          ON sn.id = CASE WHEN p.object_section = 'conditionSet' THEN p.object END
) TO 'scv-flat.parquet' (FORMAT parquet);

10 seconds and 4.8 GB of memory on the test laptop; 6,895,428 rows, every SCV in the release, in a 254 MB file. Every row has a variant name, a condition name and a submitter. Three rows for one variant, selected columns:

scv             variation_id   condition_name                                    submitter                                                   classification_code  last_evaluated
SCV008145163.1  clinvar:17662  BRCA1-related cancer predisposition               Hema, HEMA – Genetic and Molecular Diagnostic Laboratory    pathogenic           2026-09-14
SCV000806982.5  clinvar:17662  BRCA1-related disorder                            PreventionGenetics, part of Exact Sciences                  pathogenic           2026-09-13
SCV006560819.2  clinvar:17662  Inherited ovarian cancer (without breast cancer)  Genetics Laboratory, Great Ormond Street Hospital NHS …      pathogenic           2026-09-11

pmids is a list column; pandas reads it as arrays, and unnest(pmids) in DuckDB gives one row per citation. For a spreadsheet, drop the list or join it to text (array_to_string(pmids, ';')) and write CSV (Export a slice). The file is a derived table: Data Use and Citation says how to attribute it if you share it.

Why this is hard with ClinVar's XML. Each submission in the XML nests its submitter, its trait set, its citations and its classification in separate elements under the variant record, and a flat table needs a parser for each. Here they are typed columns of related tables, and one query joins them.

items.title: Export a slice to CSV or Parquet
items.text:
Spreadsheets and many tools can't read Parquet, and you rarely want a whole table anyway. Wrap any query in COPY to write its result to a file:

-- Expert-panel and practice-guideline submissions, with their variant
COPY (
  WITH prop AS (
    SELECT id, subject FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
  )
  SELECT replace(s.id, 'clinvar.submission:', '') AS scv,
         p.subject AS variant_id,
         s.classification.name AS classification,
         s.quality.name        AS level
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN prop p ON p.id = s.proposition
  WHERE s.quality.name IN ('expert panel', 'practice guidelines')
) TO 'expert_scvs.csv' (HEADER);

In 2026-11-15 that writes 25,962 rows plus a header. For another analytics tool, write Parquet instead, which keeps the column types and is far smaller: TO 'expert_scvs.parquet' (FORMAT parquet).

To share a slice as records rather than rows, so others can read it with the same tools as the full release, cut a mini-bundle instead.

items.title: Anatomy of a Table
items.text:
Release

Outputs and counts on this page are from the 2026-10-31 release, built with gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0. They change with every release; re-run a query to get today's numbers.

One bundle section, one table

The JSON bundle is organized into 20 named sections (variation, scv, condition, …). The Parquet release turns each section into exactly one table, stored as one file (variation.parquet, scv.parquet, condition.parquet, …), with one row per record in that section. This track calls them tables.

All 20 tables are generated from the bundle's schema by the same rules, so what you learn reading one applies to the rest. This page covers what they have in common: how to read a table's schema, the id column, the column types and how to reach inside nested ones, extensions, getting a whole record back, and which columns to leave alone. The column reference then documents each table individually in that shared shape. Everything here stays inside one table at a time; no joins.

Every query here except the last two runs in the live console. Paste it in and replace '<table>.parquet' with '{BASE}/<table>.parquet'. The last two scan all of scv.parquet, so they belong on your machine.

Prerequisites

The DuckDB CLI, tested with 1.5.4, run from the directory that holds the tables a query names: condition.parquet (2 MB), scv.parquet (784 MB), vcv.parquet (145 MB) and allele.parquet (701 MB), from Downloads → Parquet Files. Each query stands alone. The console needs nothing; see Start Here.

items.title: Read the schema first
items.text:
DESCRIBE lists a table's columns and types. It reads only the file's footer, so it is instant even on the largest table, locally or over the network.

DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM 'condition.parquet';

column_name    column_type
id             VARCHAR
type           VARCHAR
name           VARCHAR
aliases        VARCHAR[]
conceptType    VARCHAR
primaryCoding  STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, "system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[])
mappings       STRUCT(coding STRUCT("system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[]), relation VARCHAR)[]

Column names are the bundle's own field names, camelCase included. The types you will meet:

Type What it holds How to read it VARCHAR, BIGINT, BOOLEAN A plain value Use the column directly VARCHAR[] A list of values aliases[1] (1-based), len(aliases), unnest(aliases) for one row per element STRUCT(...) A record with named fields primaryCoding.code STRUCT(...)[] A list of records unnest(mappings), then dot into each one STRUCT(id, section)[] A list of references m.id is the referenced row's id, m.section its table

Run the same DESCRIBE on scv.parquet and most of its columns are STRUCTs: classification, strength, quality, specifiedBy, contributions, extensions. The full list for every table, with a description of each column, is in the column reference.

items.title: Every table has an id
items.text:
Every row has an id, and its shape tells you which table it belongs to (clinvar.trait:2645 is a condition, clinvar:51592 a variant; see Ids tell you where to look). Ids are how tables connect, and they are how you look up one row. Rows are stored sorted by id, so a lookup by id reads only a small part of the file.

A column that refers to another row holds that row's bare id. When it could refer to more than one table, a _section column next to it says which: object and object_section on a proposition, proposition and proposition_section on a statement.

items.title: Reading a STRUCT column
items.text:
The most common first mistake is to treat a STRUCT column as text. In scv.parquet, classification is a whole record (a GA4GH MappableConcept), not a string:

SELECT count(*) FROM 'scv.parquet' WHERE classification = 'Pathogenic';

Conversion Error: Type VARCHAR with value 'Pathogenic' can't be cast to the destination type
STRUCT("type" VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR, "extensions" STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, value_string VARCHAR)[], conceptType VARCHAR, primaryCoding STRUCT("system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR))

Name the field you want with a dot:

SELECT id,
       classification.name                AS classification,   -- what the submitter wrote
       classification.primaryCoding.code  AS code,             -- the normalized value
       quality.name                       AS submission_level
FROM 'scv.parquet'
LIMIT 5;

The same goes for strength, quality, and condition.primaryCoding:

SELECT id, name, primaryCoding.code AS medgen_cui, list_sort(aliases)[1] AS first_alias, len(aliases) AS n_aliases
FROM 'condition.parquet'
WHERE name = 'Marfan syndrome';

id                  name             medgen_cui  first_alias                   n_aliases
clinvar.trait:2645  Marfan syndrome  C0024796    FBN1-Related Marfan Syndrome          5

The order of a list such as aliases isn't guaranteed from one release to the next, so the query sorts it (list_sort) before taking the first element.

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Many records carry an extensions list: named ClinVar attributes that the GA4GH models have no field for. Each element has a name and a value, and the value can be text on one extension and a list of records on another. So an extension's value is spread over one column per kind of value, named value_<kind>, and in each element exactly one of them is set:

Slot Holds Examples value_string text clinvarReviewStatus on vcv and rcv; clinvarScvReviewStatus, submissionLevel on scv; clinvarVariationType on variation; geneContextSource on the gene context value_string_array a list of text submittedGeneSymbols on the gene context value_boolean true or false on a citation's extensions value_object one record submittedCondition, submittedConditionSet on scv and evidenceLine value_object_array a list of records clinvarHgvsList, clinvarGeneList on variation; additionalClinvarMethodCitations on scv.specifiedBy

A table's extensions has only the slots its extensions use. Pick an extension by name with a list comprehension, then read the slot:

SELECT id,
       [e.value_string FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'clinvarReviewStatus'][1] AS review_status
FROM 'vcv.parquet'
WHERE id LIKE 'VCV000051592.%'
  AND NOT regexp_matches(id, '-(PG|EP|CP|NOCP|NOCL|FLAG)(-T[0-9])?$');

id                       review_status
VCV000051592.122-G-NP    no classification provided
VCV000051592.122-G-PATH  reviewed by expert panel

When two extensions share a value_object_array slot, the slot's record has the fields of both, and the fields the other one uses are NULL: clinvarGeneList entries fill gene, relationship_type and source; clinvarHgvsList entries fill nucleotideExpression, proteinExpression, molecularConsequence and the MANE flags.

A few deeply nested positions are kept as JSON text instead, because the schema allows anything there. The one you are likely to meet is a submitted condition set's members, value_object.concepts, a list of JSON strings. Read them with DuckDB's JSON functions:

SELECT s.id,
       json_extract_string(c, '$.medgen_id')        AS medgen_id,
       json_extract_string(c, '$.normalized_match') AS condition_id
FROM (SELECT id, extensions FROM 'scv.parquet'
      WHERE id = 'clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1') s,   -- filter first, then unnest
     unnest([e.value_object.concepts FOR e IN s.extensions IF e.name = 'submittedConditionSet'][1]) AS t(c);

id                                 medgen_id  condition_id
clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1  C3280096   clinvar.trait:9587
clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1  C2673520   clinvar.trait:5535
clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1  C3469186   clinvar.trait:9582
clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1  C0162532   clinvar.trait:3370
clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1  C0268323   clinvar.trait:9601
clinvar.submission:SCV000893709.1  NULL       clinvar.trait:222

The id filter sits in a subquery so DuckDB applies it before the unnest, reading one row group of scv.parquet. With WHERE s.id = … after the unnest instead, it unnests every row first: the same answer, but a scan of all of scv.parquet (about 30 seconds locally, over a minute from the URL).

items.title: The whole record
items.text:
There is no column holding the row's JSON. The typed columns are the record: every field of every bundle record is in a column. To get a row back as JSON, use to_json:

SELECT to_json(a) AS record
FROM 'allele.parquet' a
WHERE id = 'ga4gh:VA.Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9';

record
{"id":"ga4gh:VA.Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9","type":"Allele","name":"NC_000013.11:g.32338445A>C","digest":"Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9","expressions":[{"syntax":"spdi","value":"NC_000013.11:32338444:A:C"},{"syntax":"hgvs.g","value":"NC_000013.11:g.32338445A>C"},{"syntax":"gnomad","value":"13-32338445-A-C"}],"location":"ga4gh:SL.Gga5J2ccypatzYD5tBIeQEU9K4sPXc6J","state":{"type":"LiteralSequenceExpression","length":null,"sequence":"C","repeatSubunitLength":null}}

Two things differ from the bundle record. References are bare ids where the bundle has a pointer ("location": "ga4gh:SL.…" for "#/location/ga4gh:SL.…"), and a field the record doesn't have is written as null ("length": null). For the records exactly as published, rebuild the bundle from the tables with gkm-bundle-parquet rebuild, or download the JSON bundle.

items.title: Never SELECT * on a big table
items.text:
Parquet stores each column separately and compressed. A query reads only the columns it names, so naming fewer columns means reading less. SELECT * names them all.

Here is scv.parquet built from the 2026-10-31 weekly delta (33,417 submissions), by column:

Column On disk In memory (uncompressed) description 2.74 MB 15.17 MB extensions 0.99 MB 6.82 MB id 0.18 MB 1.24 MB proposition 0.17 MB 0.70 MB everything else 0.35 MB 0.90 MB whole table 4.44 MB 24.82 MB

The table is more than five times larger once decompressed, and most of that is the free-text description and the extensions. The full release's scv.parquet is 784 MB on disk; SELECT * FROM 'scv.parquet', or loading it whole into pandas, asks for all of it, decompressed. In the browser console the tab runs out of memory.

The fix is always the same: name the columns you need. The sizes of every table are in the column reference.

items.title: A worked example: what do submitters say?
items.text:
Count every SCV by its classification. The query reads only the classification fields instead of the whole file, so it finishes in a fraction of a second on downloaded files. Over the network it needs a request per row group, which trips the console's rate limit, so run this one locally.

SELECT classification.name AS classification, count(*) AS n
FROM 'scv.parquet'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY n DESC;

It returns 44 distinct values in 2026-10-31, and some of them are the same call written differently:

classification            n
Uncertain significance    3,369,435
Likely benign             1,920,932
Benign                      649,701
Pathogenic                  535,920
Likely pathogenic           293,502
Uncertain Significance       32,732
…
pathogenic                    2,792
…
PATHOGENIC                       22

classification.name is the text the submitter sent, so case varies. Group by the normalized primaryCoding.code instead, and keep its system (the guideline the classification follows), because the same code can come from different guidelines:

SELECT classification.primaryCoding.code   AS code,
       classification.primaryCoding.system AS guideline,
       count(*) AS n
FROM 'scv.parquet'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY n DESC;

code                    guideline                                           n
uncertain significance  ACMG Guidelines, 2015                               3,401,911
likely benign           ACMG Guidelines, 2015                               1,941,309
benign                  ACMG Guidelines, 2015                                 653,132
pathogenic              ACMG Guidelines, 2015                                 538,734
likely pathogenic       ACMG Guidelines, 2015                                 302,236
not provided            ClinVar                                                29,122
…
likely oncogenic        ClinGen/CGC/VICC Guidelines for Oncogenicity, 2022      1,321
tier 1                  AMP/ASCO/CAP (AAC) Guidelines, 2017                     1,018
…

That collapses the 44 spellings into 34 code–guideline pairs. The normalization goes beyond case: the one SCV that says no known pathogenicity is counted under benign.

Next: the 20 tables and how they fit together, then joining them.

items.title: The 20 Tables
items.text:
Release

Row counts and sizes on this page are from a gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 build of the 2026-10-31 release with the 1.2.0 schema (decimal units: 1 MB is 1,000,000 bytes). They change with every release; the queries give you today's numbers. The 1.1 tables (22 tables, published at v1/1.1/parquet/ until the 1.1 line was frozen) are described only in Moving from the 1.1 Tables.

The Parquet release is 20 tables, one per bundle section. They fall into six areas that you can learn one at a time. Variants and conditions are the nouns. Propositions say what is claimed about them. Statements say who claimed it, and how confidently.

The map renders at full size in a scrollable frame. Each area has a runnable query you can expand, and each table box links to that table's column reference below.

Prerequisites

The queries on this page and in the map run in the DuckDB CLI, tested with 1.5.4, from a directory holding the tables they name, downloaded from Downloads → Parquet Files. The two queries below read the four proposition*.parquet tables (about 405 MB together). Sizes of every table are in the column reference.

items.title: The six areas
items.text:
Area Tables The question it answers 1 · Variant variation, allele, copyNumberCount, copyNumberChange, location, sequenceReference, gene Which variant is this, and where is it on the genome? 2 · Condition & therapy condition, conditionSet, therapy, therapyGroup Which disease, tumor type or drug is the claim about? 3 · Proposition propositionPathogenicity, propositionClinvarCustom, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionOncogenicity What exactly is being claimed about the variant? 4 · SCV scv, submitter, and the SCV rows of evidenceLine What did each submitter say, how, and on what evidence? 5 · RCV rcv, and the RCV rows of evidenceLine What is ClinVar's combined call for this variant and this condition? 6 · VCV vcv, and the VCV rows of evidenceLine What is ClinVar's combined call for this variant across all its conditions?

Most questions start in area 1 or 2, go through area 3, and end in one statement area. The Joining Tables page covers each of those hops. For download links and the release layout, see Downloads → Parquet Files.

items.title: How the tables follow from the bundle
items.text:
The tables are generated from the bundle's JSON Schema by gkm-bundle-parquet, with no hand-chosen column list (the schema's default column set). The same rules hold in every table:

  • One row per bundle record, and every field has a column. A column is named after its JSON field, in the bundle's camelCase (conceptType, primaryCoding, hasEvidenceLines). An object becomes a STRUCT, a list becomes a list. There is no data column: to_json() turns a row back into its JSON, and gkm-bundle-parquet rebuild turns the tables back into the bundle, record for record.
  • References hold bare ids. Where the bundle has a pointer such as #/condition/clinvar.trait:9580, the column holds clinvar.trait:9580. When a reference can point to more than one table, a <column>_section column beside it names the table (object_section, proposition_section), and a list of such references is a list of STRUCT(id, section) (members, concepts, hasEvidenceItems).
  • A field that can hold different kinds of value has one column per kind, named value_<kind>: value_string, value_object, value_object_array, value_string_array. In each element exactly one of them is set. See Extensions.
  • Rows are sorted by id. A lookup by id reads only the row groups whose id range covers it.
  • Every file says what it is. Its key-value metadata names the tool version, the table spec, the bundle schema version and the source bundle's sha256; see Which set do you have?.

A few deeply nested positions, mostly extensions inside extensions, are kept as compact JSON text in a VARCHAR; gkm-bundle-parquet generate lists them. The one you are likely to meet is the member list of a submitted condition set on scv (see Extensions); read it with json_extract_string.

items.title: Ids tell you where to look
items.text:
Every row has an id, and the id's shape names its table. A _section column names the table for you wherever a reference can go to more than one; the shapes are still the quickest way to read a result.

Id shape Example Table clinvar:<n> clinvar:51592 variation ga4gh:VA.<digest> ga4gh:VA.Apas_jvqBJU7l4DGHGlvTGRY3BBh-UR9 allele ga4gh:CN.<digest> ga4gh:CN.wGhFBul2d7nEcVf-2n9HOBuhskBqdK-C copyNumberCount ga4gh:CX.<digest> ga4gh:CX.X1aEdg3zvDBvYfZfupzYACFNXKTi1Yh2 copyNumberChange ga4gh:SL.<digest> ga4gh:SL.Gga5J2ccypatzYD5tBIeQEU9K4sPXc6J location SQ.<digest> SQ._0wi-qoDrvram155UmcSC-zA5ZK4fpLT sequenceReference ncbigene:<n> ncbigene:675 gene clinvar.trait:<n> clinvar.trait:9580 condition clinvar.traitset:<n> clinvar.traitset:10013 conditionSet (accessioned) clinvar.conditionset:vcv-<md5> clinvar.conditionset:vcv-50aae75c5e3a7740ab0c2f3ff9ebd970 conditionSet (minted) clinvar.therapy:<sha256> clinvar.therapy:b150cd67… therapy clinvar.therapygroup:<sha256> clinvar.therapygroup:3595163a… therapyGroup clinvar.submitter:<n> clinvar.submitter:500034 submitter clinvar.submission:SCV<n>.<ver> clinvar.submission:SCV000056982.2 scv, and evidenceLine for a somatic clinical-impact SCV's own evidence line SCV<n>-<CODE> SCV000056982-ASSOC a proposition table (a submission's proposition) VCV<n>-<G\|S>-<CODE>[-<LEVEL>] VCV000051592-G-PATH-CP a proposition table (an aggregate's proposition) VCV<n>.<ver>-<G\|S>-<CODE>[-<LEVEL>] VCV000051592.122-G-PATH-CP vcv RCV<n>.<ver>-<G\|S>-<CODE>[-<LEVEL>] RCV003486676.1-G-PATH-CP rcv <statement id>.contributing / .non-contributing VCV000051592.122-G-PATH-NOCP.contributing evidenceLine (a VCV or RCV statement's line)

Two details are easy to miss:

  • A proposition id is its statement's id without the version. VCV000051592-G-PATH-CP is the proposition, and VCV000051592.122-G-PATH-CP is the statement about it.
  • A proposition id's classification code names its table. PATH is in propositionPathogenicity, ONCO in propositionOncogenicity, SCI, DIAG, PROG and TR in propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, and every other code in propositionClinvarCustom (see the code table under Reading a variant's statements). A statement's proposition_section names the table directly. To read all four at once, use read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true): the four tables have different columns.

items.title: Where a traversal ends
items.text:
Five tables are leaves: they reference no other table, so a chain of joins stops there.

  • sequenceReference: the bottom of the variant chain (variation → allele → location → sequenceReference).
  • gene: reached from a variant's gene list.
  • condition: reached from a proposition, directly or through a conditionSet.
  • therapy: reached from a therapeutic-response proposition, directly or through a therapyGroup.
  • submitter: reached from an SCV's contributions.

scv is a leaf of the statement graph: RCV and VCV statements cite SCVs, but an SCV cites no other statement.

items.title: Reading a variant's statements
items.text:
A single variant usually has several VCV statements: one per classification type and aggregate level, in a germline lane and sometimes a somatic lane. The statement id encodes all three, as the diagram below shows. It also shows how somatic clinical-impact statements add an evidence-line layer, and which levels contribute to the aggregate call.

The same facts as text. A statement id reads <accession>.<version>-<lane>-<code>[-<level>], for example VCV000012871.94-G-PATH-CP.

Lane and classification code. The lane is G (germline) or S (somatic). The code is shorthand for the proposition type, and says which proposition table holds the proposition:
