Lane Code Proposition type Proposition table Root statements G PATH VariantPathogenicityProposition propositionPathogenicity 4,451,497 G NP ClinvarNotProvidedProposition propositionClinvarCustom 27,921 G DR ClinvarDrugResponseProposition propositionClinvarCustom 2,760 G OTH ClinvarOtherProposition propositionClinvarCustom 2,171 G RF ClinvarRiskFactorProposition propositionClinvarCustom 1,072 G ASSOC ClinvarAssociationProposition propositionClinvarCustom 525 G AFF ClinvarAffectsProposition propositionClinvarCustom 332 G CDFS ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition propositionClinvarCustom 192 G PROTECT ClinvarProtectiveProposition propositionClinvarCustom 99 G CS ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition propositionClinvarCustom 20 S ONCO VariantOncogenicityProposition propositionOncogenicity 2,425 S SCI VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition propositionSomaticClinicalImpact 1,317

Root statement counts are VCV roots. An SCV's proposition id uses the same codes without a lane (SCV000056982-ASSOC). A somatic clinical-impact (SCI) SCV also has an evidence line, in evidenceLine under the SCV's own id, whose targetProposition names the specific impact: -TR (therapeutic response), -DIAG or -PROG, all in propositionSomaticClinicalImpact with the SCI propositions. Its tier is in evidenceOutcome: Level A/B is Tier I, Level C/D is Tier II.

Aggregate level. The level suffix matches the quality.name of the submissions it groups:

Level quality.name Precedence PG practice guidelines 5 EP expert panel 4 CP criteria provided 3 NOCP no assertion criteria provided 2 NOCL no classification 1 FLAG flagged set apart

A root statement takes its call from the highest level present, and the levels below it are marked non-contributing. Which level contributes therefore depends on the variant: a variant whose best submissions are NOCP contributes NOCP. Two exceptions: PG and EP both contribute when both are present (the practice guideline doesn't mask the expert panel), and flagged submissions never contribute.

items.title: Reading a table remotely
items.text:
Every table can be queried straight from https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/<table>.parquet, without downloading it. How well that works depends on what you ask:

  • Cheap on any table: DESCRIBE, count(*), and LIMIT reads. These touch only the file's footer or its first chunk, so they return in about a second even on the 1.66 GB variation.parquet.
  • Fine on small tables: full scans of anything up to tens of megabytes (condition, conditionSet, gene, submitter, therapy, the three smaller proposition tables).
  • Download first for big tables: a full scan or GROUP BY over variation, scv, allele, location, propositionPathogenicity, evidenceLine, vcv or rcv reads every row group, one request each, in a burst. Remotely that takes tens of seconds, and a heavier query can hit the CDN's rate limit (HTTP 429). Download the table once and query it locally. See Working at Scale.

The sizes in the reference below tell you which category a table is in.

items.title: Column reference
items.text:
Every column of every table, from DESCRIBE, with the 2026-10-31 row counts and file sizes. Types are shown compactly: STRUCT(a, b) lists only the top-level fields, and [] marks a list. Expand Full nested types under a table for the complete DuckDB type, or run DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM '<table>.parquet' yourself.

Read a STRUCT field with a dot (classification.name) and a list with unnest(…) or an index (members[1]). Anatomy of a Table walks through both.

items.title: variation
items.text:
ClinVar's variants, one row per ClinVar Variation id, as Cat-VRS CategoricalVariant records. The subject of every proposition. Each row points at the concrete VRS variant(s) that define it.

variation.parquet · 4,708,791 rows · 1.66 GB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar:<variation id>, e.g. clinvar:51592. type VARCHAR Always CategoricalVariant. name VARCHAR ClinVar's preferred name, e.g. NM_000059.4(BRCA2):c.4090A>C (p.Ile1364Leu). extensions STRUCT(name, id, extensions, description, value_string, value_object_array)[] Named ClinVar attributes. Text attributes are in value_string: clinvarVariationType, clinvarSubclassType, definingVrsVariationType, categoricalVariationType, clinvarCytogeneticLocation, and the VRS processing notes vrsProcessingException and vrsPreProcessingIssue. Two lists are in value_object_array, which has the fields of both: clinvarHgvsList (nucleotideExpression, nucleotideType, maneSelect, manePlus, proteinExpression, molecularConsequence) and clinvarGeneList (gene, a bare ncbigene:… id → gene.id, relationship_type, source). A nucleotideExpression.extensions entry, JSON text, keeps ClinVar's submitted text when it wasn't valid HGVS. members STRUCT(id, section)[] The concrete VRS variants that are members of this category: section is allele, copyNumberCount or copyNumberChange, and id is that table's id. constraints STRUCT(type, …, copyChange, copies, copies_min, copies_max, allele, allele_section, allele_json, relations, location, location_section, location_json, matchCharacteristic, …)[] Cat-VRS constraints that define the category: DefiningAlleleConstraint (allele → allele.id, with allele_section = allele), DefiningLocationConstraint (location → location.id, and matchCharacteristic), CopyCountConstraint (copies, with copies_min / copies_max), CopyChangeConstraint (copyChange). relations lists allowed relations such as liftover_to, transcribed_to. The struct has every Cat-VRS constraint field; ClinVar-GKM leaves the others (adjoinedElements, functionalDomains, linker, …) NULL, and allele_json / location_json would hold an inline object instead of a reference. mappings STRUCT(coding, relation)[] Identifiers for this variant in other systems: {coding{system, code, iris}, relation}. Always the ClinVar id (exactMatch); often dbSNP and ClinGen Allele Registry; sometimes dbVar, OMIM, UniProt, GTR and locus-specific databases. Full nested types — variation

items.title: allele
items.text:
VRS Allele records: a specific sequence change at a location. Reached from variation.members[] and constraints[].allele (ga4gh:VA. prefix).

allele.parquet · 4,615,593 rows · 700.8 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR ga4gh:VA.<digest>, the GA4GH computed identifier. type VARCHAR Always Allele. name VARCHAR An HGVS expression for the allele, e.g. NC_000013.11:g.32338445A>C. digest VARCHAR The digest part of the id (the id without ga4gh:VA.). expressions STRUCT(syntax, value)[] The allele written other ways: spdi (NC_000013.11:32338444:A:C), hgvs.g, and gnomad (13-32338445-A-C) where it applies. location VARCHAR ga4gh:SL.… → location.id. state STRUCT(type, length, sequence, repeatSubunitLength) The allele's sequence: for a LiteralSequenceExpression, state.sequence is the alternate bases; a ReferenceLengthExpression has length and repeatSubunitLength.

items.title: copyNumberCount
items.text:
VRS CopyNumberCount records: an absolute copy count over a region (ga4gh:CN. prefix).

copyNumberCount.parquet · 47,469 rows · 4.9 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR ga4gh:CN.<digest>. type VARCHAR Always CopyNumberCount. digest VARCHAR The digest part of the id. location VARCHAR ga4gh:SL.… → location.id. copies BIGINT The absolute copy number.

items.title: copyNumberChange
items.text:
VRS CopyNumberChange records: a relative copy gain or loss over a region (ga4gh:CX. prefix).

copyNumberChange.parquet · 31,745 rows · 3.3 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR ga4gh:CX.<digest>. type VARCHAR Always CopyNumberChange. digest VARCHAR The digest part of the id. location VARCHAR ga4gh:SL.… → location.id. copyChange VARCHAR gain or loss.

items.title: location
items.text:
VRS SequenceLocation records: a span on a reference sequence, shared by alleles and copy-number variants.

location.parquet · 4,226,867 rows · 427.3 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR ga4gh:SL.<digest>. type VARCHAR Always SequenceLocation. digest VARCHAR The digest part of the id. sequenceReference VARCHAR SQ.… → sequenceReference.id. start BIGINT Start coordinate (0-based, interbase). NULL when the start is an uncertain range; use start_min / start_max. start_min BIGINT Lower bound of the start. Equals start for a definite start; for a range, the range's first value, or NULL when the range is open below. start_max BIGINT Upper bound of the start. Equals start for a definite start; for a range, its second value. end BIGINT End coordinate (interbase). NULL when the end is an uncertain range; use end_min / end_max. Quote it: "end" is a reserved word. end_min BIGINT Lower bound of the end. Equals end for a definite end; for a range, its first value. end_max BIGINT Upper bound of the end. Equals end for a definite end; for a range, its second value, or NULL when the range is open above.

In the bundle, an uncertain coordinate is a two-element list ("start": [null, 18445861]), so the bundle field becomes three columns. start_max and end_min bound the span the variant certainly covers, and are set on every row, so window queries can use them without skipping uncertain-range locations (71,989 locations in 2026-10-31, all of them copy-number variant locations). start_min and end_max bound the widest span it may cover.

end is a reserved word

DuckDB and BigQuery both reject an unquoted end (SELECT end FROM … is a syntax error). Write "end" (`end` in BigQuery), or alias it: SELECT start, "end" AS stop FROM 'location.parquet'.

items.title: sequenceReference
items.text:
The reference sequences locations are placed on: RefSeq chromosomes, transcripts and other sequences, keyed by their GA4GH refget id. A leaf: it references nothing.

sequenceReference.parquet · 216 rows · 19.7 KB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR SQ.<digest>, the refget accession (no ga4gh: prefix). type VARCHAR Always SequenceReference. name VARCHAR The RefSeq accession, e.g. NC_000013.11, NM_000059.4. extensions STRUCT(name, value_string)[] On chromosomes, assembly (e.g. GRCh38). refgetAccession VARCHAR Same value as id. residueAlphabet VARCHAR na (nucleic acid). moleculeType VARCHAR genomic, mRNA, or RNA.

items.title: gene
items.text:
Genes referenced by variants' gene lists, keyed by NCBI Gene id. A leaf.

gene.parquet · 92,989 rows · 3.4 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR ncbigene:<n>, e.g. ncbigene:675 (BRCA2). type VARCHAR Always MappableConcept. name VARCHAR The gene symbol, e.g. BRCA2. conceptType VARCHAR Always gene. primaryCoding STRUCT(name, system, code, iris) The NCBI Gene coding; primaryCoding.code is the bare number (675). mappings STRUCT(coding, relation)[] Cross-references, e.g. the HGNC id.

items.title: condition
items.text:
ClinVar's conditions (traits): diseases, phenotypes, findings, one row per ClinVar trait. The object of most propositions. A leaf.

condition.parquet · 23,426 rows · 2.0 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar.trait:<n>, e.g. clinvar.trait:9580. type VARCHAR Always MappableConcept. name VARCHAR Preferred name, e.g. Hereditary spastic paraplegia 48. aliases VARCHAR[] Alternate names. conceptType VARCHAR Disease, Phenotype, Trait, or Condition. primaryCoding STRUCT(name, system, code, iris) The MedGen coding; primaryCoding.code is the MedGen CUI (e.g. C3150901). mappings STRUCT(coding, relation)[] Cross-references {coding{system, code, iris}, relation}: MONDO, Orphanet, OMIM, HPO, and others. Full nested types — condition 
primaryCoding  STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, "system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[])
mappings  STRUCT(coding STRUCT("system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[]), relation VARCHAR)[]

items.title: conditionSet
items.text:
Sets of conditions a single proposition is about. Two kinds of row share the table: accessioned ClinVar TraitSets (clinvar.traitset:, 5,409 rows) and sets minted for VCV-level aggregates (clinvar.conditionset:vcv-…, 95,455 rows).

conditionSet.parquet · 100,864 rows · 5.0 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar.traitset:<n> (accessioned) or clinvar.conditionset:vcv-<md5> (minted). type VARCHAR Always ConceptSet. conceptSetType VARCHAR For TraitSets, ClinVar's set type: Disease, Finding, TraitChoice, DrugResponse. NULL on minted sets. concepts STRUCT(id, section)[] The members: section is condition for a clinvar.trait: id, or conditionSet for a nested clinvar.traitset: (on minted sets). Join concepts[].id to condition.id (see Joining → Seam B). membershipOperator VARCHAR AND (all members together) or OR (any member). Minted sets are OR.

items.title: therapy
items.text:
Drug therapies named by therapeutic-response propositions. A leaf.

therapy.parquet · 38 rows · 5.1 KB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar.therapy:<sha256> (content-addressed). type VARCHAR Always MappableConcept. name VARCHAR The therapy name. conceptType VARCHAR Always Drug.

items.title: therapyGroup
items.text:
Combination therapies: a set of therapy members.

therapyGroup.parquet · 10 rows · 5.6 KB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar.therapygroup:<sha256>. type VARCHAR Always ConceptSet. concepts VARCHAR[] Member ids, clinvar.therapy:… → therapy.id. membershipOperator VARCHAR Always AND: the members are given together.

items.title: 3 · Proposition
items.text:
Propositions are grouped by meaning, in four tables. A proposition's table depends only on its type.

Table Proposition types (id codes) Rows Size propositionPathogenicity VariantPathogenicityProposition (PATH) 27,981,342 400.6 MB propositionClinvarCustom the 9 Clinvar* types and ClinvarUndefinedProposition (NP, DR, OTH, RF, ASSOC, AFF, CDFS, PROTECT, CS, UNDEF) 186,189 2.4 MB propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition (SCI), VariantDiagnosticProposition (DIAG), VariantPrognosticProposition (PROG), VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition (TR) 12,607 146.8 KB propositionOncogenicity VariantOncogenicityProposition (ONCO) 12,233 153.6 KB

items.title: The columns
items.text:
Every proposition table has the first seven columns below (id to geneContextQualifier), then the qualifiers its proposition types allow:

Column Type Description id VARCHAR SCV<n>-<CODE> for a submission's proposition; VCV<n>-<G|S>-<CODE>[-<LEVEL>] or RCV… for an aggregate's, e.g. VCV000051592-G-PATH-CP. Matches the proposition of at most one statement. type VARCHAR The proposition class, e.g. VariantPathogenicityProposition, ClinvarRiskFactorProposition. subject VARCHAR clinvar:<n> → variation.id. predicate VARCHAR The relation, e.g. isCausalFor, isRiskFactorFor, hasClinicalSignificanceFor, predictsSensitivityTo. object VARCHAR The object's id. Dispatch on object_section. object_section VARCHAR The table object is in: condition, conditionSet, therapy or therapyGroup. Only therapeutic-response propositions have a therapy object. geneContextQualifier STRUCT(type, name, extensions, conceptType, primaryCoding, mappings) The gene a submission's proposition is framed around; all four tables. See Gene context. modeOfInheritanceQualifier STRUCT(type, name, extensions, conceptType, primaryCoding) propositionPathogenicity and propositionClinvarCustom. .name is e.g. Autosomal dominant inheritance; .primaryCoding.code is the HPO id (HP:0000006) when there is one. Germline SCV propositions only. penetranceQualifier STRUCT(type, name, extensions, conceptType) propositionPathogenicity and propositionClinvarCustom. .name is e.g. low. Germline SCV propositions only. conditionQualifier VARCHAR propositionSomaticClinicalImpact only: the tumor or condition context of a therapeutic-response proposition, → condition.id (13 rows). conditionQualifier_section VARCHAR The table conditionQualifier is in (condition).

So the four tables don't share one schema. To read them as one table, use union_by_name: a column a table lacks is NULL in its rows.

SELECT id, type, object, object_section,
       geneContextQualifier.name AS gene,
       modeOfInheritanceQualifier.name AS moi
FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet', union_by_name = true)
WHERE subject = 'clinvar:51592';

Without union_by_name = true, DuckDB takes the column list from the first file, propositionClinvarCustom: naming conditionQualifier is a binder error, and reading modeOfInheritanceQualifier fails with a schema mismatch when the scan reaches the second file, propositionOncogenicity, which lacks it. A query that reads only the seven columns every table has (id to object_section, and geneContextQualifier) works either way.

Full nested types — the qualifiers 
geneContextQualifier  STRUCT("type" VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR, "extensions" STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, id VARCHAR, "extensions" VARCHAR[], description VARCHAR, value_string VARCHAR, value_string_array VARCHAR[])[], conceptType VARCHAR, primaryCoding STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, "system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[]), mappings STRUCT(coding STRUCT("system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[]), relation VARCHAR)[])
penetranceQualifier  STRUCT("type" VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR, "extensions" STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, value_string VARCHAR)[], conceptType VARCHAR)
modeOfInheritanceQualifier  STRUCT("type" VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR, "extensions" STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, value_string VARCHAR)[], conceptType VARCHAR, primaryCoding STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, "system" VARCHAR, code VARCHAR, iris STRUCT(id VARCHAR, section VARCHAR)[]))

items.title: propositionPathogenicity
items.text:
Germline pathogenicity claims (VariantPathogenicityProposition, predicate isCausalFor) at every level. By far the largest proposition table. object_section is condition or conditionSet (2,964,682 rows, mostly VCV propositions over several conditions). 6,799,416 SCV rows carry a gene-context qualifier.

propositionPathogenicity.parquet · 27,981,342 rows · 400.6 MB · columns: the seven common ones, penetranceQualifier, modeOfInheritanceQualifier

items.title: propositionClinvarCustom
items.text:
ClinVar's non-pathogenicity germline classifications, which have no standard VA-Spec proposition: not provided, drug response, risk factor, association, affects, protective, confers sensitivity, other, conflicting data from submitters, plus ClinvarUndefinedProposition, the fallback for a classification that maps to no defined type (no rows so far). object_section is condition or conditionSet.

propositionClinvarCustom.parquet · 186,189 rows · 2.4 MB · columns: the seven common ones, modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier

items.title: propositionSomaticClinicalImpact
items.text:
Somatic clinical impact: the clinical significance (SCI) that SCV, VCV and RCV statements classify, and the diagnostic (DIAG), prognostic (PROG) and therapeutic-response (TR) propositions that SCI evidence lines target. No statement classifies a DIAG, PROG or TR proposition directly; they are reached through evidenceLine.targetProposition. The 13 TR rows have a therapy or therapyGroup object and a conditionQualifier; every other row's object is a condition or conditionSet.

propositionSomaticClinicalImpact.parquet · 12,607 rows · 146.8 KB · columns: the seven common ones, conditionQualifier, conditionQualifier_section

items.title: propositionOncogenicity
items.text:
Somatic oncogenicity claims (VariantOncogenicityProposition, predicate isOncogenicFor). The object is the tumor type: almost always a condition, but 32 rows name a minted conditionSet.

propositionOncogenicity.parquet · 12,233 rows · 153.6 KB · columns: the seven common ones

items.title: Gene context
items.text:
geneContextQualifier is filled in only on SCV propositions; every VCV and RCV proposition has NULL. In 2026-10-31, 6,843,043 SCV propositions carry it, 6,799,416 of them in propositionPathogenicity.

Field What it holds geneContextQualifier.name The gene's symbol, e.g. KRAS. For the placeholder, the submitter's symbol (see below). geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code The gene's NCBI Gene number, e.g. 3845. 'ncbigene:' || …code joins gene.id. NULL for the placeholder. extension submittedGeneSymbols (value_string_array) The gene symbols the submitter gave, verbatim and in submitted order (e.g. [MYCN, MYCNOS]). Absent when there are none. extension geneContextSource (value_string) Where the gene came from; see the table below. 
SELECT p.id,
       p.geneContextQualifier.name                                          AS gene,
       'ncbigene:' || p.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code             AS gene_id,
       [e.value_string FOR e IN p.geneContextQualifier.extensions
        IF e.name = 'geneContextSource'][1]                                 AS source,
       [e.value_string_array FOR e IN p.geneContextQualifier.extensions
        IF e.name = 'submittedGeneSymbols'][1]                              AS submitted
FROM 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p
WHERE p.subject = 'clinvar:12582' AND p.geneContextQualifier IS NOT NULL;
  • One representative gene per variant. The qualifier comes from the variant, not from the submission. Upstream, clinvar-ingest-bq-tools picks one gene for each variant with its single-gene method: a point-in-time priority procedure that starts from MANE transcripts and gene symbols in the variant's name, then ClinVar's gene associations. A few genes it picks come only from a variant's name and are not ones ClinVar associates; those are not in gene.parquet, so the id won't join for them. Every SCV of the variant gets that same gene. The submitter did not assert it, and the Parquet doesn't say which step chose it.
  • The code is the gene's own NCBI Gene coding, never looked up from a symbol.
  • submittedGeneSymbols is what the submitter named. It can list several genes, and may leave out the representative gene.

  • geneContextSource is filled in on every SCV proposition that has the qualifier:

    Value Meaning 2026-10-31 submittedSymbolMatches The submitter's symbols include the qualifier's symbol, possibly with other genes. 5,917,880 submittedSymbolDiffers The submitter gave symbols, but none equals the qualifier's symbol. Most are a previous symbol of the same gene (GBA for GBA1); the genes are not necessarily different. 28,648 inferredFromVariant The submitter gave no symbols. 891,903 submittedNotNormalized The placeholder: the variant has no single representative gene. 4,612

    Symbols are compared after trimming spaces and ignoring case (C19ORF12 matches C19orf12). - The placeholder. When the variant has no single representative gene but the submitter named genes, geneContextQualifier.name is the submitter's symbol and primaryCoding is NULL. The name is not a normalized gene. Several symbols are joined with , in submitted order (5 SCVs, e.g. DLK1, MEG3). There are 4,612 of these SCVs in 2026-10-31: 4,575 in propositionPathogenicity and 37 in propositionClinvarCustom.

    Because a placeholder's name is a submitted symbol, a filter such as geneContextQualifier.name = 'TP53' also matches placeholders: 29 TP53 rows in 2026-10-31 (77 for BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53 and MLH1 together). To get only normalized genes, require geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code IS NOT NULL.

This is not the variant's gene list. The gene list (clinvarGeneList in variation.extensions) relates a variant to every gene ClinVar associates with it: many genes per variant, including genes a large copy-number variant merely overlaps. Use the gene list to find a gene's variants, as in the gene rollup recipe; use the gene context for the one gene a submission's proposition is framed around.

items.title: scv
items.text:
SCV statements: each submitter's classification of a variant, one row per ClinVar submission (SCV accession). The leaves every aggregate cites.

scv.parquet · 6,881,795 rows · 784.1 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar.submission:SCV<n>.<ver>, e.g. clinvar.submission:SCV000056982.2. type VARCHAR Always Statement. description VARCHAR The submitter's free-text comment on the classification, or NULL. extensions STRUCT(name, id, extensions, description, value_string, value_object)[] Named ClinVar attributes. In value_string: clinvarScvId, clinvarScvVersion, clinvarScvReviewStatus, submissionLevel, submittedScvLocalKey, submittedScvClassification. In value_object: the submitter's original condition, submittedCondition (one condition: name, type, medgen_id, xrefs, mapping, normalized_match, condition → condition.id, …) or submittedConditionSet (conditionSet → conditionSet.id, multiple_condition_explanation, and concepts, a list of each member's object as JSON text). See Extensions. specifiedBy STRUCT(type, name, extensions, methodType, reportedIn) The method: methodType (ClinVar collection method: clinical testing, curation, research, …), name (the assertion criteria, e.g. ACMG guidelines), reportedIn (the criteria document) and extensions. When ClinVar lists more than one citation for the method, the others are in the extension additionalClinvarMethodCitations (value_object_array). contributions STRUCT(type, contributor, activityType, date)[] contributor is a clinvar.submitter: id → submitter.id; activityType is submitted, created, or evaluated; date is ISO text (2014-04-01), so cast it with CAST(date AS DATE). reportedIn STRUCT(type, name, extensions, documentType, urls, doi, pmid)[] Citations supporting the submission, one Document per ClinVar citation: pmid, doi, urls, name (ClinVar's label, e.g. ACMG, 2015) and documentType (e.g. general, practice guideline). extensions keep ClinVar's citation text (clinvarCitationText) and any repaired or unusable id; see citation Documents. A text-only citation carries only clinvarCitationText. proposition VARCHAR The id of the proposition this statement classifies. One statement per proposition. proposition_section VARCHAR The proposition table that holds it: propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact or propositionClinvarCustom. Read that one file (Joining → Seam C). direction VARCHAR supports, disputes, or neutral: the direction of the classification relative to the proposition (e.g. a Benign call disputes a pathogenicity proposition). strength STRUCT(type, name, conceptType, primaryCoding) strength.name is Definitive, Likely, Strong, Potential, or NULL; primaryCoding names the guideline (system) and code. quality STRUCT(type, name, conceptType) quality.name is the submission level: practice guidelines, expert panel, criteria provided, no assertion criteria provided, no classification, or flagged. classification STRUCT(type, name, extensions, conceptType, primaryCoding) classification.name is the submitted call (e.g. Pathogenic, Likely benign), not case-normalized; primaryCoding is {system, code} (e.g. ACMG Guidelines, 2015, pathogenic). classification.extensions may carry the submitter's description. hasEvidenceLines VARCHAR[] Ids of this statement's evidence lines in evidenceLine; set only on somatic clinical-impact SCVs, where it is the SCV's own id. NULL otherwise. Full nested types — scv

items.title: evidenceLine
items.text:
Every evidence line in the release, in one table: the lines of SCV, VCV and RCV statements. Two kinds of row:

  • SCV lines (1,568 rows): only somatic clinical impact (SCI) submissions have them. The id is the SCV's own id (clinvar.submission:SCV…), and the line points at the specific impact (therapeutic response, diagnostic, prognostic) with its AMP/ASCO/CAP tier.
  • VCV and RCV lines (9,410,235 and 12,208,356 rows): which statements each aggregate statement cites, and whether they contribute. The id is <statement id>.contributing or <statement id>.non-contributing.

evidenceLine.parquet · 21,620,159 rows · 264.6 MB

Column Type Description id VARCHAR clinvar.submission:SCV<n>.<ver> (an SCV line, same id as the scv row), or VCV…/RCV… + .contributing / .non-contributing, e.g. VCV000051592.122-G-PATH-NOCP.contributing. Filter with id LIKE 'VCV%' to read one kind. type VARCHAR Always EvidenceLine. extensions STRUCT(name, id, extensions, description, value_object)[] SCV lines: the submitter's original condition (submittedCondition), same shape as on scv. targetProposition VARCHAR SCV lines: the specific-impact proposition (…-DIAG, …-PROG or …-TR) → propositionSomaticClinicalImpact.id. directionOfEvidenceProvided VARCHAR supports / disputes / neutral, relative to the citing statement's proposition. evidenceOutcome STRUCT(type, name, conceptType) SCV lines: .name is Level A/B (Tier I) or Level C/D (Tier II). hasEvidenceItems STRUCT(id, section)[] VCV and RCV lines: the cited statements. On a root statement's line these are its level statements (section = vcv or rcv, ids …-CP, …-NOCL); on a level statement's line they are SCVs (section = scv). strengthOfEvidenceProvided STRUCT(type, name, conceptType) VCV and RCV lines: .name is Contributing or Non-contributing, whether the cited items count toward the aggregate classification. The organizations that submit to ClinVar. A leaf, referenced from scv.contributions[].contributor.

RCV aggregate statements: ClinVar's rollup of SCVs for one variant and one condition. Each RCV accession yields a root statement plus one statement per contributing level. Their evidence lines are the RCV… rows of evidenceLine.
