items.title: Pipeline Overview
items.text:
What this page answers

How ClinVar's XML release becomes a ClinVar-GKM bundle: the steps, what each one builds, and where each is documented. Read it to understand where the data comes from; to trace one field back to ClinVar, see Where a Value Comes From. Maintainers running a release start at For Maintainers: Running a Release.

The ClinVar-GKM pipeline transforms ClinVar XML release data into the GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) schema set (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec) through a series of BigQuery stored procedures with an external VRS Python processing step.

In outline: ClinVar's XML is first loaded into relational BigQuery tables by the upstream clinvar-ingest pipeline. From those tables the pipeline picks one expression per variant and computes its VRS identifier with vrs-python, builds each ClinVar variation as a Cat-VRS categorical variant, maps the submitted conditions to ClinVar traits, turns each submission into an SCV statement with its proposition, and aggregates the SCVs into VCV and RCV statements. The last steps record what changed since the previous release, then export, assemble, validate and publish the bundles and Parquet. Where a Value Comes From traces each bundle field through these steps.

The two most expensive stages — Variation Identity and VRS Processing — run incrementally: they recompute only the variations that changed since the prior release and carry the rest forward, driven by the release-to-release diff (dataset_diff_on). Both run in the clinvar-ingest pipeline (v2.7.0 and later), which calls this repository's dataset_diff_on, variation_identity and variation_vrs_changed procedures; this project's release starts after them, at the check of the VRS translation (see Single-command run).

items.title: Pipeline Steps
items.text:
The pipeline executes in the following order. Each step is a BigQuery stored procedure unless otherwise noted.

┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Variation Identity        │  variation_identity[_incremental]
│    Extract & normalize       │  → variation_identity table
│    variant data              │  (run by clinvar-ingest)
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 2. VRS Processing            │  Export + vrs-python run by
│    Export → cloud vrsify →   │  clinvar-ingest; the release
│    Import back to BigQuery   │  starts here → gkm_vrs table
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 3. Cat-VRS Generation        │  gkm_catvar_proc
│    Canonical alleles &       │  → gkm_catvar table
│    categorical variants      │
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 4. Conditions & Traits       │  gkm_scv_condition_proc
│    Map traits, build         │  → condition mapping &
│    conditions & condition    │    condition set tables
│    sets                      │
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 5. SCV Statements            │  gkm_scv_statement_proc
│    Build SCV records,        │  → gkm_dict_scv table
│    propositions & statements │
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 6. VCV Statements            │  gkm_vcv_proc +
│    Aggregate SCVs into       │  gkm_vcv_statement_proc
│    variant-level statements  │  → gkm_dict_vcv table
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 7. RCV Statements            │  gkm_rcv_proc +
│    Aggregate SCVs into       │  gkm_rcv_statement_proc
│    condition-level statements│  → gkm_dict_rcv table
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 8. Change log + deltas       │  gkm_change_log +
│    A/U/D per dict + delta    │  gkm_delta_build
│    payloads for publishing   │  → gkm_change_log, delta_<dict>
└──────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
│ 9. Export & Distribute       │  release-gkm.sh (fulls),
│    Export NDJSON to GCS,     │  release-gkm-delta.sh,
│    assemble JSON bundles,    │  release-gkm-parquet.sh
│    upload to R2; build the   │  (gkm-bundle-parquet)
│    Parquet from the bundle   │  → R2 public bucket
└──────────────────────────────┘

items.title: Documentation Tracks
items.text:
The pipeline documentation serves two audiences:

  • Pipeline (this section) — documents how data flows through BigQuery stored procedures, including internal table schemas, transformation logic, and step-by-step workflows. Each step is tagged as Pipeline table, JSON artifact, or Internal to indicate its role
  • Output Reference — documents the JSON output files from a consumer perspective, covering record structure, field meanings, and usage guidance

items.title: Detailed Documentation
items.text:
Each pipeline step has its own documentation page:

  • Where a Value Comes From — each bundle field traced to its ClinVar source, procedure and step
  • Variation Identity — variant extraction, normalization, VRS class assignment
  • VRS Processing — external VRS Python step
  • Cat-VRS — categorical variant generation
  • Conditions & Traits — condition mapping, traits, condition sets
  • SCV Statements — SCV records, propositions, final statements
  • VCV Statements — aggregate variant-level VCV statements
  • RCV Statements — aggregate condition-level RCV statements
  • Export & Distribute — export to GCS, assemble bundle, upload to R2

items.title: For Maintainers: Running a Release
items.text: This section is for maintainers who run releases; readers of the data can skip it. The downstream gkm_* procedures also have incremental wrappers, but from 1.1.0 the weekly run builds them in full (run-release.sh <date> --full-procs). The incremental wrappers proved no cheaper (about 0.22 TiB billed per dataset, against about 0.20 TiB for a full build) and fell back to a full build without saying so; ADR 0007 workstream 3 decides their future.

items.title: Single-command run
items.text:
Prerequisites

The commands on this page are maintainer commands, run from the root of a clone of this repository. They need the setup in Export & Distribute: Prerequisites: the Google Cloud SDK signed in to clingen-dev, write access to its BigQuery datasets and to gs://clinvar-gkm, the right to execute its Cloud Run jobs, the r2 AWS profile, the Cloudflare purge credentials, venv/3.12 with orjson, and uv.

The clinvar-ingest pipeline (v2.7.0 and later) runs everything up to the VRS translation for every release: it ingests the XML, runs dataset_diff_on and variation_identity_incremental, exports the changed variations to vi.jsonl.gz, and translates them with its clinvar-ingest-vrsify Cloud Run job. This project's release starts after that. The run-release.sh orchestrator chains four steps: a check that the upstream translation is complete and belongs to the current export (check-cloud-vrsify.sh), the transform/load/procedures step (vrs-to-bq-table.sh), the export/publish step (release-gkm.sh, release-gkm-delta.sh), and the Parquet step (release-gkm-parquet.sh), which builds the latest Parquet set from the published weekly full with gkm-bundle-parquet (PyPI, pinned to 2.0.0):

./src/scripts/run-release.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> --full-procs # all four steps, the gkm procs full (the weekly mode after 1.1.0)
./src/scripts/run-release.sh <yyyy-mm-dd>              # the same, with the incremental gkm procs
./src/scripts/run-release.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> --dry-run    # steps 1 and 2 as usual; steps 3 and 4 only print their R2 writes
./src/scripts/run-release.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> --skip-parquet   # leave parquet/ as it is (skip step 4)
./src/scripts/run-release.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> --start-step 3   # resume from a step (1-4); 4 runs only the Parquet step

Billed, and written to the live dataset and line

Step 2 runs the Cloud Run transform (it writes vi-final.jsonl.gz to GCS), loads gkm_vrs, and runs the gkm procedures, which bill about 0.2 TiB per full build and replace the gkm_* tables of the release's dataset in clingen-dev (PROJECT_ID). Steps 3 and 4 publish to the public R2 line. --dry-run gates only steps 3 and 4: it still writes the gkm_pipeline_version stamp, runs the transform and the procedures, and bills them.

Step 1 only checks that the upstream output, vi-vrs-python.jsonl.gz, is the translation of the release's current vi.jsonl.gz, and stops the release at once otherwise (it does not wait); run the release again once it is (see Checking the cloud output). --start-step 2 runs the same check first, so every gkm_vrs load is checked. No step needs local SeqRepo, UTA or gene-normalizer services.

--full-procs builds the step-2 gkm procedures full (catvar, SCV, RCV, VCV); the gkm_vrs load still follows the data. Weekly runs after 1.1.0 use --full-procs until ADR 0007 workstream 3 decides on the incremental procedures, which were seen to fall back to full builds without saying so. --dry-run runs the build steps but has the release steps only print what they would upload; it is not free and does not leave BigQuery untouched (see the warning above).

The individual stages are documented below.

items.title: Step 1: Variation Identity
items.text:
Run by clinvar-ingest, not by this project's release. clinvar-ingest calls the incremental build for every release; the procedures (dataset_diff_on, variation_identity, variation_vrs_changed) still live in src/procedures/ here (see Incremental Rebuild). By hand, from the BigQuery console, with <release-date> the release to build (YYYY-MM-DD):

-- what clinvar-ingest runs: recompute only changed variations, carry the rest forward
CALL `clinvar_ingest.variation_identity_incremental`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);

-- full rebuild: first release, or after a variation_identity transform change
CALL `clinvar_ingest.variation_identity`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);

Rewrites a live dataset

Each procedure builds the dataset of the newest release on or before its date (clinvar_ingest.schema_on) and replaces its tables there; with CURRENT_DATE() that is the newest release. The calls are billed. They need BigQuery Job User and Data Editor access in clingen-dev.

items.title: Step 2: VRS Processing
items.text: clinvar-ingest exports the changed variations and translates them with vrs-python (the clinvar-ingest-vrsify Cloud Run job); this project's release checks the translation and loads it back — incremental by default (only changed variations are vrsified; unchanged gkm_vrs results carry forward). See VRS Processing.

items.title: Step 3: Cat-VRS through the Change Log
items.text:
vrs-to-bq-table.sh runs these after loading gkm_vrs. The full builds, in the order it calls them, from the BigQuery console (<release-date> as above; the same live-dataset warning applies, and a full build bills about 0.2 TiB):

CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_catvar_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_scv_condition_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_scv_statement_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_rcv_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_rcv_statement_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_vcv_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_vcv_statement_proc`(DATE '<release-date>', FALSE);
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_change_log`(DATE '<release-date>');
CALL `clinvar_ingest.gkm_delta_build`(DATE '<release-date>');
-- NOTE: gkm_json_proc is retired (Plan 4) — its JSON-render tables were unpublished;
-- the gkm_dict_* tables are the published product and are built by the procs above.

The statement procedures name each proposition's bundle section with the UDF clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section(type), which must be deployed with them. The script also runs gkm_scv_changed and gkm_rcvvcv_changed, which build the changed-id sets, before the SCV and RCV/VCV procedures; without --full-procs it calls each procedure's _incremental wrapper instead of its full build.

items.title: Step 4: Export & Distribute
items.text:
The gkm_dict_* tables are the published product. Full bundles, deltas and the latest Parquet are published by separate scripts; the Parquet set is built from the published weekly full, not from BigQuery:

# Weekly full bundle (export NDJSON, assemble, validate, upload to weekly/)
./src/scripts/release-gkm.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --weekly

# Weekly delta (added + updated records + change manifest)
./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version>

# Latest Parquet (gkm-bundle-parquet builds it from the published weekly full, verifies it, overwrites parquet/)
./src/scripts/release-gkm-parquet.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version>

<yyyy-mm-dd> is a release in the line's current month (an older weekly full is refused), and <version> is the pipeline version in its dataset name, clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version>. Each command bills BigQuery for its export and publishes to the live R2 line; --no-upload stops before R2, and --dry-run prints the writes. See Export & Distribute: Full Example for the order run-release.sh runs them in.

The full and delta scripts validate every record of their bundle strictly before upload, with jsonschema-rs, and stop if any fails. The GA4GH GKM Toolkit gives the same verdicts but takes hours where jsonschema-rs takes minutes; it cross-checks a sample at each version release (Release Validation). See Export & Distribute, and Step 5 there for the Parquet build and its checks.

release-gkm.sh exports bundle NDJSON (export-gkm-dicts.sh), assembles and validates it, and uploads the bundle; it writes no Parquet. Its steps can be run individually, and --start-step resumes it from a step:

# 1. Export dictionary tables to a GCS prefix of your own, cleared first (bundle NDJSON)
gsutil -m rm -r gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts-<user>/ 2>/dev/null || true
./src/scripts/export-gkm-dicts.sh clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version> clinvar-gkm gkm-dicts-<user>

# 2. Assemble NDJSON into JSON bundle (deletes the shards), then validate it strictly
venv/3.12/bin/python3 ./src/scripts/assemble-gkm-dicts.py gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts-<user>/ <yyyy-mm-dd>
./src/scripts/validate-bundle.sh /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --engine rs

# 3. Upload the validated bundle to R2 as the weekly full (writes to the live line)
./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --weekly

See Export for details on each step.

items.title: Export & Distribute
items.text:
The final pipeline step exports the gkm_dict_* tables from BigQuery, assembles them into a single keyed JSON bundle, and uploads to Cloudflare R2 for public distribution. A last step builds the single latest Parquet set from the published bundle with gkm-bundle-parquet.

The gkm_dict_* tables are the published product — they are built directly by the statement procedures (steps 5–7) and the change-log step (step 8). The retired gkm_json_proc is not part of this path; its inlined JSON-render tables were never published. See Retired: gkm_json_proc.

Distribution follows a full + delta model:

  • A weekly full bundle (JSON) is published for every release via release-gkm.sh --weekly / upload-gkm-to-r2.sh --weekly, into weekly/.
  • The official monthly full bundle (JSON) is published once a month. run-release.sh normally makes it a server-side copy of its source release's weekly full (upload-gkm-to-r2.sh --month-label=YYYY-MM --from-weekly), and re-exports it with release-gkm.sh --month-label=YYYY-MM when that weekly full is gone.
  • A weekly delta — added and updated records plus a change manifest — is published for every release via release-gkm-delta.sh / upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh.
  • The latest Parquet — one table per bundle section — is built from every release's published weekly full by gkm-bundle-parquet via release-gkm-parquet.sh / upload-gkm-parquet-to-r2.sh. It is not kept per release. BigQuery exports no Parquet.
  • Every bundle gets a <file>.sha256 sidecar.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
The commands on this page are maintainer commands. They run from the root of a clone of this repository, use the project's Google Cloud resources, and publish to the public R2 bucket. The Pipeline Overview and VRS Processing pages need the same setup.

Billed, and published to the live line

  • BigQuery bills the export. The EXPORT DATA queries of Step 1 scan about 55–60 GB per full export (bq extract is not billed). The procedures that build the gkm_dict_* tables bill about 0.2 TiB per full build (Pipeline Overview).
  • GCS. Steps 1 and 2 write NDJSON to gs://clinvar-gkm/, and the assembler deletes the prefix it read (unless --keep-source). gkm-dicts/ and gkm-deltas/ are the release scripts' staging prefixes; a hand run uses a prefix of its own.
  • R2. Steps 3–5 write to the live version line (R2_LINE, default v1/1.2/) and regenerate its index.json, which every reader sees. --dry-run prints the writes instead, and --no-upload stops before R2.
  • Repository — a clone with its submodules (git submodule update --init --recursive); validation reads the schemas of the va-spec submodule. Run every command from the repository root.
  • Google Cloud SDK — bq, gsutil and gcloud, signed in with gcloud auth login, with the default project set: gcloud config set project clingen-dev. export-gkm-dicts.sh names its tables without a project, so it runs in gcloud's default project; run-release.sh and check-cloud-vrsify.sh read PROJECT_ID (default clingen-dev). The scripts call only these CLIs, so Application Default Credentials are not needed.
  • Google Cloud access in clingen-dev — to run queries and procedures and write tables (for example the BigQuery Job User and BigQuery Data Editor roles), to write and delete objects in gs://clinvar-gkm (Storage Object Admin), and, for the VRS transform, to execute Cloud Run jobs.
  • AWS CLI with an r2 profile — an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on the clinvar-gkm bucket, stored with aws configure --profile r2 (the token's access key ID and secret, region auto). The scripts add the R2 endpoint themselves. --dry-run lists the bucket too, so it also needs the profile.
  • Cloudflare purge credentials — CF_ZONE_ID and CF_PURGE_TOKEN, in the environment or in ~/.config/clinvar-gkm/cloudflare.env (CF_ENV_FILE sets another path). The uploads, the Parquet --purge and the month rollover use them to clear the CDN copy of new, overwritten, moved or deleted files (the CDN may have cached a 404 for a new path requested before it existed). Without them the purge is skipped with a warning, and the CDN can serve the old copy until it expires.

  • Python 3.12 with orjson — the release scripts use venv/3.12/bin/python3 when it exists, and python3 otherwise. orjson is required (Step 2) and is in the project requirements. make venv/3.12 creates the environment (it needs python3.12 on the PATH); then install the requirements into it:

    make venv/3.12
venv/3.12/bin/pip install -r .requirements.txt

  • uv — validate-bundle.sh builds its validation environment with uv, and uvx runs the pinned gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0 (Step 5). ./src/scripts/validate-bundle.sh --check-setup --engine rs confirms that uv, the environment and the schema tree are ready.

  • curl and shasum — installed on macOS; on Linux, shasum comes with Perl.
  • Environment variables (all optional):
    • R2_LINE — the version line written (default v1/1.2/)
    • STAGE_DIR — where bundles and the Parquet build are staged (default /tmp); a full bundle is about 5 GB, and the Parquet build needs about 25 GB free
    • PROJECT_ID — the GCP project of run-release.sh and check-cloud-vrsify.sh (default clingen-dev)
    • GKS_FULL, INCREMENTAL — vrs-to-bq-table.sh only; see VRS Processing
    • PARQUET_TOOL_CMD, PARQUET_MEMORY_LIMIT — Step 5; see Options and Resources

items.title: Workflow
items.text: The export and distribution process has five steps. release-gkm.sh runs Steps 1–3 for a full bundle, release-gkm-delta.sh runs Step 4, and release-gkm-parquet.sh runs Step 5. run-release.sh calls all three for every release (Steps 1–4 are its step 3, Step 5 its step 4). Each step can also be run on its own.

items.title: Step 1: Export Dictionaries to GCS
items.text:
export-gkm-dicts.sh exports the dictionary and statement tables from BigQuery to Google Cloud Storage as sharded, gzip-compressed NDJSON for bundle assembly (gkm-dicts/). Most tables use bq extract; variation, conditionSet, evidenceLine, scv and the proposition sections use EXPORT DATA queries, which filter rows, keep INT64 values numeric, or collapse the typed extension values to value. BigQuery exports no Parquet: the Parquet set is built from the published bundle (Step 5).

./src/scripts/export-gkm-dicts.sh <dataset> <gcs_bucket> [prefix] [--delta]

release-gkm.sh clears gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts/ and then runs the script on the release's dataset, clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version>. The script itself doesn't clear its prefix, so shards an earlier run left there would be assembled too. By hand, export to a prefix of your own and clear it first (the EXPORT DATA queries are billed, about 55–60 GB scanned):

gsutil -m rm -r gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts-<user>/ 2>/dev/null || true
./src/scripts/export-gkm-dicts.sh clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version> clinvar-gkm gkm-dicts-<user>

--delta reads the delta_gkm_dict_* tables instead (what release-gkm-delta.sh runs).

The three proposition tables are exported as the four proposition sections. clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section(type) names each row's section, and the export first asserts that every proposition maps to one of them, so an unmapped type fails the export instead of dropping rows. The script writes these 22 outputs:

Source table NDJSON output gkm_dict_sequence_reference sequenceReference-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_location location-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_allele allele-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_copy_number_count copyNumberCount-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_copy_number_change copyNumberChange-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_gene gene-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_variation variation-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_condition condition-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_condition_set conditionSet-*.ndjson.gz (sets with 2 or more members) gkm_dict_therapy therapy-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_therapygroup therapyGroup-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_submitter submitter-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_evidence_line evidenceLine-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_proposition, gkm_dict_vcv_proposition, gkm_dict_rcv_proposition propositionPathogenicity-*, propositionOncogenicity-*, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact-*, propositionClinvarCustom-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_vcv_evidence_line vcv_evidenceLine-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_rcv_evidence_line rcv_evidenceLine-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_scv scv-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_vcv vcv-*.ndjson.gz gkm_dict_rcv rcv-*.ndjson.gz

BigQuery shards large tables across multiple files automatically.

items.title: Step 2: Assemble Bundle
items.text:
assemble-gkm-dicts.py reads all NDJSON shard files and assembles them into a single keyed JSON bundle file.

venv/3.12/bin/python3 ./src/scripts/assemble-gkm-dicts.py <source> <date> [--keep-source] [--copy-to-gcs] [--output PATH]

<source> is a local path or gs:// URI containing the NDJSON shards. <date> is the ClinVar release date (YYYY-MM-DD); the output path is /tmp/clinvar-gkm-{date}.json.gz unless --output names another. By default, source files are deleted after assembly; use --keep-source to retain them.

Continuing from the export above, assemble the bundle, then validate it strictly as release-gkm.sh does:

venv/3.12/bin/python3 ./src/scripts/assemble-gkm-dicts.py gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts-<user>/ <yyyy-mm-dd>
./src/scripts/validate-bundle.sh /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --engine rs

The script assembles 20 bundle sections in a fixed order: sequenceReference, location, allele, copyNumberCount, copyNumberChange, gene, variation, condition, conditionSet, therapy, therapyGroup, submitter, propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom, evidenceLine, scv, vcv, rcv. The therapy / therapyGroup sections hold content-addressed (deduplicated) drug therapies referenced by VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition.object via #/therapy/ and #/therapyGroup/. Each section is a keyed object where the key is the record's unique identifier. Propositions from SCV, VCV, and RCV are delivered in four sections grouped by meaning — propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact (clinical significance, diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic response), propositionClinvarCustom (the Clinvar* types) — split by the one canonical function clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section(type), which fails the export on an unmapped type; evidence line shards are merged into a single evidenceLine section.

items.title: Record Text
items.text:
Every record — in a full bundle and in a delta — passes through the same cleanup and serialization in the assembler, so an unchanged record has the same bytes in every release:

  • Cleanup — null and empty fields are dropped, and typed extension values (value_<type>) collapse to value
  • Canonical lists — the arrays whose order carries no meaning and has been seen to change between releases are sorted by each element's compact, key-sorted JSON text; today that is condition aliases (the trait's alternate names). The list is UNORDERED_ARRAYS in gkm_json_cleanup.py, and an array enters it only when every schema marks it ordered: false. All other arrays keep the pipeline's order
  • Text — each record is one line of compact JSON (no insignificant whitespace, raw UTF-8) with its object keys sorted at every depth, independent of the column order of the BigQuery tables
  • Layout — schema_version is the first top-level key, followed by the sections in the fixed order above

orjson writes this text, so the assembler requires it and stops without it. Install it in the environment the release scripts use (see Prerequisites):

venv/3.12/bin/pip install orjson

release-gkm.sh then validates every record of the assembled full bundle with validate-bundle.sh --engine rs and stops before upload if any fails (see Strict validation stops the release).

items.title: Step 3: Upload the Weekly and Monthly Fulls to R2
items.text:
upload-gkm-to-r2.sh uploads a full bundle and its .sha256 sidecar to Cloudflare R2, as one of two kinds:

  • --weekly — the weekly full of <export_date>, written to weekly/clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz; when it is the newest weekly full it is also copied to weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz. A weekly full older than the line's current month is refused.
  • --month-label=YYYY-MM — the official monthly, published once a month, aligned to ClinVar's own monthly VCV releases: when a new ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM.xml.gz appears at ClinVar's XML index, run-release.sh publishes our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut datetime (ADR 0002). <export_date> is that source release, so the month slot is set independently of it (e.g. the 2026-07 full is built from our 2026-06-27 release, the last one before ClinVar's _2026-07 cut). With --from-weekly the monthly is a server-side copy of weekly/clinvar-gkm_<export_date>.json.gz and no local bundle is needed (pass -). When it is the newest monthly it is also copied to clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, and the index records <export_date> as the monthly's source_release.
./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh <export_date> <dataset_version> <bundle_file|-> \
  [--weekly | --month-label=YYYY-MM [--from-weekly]] [--dry-run] [--purge]

# A release's weekly full (+ sha256 sidecar); the release must be in the line's current month
./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --weekly

# The <yyyy-mm> official monthly, as a server-side copy of the weekly full of its ADR 0002 source release
./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh <source-release> <version> - --month-label=<yyyy-mm> --from-weekly

# Preview: lists the bucket and prints the writes, uploading nothing
./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --weekly --dry-run

Writes to the live line

Without --dry-run, these commands write to the public line (R2_LINE) and regenerate its index.json. The guards also apply to --dry-run: a weekly full dated before the line's current month is refused, and --from-weekly stops when the source release's weekly full is no longer in R2 (re-export it with release-gkm.sh <source-release> <version> --month-label=<yyyy-mm> instead). Pass --weekly or --month-label: without either, the script publishes the bundle as the monthly of <export_date>'s own month, which is not the ADR 0002 mapping.

The R2 layout mirrors NCBI's ClinVar XML folder (ADR 0009). Under the line folder v1/1.2/:

  • top level — official monthly fulls for the current year (clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mm.json.gz) plus a stable clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, each with a .sha256 sidecar
  • weekly/ — a weekly full bundle for every release of the current month (clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz) plus a stable clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz
  • archive/{yyyy}/ — monthly fulls from prior years, and their deltas under archive/{yyyy}/deltas/{yyyy-mm}/

Rollovers are done by r2-rollover.sh <release_date>, which run-release.sh runs before the weekly uploads and again after any monthly is published; it is idempotent, so a run with nothing to move does nothing. New month (the first release dated in a new month): the finished month's deltas move into deltas/{yyyy-mm}/ and its weekly fulls are deleted, except the newest, which is kept until the new month's official monthly is published (the monthly's source candidate) and deleted by the run that publishes it. New year: the finished year's monthlies and delta folders move into archive/{yyyy}/. Each move or delete is followed by a CDN purge of the old paths. After upload, generate-r2-index.sh regenerates the line's index.json, which lists the monthlies (with their sha256 and source_release, the release each was built from), the weekly fulls, the deltas wherever they now sit, the archive years and the Parquet dataset.

items.title: Step 4: Publish the Weekly Delta
items.text:
release-gkm-delta.sh publishes the per-release delta for every ClinVar release. It exports the delta_<dict> change tables produced by step 8 of the pipeline, assembles a delta bundle (added + updated records, same section structure as the full), builds the delta manifest, and uploads them to R2. Deltas carry no Parquet.

./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh <export_date> <dataset_version> [--start-step=N] [--dry-run] [--no-upload]

# Build and strictly validate a release's delta, keeping it in STAGE_DIR; nothing is written to R2
./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --no-upload

# Publish it to deltas/ in the live line
./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --start-step=3

The upload is refused unless the delta follows the newest delta already in the line (the chain check below), so a delta is published for each release in order.

The internal steps are: export delta tables to GCS, assemble and strictly validate the delta bundle, then build the manifest (build-delta-manifest.py) and upload (upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh).

Strict validation stops the release

Every delta record is validated with jsonschema-rs by validate-bundle.sh --engine rs before upload, as every full is (see Release Validation). run-release.sh does this at the start of stage 5, so a failing delta stops the release with R2 untouched; the bundle stays in STAGE_DIR for inspection. The check needs uv and the va-spec submodule (git submodule update --init --recursive), and run-release.sh confirms both at startup.

--start-step=3 publishes the staged bundle without validating it again, so only use it on a bundle that passed.

Every full bundle is validated too: release-gkm.sh validates each full it assembles, the weekly full and any re-exported monthly, before upload, and run-release.sh builds the weekly full with the delta, so a failing full also stops the release with R2 untouched. The GKM Toolkit takes hours on a full, so fulls are validated with jsonschema-rs instead (validate-bundle.sh --engine rs): the same bundle schema, the same schema/ registry and the same document for each record, in minutes. jsonschema-rs is not the GKM Toolkit. Its verdicts are tested against the toolkit's: both engines must name the same failing records in a bundle with planted violations (src/scripts/tests/test_validate_bundle_rs.py). It reads only the one-record-per-line layout the assembler writes and stops on any other. Run ./src/scripts/validate-bundle.sh <bundle.json.gz> --engine toolkit on a full by hand when the official validator's verdict is needed, as for a version release; without --engine, the script uses jsonschema-rs.

The uploader writes:

  • deltas/ — the delta bundle (clinvar-gkm-delta_<yyyy-mmdd>.json.gz), its .sha256 sidecar, and its manifest (clinvar-gkm-delta_<yyyy-mmdd>.manifest.json); the current month's deltas sit here, earlier months in deltas/<yyyy-mm>/

build-delta-manifest.py derives each section's added / updated counts and deleted primary-key list from the dataset's gkm_change_log, and records baseline_release, compare_release, pipeline_version, and counts. The uploader then completes the manifest: checkpoint_full ({path, release, month, sha256}, the newest official monthly whose source_release is on or before the delta's baseline_release, with release set to that source_release) so a consumer knows which monthly the delta chain replays onto, plus schema_version, bundle ({name, path, size, sha256}) and sha256. It also checks the chain: a delta whose baseline_release is not the release of the newest delta already in the line is refused (--allow-gap overrides). Monthlies are therefore published before the deltas that follow them. See Weekly Deltas for the manifest shape and the consumer replay model.

items.title: Step 5: Build and Publish the Latest Parquet
items.text:
One Parquet set is published per version line, at v1/1.2/parquet/, and overwritten every release (ADR 0009). It is built from the published weekly full of the newest release by gkm-bundle-parquet, a separate, independently versioned tool for any GKM bundle, installed from PyPI and pinned to 2.0.0. BigQuery exports no Parquet: every table and value is derived from the bundle, so the bundle stays the record and the Parquet set is a convenience that can be regenerated from it. To build the same tables yourself, or cut a mini-bundle from a full bundle, see Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles.

run-release.sh runs this step as its step 4, after its step 3 has uploaded the weekly full; --skip-parquet skips it and leaves the previous set in place. It can also be run on its own for a release that is already published:

./src/scripts/release-gkm-parquet.sh <export_date> <dataset_version> [--start-step=N] [--dry-run] [--no-upload] [--purge]

Without --no-upload or --dry-run, it overwrites parquet/ in the live line.

items.title: What It Builds
items.text: The tables are the tool's default column set, generated from the bundle schema: no column set is kept in this repo. For the bundle schema of the assembler's SCHEMA_VERSION (https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/<SCHEMA_VERSION>/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json), the tool makes one table per bundle section (20 tables) and one column for every property the section's record schema allows, read the way the schema says: #/<section>/<id> pointers become ids and declared foreign keys, nested objects become STRUCTs, and lists become lists of STRUCTs. See the tool's generate page for the rules. A schema change in this repo therefore changes the tables with no Parquet-specific work. The table and column reference is in Parquet Tables.

items.title: How It Runs
items.text:
1. Find the bundle. The input is <line>weekly/clinvar-gkm_<yyyy-mmdd>.json.gz at its public URL, with the sha256 from its published .sha256 sidecar. A release with no weekly full — the release that starts a new version line with run-release.sh --bootstrap-monthly publishes only its checkpoint monthly — is read from the monthly that the line's index.json lists with this release as its source_release (never 00-latest), with the sha256 the index gives. With neither, the step stops.

  2. gkm-bundle-parquet build streams the bundle from that URL, checks its sha256, and writes the tables:

    uvx gkm-bundle-parquet@2.0.0 build --full <bundle URL> --sha256 <sha256> \
  --bundle-schema https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/<SCHEMA_VERSION>/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json \
  --version-property schema_version --out <dir> --work-dir <dir>.work

    The build rebuilds every record from the tables and compares it with its source, and records a records sha256 of the bundle in its manifest.json. 3. gkm-bundle-parquet verify --bundle-recompute reads the bundle again and checks every table's id sets and values against it. 4. gkm-bundle-parquet verify --roundtrip rebuilds the bundle's records from the tables and checks them against the records sha256: the set is record-identical to the bundle (every record by key, JSON-equal; key order, array order and whitespace don't count). See the tool's round trip page. 5. Upload (upload-gkm-parquet-to-r2.sh) overwrites each table and table-spec.json in parquet/, then writes parquet/manifest.json: the tool's manifest (tool version, table spec version, the source bundle and its sha256, the records sha256, the files) plus what only this repo knows (source_release, dataset, build_date, the ClinVar attribution, disclaimer and license). It refuses a manifest another builder wrote, a release or schema version that differs from this release's, and files that differ from the ones the tool wrote. It then deletes any file in parquet/ that is no longer produced, regenerates index.json, and with --purge (which run-release.sh passes) purges the folder from the CDN.

A failure in steps 1–4 stops before anything on R2 changes. After run-release.sh step 3, a failure is non-fatal to the release: parquet/ keeps the previous set, and its manifest and the index keep saying which release it was built from.

items.title: Options and Resources
items.text:
• --no-upload stops after the verify steps and keeps the build in STAGE_DIR (default /tmp) for inspection; --start-step=3 publishes it later. --dry-run prints the commands and uploads nothing.
  • PARQUET_TOOL_CMD replaces the pinned tool command, e.g. to test an unpublished checkout: PARQUET_TOOL_CMD="uvx --from /path/to/gkm-bundle-parquet gkm-bundle-parquet". The pin is bumped deliberately, because the output depends on the tool version.
  • PARQUET_MEMORY_LIMIT sets DuckDB's memory limit (e.g. 32GB); the tool's default is half the machine's memory. A lower limit spills more to the work directory.
  • Disk and memory: leave about 25 GB free in STAGE_DIR for the set and DuckDB's spill files. The full-size check of 2.0.0 on a weekly full took 38 minutes and used about 65 GB of memory on a 128 GB machine.

To check a bundle against its schema with the same tool, see its validate page.

items.title: R2 bucket CORS policy
items.text:
The release browsers on the Downloads pages — the Monthly Full Bundles, Weekly Full Bundles, Weekly Deltas, and Parquet Files child pages, plus the Downloads hub's Latest Release view — each do a cross-origin fetch() of index.json from the docs site. That only works if the public R2 bucket serves a CORS policy allowing GET from other origins — otherwise the browsers block the read and can't populate (they then show a network/CORS message with a curl fallback).

The policy is checked in at src/scripts/r2-cors.json (GET/HEAD from * — appropriate for public, read-only data). It is not applied by the release scripts, because their object-scoped r2 upload token cannot read or write bucket configuration (PutBucketCors → AccessDenied). Apply it once with an Admin Read & Write R2 token (Cloudflare dashboard: R2 → Manage R2 API Tokens), stored as an AWS profile with aws configure --profile r2admin (region auto). The script writes the live bucket's configuration:

./src/scripts/apply-r2-cors.sh            # profile r2admin; another profile: ./src/scripts/apply-r2-cors.sh PROFILE

Or paste r2-cors.json's rules into the Cloudflare dashboard: R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → CORS Policy. It only needs to be re-applied if the bucket is recreated or the policy is cleared.

items.title: Retired: gkm_json_proc
items.text: gkm_json_proc previously rendered the statement and dictionary tables into inlined JSON columns. Those render tables were never published — the export assembles the bundle directly from the gkm_dict_* tables — so the procedure has been retired from the hot path. The null/empty stripping it used to perform is now applied during assembly (assemble-gkm-dicts.py), matching the old remove_empty cleanup. gkm_json_proc is not a live pipeline step and not a downstream consumer of the dictionary tables.

items.title: Full Example
items.text:
The weekly publish of one release by hand, in the order run-release.sh runs it (its steps 3 and 4; see Single-command run). run-release.sh also publishes any monthly that is due, so prefer it for a real release. <yyyy-mm-dd> is a release in the line's current month whose dataset, clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version>, is built, and whose delta follows the newest delta in the line.

Billed, and published to the live line

The --no-upload commands bill BigQuery for their exports. Every later command writes to the public line (R2_LINE) and regenerates its index.json. Add --dry-run to any of them to print the writes instead. See Prerequisites for the access each needs.

# Build and strictly validate the delta and the weekly full; nothing is written to R2
./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --no-upload
./src/scripts/release-gkm.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --weekly --no-upload

# Month or year rollover of the line (does nothing when none is due), then publish the weekly full and the delta
./src/scripts/r2-rollover.sh <yyyy-mm-dd>
./src/scripts/release-gkm.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --weekly --start-step=3
./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --start-step=3

# Rebuild the latest Parquet from the weekly full just published
./src/scripts/release-gkm-parquet.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> --purge

When ClinVar has published a new monthly XML since the line's newest monthly, run-release.sh publishes it after the weekly full, from its ADR 0002 source release (see Step 3), and runs r2-rollover.sh again.

release-gkm.sh runs export, assembly and validation, and upload as steps 1, 2 and 3; --start-step resumes it from one, and step 3 reads the bundle from STAGE_DIR. The same steps by hand (Steps 1–3 above):

# 1. Export the dictionary tables to a GCS prefix of your own, cleared first
gsutil -m rm -r gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts-<user>/ 2>/dev/null || true
./src/scripts/export-gkm-dicts.sh clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version> clinvar-gkm gkm-dicts-<user>

# 2. Assemble the NDJSON into one bundle (this deletes the shards), then validate it strictly
venv/3.12/bin/python3 ./src/scripts/assemble-gkm-dicts.py gs://clinvar-gkm/gkm-dicts-<user>/ <yyyy-mm-dd>
./src/scripts/validate-bundle.sh /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --engine rs

# 3. Upload the validated bundle as the weekly full (writes to the live line)
./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> <version> /tmp/clinvar-gkm-<yyyy-mm-dd>.json.gz --weekly

items.title: Sub-Bundle Extraction
items.text:
Not a maintainer? Use gkm-bundle-parquet select

This page describes a maintainer script that needs the project's BigQuery datasets. To cut a self-contained subset out of a published bundle, use gkm-bundle-parquet select instead: see Cut a mini-bundle.

sub-bundle.py pulls a list of statements — SCV, VCV, and/or RCV — out of a built release dataset into a single, self-contained sub-bundle: a JSON object of named sections in which every #/section/key reference resolves within the file. It is the practical companion to the ID References model — useful for building worked examples, inspecting the complete object graph behind a statement, and producing small fixtures for downstream testing.

The script lives at src/scripts/sub-bundle.py.

Maintainer tool

This is a pipeline-maintainer utility, not a general-audience download. It reads the BigQuery gkm_dict_* tables of a built release directly, so it requires access to the project's BigQuery datasets. Consumers of a published .json.gz bundle already have every section and can resolve references locally — see ID References for the small resolve() helper.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
Given one or more statement identifiers, the script starts from each statement and transitively resolves every reference it carries across the gkm_dict_* tables — proposition → variation → allele → location → sequenceReference / gene, condition / conditionSet, therapy / therapyGroup, submitter, and evidence lines — until the graph is closed. The result is a bundle with the same section structure as a full release, containing only the objects the requested statements need.

  • One combined bundle. All requested statements are assembled into a single JSON object, not one document per statement. References shared across statements (a common variation, condition, or therapy) are emitted once — the output is deduplicated.
  • SCV, VCV, and RCV. Identifiers may be mixed. A VCV or RCV statement pulls in its contributing SCVs (via each evidence line's hasEvidenceItems → #/scv/), so a VCV/RCV sub-bundle is self-contained all the way down to the VRS sequence references.
  • Bundle-faithful objects. Each object is transformed exactly as the release export does — typed extension values (value_string, …) collapsed to a single value, and null/empty fields stripped.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Access to a built release dataset — one that has the gkm_dict_* tables from a completed release (run-release.sh step 2). The script reads BigQuery directly; it does not operate on a published .json.gz bundle.
  • The bq CLI authenticated to the dataset's project (gcloud auth login), with the right to run query jobs there (BigQuery Job User) and read the dataset. See Export & Distribute: Prerequisites for the shared setup.
  • Python 3 (standard library only), run from the root of a clone of this repository: the script reads the bundle schema in schema/clinvar-gkm/.

Billed queries

Every run issues BigQuery queries, which are billed by the bytes they read. Each fetch reads whole rows of its table, so a run reads every table it touches in full, whatever the number of ids: about 25 GB for SCVs (mostly gkm_dict_scv and gkm_dict_variation, about 10 GB each), and up to about 40 GB when VCVs or RCVs are included (sizes of the 2026-08-16 dataset). The bq query in the last example below reads about 1 GB.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset <DATASET> [--project <PROJECT>]
                                   [--ids-file <FILE>] [--stdin] [--submitter <ID>]
                                   [-o <OUT>] [<id> ...]
Option Description --dataset Required. Built release dataset, e.g. clinvar_2026_08_16_v2_5_0. --project GCP project (default clingen-dev). <id> ... SCV/VCV/RCV identifiers as arguments (mixed). --ids-file Read identifiers from a file, one per line. --stdin Also read identifiers from standard input (or pass - as an argument). --submitter Include every SCV contributed by this submitter (clinvar.submitter:{id} or bare {id}). Repeatable, and combinable with explicit ids. -o, --out Write the bundle to a file (default: stdout).

Each identifier may be a full statement key (SCV004101425.2, VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP, RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP) or a bare accession (VCV000012582.63) to include every statement under it. An SCV accession is normalized to its clinvar.submission: key automatically.

--submitter resolves every SCV whose contributions[].contributor cites that submitter. A large submitter can contribute thousands of SCVs; to keep individual bundles manageable, select the SCV keys once and split them across several --ids-file runs (see the last example).

items.title: Examples
items.text:
# A built release dataset of the current line, e.g. the newest release's
DATASET=clinvar_<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<version>

# A few statements, mixed types, to one bundle file
python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset "$DATASET" \
    SCV004101425.2 VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP -o bundle.json

# Identifiers from a file
python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset "$DATASET" \
    --ids-file ids.txt -o bundle.json

# Identifiers piped on stdin
cat ids.txt | python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset "$DATASET" -

# Every SCV from a submitter (e.g. 196472 = IGM Clinical Laboratory, Nationwide Children's Hospital)
python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset "$DATASET" \
    --submitter 196472 -o nch-igm.json

# A large submitter split across two bundles: list the SCV keys, split, bundle each half
bq query --project_id=clingen-dev --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv --quiet --max_rows=100000 \
  "SELECT id FROM \`${DATASET}.gkm_dict_scv\`
   WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(contributions) c
                WHERE c.contributor='#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:196472')
   ORDER BY id" | tail -n +2 > nch_scvs.txt
split -l $(( ($(wc -l < nch_scvs.txt) + 1) / 2 )) nch_scvs.txt nch_half_   # two halves; portable (macOS and Linux)
python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset "$DATASET" --ids-file nch_half_aa -o nch-1.json
python3 src/scripts/sub-bundle.py --dataset "$DATASET" --ids-file nch_half_ab -o nch-2.json

items.title: Output
items.text:
The output is a single bundle object — the same { "<section>": { "<key>": <object> } } shape as a full release, ordered sequenceReference → … → scv/vcv/rcv. Every #/… pointer inside resolves to a key present in the file.

The file starts with schema_version, read from the bundle schema's schema_version const, so a sub-bundle is a complete bundle that validates against the ClinVar-GKM bundle schema as-is.

Records are written one per line — each section is keyed on its own line and every object value is emitted as a single compact line. The file stays one valid JSON document, but has roughly one line per record rather than one per field, so a large sub-bundle (thousands of statements) is a few thousand lines instead of hundreds of thousands — much easier to grep, diff, or scroll.

{
  "sequenceReference": { "SQ.dLZ15tNO…": { ... } },
  "location":          { "ga4gh:SL.MVuZ…": { ... } },
  "allele":            { "ga4gh:VA.EE08…": { ... } },
  "gene":              { "ncbigene:672": { ... } },
  "variation":         { "clinvar:17662": { ... } },
  "condition":         { "clinvar.trait:76328": { ... } },
  "submitter":         { "clinvar.submitter:509268": { ... } },
  "propositionPathogenicity": { "SCV004101425-PATH": { ... } },
  "scv":               { "clinvar.submission:SCV004101425.2": { ... } }
}

A progress line on stderr reports how many statements matched and the per-section object counts.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
The script resolves the graph efficiently rather than one object at a time:

  • Batched breadth-first traversal. Each round collects all pending references, groups them by source table, and issues one query per table — so a list of N statements is a handful of queries, not N× the work.
  • Prefix-routed proposition/evidence resolution. A #/proposition…/ (any of the four proposition sections) or #/evidenceLine/ reference is resolved from the SCV-, VCV-, or RCV-specific table based on the key's SCV/VCV/RCV prefix.
  • Global dedup. Every referenced object is fetched at most once across the whole run; the final bundle contains one copy of each.

items.title: Example fragments
items.text: The files in examples/ are made by a different script, src/scripts/extract-example.py. It reads a published full bundle (.json.gz), not BigQuery, and writes bounded fragments: each holds one statement or variation and the records it references, but keeps pointers into scv and variation unresolved. A VCV or RCV fragment holds its nested layer statements, down to the #/scv/ pointers. See Examples for the rule.

items.title: Where a Value Comes From
items.text:
What this page answers

Where a value in a published bundle came from: the ClinVar data it was read from, and the pipeline step that built it. Read it when you need to know whether a field is ClinVar's own value, a lookup, or something the pipeline computed, or to find the procedure page that explains it in full.

Every value in a bundle starts in ClinVar's XML release. The upstream clinvar-ingest pipeline loads the XML into relational BigQuery tables (variation, scv_summary, clinical_assertion, trait, rcv_mapping and others); the procedures in src/procedures/ read those tables and build one gkm_dict_* table per bundle section; the assembler turns those tables into the bundle (Export & Distribute).

items.title: How to Read the Tables
items.text:
Each table below has four columns:

  • Field — the bundle section and property, as on the Output Format pages
  • ClinVar source — the ingested table and column the procedure reads. Where it reads part of a record's content (the rest of the XML element, kept as JSON), the XML element is named, e.g. HGVSlist element. Lookup marks a value taken from a ClinVar-GKM mapping table rather than from the release, and Computed one the pipeline derives.
  • Built in — the pipeline page and step that document it, and the procedure file
  • Notes — what happens to the value on the way

items.title: From Tables to the Bundle
items.text: The assembler (src/scripts/assemble-gkm-dicts.py with gkm_json_cleanup.py) changes the form of values, not their content. It drops null and empty fields, collapses typed extension values (value_<type>) to value, sorts the few arrays whose order carries no meaning, and writes each record as compact JSON with its keys sorted, so an unchanged record has the same bytes in every release (Export & Distribute, Step 2).

items.title: Tracing One Value
items.text:
The proposition of clinvar.submission:SCV008145211.1 (the record in the annotated walk-through) has "object": "#/condition/clinvar.trait:66395". Its path back to ClinVar:

  1. The submitter named the condition with a MONDO code, MONDO:0800400, on the submitted trait (clinical_assertion_trait).
  2. gkm_scv_condition_proc matched that code to ClinVar trait 66395 through ClinVar's trait mapping; the SCV's submittedCondition extension records it as "normalized_resolution": "tm reftype xref mondo" and "condition": "clinvar.trait:66395" (Condition Mapping).
  3. The condition record clinvar.trait:66395 comes from the trait table: its name, RP1-related dominant retinopathy, and its MedGen primaryCoding, CN322606 (Traits).
  4. gkm_scv_statement_proc wrote the proposition's object as a pointer to that record (Step 5: Primary Proposition).

items.title: Overview
items.text:
VRS processing is the step between Variation Identity extraction and Cat-VRS generation. It translates the selected SPDI or HGVS expression for each variation's defining allele into a GA4GH VRS (Variation Representation Specification) object — producing a computable, digest-identified representation of the variant.

The work is split between two repositories:

  • clinvar-ingest (pipeline v2.7.0 and later) exports each release's changed variation_identity rows to gs://clinvar-gkm/YYYY-MM-DD/dev/vi.jsonl.gz, and its Cloud Run job clinvar-ingest-vrsify translates them with vrs-python against a RefgetStore of genomic sequences, with no local services.
  • This project's release (run-release.sh) starts after that: step 1 runs src/scripts/check-cloud-vrsify.sh, which checks that the translation belongs to the current export, and step 2 runs src/scripts/vrs-to-bq-table.sh, which transforms the translation, loads gkm_vrs, and runs the downstream procedures. Export and publish follow: release-gkm.sh (full bundles), release-gkm-delta.sh (deltas) and release-gkm-parquet.sh (the latest Parquet). See Single-command run.

This step is incremental. VRS translation is per-variation (no cross-variation dependency), so diffing variation_identity between releases is a clean driver: the export holds only the variations whose variation_identity changed since the prior release (~0.3% of a weekly release, versus the whole ~4.5M snapshot), and the gkm_vrs load carries the prior release's results forward for the unchanged variations. This is where the largest cost reduction in the whole pipeline lands, because VRS translation is the most expensive stage.

The location transformation step uses a lightweight Cloud Run job defined in this project under src/vrs-location-transformer/.

items.title: Step 1: Export variation_identity (clinvar-ingest)
items.text:
clinvar-ingest's stored procedures job runs, for every release, dataset_diff_on, variation_identity_incremental and variation_vrs_changed, then exports only the changed variations' variation_identity rows to gs://clinvar-gkm/YYYY-MM-DD/dev/vi.jsonl.gz. When no usable baseline exists, every variation counts as changed and the export holds the whole table. The procedures it calls live in this repository's src/procedures/, but this project's release never runs them.

Each record contains the single best expression source for a ClinVar variation — including the source expression string, fmt (spdi, hgvs, or gnomad), vrs_class, and copy number fields when applicable.

src/scripts/export-vi-table-to-gcs.sh is not part of the release. It is kept because clinvar-ingest's error message, when its own export fails, tells the operator to rerun the export with it. Don't run it after the release has been translated: a rewrite with different content no longer matches the translation.

items.title: Step 2: Translate with vrs-python (cloud vrsify)
items.text:
The clinvar-ingest-vrsify Cloud Run job (project clingen-dev, region us-east1) runs every 15 minutes. It takes the next release whose upstream stored procedures have finished, waits for that release's vi.jsonl.gz to be written, and runs the translation on Cloud Batch. It takes each release once, and never replaces an existing output. It writes, beside the input:

  • vi-vrs-python.jsonl.gz — one line per input record
  • vi-vrs-python.provenance.json — the input it read (inputs: URI, generation, MD5 and size), the output, the RefgetStore, the library versions and record counts

For each input record, the translation attempts to resolve the source expression into a VRS object according to its vrs_class. Not every variation can be resolved: records that fail resolution carry an errors field in the output. Transcript and protein expressions are not translated (the translation uses only the RefgetStore, with no UTA), and records of classes it does not translate (Unknown, Not Available, Haplotype) get a null out. The supported VRS classes are:

  • Allele — translates SPDI or HGVS into a VRS Allele with a SequenceLocation and state
  • CopyNumberChange — resolves the location and applies the copyChange designation (gain/loss)
  • CopyNumberCount — resolves the location and attaches the copies value

Each output record pairs the original variation_identity input (in) with the VRS resolution result (out).

Output: vi-vrs-python.jsonl.gz on GCS.

items.title: Checking the cloud output
items.text:
The release starts here. run-release.sh step 1 runs src/scripts/check-cloud-vrsify.sh YYYY-MM-DD; a release started with --start-step 2 runs it too, so every gkm_vrs load is checked. The check reads the objects, runs nothing, and stops the release at once (it does not wait) unless:

  • both vi-vrs-python.jsonl.gz and its provenance exist;
  • the provenance names this release's vi.jsonl.gz as its only input, with the MD5 and size that object has now;
  • the provenance names vi-vrs-python.jsonl.gz as its output, with its current size when the provenance records one.

A new generation of vi.jsonl.gz with the same MD5 passes: a re-export of unchanged variation_identity writes the same bytes. A vi.jsonl.gz with different content fails, and the cloud job does not redo the release by itself; translate the current export again upstream (clinvar-ingest vrsify-submit with --overwrite), then run the release again. If the output is not there yet, run the release again after the cloud job's next run.

items.title: Step 3: Transform VRS locations
items.text:
VRS SequenceLocation objects use array-valued start and end fields to represent imprecise ranges (inner/outer bounds). BigQuery does not natively support loading these mixed scalar/array values, so a minor transformation is needed before the data can be imported.

The vrs-to-vi-location-transformer Cloud Run job — defined in this project at src/vrs-location-transformer/ — streams the VRS output through a jq filter that flattens each location's start and end arrays into separate scalar fields: start, start_inner, start_outer, end, end_inner, end_outer. When start or end is already a scalar (precise variants), the value is left unchanged.

This job is normally invoked by the src/scripts/vrs-to-bq-table.sh orchestrator (Step 4 below), not run by hand; the direct invocation is shown for reference. It executes a billed Cloud Run job in clingen-dev and overwrites vi-final.jsonl.gz, so it needs the right to execute Cloud Run jobs there and to write gs://clinvar-gkm (see Export & Distribute: Prerequisites):

gcloud run jobs execute vrs-to-vi-location-transformer --project clingen-dev \
  --args "gs://clinvar-gkm/<yyyy-mm-dd>/dev/vi-vrs-python.jsonl.gz" \
  --args "gs://clinvar-gkm/<yyyy-mm-dd>/dev/vi-final.jsonl.gz" \
  --wait --region us-east1

Output: vi-final.jsonl.gz on GCS.

items.title: Step 4: Transform, load, run procedures
items.text:
The transform + load + downstream procedures are run by src/scripts/vrs-to-bq-table.sh (a 3-step script): the Cloud Run transform (Step 3 above), the gkm_vrs load, and the gkm_* stored procedures. Export and publish are not done here — they are handled separately by release-gkm.sh (see Export & Distribute); run-release.sh runs this script as its step 2 and then release-gkm.sh.

GKS_FULL=true ./src/scripts/vrs-to-bq-table.sh <yyyy-mm-dd>     # from the start (Cloud Run transform), gkm procs full
GKS_FULL=true ./src/scripts/vrs-to-bq-table.sh <yyyy-mm-dd> 2   # resume from a later step (2=load, 3=procs)

Billed, and written to the live dataset

The script runs in clingen-dev (set in the script, not read from PROJECT_ID) and needs the setup in Export & Distribute: Prerequisites. It executes the Cloud Run transform, replaces the release dataset's gkm_vrs, and runs the gkm procedures, which bill about 0.2 TiB per full build and replace that dataset's gkm_* tables. Run on its own, the script calls the incremental procedure wrappers unless GKS_FULL=true is set; run-release.sh --full-procs sets it. INCREMENTAL=false forces a full --replace load of gkm_vrs.

The gkm_vrs load is incremental: it clones the prior release's gkm_vrs forward and merges in only the changed variations' new results (keyed on in.variation_id), rather than a --replace full load. It self-corrects to a full --replace when no baseline gkm_vrs exists or when the staged rows are not the changed subset — so a translation of the whole table is loaded correctly without any flag change.

Because each release clones the immediately prior one, the clone lineage grows one level per release and reaches BigQuery's cap of 3 chained clones/snapshots roughly every 3 releases. When the seed clone fails with that error, the load automatically falls back to a deep copy (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE … AS SELECT *) of the baseline, which materializes a fresh depth-0 table and resets the chain — self-healing, with no manual intervention. You'll see clone chain full; reseeding via deep copy in the log on those releases; it is expected and does not change the result.

Version-invalidation

The incremental carry-forward assumes the prior release's gkm_vrs was produced by the same VRS translation and the same variation_identity transform. A variation_identity transform change is caught by the diff, once clinvar-ingest runs the changed procedure: every variation whose row changes is exported and translated again.

A change to the translation (vrs-python, the RefgetStore, or the cloud job's code) is not. Each release's provenance file records its libraries and refget_store, but the release does not compare them between releases. Re-translating every variation is an upstream run; this project's release has no full mode for it. When such a translation is in place, step 2's load self-corrects to a full --replace, and step 1's check still requires the translation's provenance to name vi.jsonl.gz as its only input.

items.title: Output Table (gkm_vrs)
items.text:
The gkm_vrs table contains one row per variation that was submitted for VRS processing. Each row is a two-part record:

Field Type Description in record The original variation_identity record — all fields from the input including variation_id, source, fmt, vrs_class, copy number fields, and metadata out record The VRS resolution result — contains id (VRS digest identifier), type (Allele, CopyNumberChange, CopyNumberCount), location, state, copyChange, copies, and errors when resolution failed

The out.location record includes the flattened position fields: start, end, start_inner, start_outer, end_inner, end_outer. For precise variants only start and end are populated; imprecise ranges use the inner/outer fields.

items.title: Current Scope and Future Direction
items.text:
Limited Scope

VRS processing currently resolves only the single best expression per variation — the defining allele for each Canonical Allele as selected by the precedence hierarchy. Only variations that vrs-python can handle are successfully resolved; the remainder carry errors in the output.

The release runs from a single command — src/scripts/run-release.sh starts at the check of the cloud translation (see Checking the cloud output) and chains the transform/load/procedures and publish steps; variation identity, the export and the translation run in clinvar-ingest. See Single-command run. No step needs local SeqRepo, UTA or gene-normalizer services.

One area of improvement remains planned:

  • Broader expression coverage — expand VRS processing to resolve all variant expressions in ClinVar — the full hgvs_list preserved in the variation_hgvs table — rather than only the single selected source. This will provide richer downstream representation with multiple VRS identities per variation.

  • Cloud Run job: vrs-to-vi-location-transformer (src/vrs-location-transformer/) — location field flattening
  • BigQuery schema: schemas/vrs_output_2_0_1.schema.json
