geneContextSource : Extension on every SCV gene context qualifier, from 1.1.0, saying where its gene came from: submittedSymbolMatches, submittedSymbolDiffers, inferredFromVariant or submittedNotNormalized. See the gene context FAQ.

Mode of Inheritance Qualifier : Proposition qualifier specifying inheritance pattern (e.g., autosomal dominant, X-linked). Maps to HPO terms.

Penetrance Qualifier : Proposition qualifier indicating penetrance level for pathogenic or risk allele classifications. Values: low, risk.

items.title: VCV Aggregation
items.text:
Aggregation : Process of combining multiple SCV submissions into higher-order VCV statements following submission-level-specific logic.

Winner-Takes-All : Aggregation strategy at the Aggregate Contribution Layer where the highest-ranked submission level's classification becomes the aggregate result. Lower-ranked levels become non-contributing.

Contributing Submission : Submission whose review status is highest-ranked within an aggregation group. Directly reflected in the aggregate classification.

Non-Contributing Submission : Submission ranked lower than the contributing submission. Preserved in the evidence structure but not reflected in the aggregate label.

Grouping Layer : First conceptual aggregation layer. Consists of Classification Grouping and Priority Grouping steps. Produces initial aggregation of SCVs into groups by submission level.

Classification Grouping (Grouping Layer) : First step of the Grouping Layer. Groups SCVs by variation + statement group + proposition type + submission level [+ tier]. Applies submission-level-specific classification and conflict detection logic.

Priority Grouping (Grouping Layer) : Second step of the Grouping Layer (somatic sci only). Aggregates tier-level groups within each submission level.

Aggregate Contribution Layer : Second and final aggregation layer. Applies winner-takes-all ranking across submission levels. Terminal layer for both germline and somatic statements.

Aggregate Review Status : Final review status of a VCV statement derived from submission level and aggregation outcome. See Aggregate Review Status.

items.title: Classification Attributes (VCV/RCV)
items.text:
classification : VCV/RCV statement-level classification attribute. Contains a single aggregate label with optional conflictingExplanation extension. The classification lives only on the statement, not on the proposition.

object : VCV/RCV proposition attribute. Contains the unique condition(s) associated with the aggregate statement. For VCV, this is a single MappableConcept or an OR ConceptSet of distinct conditions from contributing SCVs. For RCV, this is the condition sourced from gkm_scv_condition_sets — either a Condition MappableConcept or a ConditionSet ConceptSet. Extensions excluded.

items.title: Identifier Formats
items.text:
clinvar:{variation_id} : ClinVar variation identifier. References a CategoricalVariant record in the variation bundle section. Example: clinvar:12582.

clinvar.submission:SCV{id}.{version} : SCV submission identifier with version. References an SCV Statement record in the scv bundle section. Example: clinvar.submission:SCV001571657.2.

clinvar.submitter:{submitter_id} : Submitter organization identifier. References a submitter record in the submitter bundle section. Example: clinvar.submitter:508027.

clinvar.trait:{trait_id} : Condition/trait identifier. References a condition record in the condition bundle section. Example: clinvar.trait:9580.

clinvar.traitset:{trait_set_id} : Condition set identifier. References a condition set in the conditionSet bundle section. Example: clinvar.traitset:1234.

ga4gh:{type}.{digest} : VRS identity digest. References alleles or locations in the corresponding bundle sections. Example: ga4gh:VA.xXBYkzzu1AH0oyMKlbBtP2.

items.title: Output Format
items.text:
Bundle : A JSON file containing all data for a ClinVar release, organized as named sections at the root level. Each section is a keyed collection of objects of the same class, where the key is the object's unique identifier. Objects reference each other using #/ JSON pointer strings. Typed Parquet files derived from the bundle are published for the latest release only.

Bundle Section : A named top-level key in the bundle file (e.g., variation, scv, propositionPathogenicity) containing a keyed collection of objects.

JSON Pointer Reference : A #/{section}/{key} string used to reference an object in another bundle section. Example: #/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123 resolves to the allele with that key in the allele section.

items.title: Releases and Distribution
items.text:
Official monthly full : The full bundle clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz, published once a month for ClinVar's ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM, built from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut. See How Releases Work.

Weekly full : The full bundle of one weekly release, weekly/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, published for every release and kept for the current month only.

Delta : The records added or updated since the prior release, clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, with a manifest listing per-section adds, updates and deletes. See Weekly Deltas.

00-latest : The stable filenames that always hold the newest file of a kind: clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (newest official monthly) and weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (newest weekly full).

source_release : In a line's index.json, the ClinVar weekly release a monthly full, or the Parquet set, was built from.

Version line : The folder v{major}/{major}.{minor}/ (e.g. v1/1.2/) that holds every release of one schema MINOR version, with its own index.json and feed. A line is current or frozen. See Versioning & Releases.

items.title: Technical Terms
items.text:
Null Stripping : Technique where null-valued fields and empty arrays are omitted from JSON output via JSON_STRIP_NULLS(remove_empty => TRUE).

By-Reference Format : JSON structure where related objects are referenced by ID rather than embedded inline. Reduces duplication when many statements reference the same variant.

HGVS : The Human Genome Variation Society's nomenclature for sequence variants, such as NM_006269.2:c.2238_2239del. ClinVar's HGVS expressions are in a variation's clinvarHgvsList extension, and an allele's genomic hgvs.g expression in its expressions.

SPDI : NCBI's Sequence, Position, Deletion, Insertion notation for a variant, such as NC_000008.11:54626117:AAAA:AA. An allele's expressions carry it with syntax: "spdi", alongside its hgvs.g and gnomad (VCF-style chromosome-position-reference-alternate) expressions.

Inline Format : JSON structure where related objects are fully embedded within the parent. Self-contained — each record has all data needed for interpretation.

JSON Pointer : Standard format (RFC 6901) for referencing JSON values. ClinVar-GKM bundles use #/{section}/{id} pointers to link records across sections (e.g., #/variation/clinvar:12582); see ID References.

BigQuery : Google Cloud Platform data warehouse used for all ClinVar-GKM SQL procedures and table storage.

Stored Procedure : BigQuery SQL routine executing a specific pipeline step (e.g., gkm_catvar_proc, gkm_vcv_proc).

items.title: External Databases
items.text:
MedGen : Medical Genetics database providing standardized condition identifiers. Primary coding system for conditions.

OMIM (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man) : Comprehensive database of genetic disorders. Used for condition cross-references.

MONDO (Monarch Disease Ontology) : Unified disease ontology providing standardized condition identifiers.

HPO (Human Phenotype Ontology) : Standardized phenotype terms used for conditions and mode of inheritance.

Orphanet : Database of rare diseases. Used for condition cross-references.

HGNC (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee) : Official gene nomenclature database. Gene symbols and identifiers appear in gene context qualifiers.

dbSNP : NCBI SNP database. External cross-reference source for variants.

identifiers.org : Standardized URL namespace for biomedical identifiers used in mapping IRIs.

items.title: Known Issues
items.text: This page documents the current release status, data-coverage limitations, and transformation caveats of the ClinVar-GKM pipeline.

items.title: Release status
items.text: The current line is 1.2 (schema 1.2.0): the ClinVar profiles narrowed to exactly what the pipeline writes. It is built on the finalized GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) standards — VRS 2.1.1, Cat-VRS 1.1.1, VA-Spec 1.1.0, and GKM-Core 1.3.0 — and published under v1/1.2/, starting with one checkpoint monthly. The 1.1.x releases are kept, frozen, under v1/1.1/, and the 1.0.1 releases under v1/1.0/. See the Changelog for what 1.2.0 changes and 1.1.0 for the release before it.

items.title: Data coverage
items.text:
Each release includes 100% of the Germline and Somatic submission (SCV) records from the corresponding ClinVar XML release, and their classification content is carried through without modification to what ClinVar provides. However, the pipeline does not yet extract 100% of every attribute and tertiary content:

  • Case-level and functional data — aggregate case values, grouped/individual case-level evidence, and functional-data (incl. MaveDB) submissions are not currently extracted.
  • Rarely-provided attributes — some attributes that ClinVar provides only occasionally and sparsely may also not yet be represented.

If data that exists in ClinVar is missing here and would be useful to you, it can be added to the Roadmap and prioritized by community demand — open or upvote a discussion in the Ideas category. Case-level / functional data are already tracked as roadmap items (case data, functional data).

items.title: Delta reconstruction — VRS allele records (resolved in 1.1.0)
items.text: In 1.0.1, reconstructing a release's allele section from the prior release plus its weekly delta was inexact for about a dozen VRS allele records, most at the 2026-08-29 release, where the VRS line advanced, and the rest from non-deterministic ordering in allele assembly. Resolved in 1.1.0: alleles are built once per allele id with a total order, and the delta-reconstruction oracle finds no difference (0,0,0) on every section for all 16 delta pairs, including the cross-version pair 2026-08-22 → 2026-08-29. The frozen 1.0.1 deltas under v1/1.0/ keep the old behavior.

items.title: VRS normalization errors
items.text: VRS normalization does not resolve every variation. In the 2026-10-18 release, 6 of the 43,868 variations sent for normalization returned an error. The error text is in the vrsProcessingException extension on the variation's variation record. See Categorical Variant Extensions.

items.title: Malformed HGVS expressions in ClinVar
items.text: 16 HGVS expressions on 14 variations in ClinVar's VCV XML are malformed at the source, most without an HGVS type letter (g., c.). From 1.1.0 each is kept verbatim as an extension of a listed expression, either merged onto ClinVar's valid expression for the same accession or on a repaired one; see HgvsListItem. They were reported to ClinVar on 2026-10-18 (NCBI case CAS-1713568-P1W1Q1), tracked in #163.

items.title: DOIs that VA-Spec's pattern rejects
items.text: VA-Spec's Document.doi pattern rejects some valid DOIs, such as SICI-style DOIs with parentheses (ga4gh/va-spec#461). Such a DOI is kept in the clinvarDoi extension of its Document, with its doi.org URL in urls, instead of in doi. See Citations.

items.title: RCV membership lists SCVs missing from the VCV data
items.text: ClinVar's RCV-format XML runs out of sync with its VCV XML: an RCV's SCV list sometimes names SCVs that are absent from the VCV data, 2–3 a week. This is ClinVar's data, faithfully parsed. RCV statements are built only from SCVs present in the VCV data, so an RCV's evidence can list fewer SCVs than ClinVar's RCV record.

items.title: Name-derived gene context genes are not in the gene section
items.text: An SCV proposition's gene context can be a gene named in the variant's title that ClinVar does not associate with the variant (for example NR_164162.1(GLRA4):n.1091C>T → GLRA4). The bundle's gene section lists only the genes ClinVar associates with a variant, so such a gene has no gene record, and in the Parquet 'ncbigene:' || geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code finds no row in gene.parquet. In the 2026-10-11 release this is 25 variants and 31 SCV propositions. Genes with no HGNC id (LOC*) and NCBI-discontinued gene ids get no gene context, by design of the upstream method.

items.title: SCV and aggregate codes for Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic differ in case
items.text: ClinVar-GKM's classification lookup (clinvar_clinsig_types, maintained upstream in clinvar-ingest-bq-tools) codes Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic as pathogenic/Likely pathogenic, with a capital L; every other code in it is lower case. An SCV classified Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic carries that code unchanged in its classification.primaryCoding. From 1.2.0, VCV and RCV classifications also carry a primaryCoding, and its code is always lower case, so the same label is pathogenic/likely pathogenic there. Compare classification codes case-insensitively until the lookup is fixed upstream. See classification.primaryCoding.

items.title: Past Parquet is built, not downloaded
items.text:
Only the latest Parquet set of each live line is published. Tables for an earlier release are built from its bundle with gkm-bundle-parquet (2.0.0 on PyPI), which builds a full bundle in about 3.5 hours on a 16 GB machine, or 40 minutes on a 128 GiB one; a mini-bundle of the records you need takes far less. See Build Your Own Tables and Mini-Bundles.

Additional edge cases, transformation caveats, and specific limitations will be documented here as they are identified.

items.title: Release Validation
items.text:
Every release is gated before any file is published. The gates check the BigQuery tables the bundles are exported from, the real staged bundles themselves, and the Parquet dataset derived from them. A release is published only when every gate passes. This page lists the gates and the results of each release, newest first.

The step-by-step procedures, with the exact commands, are the 1.2.0 release runbook and the 1.1.0 rebuild runbook. The changes these gates verified are listed in the changelog: 1.2.0, 1.1.0.

items.title: Gates
items.text:
Gate What it checks Scope Proposition structure and reference integrity validate-proposition-conformance.sh: every proposition has the structure its type requires, and every statement and evidence-line pointer names the section its proposition is in — no old-section, unparsed, dangling, misrouted or bare reference Every dataset Expected difference Every row that differs from a snapshot taken before the rebuild is joined on its primary key and classified; each class of change must be attributed to a fix shipped in the release Every dataset that existed before the rebuild Delta reconstruction oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh: the baseline release minus the delta's deletes plus the delta's records equals the next release, compared on all 21 bundle tables Every consecutive pair of releases Strict schema validation validate-bundle.sh, with jsonschema-rs and a registry holding the repo's schema/ tree (the ClinVar-GKM schemas and the GA4GH schemas they reference), validates every record of the real staged bundle, verbatim, against the bundle schema (Draft 2020-12). A failure stops the release before upload Every full bundle and every delta (from 1.2.0; see below) Official toolkit cross-check The official GA4GH gkm-toolkit's validate_bundle_schema (ga4gh.gkm 0.4.0, python-jsonschema) validates a stratified 1% sample of the line's first full bundle (sample-bundle.py: at least 3,000 records of every section, spread over the section, copied verbatim). The tests also require both engines to name the same failing records in bundles with planted violations, including inside the layered variation, vcv and scv profiles Each version release Structural check schema_version, section order, one well-formed record per line, and per-section record counts equal to the BigQuery tables Every other full bundle No null or empty values No field anywhere carries null, "", [] or {}, except the null bound of a VRS Range, which VRS uses for an open-ended coordinate, and the empty sequence of a deletion's VRS ReferenceLengthExpression (length 0) Every staged bundle Bundle ↔ Parquet Per-section record counts, ids in both directions, and a sampled comparison of each row's data with the bundle record The Parquet dataset against the full bundle of the release it was built from

1.1.0: the official toolkit on every record. In 1.1.0 the gkm-toolkit validated the 2026-06-27 full and the 16 deltas. Each later full bundle equals the first full plus the deltas after it, which the delta-reconstruction gate proves, so those 17 files contain every distinct record that 1.1.0 publishes. The other fulls got the structural check.

From 1.2.0: jsonschema-rs on every record of every bundle. run-release.sh builds each release's delta and weekly full and validates every record of both with validate-bundle.sh before anything is uploaded; a failure stops the release. The engine is jsonschema-rs: the same bundle schema, registry and per-record documents as the toolkit, and the same Draft 2020-12 check (the toolkit's validate_bundle_schema adds no checks of its own). It takes about 15 minutes on a full bundle. The toolkit takes about 17 hours on 64 cores for a 1.2.0 full, about 3.6 times as long as for 1.1.0: the 1.2.0 profiles close each ClinVar record type with unevaluatedProperties over layered allOf/$ref schemas (71 uses, against 27 in 1.1.0), and python-jsonschema re-evaluates every layer to apply it, where jsonschema-rs does not. So the toolkit now cross-checks a sample at each version release (see the table), and the engine tests require both engines to fail the same records.

items.title: 1.2.0 Results
items.text:
1.2.0 built 3 BigQuery datasets with the 1.2.0 procedures (2026-10-31, 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15) and published the new line v1/1.2/: the checkpoint monthly clinvar-gkm_2026-11 (built from 2026-10-31), the weekly full bundles and deltas of 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15, and a Parquet dataset built from 2026-11-15. The 1.2.0 runbook gated each release with delta reconstruction, jsonschema-rs on every record, the toolkit cross-check and the Parquet checks; the other gates are marked below.

Gate Result Proposition structure and reference integrity Not run as a separate gate for 1.2.0 Expected difference Not run for 1.2.0. The 1.2.0 changes to VCV and RCV records are described in the changelog Delta reconstruction PASS on both published pairs, 0,0,0 on all 21 tables: 2026-10-31 → 2026-11-08 (across the ClinVar ingest versions v2_6_1 → v2_7_0) and 2026-11-08 → 2026-11-15. The pair 2026-10-24 → 2026-10-31 spans the change of procedures (1.1.0 → 1.2.0) and is not a published 1.2 delta Strict schema validation PASS, failing: 0, jsonschema-rs 0.61.1 on every record: the 2026-11 monthly (91,854,927 records), the 2026-11-08 weekly full (91,965,575), the 2026-11-15 weekly full (91,973,603) and the 2026-11-15 delta (39,062). The 2026-11-08 delta (1,779,702 records) was validated with the toolkit engine instead: failing: 0 Official toolkit cross-check PASS, failing: 0: the stratified 1% sample of the 2026-11 monthly, 940,700 records in 20 sections (1,771 s), and the whole 2026-11-08 delta (above) Structural check Each validation run checked schema_version 1.2.0 against the schema's constant and counted the records of every section. No separate comparison with the BigQuery counts was run No null or empty values 28 records found in the 2026-11 monthly (91,854,927 records); none in the 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15 deltas (1,779,702 and 39,062). Scanned on 2026-11-23 from the published files. In those 28 SCVs, the submittedCondition extension's original_medgen_match has an empty name (a MedGen id with no name; 27 at the top level, 1 inside concepts). The schema allows it, so schema validation passes; removing it is a follow-up. The deltas also hold 84 deletions whose ReferenceLengthExpression has an empty sequence (allowed, above). Each weekly full is the monthly plus the deltas before it, so it holds at most these 28 Bundle ↔ Parquet PASS for 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-15, with gkm-bundle-parquet 2.0.0: verify --bundle-recompute (0 groups differ) and verify --roundtrip (identical) against the full bundle, 20 tables whose rows equal the bundle's records (91,965,575 and 91,973,603). The published set is 2026-11-15's

A delta's manifest counts the condition sets its change log records, including single-member sets, which the export drops (the 2026-11-15 delta's manifest counts 149 conditionSet records, the bundle holds 138). This doesn't affect the bundles: replaying the 2026-11 monthly and both deltas gives the 2026-11-15 weekly full exactly, in all 20 sections, and replaying 2026-11-08 + the 2026-11-15 delta gives it exactly in conditionSet.

items.title: Follow-ups
items.text:
• Empty MedGen name. The export should leave out an empty original_medgen_match.name in the submittedCondition extension (28 SCVs in the 2026-11 monthly), so the no-empty-values rule holds again.
  • Gates not run for 1.2.0. Proposition structure and reference integrity, and the expected-difference comparison, weren't run; the next release runbook should run them, or say why they no longer apply.

No stamped validation reports are attached to the 1.2.0 GitHub Release.

items.title: 1.1.0 Results
items.text:
1.1.0 rebuilt 17 BigQuery datasets, 2026-06-27 through 2026-10-18, and staged 4 monthly full bundles, 3 weekly full bundles, 16 deltas and one Parquet dataset built from 2026-10-18.

Gate Result Proposition structure and reference integrity PASS on 17/17 datasets Expected difference PASS on 16/16 datasets: every difference attributed to a shipped fix Delta reconstruction PASS on 16/16 pairs, 0,0,0 (no missing, extra or differing rows) on all 21 tables, including the cross-version pair 2026-08-22 → 2026-08-29 Strict GA4GH validation PASS, failing: 0: the 2026-06-27 full (86,810,319 records), all 16 deltas and the 2026-10-18 weekly full (91,491,982 records), every section Structural check PASS on the other 5 full bundles (2026-08-04, 2026-08-29, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-04, 2026-10-11): schema_version 1.1.0, section order, well-formed records, and per-section counts equal to BigQuery No null or empty values PASS on all 4 monthly and 3 weekly full bundles and the 16 deltas Bundle ↔ Parquet PASS for 2026-10-18: all 20 sections have equal counts and ids (0 in the bundle only, 0 in Parquet only); 183,368 sampled records' data equal

items.title: Verification reports
items.text:
The strict GA4GH validation of the published files produces a stamped report for each file. Each report records:

  • the UTC run time;
  • the tool and schema versions;
  • the file's published URL and the sha256 of the bytes validated, checked against the published .sha256;
  • per section, the records and failures and the schema those records are validated against;
  • every check, and any warnings.

The 1.1.0 reports are attached to the 1.1.0 GitHub Release:

File Result Report weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz (the newest full bundle) PASS: 91,491,982 records in 20 sections, 0 failing Markdown · JSON deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz PASS: 215,170 records in 15 sections, 0 failing Markdown · JSON

Reports for the other full bundles and deltas will be added as they are produced. The report option is being contributed to the GA4GH GKM Toolkit (ga4gh/gkm-starter-kit#128).

items.title: Roadmap
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM's direction is shaped in the open. The table below is the current backlog of ideas under consideration, ordered by community upvotes. Each idea has a matching GitHub Discussion — open it and use the Upvote button (the ▲ in the bottom-left corner of the discussion's opening post) to signal you want it prioritized, and comment with your use case. Maintainers use the upvote tally to decide the order in which features and improvements are taken on.

Nothing here is a commitment or a delivery date — it's a prioritization board. Items move through Proposed → Spec'd → In progress → Shipped as they gain support and get built.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• Upvote: open an idea's discussion and click the Upvote button (the ▲ in the bottom-left corner of the discussion's opening post). The upvote tally drives the ordering above. GitHub Discussions support upvotes only — there is no downvote. Add a comment with your use case for extra signal.
  • Propose a new idea: open a discussion in the Ideas category. If the maintainers authorize it (by adding the roadmap authorized label), it appears in the table automatically.
  • Follow progress: an idea's status is updated as it moves toward implementation; the linked discussion carries the detailed conversation.

Feedback and feature requests are always welcome via the GitHub issue tracker as well.

items.title: Versioning & Releases
items.text: How the ClinVar-GKM bundle schema and its data releases are versioned, how breaking changes roll out, and how to stay informed.

items.title: Two things are versioned
items.text:
• The schema — the shape of the bundle (its fields, types, and references). It carries a semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
  • The data releases — the periodic bundles themselves: a monthly full, weekly fulls and weekly deltas, each dated. Every release conforms to a specific schema version.

items.title: What the schema version means
items.text:
Change Version bump Where it is published What it means for you MAJOR (2.0.0) Breaking A new line folder, v2/2.0/ A bundle valid under the old version may no longer validate or parse the same way — a field was removed, renamed, retyped, restructured, or made required. You may need to update your code. MINOR (1.2.0) Additive, or a correction that rewrites published bundles A new line folder, v1/1.2/ New optional fields, sections or values, or corrected content in republished bundles. Old consumers keep working unchanged. PATCH (1.1.1) Cosmetic The current line folder No change to valid instances, and no published file is rewritten — only new dated files are added.

A change to a string value's format that leaves the schema shape untouched (same fields and types) is not a schema version change — it is recorded in the Changelog. A content-only correction that must rewrite published bundles is still released as a new MINOR line, even when the schema shape is unchanged. The new line's schema $id version and every bundle's schema_version move to that MINOR too, so a bundle's schema_version always names the line folder it was published in. A PATCH never rewrites a published file.

Upstream standards are insulated

ClinVar-GKM builds on the GA4GH GKM schemas (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec). When one of those bumps, the ClinVar-GKM version changes only by the actual effect on the bundle we emit — not automatically. An upstream major release that doesn't change any field we emit is not a major change for ClinVar-GKM.

items.title: 1.1.0 and general availability
items.text:
1.1.0 is generally available (GA). It was a breaking change — the proposition sections were renamed — released as a MINOR under the initial-stabilization exception (ADR 0006). It was published into a new line folder, v1/1.1/, and the 1.0.1 generation became the frozen line v1/1.0/ (ADR 0009). The stabilization period ends with 1.1.0:

  • Published files are immutable. The bytes behind a published monthly or delta are never replaced. A rollover can move a file to a new folder without changing its name, bytes or checksum. Weekly full bundles are the one exception: they are deleted after their month, and any past week can be rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas. The index.json files, feed.xml and every 00-latest path are pointers that move with each release.
  • Every later breaking change opens a new MAJOR line (v2/2.0/), with the RFC process below.

See the 1.1.0 changelog for the migration notes.

items.title: 1.2.0: a new MINOR line
items.text:
1.2.0 narrows the ClinVar profiles to exactly what the pipeline writes, a MINOR change. It is published into a new line folder, v1/1.2/, and v1/1.1/ is frozen with "superseded_by": "v1/1.2":

  • The new line starts with a checkpoint. v1/1.2/ begins with one monthly full built with the 1.2.0 pipeline, the official monthly of the ClinVar month it is the source of (ADR 0002). Weekly fulls and deltas run forward from it, so the first delta's baseline_release is the checkpoint's source_release. Earlier releases are not republished into the new line; they stay in v1/1.1/ as 1.1.0.
  • The frozen line keeps its records. v1/1.1/ keeps its monthlies, 00-latest copy and deltas, unchanged, and gains a MANIFEST.json and a README.txt. Its weekly fulls and its Parquet set are deleted at the freeze: neither is a record (ADR 0008 (e), ADR 0009 §4).

items.title: How breaking changes roll out
items.text:
A breaking (MAJOR) change opens a new line folder, v2/2.0/, built in full — every monthly full and delta in the published window — alongside v1/. At the switch-over:

  • The prior line is frozen: it gets no new releases, and its files stay downloadable and unchanged.
  • A frozen line is kept indefinitely. There is no end-of-life date, no deprecated status and no deletion window.
  • The root manifest and the line's own index.json mark it "status": "frozen" with "superseded_by" naming the line that replaced it, and the frozen folder carries a MANIFEST.json (size and sha256 per file) and a README.txt saying what replaced it and why.

Only one line is current at a time; frozen lines accumulate. A new MINOR line (for example v1/1.2/) freezes the line it replaces in the same way, but starts from a checkpoint monthly instead of a full republish (see 1.2.0), and the frozen line drops its weekly fulls and Parquet.

The published schema always matches the data

The schema in schema/clinvar-gkm/ is the source of truth and is updated in the same change as any adjustment to the emitted bundle — so a given release's data always validates against its stated schema version, and the published examples are validated against it.

items.title: Finding and pinning a version
items.text:
Each version line lives in its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/ (v1/1.2/, later v2/2.0/), with its own index.json. PATCH releases add new dated files to their line's folder; a new MINOR or MAJOR starts a new folder, and the line it replaces is frozen and kept indefinitely, its records unchanged (the 1.1.x releases are the frozen line v1/1.1/, the 1.0.1 generation v1/1.0/). Inside a line the layout mirrors NCBI's ClinVar FTP site; see Downloads. A small root manifest at the bucket root, index.json, lists every line, its status and schema version, and where its own index.json and feed are. Its shape, as published for 1.2.0:

{
  "manifest_version": 2,
  "updated_at": "2026-11-30T00:00:00Z",
  "base_url": "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org",
  "current": "v1/1.2",
  "versions": {
    "1.2": {"line": "v1/1.2", "major": 1, "minor": 2, "status": "current", "schema": "1.2.0",
            "superseded_by": null, "index": "v1/1.2/index.json", "feed": "v1/1.2/feed.xml"},
    "1.1": {"line": "v1/1.1", "major": 1, "minor": 1, "status": "frozen", "schema": "1.1.0",
            "superseded_by": "v1/1.2", "index": "v1/1.1/index.json", "feed": "v1/1.1/feed.xml"},
    "1.0": {"line": "v1/1.0", "major": 1, "minor": 0, "status": "frozen", "schema": "1.0.1",
            "superseded_by": "v1/1.1", "index": "v1/1.0/index.json", "feed": "v1/1.0/feed.xml"}
  }
}

versions is keyed by {major}.{minor}; paths are relative to base_url. A line is current or frozen; there is no eol field.

To pin to a line, read releases from that line's index.json and ignore the others. To track the latest, follow the line whose status is current. Every bundle also carries a top-level schema_version field, so you can confirm a file's exact version from the file itself.

items.title: Versions of these docs
items.text:
The documentation is versioned by release line, like the data: 1.1 describes the v1/1.1/ line, 1.2 the v1/1.2/ line, and so on. A patch release updates its line's docs in place. Choose a version from the selector next to the site name in the header; the selector keeps you on the same page when it exists in the other version.

  • The latest release is the default. The site root, and any link without a version in it, opens the same page in the latest release. Its header is indigo.
  • An older release has a grey header and a notice that it is not the current version, with a link to the same page in the latest release. It shows the site as it was last built for that line.

Unreleased changes are not published as a docs version: the docs change with a release. A link to the former dev version (…/clinvar-gkm/dev/<page>/) opens the same page in the latest release.

The download tables and the live query console in each version read that version's data line: the 1.1 docs list the files in v1/1.1/, the 1.2 docs those in v1/1.2/. On a frozen line the weekly full bundles and the Parquet set are deleted, so those tables and the console say so and link to the latest docs (the console says so on any frozen line, even before the deletion). Each version lists the frozen lines older than its own on Previous Releases and on the Get the Data landing page: the latest release lists every frozen line, the 1.1 docs only 1.0.

The repository link at the right of the header names the source each version was built from, and its links to repository files point there too: the release tag (such as 1.1.0). The 1.1 docs are built from the main commit that documented 1.1.0 (036bec2), plus their Previous Releases page (the branch docs/line-1.1), because the 1.1.0 tag was cut without them, so their repository-file links point at that branch's commit.

To link to a page in whatever release is latest, use a link without a version, such as https://dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/reference/changelog/. To pin a link to one version, include it: …/clinvar-gkm/1.1/reference/changelog/. The decision record is ADR 0011.

items.title: Release notes
items.text:
• The Changelog records every schema change (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH) and every data re-release, with dates and migration pointers.
  • Each tagged release is listed on GitHub Releases with its source.
  • Each weekly delta's manifest gives its per-section added, updated and deleted counts; see Weekly Deltas.

items.title: Stay informed & have a say
items.text:
Subscribe

  • Watch the GitHub repository (Custom → Releases & Discussions) for release announcements and change proposals.
  • Subscribe to the release feed (Atom, each line's feed.xml, e.g. https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/feed.xml) in any feed reader.
  • Join the email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org, a Google Group for release announcements, change notices and RFCs about the repository, the data releases, tools and documentation. No GitHub account needed; see Stay Informed for how to join.

Before any breaking change, we open a Request for Comment (RFC) — a proposal with its rationale and migration impact — send subscribers an advance notice, and hold a minimum 4-week comment window so affected consumers can weigh in before the change is finalized. Every republish into a new line and every switch-over is announced in advance.

The decision records are ADR 0004 (schema versioning and release management), ADR 0006 (1.1.0 under the stabilization exception), and ADR 0008 (bundles are the public record) and ADR 0009 (R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar), proposed in PR #168.

Presented at GA4GH Connect — October 2, 2026

This primer was prepared for GA4GH Connect (October 2, 2026) to introduce ClinVar-GKM to the GKS community.

Download URLs predate 1.1.0

A ~8-minute (15-slide) introduction to ClinVar-GKM for a technical audience that knows ClinVar but is new to VA-Spec and the GKM model. It covers how ClinVar's complete data is organized today (shown with the real VCV XML schema), how the newest GKM standards (VRS 2.1.1 · Cat-VRS 1.1.1 · VA-Spec 1.1.0, on GKM-Core 1.3.0) reorganize it for consistent, accurate access, the bundle shape and class inventory, a worked example, the community profiles and ClinVar-specific implementer profiles in play, downloads, the transparency of how the data is produced, and who is adopting it for production.

items.title: Choose Your Data
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM publishes the same data in several forms. They differ in size, in how often they change, and in what they are good for. This page compares them, with their current sizes, and suggests where to start.

Sizes are from the line's index.json and Parquet manifest.json for the 2026-11-15 release. A full bundle grows by a few MB a week; Check the current sizes below reads them live.

items.title: The options
items.text:
Data Size Updated Good for Where Published Parquet tables 20 tables, 5 KB to 1.7 GB each, 4.6 GB in all; most questions need two or three (sizes) Every weekly release; one set, overwritten SQL in DuckDB, Python, R or Spark; the browser console; questions about the current data Parquet Files Weekly full bundle 4.9 GB compressed, 68.5 GB decompressed Every weekly release; kept for the current month only The newest state as JSON; loading records into the GA4GH libraries Weekly Full Bundles Official monthly full bundle 4.9 GB compressed, 68.5 GB decompressed Once a month, lined up with ClinVar's monthly release; kept for good A fixed snapshot to cite or reproduce; the starting point for deltas Monthly Full Bundles Monthly plus weekly deltas One monthly (4.9 GB), then one delta a week: usually 2 to 30 MB, up to about 150 MB Every weekly release Keeping a local copy current without downloading 4.9 GB a week; seeing exactly what changed each week Weekly Deltas, Keep Your Data Current Previous releases About 4.8 GB per monthly; deltas as above Frozen: never change Data in an older schema (1.1.x, 1.0.1), for work that was built on it Previous Releases Build your own Your choice: from a mini-bundle of one variant or one submitter to every table of a release Whenever you run it Parquet for an earlier release; a subset of ClinVar as a self-contained bundle; your own column set Build Your Own Dataset

Where to start: query the published Parquet. The Quick Start runs SQL in your browser with nothing to download; after that, download the two or three tables your question needs. To see the JSON format, download a weekly delta (a few MB) before a full bundle.

When you need a full bundle: use the newest weekly full for the current state, and the official monthly for a snapshot that matches ClinVar's monthly release. The monthly reflects the last release of the previous month, not the current week; How Releases Work explains the schedule.

A full bundle is too large to open whole

Decompressed, a full bundle is 68.5 GB. Read it streamed (gunzip -c), one record per line, rather than loading it into memory or decompressing it to disk; see Count records in a full bundle. Set Up Your Tools lists disk and memory needs.

items.title: Parquet table sizes
items.text:
Small tables are quick to download and to query over the network; the five largest are better downloaded once and queried locally. The 20 Tables explains what each holds.

Table Rows Size therapy 38 5 KB therapyGroup 10 6 KB sequenceReference 216 20 KB submitter 3,601 138 KB propositionSomaticClinicalImpact 12,607 147 KB propositionOncogenicity 12,233 154 KB condition 23,450 2.0 MB propositionClinvarCustom 186,357 2.4 MB copyNumberChange 31,753 3.3 MB gene 92,994 3.4 MB copyNumberCount 47,557 4.9 MB conditionSet 101,024 5.0 MB vcv 9,210,004 148 MB rcv 12,124,928 185 MB evidenceLine 21,646,324 265 MB propositionPathogenicity 28,020,731 403 MB location 4,230,835 428 MB allele 4,620,098 701 MB scv 6,895,428 785 MB variation 4,713,415 1.7 GB All 20 4.6 GB

items.title: Check the current sizes
items.text:
These read the live index files. They need curl and jq (Set Up Your Tools).

# Every Parquet table: file, size in bytes, rows
curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/manifest.json \
  | jq -r '.tables[] | [.file, .size, .rows] | @tsv'

# The full bundles of the current line, monthly and weekly: path, size in bytes
curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json \
  | jq -r '(.datasets.monthly[], .datasets.weekly[]) | [.path, .size] | @tsv'

# This year's weekly deltas: release, size in bytes
curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json \
  | jq -r '.deltas[] | [.release, .bundle.size] | @tsv'

items.title: Key Concepts
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM data uses a handful of ideas, each building on the one before: a variant, a proposition about it, statements that classify that proposition, the aggregate statements ClinVar builds from them, and the bundle that holds them all. This page explains each in a paragraph or two and links to its detailed page. The Glossary defines every term.

The examples follow ClinVar's variation 10 (the HFE p.His63Asp variant), the same one the Quick Start queries.

items.title: Variants: Cat-VRS variations and VRS alleles
items.text:
A ClinVar variation is what ClinVar's website shows at /clinvar/variation/10/. In ClinVar-GKM it is a variation record with the id clinvar:10, of type CategoricalVariant, from the GA4GH Cat-VRS (Categorical Variation Representation) standard. A categorical variant is a ClinVar-level concept: it names a variant the way ClinVar does, with its HGVS names, genes and cross-references.

Most variations are defined by one precise genomic change, a VRS allele (GA4GH Variation Representation Specification). A VRS allele has a computed id, such as ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY for variation 10: the same change gets the same id in any system that computes it, which is what makes VRS ids useful for matching data across sources. The allele points to its location, and the location to its sequence reference (a chromosome or transcript).

variation clinvar:10  →  allele ga4gh:VA.ELQ…  →  location ga4gh:SL.…  →  sequenceReference SQ.…

Copy-number variants are defined by a location rather than an allele, and some complex variants have no VRS definition at all. See Variations.

items.title: Propositions: what is being claimed
items.text:
A proposition is the claim a classification is about, separate from the verdict. For a germline pathogenicity classification, the proposition reads "variant clinvar:10 is causal for Hereditary hemochromatosis": a subject (the variant), a predicate (isCausalFor) and an object (a condition, or a set of conditions). Its type says what kind of claim it is, for example VariantPathogenicityProposition, VariantOncogenicityProposition or ClinvarRiskFactorProposition.

Propositions are stored in four groups by meaning: pathogenicity, oncogenicity, somatic clinical impact, and ClinVar's other classification types. Proposition Types maps every ClinVar classification type to its proposition.

Conditions are ClinVar's traits (diseases and phenotypes), with the id clinvar.trait:<id>. A proposition about several conditions points to a condition set.

items.title: Statements: SCV, the submitted classification
items.text:
A statement is a classification of a proposition. It carries:

  • the classification itself, such as Pathogenic or Likely benign
  • the proposition it classifies
  • a direction (supports, disputes, or neutral toward the proposition) and a strength
  • ClinVar's review status, and other details, as extensions

Every classification a lab or expert panel submits to ClinVar is an SCV (a ClinVar submission accession, such as SCV000219176). In ClinVar-GKM each SCV is one scv statement, with the id clinvar.submission:SCV000219176.11 (accession and version). It points to its submitter, its proposition, and the publications and methods it cites. See SCV Statements.

items.title: Aggregates: VCV and RCV statements
items.text:
ClinVar combines the SCVs about a variant into an overall call, the one at the top of the variant's page. That is a VCV (Variation in ClinVar) classification. ClinVar also combines them per variant and condition: an RCV (Reference ClinVar) classification.

In ClinVar-GKM these are vcv and rcv statements, built in layers that follow ClinVar's rules:

  • The overall call for one kind of classification, such as VCV000000010.143-G-PATH (germline pathogenicity).
  • Below it, one statement per submission level, such as …-G-PATH-CP (criteria provided) and …-G-PATH-NOCP (no assertion criteria). The overall call comes from the highest level present.
  • Each level statement cites its SCVs, through an evidence line that says whether they count toward the call (Contributing) or not (Non-contributing).

Somatic clinical-impact statements add a layer for each tier. The diagram shows how a statement id encodes its lane, classification type and level:

See VCV Statements, RCV Statements, and Review Status for how the levels rank.

items.title: Bundles, sections and pointers
items.text:
A bundle is one JSON file that holds a whole release. It is a single object with one section per kind of record (variation, allele, condition, submitter, the four proposition sections, evidenceLine, scv, vcv, rcv, …). Each section maps a record's id to the record, so every record is stored once.

Records refer to each other with pointers: strings of the form #/<section>/<id>. #/propositionPathogenicity/VCV000000010-G-PATH is the record with that id in the propositionPathogenicity section. To follow one, split it at the slashes and look the id up in that section. The map shows every section and the pointers between them:

The same records are also published as 20 Parquet tables, one per section, which you can query with SQL. See Output Format, ID References and The 20 Tables.

items.title: Releases and deltas
items.text:
A new release follows each ClinVar weekly release. Each one is published as:

  • a full bundle: every record, about 4.9 GB compressed. A weekly full is published for each release, and an official monthly full once a month, lined up with ClinVar's monthly release.
  • a delta: only the records added or changed since the previous release, usually a few MB, with a manifest that also lists the records deleted. A monthly plus the deltas after it gives the state at any later week.
  • one set of Parquet tables, rebuilt from the newest release.

Releases belong to a version line, a folder such as v1/1.2/. A change to the format starts a new line, and the old one is frozen and kept. See How Releases Work and Choose Your Data.

items.title: Quick Start
items.text:
This page follows one ClinVar variant, variation 10 (the HFE p.His63Asp variant, clinvar:10), from its name to the classifications ClinVar gives it and the conditions they are about, first in SQL and then as JSON. It takes about ten minutes, and nothing larger than a 61 MB download.

Prerequisites

  • Steps 1 to 4: a web browser. The queries run in the query console on Query with SQL, which needs nothing installed.
  • To run the queries on your machine, and the join that lists the conditions: the DuckDB CLI (tested with 1.5.4). The browser console was tested in Chrome on 2026-11-23.
  • Step 5: curl, gunzip and Python 3 (standard library only; tested with 3.14.5), and about 61 MB of disk.

Set Up Your Tools has install commands for each.

The counts and versions shown are from the 2026-11-15 release. ClinVar updates this variant often, so the version number in its ids (.143 below) and the counts may be higher when you run the queries.

items.title: Step 1: Open the console
items.text:
The console runs SQL in your browser, against the published Parquet tables of the current release. Open it on Query with SQL, paste a query below into the text box, and press Run.

Each query names the table by its URL under https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/, the current line's tables, so it runs unchanged in the console and in DuckDB on your machine. The console runs one query every 10 seconds and stops any query that runs longer than 15 seconds; each query in Steps 2 to 4 reads only a few small parts of the files and finishes in a few seconds. If one is stopped, wait for the countdown and press Run again.

items.title: Step 2: Find the variant
items.text:
ClinVar's variation 10 has the id clinvar:10 in the variation table:

SELECT id, name
FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/variation.parquet'
WHERE id = 'clinvar:10';

id          name
clinvar:10  NM_000410.4(HFE):c.187C>G (p.His63Asp)

Every row of this table is a GA4GH Cat-VRS CategoricalVariant, the standard's type for a ClinVar-style variant. Key Concepts explains it.

items.title: Step 3: See what ClinVar says about it
items.text:
ClinVar's classification of the variant, the summary at the top of its ClinVar page, is a set of VCV statements. Their ids start with the variant's VCV accession: the variation id padded to nine digits (clinvar:10 → VCV000000010). The query asks for every id from VCV000000010. up to VCV000000010/ (/ is the character after .), which is every id that starts with VCV000000010.. Tables are sorted by id, so a range like this reads only the small part of the file that holds those ids, which keeps it fast in the browser.

SELECT id,
       classification.name AS classification,
       quality.name AS quality
FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/vcv.parquet'
WHERE id >= 'VCV000000010.' AND id < 'VCV000000010/'   -- ids that start with VCV000000010.
ORDER BY id;

id                            classification                                quality
VCV000000010.143-G-NP         not provided                                  no classification
VCV000000010.143-G-NP-NOCL    not provided                                  no classification
VCV000000010.143-G-OTH        other                                         criteria provided
VCV000000010.143-G-OTH-CP     other                                         criteria provided
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH       Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity  criteria provided
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-CP    Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity  criteria provided
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-FLAG  no classifications from unflagged records     flagged
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH-NOCP  Pathogenic                                    no assertion criteria provided
VCV000000010.143-G-RF         risk factor                                   no assertion criteria provided
VCV000000010.143-G-RF-NOCP    risk factor                                   no assertion criteria provided

Each id reads <accession>.<version>-<lane>-<type>[-<level>]:

  • G is the germline lane.
  • PATH, RF, OTH and NP are the kinds of classification: pathogenicity, risk factor, other, and not provided.
  • An id with no level (…-G-PATH) is ClinVar's overall call for that kind. The ids with a level (-CP criteria provided, -NOCP no assertion criteria, -FLAG flagged) group the submissions by review level. The overall call comes from the highest level present, here -CP.

items.title: Step 4: See why it is conflicting
items.text:
The overall pathogenicity call is Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity. The statement carries ClinVar's review status, and a count of what the submissions said:

SELECT id,
       [e.value_string FOR e IN extensions IF e.name = 'clinvarReviewStatus'][1] AS review_status,
       [e.value_string FOR e IN classification.extensions IF e.name = 'conflictingExplanation'][1] AS submissions
FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/vcv.parquet'
WHERE id >= 'VCV000000010.' AND id < 'VCV000000010/'
  AND id LIKE '%-G-PATH';

id                       review_status                                   submissions
VCV000000010.143-G-PATH  criteria provided, conflicting classifications  Pathogenic(41); Likely pathogenic(2); Pathogenic, low penetrance(1); Uncertain significance(2)

What a statement claims (this variant causes these conditions) is its proposition. A VCV proposition's id is the statement id without the version:

SELECT id, subject, predicate, object
FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/propositionPathogenicity.parquet'
WHERE id = 'VCV000000010-G-PATH';

id                   subject     predicate    object
VCV000000010-G-PATH  clinvar:10  isCausalFor  clinvar.conditionset:vcv-48e5fe986b5c30669858fd0b2177c4e6

The proposition says variant clinvar:10 is causal for a condition set: the conditions the submissions named.

items.title: Run the same queries on your machine
items.text:
The queries run unchanged in the DuckDB CLI: start duckdb and paste one in, or pass it with -c:

duckdb -c "
SELECT id, classification.name AS classification, quality.name AS quality
FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/vcv.parquet'
WHERE id >= 'VCV000000010.' AND id < 'VCV000000010/'
ORDER BY id"

Joins can take longer than the console's 15-second limit, so run them on your machine. This one follows the proposition to the names of its conditions:

duckdb -c "
SELECT c.name AS condition
FROM (SELECT object
      FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/propositionPathogenicity.parquet'
      WHERE id = 'VCV000000010-G-PATH') p
JOIN 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/conditionSet.parquet' cs ON cs.id = p.object
CROSS JOIN unnest(cs.concepts) AS t(member)
JOIN 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/parquet/condition.parquet' c ON c.id = member.id
ORDER BY condition"

condition
Cardiomyopathy
Hemochromatosis type 1
Hereditary hemochromatosis
Neuroendocrine neoplasm
See cases
Variegate porphyria
not provided

The proposition is filtered inside a subquery, so DuckDB reads only the part of the 400 MB propositionPathogenicity file that holds that id; conditionSet and condition are small (7 MB together). Working at Scale explains when a remote query is cheap.

DuckDB installs its httpfs extension the first time a query reads a URL. The server allows about 55 requests per 10 seconds; a query that filters on id, like these, stays well under that.

items.title: Step 5: Read the same statement as JSON
items.text:
The Parquet tables are built from the bundle: one JSON file in which each record is stored once under its id, in a section named for its kind (variation, vcv, scv, …). A full bundle is 4.9 GB, but a weekly delta holds only the records that changed that week, in the same format. ClinVar updated variation 10 to version 143 in the 2026-11-08 release, so that week's delta (61 MB) has its VCV statements.

A delta's path changes when its month ends, so this looks it up in the line's index.json, then downloads it:

DELTA=$(curl -fsS https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.2/index.json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
index = json.load(sys.stdin)
deltas = index["deltas"] + [d for year in index.get("archives", {}).values() for d in year.get("deltas", [])]
print(next(d["bundle"]["path"] for d in deltas if d["release"] == "2026-11-08"))')
curl -fO "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/${DELTA}"

Each record in a bundle is on its own line, so a few lines of Python can stream the file and print the two records wanted: the overall pathogenicity statement and the evidence line it points to. This continues from the download above, in the same directory:

gunzip -c clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1108.json.gz | python3 -c '
import json, sys
wanted = ["VCV000000010.143-G-PATH", "VCV000000010.143-G-PATH.contributing"]
found = {}
for line in sys.stdin:
    key, _, record = line.strip().partition(": ")
    if key.strip("\"") in wanted:
        found[key.strip("\"")] = json.loads(record.rstrip(","))
for key in wanted:
    print(json.dumps(found[key], indent=2))
'

The first record printed is the statement (shown here with a few small objects on one line):

{
  "classification": {
    "conceptType": "Classification",
    "extensions": [
      {
        "name": "conflictingExplanation",
        "value": "Pathogenic(41); Likely pathogenic(2); Pathogenic, low penetrance(1); Uncertain significance(2)"
      }
    ],
    "name": "Conflicting classifications of pathogenicity",
    "primaryCoding": { "code": "conflicting classifications of pathogenicity", "system": "ClinVar" },
    "type": "MappableConcept"
  },
  "direction": "neutral",
  "extensions": [
    { "name": "clinvarReviewStatus", "value": "criteria provided, conflicting classifications" }
  ],
  "hasEvidenceLines": [
    "#/evidenceLine/VCV000000010.143-G-PATH.contributing",
    "#/evidenceLine/VCV000000010.143-G-PATH.non-contributing"
  ],
  "id": "VCV000000010.143-G-PATH",
  "proposition": "#/propositionPathogenicity/VCV000000010-G-PATH",
  "quality": { "conceptType": "Quality", "name": "criteria provided", "type": "MappableConcept" },
  "type": "Statement"
}

These are the values the SQL in Steps 3 and 4 read. In the bundle, a record points to another with a #/section/id string: #/propositionPathogenicity/VCV000000010-G-PATH is the record with that id in the propositionPathogenicity section. The second record printed is the evidence line #/evidenceLine/VCV000000010.143-G-PATH.contributing, which points down to the -CP statement, and that statement's evidence line points to the 46 submissions (SCVs) behind the call. A full bundle resolves every pointer; a delta holds only what changed that week, so the proposition and the variant itself are not in this file.
